verses.Genesis|37|12: And his brothers went to feed their father's flock in Shechem.
verses.Genesis|37|13: And Israel said to Joseph, Do not thy brothers feed the flock in Shechem? come, and I will send thee to them. And he said to him, Here I am.
verses.Genesis|37|14: And he said to him, Go, I pray thee, see whether it be well with thy brothers, and well with the flocks; and bring me word again. So he sent him out of the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
verses.Genesis|37|15: And a certain man found him, and, behold, he was wandering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
verses.Genesis|37|16: And he said, I seek my brothers: tell me, I pray thee, where they feed their flocks.
verses.Genesis|37|17: And the man said, They are departed from here; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brothers, and found them in Dothan.
verses.Genesis|37|18: And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near to them, they conspired against him to slay him.
verses.Genesis|37|19: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer comes.
verses.Genesis|37|20: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, An evil beast has devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.
verses.Genesis|37|21: And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him.
verses.Genesis|37|22: And Reuben said to them, Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might save him out of their hands, to deliver him back to his father.
verses.Genesis|37|23: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come to his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his coat, the long sleeved coat that was on him.
verses.Genesis|37|24: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty; there was no water in it.
verses.Genesis|37|25: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmaelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing gum balm and ladanum, going to carry it down to Egypt.
verses.Genesis|37|26: And Judah said to his brothers, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
verses.Genesis|37|27: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh.
verses.Genesis|37|28: And his brothers hearkened to him. Then there passed by Midianites, merchants; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
verses.Genesis|37|29: And Reuben returned to the pit; and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.
verses.Genesis|37|30: And he returned to his brothers, and said, The child is not; and I, where shall I go?
verses.Genesis|37|31: And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood;
verses.Genesis|37|32: and they sent the coat with long sleeves, and they brought it to their father; and said, This we have found: know now whether it be thy son's coat or no.
verses.Genesis|37|33: And he knew it, and said, It is my son's coat; an evil beast has devoured him; Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces.
verses.Genesis|37|34: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
verses.Genesis|37|35: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down to my son mourning into Sheol. Thus his father wept for him.
verses.Genesis|37|36: And the Midianites sold him to Egypt to Potiphar, Pharaoh's chamberlain, a captain of the guard.
verses.Genesis|38|1: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down from his brothers, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
verses.Genesis|38|2: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shua; and he took her, and went in to her.
verses.Genesis|38|3: And she conceived, and bore a son; and he called his name Er.
verses.Genesis|38|4: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and she called his name Onan.
verses.Genesis|38|5: And she yet again conceived, and bore a son; and called his name Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bore him.
verses.Genesis|38|6: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
verses.Genesis|38|7: And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord; and the Lord slew him.
verses.Genesis|38|8: And Judah said to Onan, Go in to thy brother's wife, and perform the duty of a brother in law, and raise up seed to thy brother.
verses.Genesis|38|9: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in to his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give seed to his brother.
verses.Genesis|38|10: And the thing which he did displeased the Lord: So He slew him also.
verses.Genesis|38|11: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter in law, Remain a widow at thy father's home, till Shelah my son be grown: for he said, Lest perchance he die also, as his brothers did. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
verses.Genesis|38|12: And in process of time the daughter of Shua Judah's wife died; and when Judah was comforted, he went up to his sheep shearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
verses.Genesis|38|13: And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold thy father in law goes up to Timnah to shear his sheep.
verses.Genesis|38|14: And she put off her widow's garments, and covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat by the entrance to Enaim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given to him to wife.
verses.Genesis|38|15: When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a harlot; because she had covered her face.
verses.Genesis|38|16: And he turned to her by the way, and said, Come now, I pray thee, let me come in to thee (for he knew not that she was his daughter in law.) And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayst come in to me?
verses.Genesis|38|17: And he said, I will send thee a kid from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it?
verses.Genesis|38|18: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy cord, and thy staff that is in thy hand.
verses.Genesis|38|19: And he gave it her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him. And she arose, and went away, and laid by her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
verses.Genesis|38|20: And Judah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive his pledge from the woman's hand: but he found her not.
verses.Genesis|38|21: Then he asked the men of that place, saying, Where is the harlot, that was at Enaim by the wayside? And they said, There was no harlot in this place.
verses.Genesis|38|22: And he returned to Judah, and said, I cannot find her; and also the men of the place said, There was no harlot in this place.
verses.Genesis|38|23: And Judah said, Let her take it to her, lest we be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
verses.Genesis|38|24: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law has played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by harlotry. And Judah said, Bring her out and let her be burnt.
verses.Genesis|38|25: When she was brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and the cord, and the staff.
verses.Genesis|38|26: And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She has been more righteous than I; because I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.
verses.Genesis|38|27: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins were in her womb.
verses.Genesis|38|28: And it came to pass, when she travailed, that the one put out his hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.
verses.Genesis|38|29: And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out: and she said, Why hast thou made such a breach for thyself? Therefore his name was called Pharez.
verses.Genesis|38|30: And afterward his brother came out, that had the scarlet thread upon his hand: and his name was called Zerah.
verses.Genesis|39|1: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, the chamberlain of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, a Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmaelites, who had brought him down there.
verses.Genesis|39|2: And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
verses.Genesis|39|3: And his master saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
verses.Genesis|39|4: And Joseph found favour in his sight, and served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.
verses.Genesis|39|5: And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
verses.Genesis|39|6: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand; and he knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was a good-looking person, and well favoured.
verses.Genesis|39|7: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
verses.Genesis|39|8: But he refused, and said to his master's wife, Behold, my master knows not what is with me in the house, and he has committed all that he has to my hand;
verses.Genesis|39|9: there is none greater in this house than I; neither has he kept back anything from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
verses.Genesis|39|10: And it came to pass, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
verses.Genesis|39|11: And it came to pass about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his work; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
verses.Genesis|39|12: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went outside.
verses.Genesis|39|13: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled outside,
verses.Genesis|39|14: that she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying, See, he has brought in a Hebrew to us to mock us; he came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:
verses.Genesis|39|15: and it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and went outside.
verses.Genesis|39|16: And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.
verses.Genesis|39|17: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, whom thou hast brought to us, came in to me to have his sport with me.
verses.Genesis|39|18: And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled outside.
verses.Genesis|39|19: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his anger burned.
verses.Genesis|39|20: And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.
verses.Genesis|39|21: But the Lord was with Joseph, and showed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the officer of the prison.
verses.Genesis|39|22: And the officer of the prison committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatever they did there, he was the doer of it.
verses.Genesis|39|23: The keeper of the prison looked not to anything that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it prosper.
verses.Genesis|40|1: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt, and his baker, offended their lord the king of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|40|2: And Pharaoh was angry against two of his officers, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers.
verses.Genesis|40|3: And he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
verses.Genesis|40|4: And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them, and he served them: and they continued a season in custody.
verses.Genesis|40|5: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream on the same night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.
verses.Genesis|40|6: And Joseph came in to them in the morning, and looked upon them, and, behold, they were sad.
verses.Genesis|40|7: And he asked Pharaoh's officers that were with him in custody in his lord's house, saying, Why do you look so sadly today?
verses.Genesis|40|8: And they said to him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said to them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.
verses.Genesis|40|9: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;
verses.Genesis|40|10: and on the vine were three tendrils: and it was as though it budded, and its blossoms shot forth; and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes:
verses.Genesis|40|11: and Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
verses.Genesis|40|12: And Joseph said to him, This is the interpretation of it: The three tendrils are three days:
verses.Genesis|40|13: within another three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee to thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.
verses.Genesis|40|14: But think of me when it shall be well with thee, and show kindness, I pray thee, to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:
verses.Genesis|40|15: for I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
verses.Genesis|40|16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, I also in my dream, behold, I had three baskets of white bread on my head.
verses.Genesis|40|17: And in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of baked food for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.
verses.Genesis|40|18: And Joseph answered and said, This is its interpretation: The three baskets are three days:
verses.Genesis|40|19: within another three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.
verses.Genesis|40|20: And it came to pass on the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants.
verses.Genesis|40|21: And he restored the chief butler to his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand;
verses.Genesis|40|22: but he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
verses.Genesis|40|23: Nevertheless the chief butler did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
verses.Genesis|41|1: And it came to pass at the end of two years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the River.
verses.Genesis|41|2: And, behold, there came up out of the River seven cows, well favoured, and fat of flesh; and they fed in the reed grass.
verses.Genesis|41|3: And, behold, seven other cows came up after them out of the River, ill favoured and lean of flesh; and stood by the other cows upon the brink of the River.
verses.Genesis|41|4: And the ill favoured and leanfleshed cows ate up the seven well favoured and fat cows. So Pharaoh awoke.
verses.Genesis|41|5: And he slept and dreamed a second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up on one stalk, plump and good.
verses.Genesis|41|6: And, behold, seven ears thin, and blasted by the east wind sprang up after them.
verses.Genesis|41|7: And the seven thin ears devoured the seven plump and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, it was a dream.
verses.Genesis|41|8: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all her wise men: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them to Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|41|9: Then spoke the chief butler to Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:
verses.Genesis|41|10: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the officer of the guard's house, both me and the chief baker:
verses.Genesis|41|11: and we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
verses.Genesis|41|12: And there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the officer of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.
verses.Genesis|41|13: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; I was restored to my office, and he was hanged.
verses.Genesis|41|14: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his garments, and came in to Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|41|15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it.
verses.Genesis|41|16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, it is not me: God shall give Pharaoh a favourable answer.
verses.Genesis|41|17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the River:
verses.Genesis|41|18: and, behold, there came up out of the River seven cows, fat of flesh and well favoured; and they fed in the reed grass:
verses.Genesis|41|19: and, behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ill favoured and lean of flesh, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness:
verses.Genesis|41|20: and the lean and the ill favoured cows did eat up the first seven fat cows:
verses.Genesis|41|21: and when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; for they were still ill favoured, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
verses.Genesis|41|22: And I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, full and good:
verses.Genesis|41|23: and, behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted by the east wind, sprang up after them:
verses.Genesis|41|24: and the thin ears devoured the seven good ears: and I told this to the magicians; but there was none that could explain it to me.
verses.Genesis|41|25: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: God has declared to Pharaoh what he is about to do.
verses.Genesis|41|26: The seven good cows are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.
verses.Genesis|41|27: And the seven thin and ill favoured cows that came up after them are seven years: and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine.
verses.Genesis|41|28: This is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh: What God is about to do He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|41|29: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|30: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;
verses.Genesis|41|31: and the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine following; for it shall be very grievous.
verses.Genesis|41|32: And as for the repetition of the dream to Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is fast determined by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
verses.Genesis|41|33: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|34: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty.
verses.Genesis|41|35: And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.
verses.Genesis|41|36: And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.
verses.Genesis|41|37: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
verses.Genesis|41|38: And Pharaoh said to his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom is the spirit of God?
verses.Genesis|41|39: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, since God has shown thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:
verses.Genesis|41|40: thou shalt be over my house, and according to thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.
verses.Genesis|41|41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|42: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in garments of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
verses.Genesis|41|43: and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Abrech (Bow the knee): and made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|45: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name, Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|46: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went through all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|47: And in the seven years of plenty the earth brought forth by heaps.
verses.Genesis|41|48: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up within it.
verses.Genesis|41|49: And Joseph gathered corn like the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped numbering; for it was without number.
verses.Genesis|41|50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, whom Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bore to him.
verses.Genesis|41|51: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For God, said he, has made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house.
verses.Genesis|41|52: And the name of the second he called Ephraim: For God has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.
verses.Genesis|41|53: And the seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, were ended.
verses.Genesis|41|54: And the seven years of famine began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the famine was in all the lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.Genesis|41|55: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said to all Egypt, Go to Joseph; what he says to you, do.
verses.Genesis|41|56: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: And Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold to Egypt; and the famine grew severe in the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|41|57: And all countries came to Egypt to Joseph to buy corn; because the famine was so severe in all the earth.
verses.Genesis|42|1: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, Why do you look at one another?
verses.Genesis|42|2: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: go down there, and buy for us from there, that we may live, and not die.
verses.Genesis|42|3: And Joseph's ten brothers went down to buy corn in Egypt.
verses.Genesis|42|4: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest mischief befall him.
verses.Genesis|42|5: And the sons of Israel came to buy corn among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.Genesis|42|6: And Joseph was the governor of the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brothers came, and bowed themselves down before him with their faces to the earth.
verses.Genesis|42|7: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange to them, and spoke roughly to them; and he said to them, Where do you come from? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.
verses.Genesis|42|8: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew him not.
verses.Genesis|42|9: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, You are spies; to see the nakedness of the land are you come.
verses.Genesis|42|10: And they said to him, No, my lord, but to buy food are thy servants come.
verses.Genesis|42|11: We are all one man's sons; we are true men, thy servants are no spies.
verses.Genesis|42|12: And he said to them, No, but you are come to see the nakedness of the land.
verses.Genesis|42|13: And they said, Thy servants are twelve, we are brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and, behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more.
verses.Genesis|42|14: And Joseph said to them, That is what I spoke to you, saying, you are spies:
verses.Genesis|42|15: hereby you shall be proved; by the life of Pharaoh you shall not go out of here unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.Genesis|42|16: Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and you shall be kept in prison, that your words may be proved, whether there be any truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.
verses.Genesis|42|17: And he put them all together into custody for three days.
verses.Genesis|42|18: And Joseph said to them on the third day, This do, and live: I fear God:
verses.Genesis|42|19: if you are true men, let one of your brothers be bound in the house of your confinement: and you go, carry corn for the famine of your houses:
verses.Genesis|42|20: but bring your youngest brother to me; so shall your words be verified, and you shall not die. And they did so.
verses.Genesis|42|21: And they said one to another, Truly, we are guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
verses.Genesis|42|22: And Reuben answered them, saying, Did I not speak to you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and you would not hear? therefore, behold, even his blood is required.
verses.Genesis|42|23: And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for he spoke to them by an interpreter.
verses.Genesis|42|24: And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and turned back to them, and spoke with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.
verses.Genesis|42|25: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their sacks with corn, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way: and thus it was performed.
verses.Genesis|42|26: And they loaded their asses with the corn, and departed from there.
verses.Genesis|42|27: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the lodging place, he saw his money; for, behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
verses.Genesis|42|28: And he said to his brethren, My money is returned; and, lo, it is in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this that God has done to us?
verses.Genesis|42|29: And they came to Jacob their father to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had befallen them; saying,
verses.Genesis|42|30: The man, who is the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.
verses.Genesis|42|31: And we said to him, We are true men; we are no spies:
verses.Genesis|42|32: We are twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
verses.Genesis|42|33: And the man, the lord of the country, said to us, Hereby shall I know that you are true men; leave one of your brethren here with me, and take food for the famine of your households, and be gone:
verses.Genesis|42|34: and bring your youngest brother to me: then shall I know that you are no spies, but that you are true men: so will I deliver you your brother, and you shall traffic in the land.
verses.Genesis|42|35: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man's bundle of money was in his sack: and when both they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.
verses.Genesis|42|36: And Jacob their father said to them, You have bereaved me of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and you will take Benjamin away: all these things have come upon me.
verses.Genesis|42|37: And Reuben spoke to his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him back to thee.
verses.Genesis|42|38: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in which you go, then shall you bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to Sheol.
verses.Genesis|43|1: And the famine was severe in the land.
verses.Genesis|43|2: And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the corn which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, Go back, buy us a little food.
verses.Genesis|43|3: And Judah spoke to him, saying, The man did solemnly protest to us, saying, You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.
verses.Genesis|43|4: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:
verses.Genesis|43|5: but if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down: for the man said to us, You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.
verses.Genesis|43|6: And Israel said, Why did you treat me so ill, as to tell the man whether you had another brother?
verses.Genesis|43|7: And they said, The man asked us particularly of our state, and of our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have you another brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: could we possibly know that he would say, Bring your brother down?
verses.Genesis|43|8: And Judah said to Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.
verses.Genesis|43|9: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not to thee, and set him before thee, then I shall have sinned to thee for ever.
verses.Genesis|43|10: For if we had not lingered, surely now we had returned this second time.
verses.Genesis|43|11: And their father Israel said to them, If it must be so now, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, gum, ladanum, nuts, and almonds:
verses.Genesis|43|12: and take double money in your hand; and the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks, carry it back in your hand; perhaps it was an oversight:
verses.Genesis|43|13: take also your brother, and arise, go again to the man:
verses.Genesis|43|14: and God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my children, then I am bereaved.
verses.Genesis|43|15: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and they rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.Genesis|43|16: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the ruler of his house, Bring these men home, and slaughter a beast, and make it ready; for the men shall dine with me at noon.
verses.Genesis|43|17: And the man did as Joseph bade; and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
verses.Genesis|43|18: And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Joseph's house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.
verses.Genesis|43|19: And they came near to the steward of Joseph's house, and they spoke with him at the door of the house,
verses.Genesis|43|20: and said, O sir, we came down indeed at the first time to buy food:
verses.Genesis|43|21: and it came to pass, when we came to the lodging place, that we opened our sacks, and, behold, every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight:
verses.Genesis|43|22: and we have brought it back in our hand. And other money have we brought down in our hands to buy food: we cannot tell who put our money in our sacks.
verses.Genesis|43|23: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.Genesis|43|24: And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.
verses.Genesis|43|25: And they made ready the present for when Joseph came at noon: for they had heard that they should eat bread there.
verses.Genesis|43|26: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.
verses.Genesis|43|27: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?
verses.Genesis|43|28: And they answered, Thy servant our father is in good health, he is still alive. And they bowed down their heads, and made obeisance.
verses.Genesis|43|29: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, Is this your younger brother, of whom you spoke to me? And he said, God be gracious to thee, my son.
verses.Genesis|43|30: And Joseph made haste: for his affection was kindled towards his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.
verses.Genesis|43|31: And he washed his face, and went out, and restrained himself, and said, Set on bread.
verses.Genesis|43|32: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who did eat with them, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.Genesis|43|33: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one at another.
verses.Genesis|43|34: And he took and sent portions to them from before him: but Benjamin's portion was five times as much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.
verses.Genesis|44|1: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in the mouth of his sack.
verses.Genesis|44|2: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
verses.Genesis|44|3: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.
verses.Genesis|44|4: And when they were gone out of the city, and not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, Up, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say to them, Why have you rewarded evil for good?
verses.Genesis|44|5: Is not this that from which my lord drinks, and whereby indeed he divines? you have done evil in so doing.
verses.Genesis|44|6: And he overtook them, and he spoke to them these same words.
verses.Genesis|44|7: And they said to him, Why does my lord say these words? Far be it from thy servants to do according to this thing:
verses.Genesis|44|8: behold, the money, which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again to thee out of the land of Canaan: how then should we steal out of thy lord's house silver or gold?
verses.Genesis|44|9: With whomever of thy servants it be found, let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen.
verses.Genesis|44|10: And he said, Now also let it be according to your words: he with whom it is found shall be my bondman; and you shall be blameless.
verses.Genesis|44|11: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
verses.Genesis|44|12: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and ended at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
verses.Genesis|44|13: Then they rent their clothes, and loaded every man his ass, and returned to the city.
verses.Genesis|44|14: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph's house; for he was still there: and they fell before him to the ground.
verses.Genesis|44|15: And Joseph said to them, What deed is this that you have done? do you not know that such a man as I can certainly divine?
verses.Genesis|44|16: And Judah said, What shall we say to my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are my lord's bondmen, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.
verses.Genesis|44|17: And he said, Far be it from me that I should do so: but the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my bondman; and as for you, go up in peace to your father.
verses.Genesis|44|18: Then Judah came near to him, and said, Oh my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not thy anger burn against thy servant: for thou art even as Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|44|19: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have you a father, or a brother?
verses.Genesis|44|20: And we said to my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.
verses.Genesis|44|21: And thou didst say to thy servants, Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes upon him.
verses.Genesis|44|22: And we said to my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.
verses.Genesis|44|23: And thou didst say to thy servants, Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall see my face no more.
verses.Genesis|44|24: And it came to pass when we came up to thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
verses.Genesis|44|25: And our father said, Go back, and buy us a little food.
verses.Genesis|44|26: And we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down: for we may not see the man's face, unless our youngest brother is with us.
verses.Genesis|44|27: And thy servant my father said to us, You know that my wife bore me two sons:
verses.Genesis|44|28: and the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since:
verses.Genesis|44|29: and if you take this also from me, and mischief befall him, you shall bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to Sheol.
verses.Genesis|44|30: Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad's life;
verses.Genesis|44|31: it shall come to pass, when he sees that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants shall bring down the grey hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.
verses.Genesis|44|32: For thy servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, If I bring him not to thee, then I shall have sinned to my father for ever.
verses.Genesis|44|33: Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant remain instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brothers.
verses.Genesis|44|34: For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me? lest I see the evil that shall come on my father.
verses.Genesis|45|1: Then Joseph could not restrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And no man stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brethren.
verses.Genesis|45|2: And he wept aloud: and Egypt and the house of Pharaoh heard.
verses.Genesis|45|3: And Joseph said to his brethren, I am Joseph: does my father yet live? And his brothers could not answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.
verses.Genesis|45|4: And Joseph said to his brothers, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.Genesis|45|5: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
verses.Genesis|45|6: For these two years has the famine been in the land: and there are five more years, in which there shall neither be ploughing nor harvest.
verses.Genesis|45|7: And God sent me before you to preserve you a remnant in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
verses.Genesis|45|8: So now it was not you that sent me here, but God: and He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|45|9: Hasten, and go up to my father, and say to him, Thus says thy son Joseph, God has made me lord of all Egypt: come down to me, do not delay:
verses.Genesis|45|10: and thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near me, thou, and thy children, and thy children's children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:
verses.Genesis|45|11: and there will I nourish thee; for there are still five years of famine; lest thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast, come to poverty.
verses.Genesis|45|12: And, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
verses.Genesis|45|13: And you shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen: and you shall hasten and bring down my father here.
verses.Genesis|45|14: And he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept on his neck.
verses.Genesis|45|15: And he kissed all his brethren, and wept on them: and after that his brethren talked with him.
verses.Genesis|45|16: And the report was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, Joseph's brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
verses.Genesis|45|17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Say to thy brethren, Do this: load your beasts, and go, get you to the land of Canaan;
verses.Genesis|45|18: and take your father and your households, and come to me: and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
verses.Genesis|45|19: Now thou art commanded, do this; take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
verses.Genesis|45|20: Also give no thought to your goods; for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.
verses.Genesis|45|21: And the children of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
verses.Genesis|45|22: To all of them he gave each man changes of clothing; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of clothing.
verses.Genesis|45|23: And to his father he sent after this manner; ten asses laden with the good things of Egypt and ten she asses laden with corn and bread and food for his father by the way.
verses.Genesis|45|24: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said to them, See that you do not fall out by the way.
verses.Genesis|45|25: And they went up out of Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father,
verses.Genesis|45|26: and told him, saying, Joseph is still alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And his heart fainted, for he believed them not.
verses.Genesis|45|27: And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them: and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:
verses.Genesis|45|28: and Israel said, It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive: I will go and see him before I die.
verses.Genesis|46|1: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
verses.Genesis|46|2: And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here I am.
verses.Genesis|46|3: And He said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down to Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation:
verses.Genesis|46|4: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand on thy eyes.
verses.Genesis|46|5: And Jacob rose up from Beer-sheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
verses.Genesis|46|6: And they took their cattle, and their goods, which they had acquired in the land of Canaan; and came to Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed with him:
verses.Genesis|46|7: his sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and all his seed brought he with him to Egypt.
verses.Genesis|46|8: And these are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn.
verses.Genesis|46|9: And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Pallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
verses.Genesis|46|10: And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of the Canaanite woman.
verses.Genesis|46|11: And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.Genesis|46|12: And the sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zerah: but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pharez were Hezron and Hamul.
verses.Genesis|46|13: And the sons of Issachar; Tola, and Pubba, and Job, and Shimron.
verses.Genesis|46|14: And the sons of Zebulun; Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
verses.Genesis|46|15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Padan-aram, with his daughter Dinah: all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty three.
verses.Genesis|46|16: And the sons of Gad; Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
verses.Genesis|46|17: And the sons of Asher; Jimna, and Jishba, and Jishbi, and Beriah, and Serah their sister: and the sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel.
verses.Genesis|46|18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, sixteen souls.
verses.Genesis|46|19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife; Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.Genesis|46|20: And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, daughter of Poti-pherah; the priest of On bore to him.
verses.Genesis|46|21: And the sons of Benjamin were Bela, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
verses.Genesis|46|22: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
verses.Genesis|46|23: And the sons of Dan; Hushim.
verses.Genesis|46|24: And the sons of Naphtali; Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
verses.Genesis|46|25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
verses.Genesis|46|26: All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, who came out of his loins, besides Jacob's sons' wives, all the souls were sixty six.
verses.Genesis|46|27: And the sons of Joseph, who were born him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob who came into Egypt were seventy.
verses.Genesis|46|28: And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.
verses.Genesis|46|29: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and presented himself to him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
verses.Genesis|46|30: And Israel said to Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art still alive.
verses.Genesis|46|31: And Joseph said to his brethren, and to his father's house, I will go up, and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, My brethren, and my father's house, who were in the land of Canaan, are come to me;
verses.Genesis|46|32: and the men are shepherds, for they have ever been owners of cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.
verses.Genesis|46|33: And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What is your occupation?
verses.Genesis|46|34: that you shall say, Thy servants' trade has been about cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers: that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to Egypt.
verses.Genesis|47|1: Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan; and, behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
verses.Genesis|47|2: And he took some of his brothers, five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|47|3: And Pharaoh said to his brothers, What is your occupation? And they said to Pharaoh, Thy servants are shepherds, both we, and also our fathers.
verses.Genesis|47|4: They said moreover to Pharaoh, To sojourn in the land are we come; for thy servants have no pasture for their flocks; for the famine is severe in the land of Canaan: now therefore, we pray thee, let thy servants dwell in the land of Goshen.
verses.Genesis|47|5: And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren are come to thee:
verses.Genesis|47|6: the land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowst any able men among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.
verses.Genesis|47|7: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|47|8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, How old art thou?
verses.Genesis|47|9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years: few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojournings.
verses.Genesis|47|10: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.
verses.Genesis|47|11: And Joseph provided abodes for his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.Genesis|47|12: And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father's household, with bread, according to their little ones.
verses.Genesis|47|13: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and all the land of Canaan languished by reason of the famine.
verses.Genesis|47|14: And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which they bought: and Joseph brought the money to Pharaoh's house.
verses.Genesis|47|15: And when money failed in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all Egypt came to Joseph, and said, Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for the money fails.
verses.Genesis|47|16: And Joseph said, Give your cattle; and I will give you for your cattle, if money fail.
verses.Genesis|47|17: And they brought their cattle to Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the asses: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their cattle for that year.
verses.Genesis|47|18: When that year was ended, they came to him in the second year, and said to him, We will not hide from my lord, how that our money is spent; my lord also has our herds of cattle; there is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands:
verses.Genesis|47|19: why shall we die before thy eyes, both we and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh: and give us grain, that we may live, and not die, that the land be not desolate.
verses.Genesis|47|20: And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for Egypt sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them: so the land became Pharaoh's.
verses.Genesis|47|21: And as for the people, he removed them to the cities from one end of the borders of Egypt, to the other end.
verses.Genesis|47|22: Only the land of the priests he bought not; for the priests had a portion assigned them by Pharaoh, and did eat their portion which Pharaoh gave them: therefore they sold not their lands.
verses.Genesis|47|23: Then Joseph said to the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is grain for you, and you shall sow the land.
verses.Genesis|47|24: And it shall come to pass at harvest times, that you shall give the fifth part to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
verses.Genesis|47|25: And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find favour in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's servants.
verses.Genesis|47|26: And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth part; except the land of the priests only, which became not Pharaoh's.
verses.Genesis|47|27: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt in the country of Goshen; and they took possession of it, and grew, and multiplied exceedingly.
verses.Genesis|47|28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the whole age of Jacob was a hundred and forty seven years.
verses.Genesis|47|29: And the time drew near for Israel to die: and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, If now I have found favour in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt:
verses.Genesis|47|30: but I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their buryingplace.
verses.Genesis|47|31: And he said, I will do as thou hast said. And he said, Swear to me. And he swore to him. And Israel bowed himself upon the bed's head.
verses.Genesis|48|1: And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
verses.Genesis|48|2: And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph comes to thee: and Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
verses.Genesis|48|3: And Jacob said to Joseph, God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
verses.Genesis|48|4: and said to me, Behold, I will make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a multitude of people; and will give this land to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.
verses.Genesis|48|5: And now thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, who were born to thee in the land of Egypt before I came to thee into Egypt, are mine; as Reuben and Simeon they shall be mine.
verses.Genesis|48|6: And thy issue, which thou begettest after them, shall be thine, and shall be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
verses.Genesis|48|7: And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan on the way, when yet there was but a little way to come to Ephratah: and I buried her there in the way of Ephratah; that is Beth-lehem.
verses.Genesis|48|8: And Israel beheld Joseph's sons, and said, Who are these?
verses.Genesis|48|9: And Joseph said to his father, They are my sons, whom God has given me in this place. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, to me, and I will bless them.
verses.Genesis|48|10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim from age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
verses.Genesis|48|11: And Israel said to Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God has shown me also thy children.
verses.Genesis|48|12: And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
verses.Genesis|48|13: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and he presented them to him.
verses.Genesis|48|14: And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh's head, changing his hands; for Manasseh was the first-born.
verses.Genesis|48|15: And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before Whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God Who has been my shepherd all my life long until this day,
verses.Genesis|48|16: the angel who redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.
verses.Genesis|48|17: And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
verses.Genesis|48|18: And Joseph said to his father, Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head.
verses.Genesis|48|19: And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.
verses.Genesis|48|20: And he blessed them that day, saying, By thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
verses.Genesis|48|21: And Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I die: but God shall be with you, and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
verses.Genesis|48|22: Moreover I have given to thee one portion more than thy brothers, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.
verses.Genesis|49|1: And Jacob called to his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.
verses.Genesis|49|2: Gather yourselves together, and hear, you sons of Jacob; and hearken to Israel your father.
verses.Genesis|49|3: Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power:
verses.Genesis|49|4: unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed; then thou didst defile it: he went up to my couch.
verses.Genesis|49|5: Simeon and Levi are brothers; instruments of cruelty are their swords.
verses.Genesis|49|6: Let my soul not come into their council; to their assembly let my honour not be united: for in their anger they slew a man, and in their selfwill they lamed an ox.
verses.Genesis|49|7: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.
verses.Genesis|49|8: Judah thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be on the neck of thy enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee.
verses.Genesis|49|9: Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him up?
verses.Genesis|49|10: The staff shall not depart from Judah, nor the sceptre from between his feet, until Shiloh come, and the obedience of the people be his.
verses.Genesis|49|11: Binding his foal to the vine, and his ass's colt to the choice vine; he washes his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood of grapes;
verses.Genesis|49|12: his eyes are red with wine, and his teeth white with milk.
verses.Genesis|49|13: Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the sea; and he shall be a haven for ships; and his border shall be at Zidon.
verses.Genesis|49|14: Issachar is a strong ass couching down between the sheepfolds:
verses.Genesis|49|15: and he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and he bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant to tribute.
verses.Genesis|49|16: Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.
verses.Genesis|49|17: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that bites the horse's heels, so that his rider shall fall backward.
verses.Genesis|49|18: I wait for thy salvation, O Lord.
verses.Genesis|49|19: Gad, raiders shall maraud him, but he shall overcome at the last.
verses.Genesis|49|20: Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties.
verses.Genesis|49|21: Naphtali is a hind let loose: he gives goodly words.
verses.Genesis|49|22: Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall:
verses.Genesis|49|23: the archers fiercely attacked him, and shot at him, and hated him:
verses.Genesis|49|24: but his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made supple by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob; (from thence from the shepherd, the Stone of Israel:)
verses.Genesis|49|25: by the God of thy father, Who shall help thee; and by the Almighty, Who shall bless thee, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that couches beneath, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb:
verses.Genesis|49|26: the blessings of thy father are potent above the blessings of my progenitors to the utmost bound of the everlasting hills: they shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separated from his brothers.
verses.Genesis|49|27: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.
verses.Genesis|49|28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is that which their father spoke to them, and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.
verses.Genesis|49|29: And he charged them, and said to them, I am to be gathered to my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron, the Hittite,
verses.Genesis|49|30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a buryingplace.
verses.Genesis|49|31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.
verses.Genesis|49|32: The purchase of the field and of the cave that is in it was from the children of Heth.
verses.Genesis|49|33: And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and expired, and was gathered to his people.
verses.Genesis|50|1: And Joseph fell on his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.
verses.Genesis|50|2: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel.
verses.Genesis|50|3: And forty days were fulfilled for him: for so are fulfilled the days of those who are embalmed: and Egypt wept for him seventy days.
verses.Genesis|50|4: And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found favour in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
verses.Genesis|50|5: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come back.
verses.Genesis|50|6: And Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.
verses.Genesis|50|7: And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt.
verses.Genesis|50|8: And all the house of Joseph, and his brothers, and his father's house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.
verses.Genesis|50|9: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.
verses.Genesis|50|10: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father of seven days.
verses.Genesis|50|11: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanite, saw the mourning at the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to Egypt: so that the name of it was called Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
verses.Genesis|50|12: And his sons did to him according as he had commanded them:
verses.Genesis|50|13: for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.
verses.Genesis|50|14: And Joseph returned to Egypt, he, and his brethren, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
verses.Genesis|50|15: And when Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, What if Joseph will hate us, and will pay us back the evil which we did to him.
verses.Genesis|50|16: And they sent word urgently to Joseph, saying, Thy father did command before he died, saying,
verses.Genesis|50|17: So shall you say to Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brothers, and their sin; for they did evil to thee: and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
verses.Genesis|50|18: And his brothers even went and fell down before his face; and they said, Behold, we are thy servants.
verses.Genesis|50|19: And Joseph said to them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?
verses.Genesis|50|20: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but God meant it for good, to bring it to pass at this day that much people should be saved alive.
verses.Genesis|50|21: Now therefore fear not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
verses.Genesis|50|22: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his father's house: and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
verses.Genesis|50|23: And Joseph saw Ephraim's children of the third generation: the children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were born on Joseph's knees.
verses.Genesis|50|24: And Joseph said to his brothers, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land of which He swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
verses.Genesis|50|25: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.
verses.Genesis|50|26: So Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
verses.Exodus|1|1: Now these are the names of the children of Israel who came into Egypt, with Jacob; every man came with his household.
verses.Exodus|1|5: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was already in Egypt.
verses.Exodus|1|6: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
verses.Exodus|1|7: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.
verses.Exodus|1|8: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.
verses.Exodus|1|9: And he said to his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
verses.Exodus|1|10: come, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when any war should chance, they also join our enemies, and fight against us, and so go up out of the land.
verses.Exodus|1|11: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, namely Pithom and Raamses.
verses.Exodus|1|12: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were mortified on account of the children of Israel.
verses.Exodus|1|13: And Egypt made the children of Israel serve with rigour:
verses.Exodus|1|14: and they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in mortar, and in brick, and in all manner of bondage in the field: all their bondage, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
verses.Exodus|1|15: And the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
verses.Exodus|1|16: and he said, When you do the office of midwife to the Hebrew women, you shall look upon the birth stones; if it be a son, then you shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
verses.Exodus|1|17: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.
verses.Exodus|1|18: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them, Why have you done this thing, and saved the men children alive?
verses.Exodus|1|19: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered before the midwives come to them.
verses.Exodus|1|20: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.
verses.Exodus|1|21: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
verses.Exodus|1|22: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born you shall cast into the River, and every daughter you shall save alive.
verses.Exodus|2|1: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
verses.Exodus|2|2: And the woman conceived, and bore a son: and when she saw that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.
verses.Exodus|2|3: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him a box made of papyrus, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child in it; and she laid it in the rushes by the River's brink.
verses.Exodus|2|4: And his sister stood afar off, to know what would be done to him.
verses.Exodus|2|5: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the River; and her maidens walked along by the River's side; and when she saw the box among the rushes, she sent her maid to fetch it.
verses.Exodus|2|6: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, a weeping boy. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.
verses.Exodus|2|7: Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee? And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Go.
verses.Exodus|2|8: And the maid went and called the child's mother.
verses.Exodus|2|9: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
verses.Exodus|2|10: And the child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
verses.Exodus|2|11: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out to his brothers, and looked on their burdens: and he noticed a Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
verses.Exodus|2|12: And he looked this way and that, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
verses.Exodus|2|13: And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that was in the wrong, Why dost thou smite thy fellow?
verses.Exodus|2|14: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? dost thou intend to kill me, as thou didst kill the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
verses.Exodus|2|15: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from before Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
verses.Exodus|2|16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
verses.Exodus|2|17: And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
verses.Exodus|2|18: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that you are come so soon today?
verses.Exodus|2|19: And they said, A Egyptian man delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.
verses.Exodus|2|20: And he said to his daughters, And where is he? why is it that you have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.
verses.Exodus|2|21: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
verses.Exodus|2|22: And she bore him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.
verses.Exodus|2|23: And it came to pass in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry rose up to God by reason of the bondage.
verses.Exodus|2|24: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.Exodus|2|25: And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God apprehended.
verses.Exodus|3|1: Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock far away into the desert, and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
verses.Exodus|3|2: And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, but the bush was not consumed.
verses.Exodus|3|3: And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
verses.Exodus|3|4: And when the Lord saw that he turned aside to see, God called to him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here I am.
verses.Exodus|3|5: And he said, Do not come near: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place on which thou dost stand is holy ground.
verses.Exodus|3|6: Moreover, he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.
verses.Exodus|3|7: And the Lord said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;
verses.Exodus|3|8: and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of Egypt, and to bring them up out of that land to a good land and a large, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
verses.Exodus|3|9: Now therefore, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come to me: and I have also seen the oppression with which Egypt oppresses them.
verses.Exodus|3|10: Come now therefore, and I will send thee to Pharaoh, that thou mayst bring my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
verses.Exodus|3|11: And Moses said to God, Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?
verses.Exodus|3|12: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token to thee, that I have sent thee. When thou hast brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain.
verses.Exodus|3|13: And Moses said to God, Behold, when I come to the children of Israel, and shall say to them, The God of your fathers has sent me to you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say to them?
verses.Exodus|3|14: And God said to Moses, I AM THAT I AM (I will ever be what I now am): and he said, Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel, I AM has sent me to you.
verses.Exodus|3|15: And God said moreover to Moses, Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial to all generations.
verses.Exodus|3|16: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say to them, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:
verses.Exodus|3|17: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.Exodus|3|18: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, The Lord God of the Hebrews has met with us: and now let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God.
verses.Exodus|3|19: And I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go, if not by a mighty hand.
verses.Exodus|3|20: And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in their midst: and after that he will let you go.
verses.Exodus|3|21: And I will give this people favour in the sight of Egypt: and it shall come to pass, that, when you go, you shall not go empty:
verses.Exodus|3|22: but every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her that sojourns in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and garments: and you shall put them on your sons, and on your daughters; and you shall despoil Egypt.
verses.Exodus|4|1: And Moses answered and said, But, behold they will not believe me, nor hearken to my voice: for they will say, The Lord has not appeared to thee.
verses.Exodus|4|2: And the Lord said to him, What is that in thy hand?
verses.Exodus|4|3: And he said, A rod. And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it turned into a snake; and Moses fled from it.
verses.Exodus|4|4: And the Lord said to Moses, Put out thy hand, and take it by its tail. And he put out his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:
verses.Exodus|4|5: that they may believe that the Lord God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to thee.
verses.Exodus|4|6: And the Lord said furthermore to him, Put now thy hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was diseased, as white as snow.
verses.Exodus|4|7: And he said, Put thy hand into thy bosom again. And he put his hand into his bosom again; and when he took it out of his bosom, behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.
verses.Exodus|4|8: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, nor hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
