verses.Joshua|24|15: And if it seem evil to you to serve the Lord, choose this day whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the river, or the gods of the Amorite, in whose land you dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
verses.Joshua|24|16: And the people answered and said, Far be it from us that we should forsake the Lord, to serve other gods;
verses.Joshua|24|17: for the Lord our God, he it is who brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and who did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way in which we went, and among all the people through whom we passed:
verses.Joshua|24|18: and the Lord drove out from before us all the people, even the Amorite who dwelt in the land: therefore will we also serve the Lord; for he is our God.
verses.Joshua|24|19: And Joshua said to the people, You cannot serve the Lord: for he is a holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not tolerate your transgressions nor your sins.
verses.Joshua|24|20: If you forsake the Lord, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after having done you good.
verses.Joshua|24|21: And the people said to Joshua, No; but we will serve the Lord.
verses.Joshua|24|22: And Joshua said to the people, You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord for yourselves, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses.
verses.Joshua|24|23: Now therefore put away the strange gods which are among you, and incline your heart to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.Joshua|24|24: And the people said to Joshua, The Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.
verses.Joshua|24|25: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.
verses.Joshua|24|26: And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up there under the oak, that was by the sanctuary of the Lord.
verses.Joshua|24|27: And Joshua said to all the people, Behold, this stone shall be a witness to us; for it has heard all the words of the Lord which he spoke to us: it shall be therefore a witness to you, lest you deny your God.
verses.Joshua|24|28: So Joshua let the people depart, every man to his inheritance.
verses.Joshua|24|29: And it came to pass after these things, that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being a hundred and ten years old.
verses.Joshua|24|30: And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, which is in mount Ephraim, on the north side of the hill Gaash.
verses.Joshua|24|31: And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, and who had known all the deeds of the Lord, that he had done for Israel.
verses.Joshua|24|32: And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, they buried in Shechem, in a section of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred qesita: and they became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.
verses.Joshua|24|33: And Eleazar the son of Aaron died; and they buried him in the hill of Phinehas his son, which was given him in mount Ephraim.
verses.Judges|1|1: Now after the death of Joshua it came to pass, that the children of Israel asked the Lord, saying, Who shall go up for us against the Canaanite first, to fight against them?
verses.Judges|1|2: And the Lord said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.
verses.Judges|1|3: And Judah said to Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanite; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot. So Simeon went with him.
verses.Judges|1|4: And Judah went up; and the Lord delivered the Canaanite and the Perizzite into their hand: and they smote of them in Bezek ten thousand men.
verses.Judges|1|5: And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek: and they fought against him, and they smote the Canaanite and the Perizzite.
verses.Judges|1|6: But Adoni-bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes.
verses.Judges|1|7: And Adoni-bezek said, Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered food under my table: as I have done, so God has requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
verses.Judges|1|8: Now the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
verses.Judges|1|9: And afterwards the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanite, that dwelt in the mountain, and in the south, and in the coastal plain.
verses.Judges|1|10: And Judah went against the Canaanite that dwelt in Hebron: (now the name of Hebron before was Kirjath-arba:) and they smote Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai.
verses.Judges|1|11: And from there he went against the inhabitants of Debir: and the name of Debir before was Kirjath-sepher:
verses.Judges|1|12: and Caleb said, He that smites Kirjath-sepher, and takes it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.
verses.Judges|1|13: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.
verses.Judges|1|14: And it came to pass, when she came to him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she alighted from her ass; and Caleb said to her, What wilt thou?
verses.Judges|1|15: And she said to him, Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also pools of water. And Caleb gave her the upper pools and the lower pools.
verses.Judges|1|16: And the children of the Kenites, Moses father in law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which lies in the south of Arad; and they went and dwelt among the people.
verses.Judges|1|17: And Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they slew the Canaanite that inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. And the name of the city was called Hormah.
verses.Judges|1|18: And Judah took Gaza with its border, and Askelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.
verses.Judges|1|19: And the Lord was with Judah; and he drove out the inhabitants of the mountain; but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
verses.Judges|1|20: And they gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses said: and he expelled from there the three sons of Anak.
verses.Judges|1|21: And the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusite, that inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusite dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.Judges|1|22: And the house of Joseph, they too went up against Beth-el: and the Lord was with them.
verses.Judges|1|23: And the house of Joseph sent to spy out Beth-el. (Now the name of the city before was Luz.)
verses.Judges|1|24: And the scouts saw a man come out of the city, and they said to him, Show us, we pray thee, the entrance into the city, and we will deal kindly with thee.
verses.Judges|1|25: And when he showed them the entrance to the city, they smote the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man and all his family go free.
verses.Judges|1|26: And the man went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city, and called its name Luz: which is its name to this day.
verses.Judges|1|27: Neither did Manasseh drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean and its hamlets, nor Taanach and its hamlets, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its hamlets, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its hamlets, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its hamlets: but the Canaanite persisted in dwelling in that land.
verses.Judges|1|28: And it came to pass, when Israel was strong, that they put the Canaanite to tribute, and did not utterly drive them out.
verses.Judges|1|29: Neither did Ephraim drive out the Canaanite that dwelt in Gezer; but the Canaanite dwelt in Gezer among them.
verses.Judges|1|30: Neither did Zebulun drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanite dwelt among them, and became tributaries.
verses.Judges|1|31: Neither did Asher drive out the inhabitants of Akko, nor the inhabitants of Zidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Ahlab, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob.
verses.Judges|1|32: But the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanite, the inhabitants of the land: for they did not drive them out.
verses.Judges|1|33: Neither did Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth-anath; but he dwelt among the Canaanite, the inhabitants of the land: nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and of Beth-anath became tributaries to them.
verses.Judges|1|34: And the Amorite forced the children of Dan into the mountain: for they would not allow them to come down to the valley:
verses.Judges|1|35: but the Amorite persisted in dwelling in mount Heres in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim: yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became tributaries.
verses.Judges|1|36: And the border of the Amorite was from Akrabbim, from the rock upwards.
verses.Judges|2|1: And an angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bochim, and said, I caused you to go up out of Egypt, and have brought you to the land which I swore to your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you.
verses.Judges|2|2: And you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall pull down their altars: but you have not obeyed my voice: why have you done this?
verses.Judges|2|3: Moreover, I said, I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as snares to you, and their gods shall be a trap to you.
verses.Judges|2|4: And it came to pass, when the angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice, and wept.
verses.Judges|2|5: And they called the name of that place Bochim: and they sacrificed there to the Lord.
verses.Judges|2|6: And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man to his inheritance to possess the land.
verses.Judges|2|7: And the people served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of the Lord, that he did for Israel.
verses.Judges|2|8: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being a hundred and ten years old.
verses.Judges|2|9: And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, on the north side of the hill Gaash.
verses.Judges|2|10: And also all that generation were gathered to their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord, nor yet the work which he had done for Israel.
verses.Judges|2|11: And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served the Baalim:
verses.Judges|2|12: and they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the people that were round about them, and bowed themselves down to them, and provoked the Lord to anger.
verses.Judges|2|13: And they forsook the Lord, and served the Baal and the Ashtaroth.
verses.Judges|2|14: And the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that plundered them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.
verses.Judges|2|15: Wherever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn to them: and they were greatly distressed.
verses.Judges|2|16: Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, who saved them from the hand of their plunderers.
verses.Judges|2|17: And yet they would not hearken to their judges, but they went astray after other gods, and bowed themselves down to them: they turned aside quickly out of the way in which their fathers had gone, obeying the commandments of the Lord; but they did not so.
verses.Judges|2|18: And when the Lord raised them up judges, then the Lord was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for the Lord relented on account of their groanings, caused by those that oppressed them and vexed them.
verses.Judges|2|19: And it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they relapsed, and became more corrupt than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down to them; they omitted nothing of their practices, nor of their stubborn way.
verses.Judges|2|20: And the anger of the Lord burned against Israel; and he said, Because this people has transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not hearkened to my voice;
verses.Judges|2|21: I also will not continue to drive out from before them any of the nations which Joshua left when he died:
verses.Judges|2|22: that through them I may put Israel to the proof, whether they will keep the way of the Lord to walk in it, as their fathers did keep it, or not.
verses.Judges|2|23: Therefore the Lord left those nations without driving them out hastily; and he did not give them up into the hand of Joshua.
verses.Judges|3|1: Now these are the nations which the Lord left to put Israel to the proof by them, all those who had not known all the wars of Canaan;
verses.Judges|3|2: only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing of those matters;
verses.Judges|3|3: namely, five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanite, and the Zidoni, and the Hivite, that dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baal-hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
verses.Judges|3|4: And they were for putting Israel to the proof, to know whether they would hearken to the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
verses.Judges|3|5: And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanite, the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
verses.Judges|3|6: and they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
verses.Judges|3|7: And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgot the Lord their God, and served the Baalim and the groves.
verses.Judges|3|8: Therefore the anger of the Lord burned against Israel and he sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim, king of Syria: and the children of Israel served Chushan-rishathaim eight years.
verses.Judges|3|9: And when the children of Israel cried to the Lord, the Lord raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, namely, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
verses.Judges|3|10: And the spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the Lord delivered Chushan-rishathaim, king of Syria, into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushan-rishathaim.
verses.Judges|3|11: And the land was quiet for forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
verses.Judges|3|12: And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.Judges|3|13: And he gathered to him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and they seized the city of palm trees.
verses.Judges|3|14: So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab, for eighteen years.
verses.Judges|3|15: But when the children of Israel cried to the Lord, the Lord raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a left-handed man, and by him the children of Israel sent a present to Eglon the king of Moab.
verses.Judges|3|16: But Ehud made him a sword which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he girded it under his clothes on his right thigh.
verses.Judges|3|17: And he brought the present to Eglon king of Moab: and Eglon was a very fat man.
verses.Judges|3|18: And when he had finished offering the present, he sent away the people that bore the present.
verses.Judges|3|19: But he himself turned back after reaching the carved stones that were by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand to thee, O king. The latter said, Keep silence, and all that stood by him went out from him.
verses.Judges|3|20: And Ehud came to him; and he was sitting in a cool upper chamber, which he had for himself alone. And Ehud said, I have a message from God to thee. So he arose out of his seat.
verses.Judges|3|21: And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly:
verses.Judges|3|22: and the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly; and the dirt came out.
verses.Judges|3|23: Then Ehud went out to the vestibule, and shut the doors of the chamber upon him, and locked them.
verses.Judges|3|24: When he was gone out, his servants came; and when they saw that, behold, the doors of the chamber were locked, they said, Surely he is relieving himself in the cool chamber.
verses.Judges|3|25: And they waited till it was late: and, behold, he opened not the doors of the chamber; therefore they took a key, and opened them: and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.
verses.Judges|3|26: And Ehud escaped while they tarried, and passed beyond the carved stones, and escaped into Seir.
verses.Judges|3|27: And it came to pass, when he arrived, that he blew a shofar in the mountain of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the mount, and he before them.
verses.Judges|3|28: And he said to them, Follow after me: for the Lord has delivered your enemies, namely Moab, into your hand. And they went down after him, and seized the fords of the Jordan towards Moab, and allowed no man to pass over.
verses.Judges|3|29: And they slew of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and no man escaped.
verses.Judges|3|30: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land was quiet for eighty years.
verses.Judges|3|31: And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel.
verses.Judges|4|1: And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, when Ehud was dead.
verses.Judges|4|2: And the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth.
verses.Judges|4|3: And the children of Israel cried to the Lord: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and twenty years he strongly oppressed the children of Israel.
verses.Judges|4|4: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time.
verses.Judges|4|5: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
verses.Judges|4|6: And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali, and said to him, Has not the Lord God of Israel commanded, saying, Go and gather your men to mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
verses.Judges|4|7: And I will draw out to thee to the wadi of Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thy hand.
verses.Judges|4|8: And Barak said to her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.
verses.Judges|4|9: And she said, I will surely go with thee: however thou shalt scarcely attain honour on the journey that thou goest; for the Lord shall yield Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.
verses.Judges|4|10: And Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and he went up with ten thousand men at his feet: and Deborah went up with him.
verses.Judges|4|11: Now Heber the Kenite, who was of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from Cain, and pitched his tent near the oak in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh.
verses.Judges|4|12: And they told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam was gone up to mount Tabor.
verses.Judges|4|13: And Sisera gathered together all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people that were with him, from Harosheth to the wadi of Kishon.
verses.Judges|4|14: And Deborah said to Barak, Up; for this is the day on which the Lord has delivered Sisera into thy hand: is not the Lord gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
verses.Judges|4|15: And the Lord confounded Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera alighted from his chariot, and fled away by foot.
verses.Judges|4|16: But Barak pursued after the chariots, and after the host, as far as Harosheth: and all the host of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; there was not a man left.
verses.Judges|4|17: But Sisera fled away by foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenites.
verses.Judges|4|18: And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in to her into the tent, she covered him with a blanket.
verses.Judges|4|19: And he said to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.
verses.Judges|4|20: Then he said to her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, if any man comes and inquires of thee, and says, Is there anyone here? that thou shalt say, No.
verses.Judges|4|21: Then Jael Heber's wife took a tent peg, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him, and drove the tent peg into his temple, and fastened it to the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.
verses.Judges|4|22: And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said to him, Come, and I will show thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the peg in his temple.
verses.Judges|4|23: So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.
verses.Judges|4|24: And the hand of the children of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
verses.Judges|5|1: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,
verses.Judges|5|2: In time of tumultuous strife in Israel when the people willingly offered themselves; praise the Lord.
verses.Judges|5|3: Hear, O kings; give ear, O princes; I will sing to the Lord; I will intone a melody to the God of Israel.
verses.Judges|5|4: Lord, when Thou didst go out of Seir, when Thou didst march out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens dropped, the clouds also dropped water.
verses.Judges|5|5: The mountains melted from before the Lord, that Sinai before the Lord God of Israel.
verses.Judges|5|6: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through crooked byways.
verses.Judges|5|7: The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until I Deborah arose, I arose a mother in Israel.
verses.Judges|5|8: They chose new gods; then was war in the gates: was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
verses.Judges|5|9: My heart goes out to the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless the Lord!
verses.Judges|5|10: You that ride on tawny she asses, you that sit on couches, and you that walk by the way, tell the tale.
verses.Judges|5|11: Louder than the voice of the archers; in the places of drawing water, there let them recite the righteous acts of the Lord, the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel: when the people of the Lord went down to the gates.
verses.Judges|5|12: Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead away thy captives, thou son of Abinoam.
verses.Judges|5|13: Then he made a remnant have dominion over the nobles of the people: the Lord made me have dominion over the mighty ones.
verses.Judges|5|14: From Ephraim came they, but rooted in Amalek, beyond thee, Benjamin with thy tribes; from Machir came down leaders, and from Zebulun, those that handle the marshal's staff.
verses.Judges|5|15: And the princes of Issachar were with Deborah; as was Issachar, so was Barak. Into the valley they rushed forth, at his feet. In the divisions of Reuben, great were the resolves.
verses.Judges|5|16: Why then didst thou sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben, great were the heart searchings.
verses.Judges|5|17: Gilead dwells beyond the Jordan: and why did Dan remain by the ships? Asher continued on the sea shore, and abode by his bays.
verses.Judges|5|18: Zebulun was a people that jeoparded their lives to the death and Naphtali likewise, on the high places of the field.
verses.Judges|5|19: The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of silver.
verses.Judges|5|20: They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.
verses.Judges|5|21: The wadi of Kishon swept them away, that ancient brook, the brook of Kishon. O my soul, march on in strength.
verses.Judges|5|22: Then did the horsehoofs beat from the frantic galloping of his mighty ones.
verses.Judges|5|23: Curse Meroz, said the angel of the Lord, curse bitterly its inhabitants; because they did not come to the help of the Lord, to the help of the Lord against the mighty men.
verses.Judges|5|24: Blessed above women is Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, blessed is she more than women in the tent.
verses.Judges|5|25: He asked water, but she gave him milk; she brought forth cream in a lordly dish.
verses.Judges|5|26: She put her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen's hammer; and she hammered Sisera, she smote through his head; she crushed and pierced his temple.
verses.Judges|5|27: At her feet he bent, he fell, he lay down: at her feet he bent, he fell: where he bowed, there he fell down, bereft of life.
verses.Judges|5|28: The mother of Sisera looked out at the window, and moaned through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why are the hoofbeats of his steeds so tardy?
verses.Judges|5|29: Her wise ladies answered her, she even returned answer to herself,
verses.Judges|5|30: Have they not found booty? have they not divided the prey; to every man a damsel or two; to Sisera a booty of divers colours, a plunder of many coloured needlework, dyed double worked garments for the necks of the spoilers.
verses.Judges|5|31: So let all Thy enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when it comes out in its might. And the land was quiet for forty years.
verses.Judges|6|1: And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
verses.Judges|6|2: And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel: and because of Midian the children of Israel made for themselves the tunnels which are in the mountains, and caves, and strongholds.
verses.Judges|6|3: And so it was, when Israel had sown, that Midian and Amalek, and the children of the east, came up against them;
verses.Judges|6|4: and they encamped against them, and destroyed the produce of the earth, as far as Gaza, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.
verses.Judges|6|5: For they came up with their cattle and their tents, and they came like locusts for multitude; for both they and their camels were without number: and they entered into the land to destroy it.
verses.Judges|6|6: And Israel was greatly impoverished because of Midian; and the children of Israel cried to the Lord.
verses.Judges|6|7: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel cried to the Lord because of Midian,
verses.Judges|6|8: that the Lord sent a prophet to the children of Israel, who said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I brought you up from Egypt, and brought you out of the house of slaves;
verses.Judges|6|9: and I delivered you out of the hand of Egypt, and out of the hand of all those that oppressed you, and drove them out before you, and gave you their land;
verses.Judges|6|10: and I said to you, I am the Lord your God; fear not the gods of the Amorite, in whose land you dwell: but you did not obey my voice.
verses.Judges|6|11: And there came an angel of the Lord, and sat under the terebinth which was in Ophrah, that belonged to Joash the Abi-ezrites: and his son Gideon was threshing wheat by the winepress, to hide it from Midian.
verses.Judges|6|12: And the angel of the Lord appeared to him, and said to him, The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.
verses.Judges|6|13: And Gideon said to him, Oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then has all this befallen us? and where are all his miracles which our fathers told us of saying, Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt? but now the Lord has forsaken us, and delivered us into the hand of Midian.
verses.Judges|6|14: And the Lord turned to him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of Midian: have not I sent thee?
verses.Judges|6|15: And he said to him, Oh my Lord, with what shall I save Israel? behold, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father's house.
verses.Judges|6|16: And the Lord said to him, Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite Midian as one man.
verses.Judges|6|17: And he said to him, If now I have found favour in Thy sight, then show me a sign that it is thou who talkest with me.
verses.Judges|6|18: Depart not from here, I pray thee, until I come to thee, and bring forth my present, and set it before thee. And he said, I will remain until thou come again.
verses.Judges|6|19: And Gideon went in, and made ready a kid, and unleavened cakes of an efa of flour: the meat he put in a basket, and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out to him under the terebinth, and presented it.
verses.Judges|6|20: And the angel of God said to him, Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.
verses.Judges|6|21: Then the angel of the Lord stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and the fire rose up out of the rock, and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes. Then the angel of the Lord departed out of his sight.
verses.Judges|6|22: And when Gideon perceived that he was an angel of the Lord, Gideon said, Alas, O Lord God! because I have surely seen an angel of the Lord face to face.
verses.Judges|6|23: And the Lord said to him, Peace be to thee; fear not: thou shalt not die.
verses.Judges|6|24: Then Gideon built an altar there to the Lord, and called it Jehovah-shalom: to this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abi-ezrites.
verses.Judges|6|25: And it came to pass the same night, that the Lord said to him, Take thy father's young bullock, and the second bullock of seven years old, and throw down the altar of Baal that thy father has, and cut down the Asherah that is by it:
verses.Judges|6|26: and build an altar to the Lord thy God upon the top of this strong point, on the level place, and take the second bullock, and offer a burnt sacrifice with the wood of the Asherah which thou shalt cut down.
verses.Judges|6|27: Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as the Lord had said to him: and since he feared his father's household, and the men of the city, he could not do it by day, but he did it by night.
verses.Judges|6|28: And when the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was pulled down, and the Asherah that was by it, was cut down, and the second bullock was offered upon the altar that was built.
verses.Judges|6|29: And they said one to another, Who has done this thing? And when they inquired and asked, they said, Gideon the son of Joash has done this thing.
verses.Judges|6|30: Then the men of the city said to Joash, Bring out thy son, that he may die: because he has pulled down the altar of Baal, and because he has cut down the Asherah that was by it.
verses.Judges|6|31: And Joash said to all that stood against him, Will you plead on behalf of Baal? will you save him? he that will plead for him, let him be put to death before morning: if he be a god, let him plead for himself, that his altar has been pulled down.
verses.Judges|6|32: Therefore on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, Let Baal plead against him, because he has pulled down his altar.
verses.Judges|6|33: Then all Midian and Amalek and the children of the east were gathered together, and went over, and pitched in the valley of Jezreel.
verses.Judges|6|34: But the spirit of the Lord clothed Gideon, and he blew a shofar; and Abi-ezer mustered behind him.
verses.Judges|6|35: And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh; who also mustered behind him: and he sent messengers to Asher, and to Zebulun, and to Naphtali; and they came up to meet them.
verses.Judges|6|36: And Gideon said to God, If Thou wilt save Israel by my hand, as Thou hast said,
verses.Judges|6|37: behold, I will put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; and if there be dew on the fleece only, and it be dry on all the ground elsewhere, then shall I know that Thou wilt save Israel by my hand, as Thou hast said,
verses.Judges|6|38: And it was so: for he rose up early on the morrow, and pressed the fleece together, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water.
verses.Judges|6|39: And Gideon said to God, Let not Thy anger burn against me, and I will speak but this once: let me prove, I pray Thee, but this once with the fleece; let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be dew.
verses.Judges|6|40: And God did so that night: for it was dry on the fleece only, and there was dew on all the ground.
verses.Judges|7|1: Then Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, and all the people that were with him, rose up early, and camped beside Harod: so that the host of Midian was on the north side of them, by the hill of More, in the valley.
verses.Judges|7|2: And the Lord said to Gideon, The people that are with thee are too many for me to give Midian into their hands; lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, my own hand has saved me.
verses.Judges|7|3: Now therefore, proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, Whoever is fearful and afraid, let him return and depart early from mount Gilead. And there returned of the people twenty two thousand; and ten thousand remained.
verses.Judges|7|4: And the Lord said to Gideon, The people are yet too many; bring them down to the water, and I will sift them for thee there: and it shall be, that of whom I say to thee, This shall go with thee, that one shall go with thee; and of whomever I say to thee, This shall not go with thee, that one shall not go.
verses.Judges|7|5: So he brought the people down to the water: and the Lord said to Gideon, Every one that laps of the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, him shalt thou set by himself; likewise every one that bows down upon his knees to drink.
verses.Judges|7|6: And the number of them that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, were three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water.
verses.Judges|7|7: And the Lord said to Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver Midian into thy hand: and let all the other people go every man to his place.
verses.Judges|7|8: So the people took provisions in their hands, and their shofarot: and he sent all the rest of Israel, every man to his tent, and retained those three hundred men: and the host of Midian was beneath him in the valley.
verses.Judges|7|9: And it was on the same night, that the Lord said to him, Arise, go down to the camp; for I have delivered it into thy hand.
verses.Judges|7|10: But if thou fear to go down, go thou with Pura thy boy down to the camp:
verses.Judges|7|11: and thou shalt hear what they say; and afterwards shall thy hands be strengthened to go down unto the host. Then went he down with Pura his boy to the fringe of the armed men that were in the camp.
verses.Judges|7|12: Now Midian and Amalek and all the children of the east lay along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number, as the sand by the sea side for multitude.
verses.Judges|7|13: And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man that told a dream to his fellow, and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a slice of barley bread was rolling through the camp of Midian, and it came to a tent, and smote it so that it fell, and overturned it, so that the tent tumbled down.
verses.Judges|7|14: And his fellow answered and said, This is nothing else but the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: for into his hand has God delivered Midian, and all the camp.
verses.Judges|7|15: And it was, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream, and its interpretation, that he bowed himself down to the ground, and returned to the camp of Israel and said, Arise; for the Lord has delivered into your hand the host of Midian.
verses.Judges|7|16: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a shofar in every man's hand, with empty jars, and torches within the jars.
verses.Judges|7|17: And he said to them, Whatever you see me do, do likewise: and, behold, I am going to the edge of the camp, and it shall be, whatever I do, so shall you do.
verses.Judges|7|18: When I blow on the shofar, I and all that are with me, then you blow your shofarot also on every side of all the camp, and say, The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.
verses.Judges|7|19: So Gideon, and the hundred men that were with him, came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch; and they had newly posted the sentinels: and they blew with the shofarot, and broke the jars that were in their hands.
verses.Judges|7|20: Then the three companies blew on the shofarot, and broke the jars, and held the torches in their left hands, and the shofarot in their right hands to blow on them: and they cried, The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.
verses.Judges|7|21: And they stood every man in his place round about the camp: and all the camp ran, and cried, and fled.
verses.Judges|7|22: And the three hundred blew the horns, and the Lord set every man's sword against his fellow, throughout all the camp: and the host fled to Beth-shittah in Zererath, and to the border of Abel-meholah, at Tabbath.
verses.Judges|7|23: And the men of Israel mustered together out of Naphtali and out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursued after Midian.
verses.Judges|7|24: And Gideon sent messengers throughout all mount Ephraim, saying, Come down against Midian, and seize before them the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan. Then all the men of Ephraim were mustered, and took the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.
verses.Judges|7|25: And they took two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they slew Oreb on the rock Oreb, and Zeeb they slew at the winepress of Zeeb, and pursued Midian, and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
verses.Judges|8|1: And the men of Ephraim said to him, What hast thou done to us, that thou didst not call us, when thou didst go to fight with Midian? And they quarrelled with him sharply.
verses.Judges|8|2: And he said to them, What have I done now in comparison with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abi-ezer?
verses.Judges|8|3: God has delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb: and what was I able to do in comparison with you? Then their anger was abated toward him, when he had said that.
verses.Judges|8|4: And Gideon came to the Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint, yet pursuing them.
verses.Judges|8|5: And he said to the men of Succoth, Give, I pray you, loaves of bread to the people that follow me; for they are faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian.
verses.Judges|8|6: And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thy hand, that we should give bread to thy army?
verses.Judges|8|7: And Gideon said, Therefore when the Lord has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.
verses.Judges|8|8: And he went up from there to Penuel, and spoke to them likewise: and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered him.
verses.Judges|8|9: And he spoke also to the men of Penuel, saying, When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.
verses.Judges|8|10: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their hosts with them, about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of all the camp of the children of the east: for there fell a hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword.
verses.Judges|8|11: And Gideon went up by the way of the tent dwellers, on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and smote the camp: for the camp thought itself secure.
verses.Judges|8|12: And when Zebah and Zalmunna fled, he pursued after them, and took the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and the whole camp was panic stricken.
verses.Judges|8|13: And Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle from the ascent of Heres,
verses.Judges|8|14: and caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and inquired of him: and he wrote down for him the princes of Succoth, and its elders seventy seven men.
verses.Judges|8|15: And he came to the men of Succoth, and said, Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, with whom you taunted me, saying, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thy hand, that we should give bread to thy men that are weary?
verses.Judges|8|16: And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he chastised the men of Succoth.
verses.Judges|8|17: And he beat down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city.
verses.Judges|8|18: Then said he to Zebah and Zalmunna, where are the men whom you slew at Tabor? And they answered, As thou art, so were they, the same; in shape like the sons of a king.
verses.Judges|8|19: And he said, They were my brothers, the sons of my mother: as the Lord lives, if you had saved them alive, I would not slay you.
verses.Judges|8|20: And he said to Jether his firstborn, Up, and slay them. But the youth did not draw his sword: for he feared, because he was still a lad.
verses.Judges|8|21: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon arose, and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and took away the crescents that were on their camels' necks.
verses.Judges|8|22: Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son's son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.
verses.Judges|8|23: And Gideon said to them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the Lord shall rule over you.
verses.Judges|8|24: And Gideon said to them, I would make a request of you, that you would give me every man the earrings of his spoil. (For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)
verses.Judges|8|25: And they answered, We will willingly give them. And they spread a garment, and did cast on it every man the earrings of his spoil.
verses.Judges|8|26: And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold: besides the crescents, and the eardrops, and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that were about their camels' necks.
verses.Judges|8|27: And Gideon made an efod of this, and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went astray there after it: which thing became a snare to Gideon, and to his house.
verses.Judges|8|28: Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more. And the country was in quietness for forty years in the days of Gideon.
verses.Judges|8|29: And Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
verses.Judges|8|30: And Gideon had seventy sons begotten of his body: for he had many wives.
verses.Judges|8|31: And his concubine that was in Shechem, she also bore him a son, whose name he called Abimelech.
verses.Judges|8|32: And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abi-ezrites.
verses.Judges|8|33: And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went astray after the Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god.
verses.Judges|8|34: And the children of Israel did not remember the Lord their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side:
verses.Judges|8|35: neither did they show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, namely, Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had shown to Israel.
verses.Judges|9|1: And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother's brethren, and spoke to them, and to all the family of the house of his mother's father, saying,
verses.Judges|9|2: Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, Which is better for you, that all the sons of Jerubbaal, who are seventy persons, reign over you, or that one should reign over you? remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.
verses.Judges|9|3: And his mother's brethren spoke of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words: and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech; for they said, He is our brother.
verses.Judges|9|4: And they gave him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired vain and reckless persons, who followed him.
verses.Judges|9|5: And he went to his father's house at Ophrah, and slew his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy persons, upon one stone: yet Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid him-self.
verses.Judges|9|6: And all the men of Shechem gathered together, and all the house of Millo, and went, and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.
verses.Judges|9|7: And when they told it to Jotham, he went and stood at the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried, and said to them, Hearken to me, men of Shechem, that God may hearken to you.
verses.Judges|9|8: The trees went out to anoint a king over them; and they said to the olive tree, Reign over us.
verses.Judges|9|9: But the olive tree said to them, Should I leave my fatness, with which by me they honour God and man, and go to hold sway over the trees?
verses.Judges|9|10: And the trees said to the fig tree, Come thou, and reign over us.
verses.Judges|9|11: But the fig tree said to them, Should I forsake my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to hold sway over the trees?
verses.Judges|9|12: Then said the trees to the vine, Come thou, and reign over us.
verses.Judges|9|13: And the vine said to them, Should I leave my wine, which cheers God and man, and go to hold sway over the trees?
verses.Judges|9|14: Then said all the trees to the bramble, Come thou, and reign over us.
verses.Judges|9|15: And the bramble said to the trees, If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow: and if not, fire will issue from the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.
verses.Judges|9|16: Now therefore, if you have done truly and sincerely, in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done to him according to the deserving of his hands;
verses.Judges|9|17: (for my father fought for you, and adventured his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian:
verses.Judges|9|18: and you have risen up against my father's house this day, and have slain his sons, seventy men, upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother;)
verses.Judges|9|19: if you then have dealt truly and sincerely with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you:
verses.Judges|9|20: but if not, fire will come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem, and the house of Millo; and fire will come out from the men of Shechem, and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech.
verses.Judges|9|21: And Jotham ran away, and fled, and went to Beer, and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.
verses.Judges|9|22: When Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel,
verses.Judges|9|23: then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech:
verses.Judges|9|24: that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, who slew them; and upon the men of Shechem, who had aided him in the killing of his brothers.
verses.Judges|9|25: And the men of Shechem set liers in wait for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all that passed them on the highway: and it was told Abimelech.
verses.Judges|9|26: And Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brethren, and passed through Shechem: and the men of Shechem put their confidence in him.
verses.Judges|9|27: And they went out into the fields, and gathered their vineyards, and trod the grapes, and made merry, and went into the house of their god, and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.
verses.Judges|9|28: And Gaal the son of Ebed said, Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve rather the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: for why should we serve him?
verses.Judges|9|29: And would that this people were under my hand! then would I remove Abimelech. And he said to Abimelech, Increase thy army, and come out.
verses.Judges|9|30: And when Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burned.
verses.Judges|9|31: And he sent messengers to Abimelech privately, saying, Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brethren have come to Shechem; and they are fortifying the city against thee.
verses.Judges|9|32: Now therefore, rise up by night, thou and the people that is with thee, and lie in wait in the field:
verses.Judges|9|33: and it shall be, that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, thou shalt rise early, and set upon the city: and, behold, when he and the people that are with him come out against thee, then mayst thou do to them as thou shalt find occasion.
verses.Judges|9|34: And Abimelech rose up, and all the people that were with him, by night, and they laid wait against Shechem in four companies.
verses.Judges|9|35: And Gaal the son of Ebed went out, and stood in the entrance of the city gate: and Abimelech rose up, and the people that were with him, from the ambush.
verses.Judges|9|36: And when Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, Behold, there come people down from the tops of the mountains. And Zebul said to him, Thou seest the shadow of the mountains as if they were men.
verses.Judges|9|37: And Gaal spoke again and said, See there come people down from the knoll of the land, and another company come along by the oak of Meonenim.
verses.Judges|9|38: Then Zebul said to him, Where is now thy mouth, with which thou didst say, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? is not this the people that thou hast despised? go out, I pray now, and fight with them.
verses.Judges|9|39: And Gaal went out before the men of Shechem, and fought with Abimelech.
verses.Judges|9|40: And Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many were overthrown, and wounded, right up to the entrance of the gate.
verses.Judges|9|41: And Abimelech dwelt at Arumah: and Zebul thrust out Gaal and his brothers, that they should not dwell in Shechem.
verses.Judges|9|42: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people went out into the field; and they told Abimelech.
verses.Judges|9|43: And he took the people, and divided them into three companies, and laid wait in the field, and looked, and, behold, the people were coming out of the city; and he rose up against them, and smote them.
verses.Judges|9|44: And Abimelech, and the company that was with him, rushed forward, and stood in the entrance of the city gate: and the two other companies ran upon all the people that were in the fields, and slew them.
verses.Judges|9|45: And Abimelech fought against the city, all that day, and he took the city, and slew the people that were in it, and pulled down the city, and sowed it with salt.
verses.Judges|9|46: And when all the men of the tower of Shechem heard that, they entered the stronghold of Berith.
verses.Judges|9|47: And it was told Abimelech, that all the men of the tower of Shechem were gathered together.
verses.Judges|9|48: And Abimelech went up to mount Zalmon, he and all the people that were with him; and Abimelech took an ax in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, and took it, and laid it on his shoulder, and said to the people that were with him, What you have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done.
verses.Judges|9|49: And all the people likewise cut down every man a bough, and followed Abimelech, and put them to the stronghold, and set the hold on fire upon them; so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.
verses.Judges|9|50: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, and encamped against Thebez, and took it.
verses.Judges|9|51: But there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women, and all they of the city fled there, and shut themselves in, and went up to the top of the tower.
verses.Judges|9|52: And Abimelech came to the tower, and fought against it, and approached right up to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
verses.Judges|9|53: And a woman cast an upper millstone upon Abimelech's head, and crushed his skull.
verses.Judges|9|54: Then he called hastily to the lad, his armourbearer, and said to him, Draw thy sword, and slay me, so that men should not say of me, A woman slew him. And his lad pierced him, and he died.
verses.Judges|9|55: And when the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they departed every man to his place.
verses.Judges|9|56: Thus God made reparation for the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did to his father, in slaying his seventy brothers:
verses.Judges|9|57: and all the evil of the men of Shechem did God requite upon their heads: and upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal.
verses.Judges|10|1: And after Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, and he dwelt in Shamir in mount Ephraim.
verses.Judges|10|2: And he judged Israel twenty three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.
verses.Judges|10|3: And after him arose Jair, the Gileadite, and judged Israel twenty two years.
verses.Judges|10|4: And he had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havoth-jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
verses.Judges|10|5: And Jair died, and was buried in Camon.
verses.Judges|10|6: And the children of Israel continued to do evil in the sight of the Lord, and served the Baalim, and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, and the gods of Zidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsook the Lord, and served him not.
verses.Judges|10|7: And the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines, and into the hands of the children of Ammon.
verses.Judges|10|8: And that year they afflicted and oppressed the children of Israel: and thus for eighteen years, all the children of Israel that were on the other side of the Jordan in the land of the Amorite, which is in Gilead.
verses.Judges|10|9: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim; so that Israel was sorely distressed.
verses.Judges|10|10: And the children of Israel cried to the Lord, saying, We have sinned against Thee, because we have forsaken our God, and have served the Baalim.
verses.Judges|10|11: And the Lord said to the children of Israel, Did not I deliver you from Egypt, and from the Amorite, from the children of Ammon, and from Philistines?
verses.Judges|10|12: The Zidonians also, and Amalek and Maon, did oppress you; and you cried to me, and I delivered you out of their hand.
verses.Judges|10|13: Yet you have forsaken me, and served other gods: therefore I will deliver you no more.
verses.Judges|10|14: Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your trouble.
verses.Judges|10|15: And the children of Israel said to the Lord, We have sinned: do to us whatever seems good to Thee; only deliver us, we pray Thee, this day.
verses.Judges|10|16: And they put away the foreign gods from among them, and served the Lord: and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel.
verses.Judges|10|17: Then the children of Ammon mustered together, and encamped in Gilead. And the children of Israel assembled themselves together, and encamped in Mizpeh.
verses.Judges|10|18: And the people and princes of Gilead said to one another, What man is he that will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.
verses.Judges|11|1: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of a harlot: and Gilead begot Jephthah.
verses.Judges|11|2: And Gilead's wife bore him sons; and his wife's sons grew up, and they drove out Jephthah, and said to him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father's house; for thou art the son of a strange woman.
verses.Judges|11|3: Then Jephthah fled from his brothers, and dwelt in the land of Tob: and idle fellows joined themselves to Jephthah, and went out with him.
verses.Judges|11|4: And it came to pass in the course of time, that the children of Ammon made war against Israel.
verses.Judges|11|5: And when the children of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob:
verses.Judges|11|6: and they said to Jephthah, Come, and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.
verses.Judges|11|7: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, Did you not hate me, and expel me out of my father's house? and why have you come to me now when you are in distress?
verses.Judges|11|8: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, Therefore we turn again to thee now, that thou mayst go with us, and fight against the children of Ammon, and be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.
verses.Judges|11|9: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, If you bring me back home to fight against the children of Ammon, and the Lord deliver them before me, shall I be your head?
verses.Judges|11|10: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, The Lord is witness between us, if we do not so according to thy words.
verses.Judges|11|11: Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and captain over them: and Jephthah uttered all his words before the Lord in Mizpeh.
verses.Judges|11|12: And Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land?
verses.Judges|11|13: And the king of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Jephthah, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon as far as the Jabbok, and the Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably.
verses.Judges|11|14: And Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the children of Ammon:
verses.Judges|11|15: and said to him, Thus says Jephthah, Israel did not take away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon:
verses.Judges|11|16: but when Israel came up from Egypt, and walked through the wilderness to the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh;
verses.Judges|11|17: then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Let me, I pray thee, pass through thy land: but the king of Edom would not hearken. And in like manner they sent to the king of Moab: but he would not consent: and so Israel remained in Kadesh.
verses.Judges|11|18: Then they went along through the wilderness, and went round the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and camped on the other side of Arnon, but came not within the border of Moab: for Arnon was the border of Moab.
verses.Judges|11|19: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorite, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, Let us pass, we pray thee, through thy land to my place.
verses.Judges|11|20: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and pitched in Jahaz and fought against Israel.
verses.Judges|11|21: And the Lord God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorite, the inhabitants of that country.
verses.Judges|11|22: And they possessed all the border of the Amorite from Arnon even as far as Jabbok, and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
verses.Judges|11|23: So now the Lord God of Israel has driven out the Amorite from before his people Israel, and shouldst thou possess their land?
verses.Judges|11|24: Wilt not thou possess that which Chemosh thy god gives thee to possess? So likewise that which the Lord our God has voided before us, that shall we possess.
verses.Judges|11|25: And now art thou at all better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them,
verses.Judges|11|26: while Israel dwelt in Heshbon and its hamlets, and in Aroer and its hamlets, and in all the cities that are along by the shores of Arnon, for three hundred years? why did you not recover them within that time?
verses.Judges|11|27: But I have not sinned against thee, but thou doest me wrong to war against me: the Lord the Judge be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.
verses.Judges|11|28: Howbeit the king of the children of Ammon did not hearken to the words of Jephthah which he sent him.
verses.Judges|11|29: Then the spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah and he passed over Gilead, and Manasseh, and passed over Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed over to the children of Ammon.
verses.Judges|11|30: And Jephthah vowed a vow to the Lord, and said, If Thou shalt deliver the children of Ammon into my hands,
verses.Judges|11|31: then whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall surely be the Lord's, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.
verses.Judges|11|32: So Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them: and the Lord delivered them into his hands.
verses.Judges|11|33: And he smote them from Aroer, as far as Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel-keramim, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.
verses.Judges|11|34: And Jephthah came to Mizpeh to his house, and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances: and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter.
verses.Judges|11|35: And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he rent his clothes, and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou hast become the cause of trouble to me: for I have opened my mouth to the Lord, and I cannot go back.
verses.Judges|11|36: And she said to him, My father, if thou hast opened thy mouth to the Lord, do to me according to that which has proceeded out of thy mouth; seeing that the Lord has taken vengeance for thee of thy enemies, of the children of Ammon.
verses.Judges|11|37: And she said to her father, Let this thing be done for me: let me alone two months, that I may go and wander down the mountain sides, and bewail my virginity, I and my friends.
verses.Judges|11|38: And he said, Go. And he sent her away for two months: and she went with her companions, and wept for her virginity upon the mountains.
verses.Judges|11|39: And it came to pass at the end of two months, that she returned to her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed: and she knew no man. And it was a custom in Israel,
verses.Judges|11|40: that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah, the Gileadite four days in the year.
verses.Judges|12|1: And the men of Ephraim were mustered, and crossed to Zaphon, and said to Jephthah, Why didst thou pass over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go with thee? we will burn thy house upon thee with fire.
verses.Judges|12|2: And Jephthah said to them, I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, you delivered me not out of their hands.
verses.Judges|12|3: And when I saw that you delivered me not, I took my life in my hands, and passed over against the children of Ammon; and the Lord delivered them into my hand: why then are you come up to me this day, to fight against me?
verses.Judges|12|4: Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim, for they had said, You of Gilead are outcasts of Ephraim amongst Ephraim and amongst Manasseh.
verses.Judges|12|5: And Gilead seized the passages of the Jordan before Ephraim: and it was so, that when the fugitives of Ephraim would say, let me cross; that the men of Gilead would say to him, Art thou an Ephraimite? If he said, No;
verses.Judges|12|6: then they said to him, say now Shibboleth: and he said Shibboleth: for he could not frame to pronounce it right. Then they took him, and slew him at the fords of the Jordan; and there fell at that time of Ephraim forty two thousand.
verses.Judges|12|7: And Jephthah judged Israel for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died, and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
verses.Judges|12|8: And after him Ibzan of Beth-lehem judged Israel.
verses.Judges|12|9: And he had thirty sons, and thirty daughters, whom he sent abroad, and took in thirty daughters from abroad for his sons. And he judged Israel for seven years.
verses.Judges|12|10: Then died Ibzan, and was buried at Beth-lehem.
verses.Judges|12|11: And after him Elon, a Zebulonite, judged Israel, and he judged Israel for ten years.
verses.Judges|12|12: And Elon the Zebulonite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the country of Zebulun.
verses.Judges|12|13: And after him Abdon the son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, judged Israel.
verses.Judges|12|14: And he had forty sons and thirty grandsons, that rode on seventy ass colts: and he judged Israel for eight years.
verses.Judges|12|15: And Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the mount of the Amalekite.
verses.Judges|13|1: And the children of Israel continued to do evil in the sight of the Lord; and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
verses.Judges|13|2: And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bore not.
verses.Judges|13|3: And the angel of the Lord appeared to the woman, and said to her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.
verses.Judges|13|4: Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink neither wine nor strong drink, and eat no unclean thing:
verses.Judges|13|5: for, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
verses.Judges|13|6: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of an angel of God, very terrible: but I asked him not from where he was, neither did he tell me his name:
verses.Judges|13|7: but he said to me, Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink, neither eat any unclean thing: for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death.
verses.Judges|13|8: Then Manoah entreated the Lord, and said, O my Lord, let the man of God whom Thou didst send come again to us, and teach us what we shall do to the child that shall be born.
verses.Judges|13|9: And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again to the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her.
verses.Judges|13|10: And the woman made haste, and ran, and told her husband, and said to him, Behold, the man has appeared to me, that came to me the other day.
verses.Judges|13|11: And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said to him, Art thou the man that didst speak to the woman? And he said, I am.
verses.Judges|13|12: And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass. What shall be the rule for the child, and what shall be done with him?
verses.Judges|13|13: And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, Of all that I said to the woman let her take heed.
verses.Judges|13|14: She may not eat of anything that comes of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: all that I commanded her let her observe.
verses.Judges|13|15: And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, I pray thee, let us detain thee, until we shall have made ready a kid for thee.
verses.Judges|13|16: And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, Though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread: and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it to the Lord. For Manoah knew not that he was an angel of the Lord.
verses.Judges|13|17: And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, What is thy name, that when thy sayings come to pass we may do thee honour?
verses.Judges|13|18: And the angel of the Lord said to him, Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is hidden?
verses.Judges|13|19: So Manoah took the kid with the meal offering, and offered it upon the rock to the Lord: and the angel did wondrously, and Manoah and his wife looked on.
verses.Judges|13|20: For it came to pass, when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife looked on it, and fell on their faces to the ground.
verses.Judges|13|21: But the angel of the Lord appeared no more to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.
verses.Judges|13|22: And Manoah said to his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God.
verses.Judges|13|23: But his wife said to him, If the Lord desired to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hands, neither would he have shown us all these things, nor would as at this have told us such things as these.
verses.Judges|13|24: And the woman bore a son, and called his name Samson: and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him.
verses.Judges|13|25: And the spirit of the Lord began to move him in Mahaneh-dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.Judges|14|1: And Samson went down to Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines.
verses.Judges|14|2: And he came up, and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines: now therefore get her for me to wife.
verses.Judges|14|3: Then his father and his mother said to him, Is there no woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said to his father, Get her for me; for she pleases me well.
verses.Judges|14|4: But his father and his mother knew not that it was of the Lord, that he sought a pretext against the Philistines: for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel.
verses.Judges|14|5: Then Samson went down, and his father and his mother, to Timnath, and came to the vineyards of Timnath: and, behold, a young lion roared against him.
verses.Judges|14|6: And the spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him, and he tore him as he would have torn a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done.
verses.Judges|14|7: And he went down, and talked with the woman; and she pleased Samson well.
verses.Judges|14|8: And after a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion: and, behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass of the lion.
verses.Judges|14|9: And he scraped it out in his hands, and went on his way, eating, and came to his father and mother, and he gave them, and they did eat: but he told them not that he had taken the honey out of the carcass of the lion.
verses.Judges|14|10: So his father went down to the woman: and Samson made there a feast; for so used the young men to do.
verses.Judges|14|11: And it came to pass, when they saw him, that they brought thirty companions to be with him.
verses.Judges|14|12: And Samson said to them, I will now propound a riddle to you: if you can declare it me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty sheets and thirty changes of garments:
verses.Judges|14|13: but if you cannot declare it me, then you shall give me thirty sheets and thirty changes of garments. And they said to him, Propound thy riddle, that we may hear it.
verses.Judges|14|14: And he said to them, Out of the eater came forth food, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not in three days expound the riddle.
verses.Judges|14|15: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that they said to Samson's wife, Entice thy husband, that he may declare to us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father's house with fire: have you called us to take possession of our goods?
verses.Judges|14|16: And Samson's wife wept before him, and said, Thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not: thou hast propounded a riddle to the children of my people, and hast not told it me. And he said to her, Behold, I have not told it my father nor my mother and shall I tell it thee?
verses.Judges|14|17: And she wept before him the seven days, while their feast lasted: and it came to pass on the seventh day, that he told her, because she harassed him: and she told the riddle to the children of her people.
verses.Judges|14|18: And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, What is sweeter than honey? and what is stronger than a lion? And he said to them, If you had not ploughed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle.
verses.Judges|14|19: And the spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, and slew thirty men of them, and took their clothing, and gave the changes of garments to them who had expounded the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father's house.
verses.Judges|14|20: But Samson's wife was given to his companion, whom he had as his friend.
verses.Judges|15|1: But it came to pass after a while, in the time of wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a kid; and he said, I will go in to my wife into the chamber. But her father would not permit him to go in.
verses.Judges|15|2: And her father said, I thought indeed that thou didst hate her; therefore I gave her to thy companion: is not her younger sister fairer than she? take her, I pray thee, instead of her.
verses.Judges|15|3: And Samson said concerning them, Now shall I be blameless in regard to the Philistines, when I do them a mischief.
verses.Judges|15|4: And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the midst between two tails.
verses.Judges|15|5: And when he had set the torches on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks, and also the standing corn, together with the oliveyards.
verses.Judges|15|6: Then the Philistines said, Who has done this? And they answered, Samson, the son in law of the Timnite, because he had taken his wife, and given her to his companion. And the Philistines went up, and burnt her and her father with fire.
verses.Judges|15|7: And Samson said to them, If this is what you have done, I will be avenged on you, and after that I will cease.
verses.Judges|15|8: And he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter: and he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock Etam.
verses.Judges|15|9: Then the Philistines went up, and pitched in Judah, and ranged themselves against Lehi.
verses.Judges|15|10: And the men of Judah said, Why are you come up against us? And they answered, To bind Samson are we come up, to do to him as he has done to us.
verses.Judges|15|11: Then three thousand men of Judah went to the cleft of the rock Etam, and said to Samson, Knowst thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what is this that thou hast done to us? And he said to them, As they did to me, so have I done to them.
verses.Judges|15|12: And they said to him, We have come down to bind thee, that we may deliver thee into the hand of the Philistines. And Samson said to them, Swear to me, that you will not fall upon me yourselves.
verses.Judges|15|13: And they spoke to him, saying, No; but we will bind thee fast, and deliver thee into their hand: but surely we will not kill thee. And they bound him with two new cords, and brought him up from the rock.
verses.Judges|15|14: And when he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted against him: and the spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him: and the cords that were upon his arms became as flax that was burnt with fire, and his bands melted from off his hands.
verses.Judges|15|15: And he found a new jawbone of an ass, and put out his hand, and took it, and slew a thousand men with it.
verses.Judges|15|16: And Samson said, With the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps; with the jaw of an ass have I slain a thousand men.
verses.Judges|15|17: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking, that he cast away the jawbone out of his hand, and called that place Ramath-lehi.
verses.Judges|15|18: And he was very thirsty, and called on the Lord, and said, Thou hast given this great deliverance into the hand of Thy servant: and now shall I die of thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?
verses.Judges|15|19: But God split the hollow place that was in Lehi, and water came out; and when he had drunk, his spirit was restored, and he revived: therefore he called the name of it En-hakkore, which is in Lehi to this day.
verses.Judges|15|20: And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines for twenty years.
verses.Judges|16|1: Then Samson went to Gaza, and saw there a harlot, and went in to her.
verses.Judges|16|2: And it was told the Azzatim, saying, Samson has come here. And they surrounded him, and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and were quiet all the night, saying, In the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.
