verses.1 Samuel|9|6: And he said to him, Behold now, there is in this city a man of God, and he is an honourable man; all that he says is sure to come about: now let us go there; perhaps he can show us our way that we should go.
verses.1 Samuel|9|7: Then said Saul to his servant, But, behold, if we go, what shall we bring the man? for the bread is spent in our vessels, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God: what have we?
verses.1 Samuel|9|8: And the servant answered Saul again, and said, Behold, there is in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver: that will I give to the man of God, to tell us our way.
verses.1 Samuel|9|9: (Beforetime in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, thus he spoke, Come, and let us go to the seer: for he that is now called a prophet was beforetime called the seer.)
verses.1 Samuel|9|10: Then said Saul to his servant, Well said; come, let us go. So they went to the city where the man of God was.
verses.1 Samuel|9|11: And as they went up the hill to the city, they found some girls going out to draw water, and they said to them, Is the seer here?
verses.1 Samuel|9|12: And they answered them, and said, He is; behold, he is before you: make haste now, for he came today to the city; for the people are making a sacrifice today in the high place:
verses.1 Samuel|9|13: as you come into the city, you shall find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat: for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice; and afterwards those that are invited eat. Now therefore go up; for about this time you shall find him.
verses.1 Samuel|9|14: And they went up into the city: and when they were come into the city, behold, Samuel came out towards them, to go up to the high place.
verses.1 Samuel|9|15: Now the Lord had revealed to Samuel a day before Saul came, saying,
verses.1 Samuel|9|16: To morrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be a prince over my people Israel, that he may save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come to me.
verses.1 Samuel|9|17: And when Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said to him, Behold the man of whom I spoke to thee! this one shall reign over my people.
verses.1 Samuel|9|18: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, where the seer's house is.
verses.1 Samuel|9|19: And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am the seer: go up before me to the high place; for you shall eat with me today, and to morrow I will let thee go, and will tell thee all that is in thy heart.
verses.1 Samuel|9|20: And as for thy asses that were lost three days ago, set not thy mind on them; for they are found. And on whom is all the desire of Israel? Is it not on thee, and on all thy father's house?
verses.1 Samuel|9|21: And Saul answered and said, Am not I a Benjamin, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then dost thou speak so to me?
verses.1 Samuel|9|22: And Samuel took Saul and his servant, and brought them into the dining chamber, and made them sit in the chiefest place among those that were invited, who were about thirty persons.
verses.1 Samuel|9|23: And Samuel said to the cook, Bring the portion which I gave thee, of which I said to thee, Set it aside by thee.
verses.1 Samuel|9|24: And the cook took up the shoulder, and that which was upon it, and set it before Saul. And (Samuel) said, Behold that which is left is set before thee; eat: for it has been kept for thee for this appointed time, when I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day.
verses.1 Samuel|9|25: And when they were come down from the high place into the city, Samuel spoke with Saul upon the top of the house.
verses.1 Samuel|9|26: And they arose early: and it came to pass at about daybreak, that Samuel called Saul to the top of the house, saying, Up, that I may send thee away. And Saul arose, and they went out both of them, he and Samuel out of doors.
verses.1 Samuel|9|27: And as they were going down to the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us, (and he passed on,) but stand thou still awhile, that I may make known to thee the word of God.
verses.1 Samuel|10|1: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Has not the Lord anointed thee to be a prince over his inheritance?
verses.1 Samuel|10|2: When thou art departed from me today, then thou shalt find two men by Rachel's tomb in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say to thee, The asses which thou wentest to seek are found: and, thy father has left the matter of the asses, and has become anxious about you, saying, What shall I do about my son?
verses.1 Samuel|10|3: Then shalt thou go on forward from there, and thou shalt come to the oak of Tabor, and there shall meet thee three men going up to God to Beth-el, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine:
verses.1 Samuel|10|4: and they will greet thee, and give thee two loaves of bread; which thou shalt receive from their hands.
verses.1 Samuel|10|5: After that thou shalt come to the hill of God, where the garrisons of the Philistines are, and it shall come to pass, when thou art come there to the city, that thou shalt meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a lute, and a timbrel, and a pipe, and a lyre, before them; and they shall prophesy:
verses.1 Samuel|10|6: and the spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.
verses.1 Samuel|10|7: And let it be, when these signs are come to thee, that thou do as occasion serve thee; for God is with thee.
verses.1 Samuel|10|8: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down to thee, to offer burnt offerings, and to make sacrifices of peace offerings; seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and show thee what thou shalt do.
verses.1 Samuel|10|9: And it was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.
verses.1 Samuel|10|10: And when they came there to the hill, behold, a company of prophets met him; and the spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them.
verses.1 Samuel|10|11: And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, then the people said one to another, What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also one of the prophets?
verses.1 Samuel|10|12: And one of the same place answered and said, But who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also one of the prophets?
verses.1 Samuel|10|13: And when he had made an end of prophesying, he came to the high place.
verses.1 Samuel|10|14: And Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant, Where did you go to? And he said, To seek the asses: and when we saw that they were not to be found, we came to Samuel.
verses.1 Samuel|10|15: And Saul's uncle said, Tell me, I pray thee, what Samuel said to you.
verses.1 Samuel|10|16: And Saul said to his uncle, He told us plainly that the asses were found. But of the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel spoke, he told him not.
verses.1 Samuel|10|17: And Samuel called the people together to the Lord to Mizpah.
verses.1 Samuel|10|18: And he said to the children of Israel, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and delivered you out of the hand of Egypt, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms, and of them that oppressed you:
verses.1 Samuel|10|19: and you have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you from all your calamities and tribulations; and you have said to him, Only set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before the Lord by your tribes, and by your thousands,
verses.1 Samuel|10|20: And Samuel caused all the tribes of Israel to come near, and the tribe of Benjamin was picked (by lot).
verses.1 Samuel|10|21: Then he caused the tribe of Benjamin to come near by its families, and the family of Matri was picked, and Saul the son of Kish was picked: and when they sought him, he could not be found.
verses.1 Samuel|10|22: Therefore they inquired again of the Lord, Did the man come here? And the Lord answered, Behold, he is hidden among the baggage.
verses.1 Samuel|10|23: And they ran and fetched him from there: and when he stood among the people, he was taller than any of the people from his shoulders upwards.
verses.1 Samuel|10|24: And Samuel said to all the people, Do you see him whom the Lord has chosen, that there is none like him among all the people? And all the people shouted, and said, Long live the king.
verses.1 Samuel|10|25: Then Samuel told the people the rules of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the Lord. And Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
verses.1 Samuel|10|26: And Saul also went home to Gibeah; and there went with him the warriors, whose hearts God had touched.
verses.1 Samuel|10|27: But some base fellows said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he held his peace.
verses.1 Samuel|11|1: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh-gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, Make a league with us, and we will serve thee.
verses.1 Samuel|11|2: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, On this condition will I make a league with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a disgrace upon all Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|11|3: And the elders of Jabesh said to him, Give us seven days' respite, that we may send messengers to all the territory of Israel: and then, if there be no man to save us, we will come out to thee.
verses.1 Samuel|11|4: Then came the messengers to Gibeah of Saul, and told the tidings in the ears of the people: and all the people raised their voices, and wept.
verses.1 Samuel|11|5: And, behold, Saul came after the herd out of the field; and Saul said, What ails the people that they weep? And they told him the tidings of the men of Jabesh,
verses.1 Samuel|11|6: And the spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger burned greatly.
verses.1 Samuel|11|7: And he took a yoke of oxen, and cut them up in pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hands of messengers, saying, Whoever comes not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen. And the fear of the Lord fell on the people and they came out with one consent.
verses.1 Samuel|11|8: And when he numbered them in Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah, thirty thousand.
verses.1 Samuel|11|9: And they said to the messengers that came, Thus shall you say to the men of Jabesh-gilead, To morrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help. And the messengers came and reported to the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.
verses.1 Samuel|11|10: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, To morrow we will come out to you, and you shall do with us all that seems good in your eyes.
verses.1 Samuel|11|11: And it was so on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and smote Ammon until the heat of the day: and those that remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
verses.1 Samuel|11|12: And the people said to Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death.
verses.1 Samuel|11|13: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for today the Lord has wrought salvation in Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|11|14: Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.
verses.1 Samuel|11|15: And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal: and there they made sacrifices of peace offerings before the Lord; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
verses.1 Samuel|12|1: And Samuel said to all Israel, Behold, I have hearkened to your voice in all that you said to me, and have made a king over you.
verses.1 Samuel|12|2: And now, behold, the king walks before you: and I am old and greyheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood to this day.
verses.1 Samuel|12|3: Behold, here I am: answer me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe with which to blind my eyes? and I will restore it you.
verses.1 Samuel|12|4: And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand,
verses.1 Samuel|12|5: And he said to them, The Lord is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that you have not found anything in my hand. And they answered, He is witness.
verses.1 Samuel|12|6: And Samuel said to the people, It is the Lord that made Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.1 Samuel|12|7: Now therefore stand still, that I may plead with you before the Lord concerning all the righteous acts of the Lord, which he did to you and to your fathers.
verses.1 Samuel|12|8: When Jacob was come into Egypt, and your fathers cried to the Lord, then the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt, and made them dwell in this place.
verses.1 Samuel|12|9: And when they forgot the Lord their God, he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
verses.1 Samuel|12|10: And they cried to the Lord, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord, and have served the Baalim and the Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve Thee.
verses.1 Samuel|12|11: And the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies round about, and you dwelled secure.
verses.1 Samuel|12|12: And when you saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, No; but a king shall reign over us: when the Lord your God was your king.
verses.1 Samuel|12|13: Now therefore behold the king whom you have chosen, and whom you have desired! for behold, the Lord has set a king over you.
verses.1 Samuel|12|14: If you will fear the Lord, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, and if both you and also the king that reigns over you will follow the Lord your God –
verses.1 Samuel|12|15: but if you will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers.
verses.1 Samuel|12|16: Now therefore stand and see this great thing, which the Lord will do before your eyes.
verses.1 Samuel|12|17: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call to the Lord, and he shall send thunder and rain; that you may know and see that your wickedness is great, which you have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking for a king for yourselves.
verses.1 Samuel|12|18: So Samuel called to the Lord; and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
verses.1 Samuel|12|19: And all the people said to Samuel, Pray for thy servants to the Lord thy God, that we die not: for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for a king for ourselves.
verses.1 Samuel|12|20: And Samuel said to the people, Fear not: you have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart;
verses.1 Samuel|12|21: and turn not aside: for then you should go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.
verses.1 Samuel|12|22: For the Lord will not abandon his people for his great name's sake: because it has pleased the Lord to make you his people.
verses.1 Samuel|12|23: Moreover as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
verses.1 Samuel|12|24: only fear the Lord, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great are the things which he has done for you.
verses.1 Samuel|12|25: But if you shall still do wickedly, you shall be swept away, both you and your king.
verses.1 Samuel|13|1: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
verses.1 Samuel|13|2: Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel, of whom two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in mount Beth-el, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent.
verses.1 Samuel|13|3: And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the shofar throughout all the land saying, Let the Hebrews hear.
verses.1 Samuel|13|4: And all Israel heard say that Saul had smitten the garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel also had become odious to the Philistines. And the people mustered after Saul at Gilgal.
verses.1 Samuel|13|5: And the Philistines gathered themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people like the sand on the sea shore for multitude: and they came up, and encamped in Michmash, eastward from Beth-aven.
verses.1 Samuel|13|6: When the men of Israel saw that they were in straits, (for the people were hardpressed,) then the people hid themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in strongholds, and in pits.
verses.1 Samuel|13|7: And some of the Hebrews went over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
verses.1 Samuel|13|8: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattering from him.
verses.1 Samuel|13|9: And Saul said, Bring me here the burnt offering and the peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
verses.1 Samuel|13|10: And it came to pass, that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might greet him.
verses.1 Samuel|13|11: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
verses.1 Samuel|13|12: therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication to the Lord: I forced myself therefore, and offered the burnt offering.
verses.1 Samuel|13|13: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee: for now the Lord would have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
verses.1 Samuel|13|14: But now thy kingdom shall not endure: the Lord has sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord has commanded him to be a prince over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee.
verses.1 Samuel|13|15: And Samuel arose, and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men.
verses.1 Samuel|13|16: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, dwelt in Gibeah of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
verses.1 Samuel|13|17: And the raiding parties came out of the camp of the Philistines in three groups: one group turned to the way of Ophrah to the land of Shual:
verses.1 Samuel|13|18: and another group turned the way to Beth-horon: and another group turned to the way of the border that looked over the valley of Zeboim towards the wilderness.
verses.1 Samuel|13|19: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:
verses.1 Samuel|13|20: but all Israel went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his spade, and his ax, and his mattock.
verses.1 Samuel|13|21: And there was a charge for filing the mattocks, and the spades, and the three-pronged forks, and the axes, and for setting the goads.
verses.1 Samuel|13|22: So it came to pass on the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear to be found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.
verses.1 Samuel|13|23: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the passage of Michmash.
verses.1 Samuel|14|1: Now it came to pass one day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man that bore his armour, Come, and let us go over to the garrison of the Philistines, that is on the other side. But he did not tell his father.
verses.1 Samuel|14|2: And Saul was sitting on the far side of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree which was in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
verses.1 Samuel|14|3: and Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, I-chabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, was the Lord's priest in Shiloh, wearing an efod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.
verses.1 Samuel|14|4: And between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the garrison of the Philistines, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
verses.1 Samuel|14|5: The one point rose up abruptly northwards over against Michmash, and the other southwards over against Geba.
verses.1 Samuel|14|6: And Jonathan said to the young man that bore his armour, Come, and let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the Lord will perform a deed for us: for there is no restraint upon the Lord to save by many or by few.
verses.1 Samuel|14|7: And his armourbearer said to him, Do all that is in thy heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.
verses.1 Samuel|14|8: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over to these men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.
verses.1 Samuel|14|9: If they say thus to us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up to them.
verses.1 Samuel|14|10: But if they say thus, Come up to us; then we will go up: for the Lord has delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign to us.
verses.1 Samuel|14|11: And both of them showed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come out of the holes where they have hidden themselves.
verses.1 Samuel|14|12: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will show you something. And Jonathan said to his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the Lord has delivered them into the hand of Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|14|13: And Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.
verses.1 Samuel|14|14: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armour-bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow, which a yoke of oxen might plough.
verses.1 Samuel|14|15: And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the raiding parties, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.
verses.1 Samuel|14|16: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and disintegrated.
verses.1 Samuel|14|17: Then said Saul to the people that were with him. Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.
verses.1 Samuel|14|18: And Saul said to Ahiah, Bring the ark of God here. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|14|19: And it came to pass, while Saul talked to the priest, that the noise that was in the camp of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said to the priest, Withdraw thy hand.
verses.1 Samuel|14|20: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great confusion.
verses.1 Samuel|14|21: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, who went up with them into the camp from the country round about, they also turned to be with the men of Israel that were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.1 Samuel|14|22: Likewise all the men of Israel who had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, they also pursued them closely in the battle.
verses.1 Samuel|14|23: So the Lord saved Israel that day: and the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.
verses.1 Samuel|14|24: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eats any food until evening, that I may be avenged on my enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
verses.1 Samuel|14|25: And all the people came to a wood; and there was honey on the ground.
verses.1 Samuel|14|26: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, a stream of honey; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.
verses.1 Samuel|14|27: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: and he put out the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in a honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were brightened.
verses.1 Samuel|14|28: Then one of the people answered and said, Thy father strictly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eats any food this day. And the people were faint.
verses.1 Samuel|14|29: Then said Jonathan, My father has troubled the land: see, I pray you, how my eyes have brightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.1 Samuel|14|30: How much more, if only the people had eaten freely today of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?
verses.1 Samuel|14|31: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
verses.1 Samuel|14|32: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.
verses.1 Samuel|14|33: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, You have transgressed: roll a great stone to me this day.
verses.1 Samuel|14|34: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say to them, Bring me here every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.
verses.1 Samuel|14|35: And Saul built an altar to the Lord: that was the first altar that he built to the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|14|36: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morninglight, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatever seems good to thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near here to God.
verses.1 Samuel|14|37: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt Thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.
verses.1 Samuel|14|38: And Saul said, Draw near, all you chiefs of the people: and know and see wherein this sin has been this day.
verses.1 Samuel|14|39: For, as the Lord lives, who saves Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.
verses.1 Samuel|14|40: Then said he to all Israel, Be you on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said to Saul, Do what seems good to thee.
verses.1 Samuel|14|41: Therefore Saul said to the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were picked: but the people escaped.
verses.1 Samuel|14|42: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was picked.
verses.1 Samuel|14|43: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand, and, lo, I must die.
verses.1 Samuel|14|44: And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.
verses.1 Samuel|14|45: And the people said to Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who has wrought this great salvation in Israel? Far be it! as the Lord lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground; for he has wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.
verses.1 Samuel|14|46: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.1 Samuel|14|47: So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and wherever he turned himself, he did them mischief.
verses.1 Samuel|14|48: And he gathered a host, and smote Amalek, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.
verses.1 Samuel|14|49: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Jishbi, and Melchi-shua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:
verses.1 Samuel|14|50: and the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
verses.1 Samuel|14|51: And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
verses.1 Samuel|14|52: And there was hard warfare against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him to himself.
verses.1 Samuel|15|1: And Samuel said to Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken to the voice of the words of the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|15|2: Thus says the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
verses.1 Samuel|15|3: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
verses.1 Samuel|15|4: And Saul gathered the people together, and numbered them in Telaim two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.1 Samuel|15|5: And Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.
verses.1 Samuel|15|6: And Saul said to the Kenites, Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekite, lest I destroy thee with them: for thou hast shown kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among Amalek.
verses.1 Samuel|15|7: And Saul smote Amalek from Havilah until the approach to Shur, that is over against Egypt.
verses.1 Samuel|15|8: And he took Agag the king of Amalek alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
verses.1 Samuel|15|9: But Saul and the people had pity on Agag, and on the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but everything that was of little value and weak, they destroyed utterly.
verses.1 Samuel|15|10: Then came the word of the Lord to Samuel saying,
verses.1 Samuel|15|11: I regret that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and he has not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried to the Lord all night.
verses.1 Samuel|15|12: And when Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a monument, and is gone about, and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal.
verses.1 Samuel|15|13: And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said to him, Blessed be thou of the Lord: I have performed the commandment of the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|15|14: And Samuel said, What means then this bleating of the sheep in my ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
verses.1 Samuel|15|15: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekite: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice to the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.
verses.1 Samuel|15|16: Then Samuel said to Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what the Lord said to me this night. And he said to him, Say on.
verses.1 Samuel|15|17: And Samuel said, Though thou wast little in thy own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the Lord anointed thee king over Israel?
verses.1 Samuel|15|18: And the Lord sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy those sinners, the men of Amalek, and fight against them until they are consumed.
verses.1 Samuel|15|19: Why then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst do evil in the sight of the Lord?
verses.1 Samuel|15|20: And Saul said to Samuel, Indeed, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone along the road which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed Amalek.
verses.1 Samuel|15|21: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the devoted property, to sacrifice to the Lord thy God in Gilgal.
verses.1 Samuel|15|22: And Samuel said, Has the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
verses.1 Samuel|15|23: For rebellion is like the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is like idolatry and terafim. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord he has also rejected thee from being king.
verses.1 Samuel|15|24: And Saul said to Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
verses.1 Samuel|15|25: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, and I will bow down to the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|15|26: And Samuel said to Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord has rejected thee from being king over Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|15|27: And as Samuel turned about to go away, he laid hold of the corner of his robe, and it tore.
verses.1 Samuel|15|28: And Samuel said to him, The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and has given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.
verses.1 Samuel|15|29: And also the Eternal One of Israel will not lie nor change his mind: for he is not a man, that he should change his mind.
verses.1 Samuel|15|30: Then he said, I have sinned: yet do me honour now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord thy God.
verses.1 Samuel|15|31: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|15|32: Then said Samuel, Bring here to me Agag the king of Amalek. And Agag came to him in chains. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
verses.1 Samuel|15|33: And Samuel said, As thy sword has made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.
verses.1 Samuel|15|34: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|15|35: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|16|1: And the Lord said to Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thy horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse, the Beth-lehemite: for I have provided for me a king among his sons,
verses.1 Samuel|16|2: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hears it, he will kill me. And the Lord said, Take a heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|16|3: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint to me him whom I name to thee.
verses.1 Samuel|16|4: And Samuel did that which the Lord spoke, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou in peace?
verses.1 Samuel|16|5: And he said, In peace: I am come to sacrifice to the Lord: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
verses.1 Samuel|16|6: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the Lord's anointed is before him.
verses.1 Samuel|16|7: But the Lord said to Samuel, Look not on his countenance, nor on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for it is not as a man sees; for a man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
verses.1 Samuel|16|8: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither has the Lord chosen this.
verses.1 Samuel|16|9: Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, Neither has the Lord chosen this.
verses.1 Samuel|16|10: And Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, The Lord has not chosen these.
verses.1 Samuel|16|11: And Samuel said to Jesse, Are these all thy children? And he said, There remains yet the youngest, and he is tending the sheep. Then Samuel said to Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he comes here.
verses.1 Samuel|16|12: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with fine eyes, and good looking. And the Lord said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
verses.1 Samuel|16|13: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day onwards. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
verses.1 Samuel|16|14: But the spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord tormented him.
verses.1 Samuel|16|15: And Saul's servants said to him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God is tormenting thee.
verses.1 Samuel|16|16: Let our lord now command thy servants, who are before thee, to seek out a man, who knows how to play on the lyre: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he will play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.
verses.1 Samuel|16|17: And Saul said to his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.
verses.1 Samuel|16|18: Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Beth-lehemite, that knows how to play, and a fine warrior, and a man of war, and prudent in speech, and a comely person, and the Lord is with him.
verses.1 Samuel|16|19: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, who is with the sheep.
verses.1 Samuel|16|20: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son to Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|16|21: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.
verses.1 Samuel|16|22: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he has found favour in my eyes.
verses.1 Samuel|16|23: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took a lyre, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
verses.1 Samuel|17|1: Now the Philistines gathered together their camps to battle, and were gathered together at Shocho, which belongs to Judah, and pitched between Shocho and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.
verses.1 Samuel|17|2: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and they encamped by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
verses.1 Samuel|17|3: And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
verses.1 Samuel|17|4: And there went out a champion out of the camps of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
verses.1 Samuel|17|5: And he had a helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a body armour of scales; and the weight of the body armour was five thousand shekels of brass.
verses.1 Samuel|17|6: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a javelin of brass between his shoulders.
verses.1 Samuel|17|7: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver's beam; and his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and a shieldbearer went before him.
verses.1 Samuel|17|8: And he stood and cried to the armies of Israel, and said to them, Why are you come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and you are servants to Saul? choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
verses.1 Samuel|17|9: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall you be our servants, and serve us.
verses.1 Samuel|17|10: And the Philistine said, I defy the ranks of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
verses.1 Samuel|17|11: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
verses.1 Samuel|17|12: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man was old in the days of Saul, an aged man.
verses.1 Samuel|17|13: And the three eldest sons of Jesse went and followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
verses.1 Samuel|17|14: And David was the youngest: and the three eldest followed Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|17|15: But David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep at Beth-lehem.
verses.1 Samuel|17|16: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself for forty days.
verses.1 Samuel|17|17: And Jesse said to David his son, Take now for thy brothers an efa of this parched corn, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brothers;
verses.1 Samuel|17|18: and carry these ten cheeses to the captain of their thousand, and inquire of thy brothers' welfare, and take a token from them.
verses.1 Samuel|17|19: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
verses.1 Samuel|17|20: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the barricade, as the host was going out to the frontline, shouting for the battle.
verses.1 Samuel|17|21: For Israel and the Philistines were drawn up, army against army.
verses.1 Samuel|17|22: And David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran into the line of battle, and came and saluted his brethren.
verses.1 Samuel|17|23: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, Goliath the Philistine was his name, from Gath, out of the ranks of the Philistines, and spoke those same words: and David heard them.
verses.1 Samuel|17|24: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were greatly afraid.
verses.1 Samuel|17|25: And the men of Israel said, Have you seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who kills him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|17|26: And David spoke to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that kills yonder Philistine, and takes away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should taunt the armies of the living God?
verses.1 Samuel|17|27: And the people answered him after the aforementioned manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that kills him.
verses.1 Samuel|17|28: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spoke to the men: and Eliab's anger burned against David, and he said, Why didst thou come down here? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy insolence, and thy peevishness; for thou art come down to see the battle.
verses.1 Samuel|17|29: And David said, What have I now done? It was only a word.
verses.1 Samuel|17|30: And he turned from him towards another, and spoke after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.
verses.1 Samuel|17|31: And when the words were heard which David spoke, they rehearsed them before Saul: and he sent for him.
verses.1 Samuel|17|32: And David said to Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
verses.1 Samuel|17|33: And Saul said to David, thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
verses.1 Samuel|17|34: And David said to Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:
verses.1 Samuel|17|35: and I went out after it, and smote it, and delivered it out of its mouth: and when it arose against me, I caught it by its beard, and smote it, and slew it.
verses.1 Samuel|17|36: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he has defied the armies of the living God.
verses.1 Samuel|17|37: And David said, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said to David, Go, and the Lord be with thee.
verses.1 Samuel|17|38: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put a helmet of brass upon his head; also he clothed him with a coat of mail.
verses.1 Samuel|17|39: And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he essayed to go; but he had not tried it out. And David said to Saul, I cannot walk with these; for I have not tried them. And David put them off him.
verses.1 Samuel|17|40: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, and in his knapsack; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
verses.1 Samuel|17|41: And the Philistine came on and drew near to David; and the shield-bearer went before him.
verses.1 Samuel|17|42: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, though ruddy, and good-looking.
verses.1 Samuel|17|43: And the Philistine said to David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with sticks? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.1 Samuel|17|44: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh to the birds of the sky, and to the beasts of the field.
verses.1 Samuel|17|45: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast taunted.
verses.1 Samuel|17|46: This day will the Lord deliver thee into my hand; and I will smite thee, and take thy head from thee; and I will give the carcass of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the sky, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.1 Samuel|17|47: And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saves not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's, and he will give you into our hands.
verses.1 Samuel|17|48: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew near to meet David, that David hastened, and ran to the enemy line towards the Philistine.
verses.1 Samuel|17|49: And David put his hand in his bag, and took from there a stone, and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone buried itself in his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
verses.1 Samuel|17|50: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
verses.1 Samuel|17|51: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of its sheath, and slew him, and with it he cut off his head. And when the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.
verses.1 Samuel|17|52: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until the approaches of Gai, and to the gates of Ekron. And the dead of the Philistines fell by the way to Shaaraim, and to Gath, and to Ekron.
verses.1 Samuel|17|53: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they plundered their tents.
verses.1 Samuel|17|54: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; and he put his armour in his tent.
verses.1 Samuel|17|55: And when Saul saw David go out against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? And Abner said, By thy life, O king, I know not.
verses.1 Samuel|17|56: And the king said, Inquire thou whose son the young man is.
verses.1 Samuel|17|57: And as David returned from slaying the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
verses.1 Samuel|17|58: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, lad? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse, the Beth-lehemite.
verses.1 Samuel|18|1: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking to Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
verses.1 Samuel|18|2: And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father's house.
verses.1 Samuel|18|3: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
verses.1 Samuel|18|4: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, and even his sword, and his bow, and his girdle.
verses.1 Samuel|18|5: And David went out wherever Saul sent him, and succeeded: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul's servants.
verses.1 Samuel|18|6: And it came to pass on their return, when David returned from slaying the Philistine, that the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with timbrels, and a joyful song, and with lutes.
verses.1 Samuel|18|7: And the women answered one another as they danced, and said, Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
verses.1 Samuel|18|8: And Saul was very angry, and the saying displeased him; and he said, They have given David ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom?
verses.1 Samuel|18|9: And Saul viewed David with suspicion from that day and onwards.
verses.1 Samuel|18|10: And it came to pass on the morrow, that an evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and he raved in the midst of the house: and David played with his hand, as at other times: and the spear was in Saul's hand.
verses.1 Samuel|18|11: And Saul raised the spear; for he said, I will smite David to the wall with it. And David turned aside out of his presence twice.
verses.1 Samuel|18|12: And Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him, and was departed from Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|18|13: Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him a captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
verses.1 Samuel|18|14: And David succeeded in all his ways; and the Lord was with him.
verses.1 Samuel|18|15: Wherefore when Saul saw that he succeeded so well, he was afraid of him.
verses.1 Samuel|18|16: But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.
verses.1 Samuel|18|17: And Saul said to David, Behold my elder daughter Merab, her will I give thee to wife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight the Lord's battles. For Saul said, Let not my hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.
verses.1 Samuel|18|18: And David said to Saul, Who am I? and what is my life, or my father's family in Israel, that I should be son in law to the king?
verses.1 Samuel|18|19: And so it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul's daughter should have been given to David, that she was given to Adriel the Meholathite to wife.
verses.1 Samuel|18|20: And Michal Saul's daughter loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.
verses.1 Samuel|18|21: And Saul said, I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. And Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son in law through the second.
verses.1 Samuel|18|22: And Saul commanded his servants, saying, Speak with David secretly, and say, Behold, the king has delight in thee, and all his servants love thee: now therefore be the king's son in law.
verses.1 Samuel|18|23: And Saul's servants spoke those words in the ears of David. And David said, Seems it to you a light thing to be a king's son in law, seeing that I am a poor man, and insignificant?
verses.1 Samuel|18|24: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, In this manner did David speak.
verses.1 Samuel|18|25: And Saul said, Thus shall you say to David, The king desires no dowry, but a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king's enemies. But Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
verses.1 Samuel|18|26: And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king's son in law. Now, before the days were expired,
verses.1 Samuel|18|27: David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, that he might be the king's son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.
verses.1 Samuel|18|28: And Saul saw and knew that the Lord was with David, and that Michal Saul's daughter loved him.
verses.1 Samuel|18|29: And Saul continued to be afraid of David; and Saul became David's enemy continually.
verses.1 Samuel|18|30: Then the princes of the Philistines went out: and it came to pass, after they went out, that David proved himself more competent than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was highly prized.
verses.1 Samuel|19|1: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan, the son of Saul, delighted much in David:
verses.1 Samuel|19|2: and Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeks to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself in the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself:
verses.1 Samuel|19|3: and I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where thou art, and I will speak with my father about thee; and I will see what the position is, and I will tell thee.
verses.1 Samuel|19|4: And Jonathan spoke good of David to Saul his father, and said to him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he has not sinned against thee, and because his deeds have been very good towards thee:
verses.1 Samuel|19|5: for he did take his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine, and the Lord performed a great salvation for all Israel: thou didst see it, and didst rejoice: why then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without cause?
verses.1 Samuel|19|6: And Saul hearkened to the voice of Jonathan: and Saul swore, As the Lord lives, he shall not be slain.
verses.1 Samuel|19|7: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan related all those things to him. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as in times past.
verses.1 Samuel|19|8: And there was war again: and David went out, and fought with the Philistines, and slew them with a great slaughter; and they fled from him.
verses.1 Samuel|19|9: And an evil spirit from the Lord came upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand: and David played with his hand.
verses.1 Samuel|19|10: And Saul sought to smite David even to the wall with the spear; but he slipped away out of Saul's presence, so that he smote the spear into the wall: and David fled, and escaped that night.
verses.1 Samuel|19|11: And Saul sent messengers to David's house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal David's wife told him, saying, If thou save not thy life tonight, to morrow thou shalt be slain.
verses.1 Samuel|19|12: So Michal let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.
verses.1 Samuel|19|13: And Michal took the terafim, and laid them on the bed, and put the pillow of goats' hair at its head, and covered it with a cloth.
verses.1 Samuel|19|14: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He is sick.
verses.1 Samuel|19|15: And Saul sent the messengers again to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.
verses.1 Samuel|19|16: And when the messengers were come in, behold, the terafim were in the bed, with a pillow of goats' hair at its head.
verses.1 Samuel|19|17: And Saul said to Michal, Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away my enemy, that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said to me, Let me go; why should I kill thee?
verses.1 Samuel|19|18: So David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.
verses.1 Samuel|19|19: And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.
verses.1 Samuel|19|20: And Saul sent messengers to take David: and when they saw the band of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel stationed over them, the spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
verses.1 Samuel|19|21: And when it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they prophesied also.
verses.1 Samuel|19|22: Then he went himself to Ramah, and came to the great pit that is in Sechu: and he asked and said, Where are Samuel and David? And someone said, Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah. And he went there to Naioth in Ramah:
verses.1 Samuel|19|23: and the spirit of God was upon him also, and he went on, prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
verses.1 Samuel|19|24: And he even stripped off his clothes, and he himself prophesied before Samuel, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, Is Saul also one of the prophets?
verses.1 Samuel|20|1: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? what is my crime? and what is my sin before thy father, that he seeks my life?
verses.1 Samuel|20|2: And he said to him, Far be it! thou shalt not die: behold, my father will do nothing either great or small, without revealing it to me: and why should my father hide this thing from me? it is not so.
verses.1 Samuel|20|3: And David swore moreover, and said, Thy father certainly knows that I have found favour in thy eyes; and he says, Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved: but truly as the Lord lives, and as thy soul lives, there is but a step between me and death.
verses.1 Samuel|20|4: Then Jonathan said to David, Whatever thy soul desires, I will do for thee.
verses.1 Samuel|20|5: And David said to Jonathan, Behold, to morrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit with the king at the meal: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field until the third day at evening.
verses.1 Samuel|20|6: If thy father should miss me, then say, David earnestly asked leave of me that he might run to Beth-lehem his city: for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.
verses.1 Samuel|20|7: If he say thus, It is well; then thy servant shall have peace: but if he be very angry, then you should know that evil is determined by him.
verses.1 Samuel|20|8: Therefore deal kindly with thy servant; for thou hast brought thy servant into a covenant of the Lord with thee: but if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for why shouldst thou bring me to thy father?
verses.1 Samuel|20|9: And Jonathan said, Far be it from thee: for if I knew certainly that evil were determined by my father to come upon thee, then would not I tell it thee?
verses.1 Samuel|20|10: Then said David to Jonathan, Who shall tell me if thy father answer thee roughly?
verses.1 Samuel|20|11: And Jonathan said to David, Come, and let us go out into the field. And they went out both of them into the field.
verses.1 Samuel|20|12: And Jonathan said to David, O Lord God of Israel, when I have sounded my father to morrow, or the third day about this time, and if there be good intended towards David, shall I then not send to thee, and let thee know?
verses.1 Samuel|20|13: the Lord do so and much more to Jonathan; moreover, if it please my father to do thee evil, then I will let thee know, and send thee away, that thou mayst go in peace: and the Lord be with thee, as he has been with my father.
verses.1 Samuel|20|14: And thou shalt not only while yet I live, even before I die, show me the loyal love of the Lord:
verses.1 Samuel|20|15: but also thou shalt not cut off thy covenant love from my house for ever: no, not when the Lord has cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.
verses.1 Samuel|20|16: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, Let the Lord even require it at the hand of David's enemies.
verses.1 Samuel|20|17: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
verses.1 Samuel|20|18: Then Jonathan said to David, Tomorrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.
verses.1 Samuel|20|19: And on the third day, thou shalt be greatly missed; then thou shalt go down to the place where thou didst hide thyself on that day (of the deed), and shalt remain by the stone Ezel.
verses.1 Samuel|20|20: And I will shoot three arrows on the side of it, as though I shot at a mark.
verses.1 Samuel|20|21: And, behold, I will send a lad, saying, Go, find out the arrows. If I expressly say to the lad, Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee, take them; then come thou: for it is well for thee, and there is nothing to fear; as the Lord lives.
verses.1 Samuel|20|22: But if I say thus to the young man, Behold, the arrows are beyond thee; go thy way: for the Lord has sent thee away.
verses.1 Samuel|20|23: And as touching the matter which thou and I have spoken of, behold, the Lord be between thee and me for ever.
verses.1 Samuel|20|24: So David hid himself in the field: and when the new moon was come, the king sat down to eat the meal.
verses.1 Samuel|20|25: And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, upon a seat by the wall: and Jonathan, arose, and Abner sat by Saul's side, and David's place was empty.
verses.1 Samuel|20|26: Nevertheless Saul spoke not anything that day: for he thought, It is an accidental pollution, he is not clean; yes, indeed, he is not clean.
verses.1 Samuel|20|27: And it came to pass on the morrow after the new moon which was the second day, that David's place was empty: and Saul said to Jonathan his son, Why does the son of Jesse not come to the meal, neither yesterday, nor today?
verses.1 Samuel|20|28: And Jonathan answered Saul, David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Beth-lehem:
verses.1 Samuel|20|29: and he said, Let me go, I pray thee; for our family has a sacrfice in the city; and my brother, he has commanded me to be there: and now, if I have found favour in thine eyes, let me get away, I pray thee, and see my brothers. Therefore he does not come to the king's table.
verses.1 Samuel|20|30: Then Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, Thou perverse and rebellious son, do not I know that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine own disgrace, and to the disgrace of thy mother's nakedness?
verses.1 Samuel|20|31: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom. And now send and fetch him to me for he shall surely die.
verses.1 Samuel|20|32: And Jonathan answered Saul his father, and said to him, Why should he be slain? what has he done?
verses.1 Samuel|20|33: And Saul raised the spear at him to smite him: whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David.
verses.1 Samuel|20|34: So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and ate no food on the second day of the new moon: for he was grieved for David, because his father had put him to shame.
verses.1 Samuel|20|35: And it came to pass in the morning, that Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a little lad with him.
verses.1 Samuel|20|36: And he said to his lad, Run, find out now the arrows which I shoot. And as the lad ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
verses.1 Samuel|20|37: And when the lad was come to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried after the lad, and said, But the arrow is beyond thee?
verses.1 Samuel|20|38: And Jonathan cried after the lad. Make speed, haste, stay not. And Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows, and came to his master.
verses.1 Samuel|20|39: But the lad knew not anything: only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
verses.1 Samuel|20|40: And Jonathan gave his weapons to his lad, and said to him, Go, carry them to the city.
verses.1 Samuel|20|41: And as soon as the lad was gone, David arose out of a place toward the south, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed himself three times: and they kissed one another, and wept one with another, until David exceeded.
verses.1 Samuel|20|42: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, seeing that we have sworn both of us in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever.
verses.1 Samuel|21|1: And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.
verses.1 Samuel|21|2: Then David came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech was afraid at meeting David, and said to him, Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?
verses.1 Samuel|21|3: And David said to Ahimelech the priest, The king has commanded me a business, and has said to me, Let no man know anything of the business about which I am sending thee, and what I have commanded thee: and I have despatched my servants to such and such a place.
verses.1 Samuel|21|4: Now therefore what is under thy hand? give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatever there is.
verses.1 Samuel|21|5: And the priest answered David, and said, There is no common bread in my hand, but there is hallowed bread; if the young men have kept themselves at least from women.
verses.1 Samuel|21|6: And David answered the priest, and said to him, Of a truth women have been kept from us as always when I am on a journey, and the vessels of the young men are holy, (although it is a common journey,) how much more today when there will be hallowed bread in their vessel.
verses.1 Samuel|21|7: So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the showbread, that was taken from before the Lord, to put hot bread in its place on the day when it was taken away.
verses.1 Samuel|21|8: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the Lord; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|21|9: And David said to Ahimelech, And is there not here under thy hand a spear or a sword? for I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business was urgent.
verses.1 Samuel|21|10: And the priest said, The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom thou didst slay in the valley of Elah, behold it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the efod: if thou wilt take that, take it: for there is no other save that here. And David said, There is none like that; give it to me.
verses.1 Samuel|21|11: And David arose, and fled that day from before Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.
verses.1 Samuel|21|12: And the servants of Achish said to him, Is not this David the king of the land? did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying, Saul has slain his thousands, but David his ten thousands?
verses.1 Samuel|21|13: And David laid up these words in his heart, and was sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
verses.1 Samuel|21|14: And he changed his be-haviour before them, and feigned himself mad in their hands, and scratched on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle run down upon his beard.
verses.1 Samuel|21|15: Then said Achish to his servants, Lo, you see the man is mad: why then have you brought him to me?
verses.1 Samuel|21|16: Am I short of mad men, that you have brought this fellow to play the mad man in my presence? Shall this fellow come into my house?
verses.1 Samuel|22|1: David therefore departed from there, and escaped to the cave of Adullam: and when his brothers and all his father's house heard it, they went down there to him.
verses.1 Samuel|22|2: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves to him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.
verses.1 Samuel|22|3: And David went thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said to the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray thee, come out, and be with you, till I know what God will do for me.
verses.1 Samuel|22|4: And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they dwelt with him all the while that David was in the fortress.
verses.1 Samuel|22|5: And the prophet Gad said to David, Do not abide in the fortress; depart, and get thee into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hareth.
verses.1 Samuel|22|6: When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him (now Saul dwelt in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;)
verses.1 Samuel|22|7: then Saul said to his servants that stood about him, Hear now, you Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds;
verses.1 Samuel|22|8: that all of you have conspired against me and there is none that gave me an intimation when my son made a league with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or lets me know that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
verses.1 Samuel|22|9: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, who was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
verses.1 Samuel|22|10: And he inquired of the Lord for him, and gave him food, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
verses.1 Samuel|22|11: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father's house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.
verses.1 Samuel|22|12: And Saul said, Hear now, thou son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.
verses.1 Samuel|22|13: And Saul said to him, Why have you conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
verses.1 Samuel|22|14: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, who is the king's son in law, and gives heed at thy bidding, and is honourable in thy house?
verses.1 Samuel|22|15: Did I then begin to inquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing to his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
verses.1 Samuel|22|16: And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father's house.
verses.1 Samuel|22|17: And the king said to the runners that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the Lord; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not reveal it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|22|18: And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day eighty five persons that did wear a linen efod.
verses.1 Samuel|22|19: And Nob, the city of the priests, he smote with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
verses.1 Samuel|22|20: And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar escaped, and fled after David,
verses.1 Samuel|22|21: And Abiathar told David that Saul had slain the Lord's priests.
verses.1 Samuel|22|22: And David said to Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father's house.
verses.1 Samuel|22|23: Remain with me, fear not: for he that seeks my life seeks thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.
verses.1 Samuel|23|1: Then they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are plundering the threshingfloors.
verses.1 Samuel|23|2: Therefore David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And the Lord said to David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.
verses.1 Samuel|23|3: And David's men said to him, Behold, we are afraid here in Judah: how much more then if we come to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?
verses.1 Samuel|23|4: Then David inquired of the Lord yet again. And the Lord answered him and said, Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into thy hand.
verses.1 Samuel|23|5: So David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
verses.1 Samuel|23|6: And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came down with an efod in his hand.
verses.1 Samuel|23|7: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keilah. And Saul said, God has delivered him into my hand; for he is shut in, by entering a town that has gates and bars.
verses.1 Samuel|23|8: And Saul called all the people together to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.
verses.1 Samuel|23|9: And David knew that Saul devised that mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring the efod here.
verses.1 Samuel|23|10: Then said David, O Lord God of Israel, Thy servant has certainly heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
verses.1 Samuel|23|11: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as Thy servant has heard? O Lord God of Israel, I beseech Thee, tell Thy servant. And the Lord said, He will come down.
verses.1 Samuel|23|12: Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul? And the Lord said, They will deliver thee up.
verses.1 Samuel|23|13: Then David and his men, who were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went wherever they could go. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah; and he forbore to go after.
verses.1 Samuel|23|14: And David dwelt in the wilderness in strongholds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand.
verses.1 Samuel|23|15: And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood.
verses.1 Samuel|23|16: And Jonathan Saul's son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.
verses.1 Samuel|23|17: And he said to him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next to thee; and that also Saul my father knows.
verses.1 Samuel|23|18: And they two made a covenant before the Lord: and David dwelt in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.
verses.1 Samuel|23|19: Then came up the Ziphim to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Is not David hiding himself with us in strongholds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the right hand of the Jeshimon?
verses.1 Samuel|23|20: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all thy heart's desire; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand.
verses.1 Samuel|23|21: And Saul said, Blessed are you of the Lord; for you have had compassion on me.
verses.1 Samuel|23|22: Go, I pray you, be more vigilant, and ascertain his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there: for it is told me that he acts with great cunning.
verses.1 Samuel|23|23: See therefore and take note of all the lurking places where he hides himself, and come back to me with the certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Judah.
verses.1 Samuel|23|24: And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the right hand of the Jeshimon.
verses.1 Samuel|23|25: Then Saul and his men went to seek him. And they told David: so that he came down into a rock, and dwelt in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.
verses.1 Samuel|23|26: And Saul went on his side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them.
verses.1 Samuel|23|27: But there came a messenger to Saul, saying, Make haste, and come; for the Philistines are raiding the land.
verses.1 Samuel|23|28: Wherefore Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth.
verses.1 Samuel|24|1: And David went up from there, and dwelt in strong holds at En-gedi.
verses.1 Samuel|24|2: And it came to pass when Saul was returned from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.
verses.1 Samuel|24|3: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.
verses.1 Samuel|24|4: And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to relieve himself: and David and his men remained in the back of the cave.
