verses.1 Samuel|24|5: And the men of David said to him, Behold the day of which the Lord said to thee, Behold, I will deliver thy enemy into thy hand, that thou mayst do to him as it shall seem good to thee. Then David arose, and secretly cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
verses.1 Samuel|24|6: And it came to pass afterwards, that David's heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul's robe.
verses.1 Samuel|24|7: And he said to his men, The Lord forbid that I should do this thing to my master, the Lord's anointed, to stretch forth my hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the Lord.
verses.1 Samuel|24|8: So David scolded his servants with these words, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. But Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
verses.1 Samuel|24|9: David also arose afterwards, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself.
verses.1 Samuel|24|10: And David said to Saul, Why dost thou listen to men's words, saying, Behold, David seeks thy hurt?
verses.1 Samuel|24|11: Behold, this day thy eyes have seen how the Lord had delivered thee to day into my hand in the cave: and some told me to kill thee: but my eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put out my hand against my lord; for he is the Lord's anointed.
verses.1 Samuel|24|12: Moreover, my father, see, indeed, see the corner of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the corner of thy robe, and did not kill thee, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against thee; yet thou huntest my soul to take it.
verses.1 Samuel|24|13: The Lord judge between me and thee, and the Lord avenge me of thee; but my hand shall not be upon thee.
verses.1 Samuel|24|14: As the proverb of the ancients says, Wickedness proceeds from the wicked: but my hand shall not be upon thee.
verses.1 Samuel|24|15: After whom is the king of Israel come out? after whom dost thou pursue? after a dead dog, after a single flea.
verses.1 Samuel|24|16: The Lord therefore be judge, and judge between me and thee, and let him see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of thy hand.
verses.1 Samuel|24|17: And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.
verses.1 Samuel|24|18: And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rendered me good, whereas I have rendered thee evil.
verses.1 Samuel|24|19: And thou hast declared this day how thou hast dealt well with me: seeing that when the Lord had delivered me into thy hand, thou didst not kill me.
verses.1 Samuel|24|20: For if a man finds his enemy, does he let him go away safe? so may the Lord reward thee good for what thou hast done to me this day.
verses.1 Samuel|24|21: And now, behold, I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thy hand.
verses.1 Samuel|24|22: Swear now therefore to me by the Lord, that thou wilt not cut off my seed after me, and that thou wilt not destroy my name out of my father's house.
verses.1 Samuel|24|23: And David swore to Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men went up to the fortress.
verses.1 Samuel|25|1: Now Samuel died; and all Israel were gathered together to mourn him, and they buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
verses.1 Samuel|25|2: And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in the Carmel; and the man was very wealthy, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in the Carmel.
verses.1 Samuel|25|3: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and fair of form: but the man was hardhearted and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
verses.1 Samuel|25|4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
verses.1 Samuel|25|5: And David sent out ten young men, and David said to the young men, Go up to the Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:
verses.1 Samuel|25|6: and thus shall you say to him, A hearty greeting! Peace be both to thee, and peace to thy house, and peace to all that thou hast.
verses.1 Samuel|25|7: And now I have heard that thou hast shearers: now thy shepherds who were with us, we hurt them not, neither was there anything of theirs missing, all the while they were on the Carmel.
verses.1 Samuel|25|8: Ask thy young men, and they will tell thee. Therefore, let the young men find favour in thy eyes: for we come on a festive occasion: give, I pray thee, to my servants and to David thy son, whatever thy generosity prompts thee.
verses.1 Samuel|25|9: And when David's young men came, they spoke to Nabal according to all those words in the name of David, and waited.
verses.1 Samuel|25|10: And Nabal answered David's servants, and said, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there are many servants nowadays that break away every man from his master.
verses.1 Samuel|25|11: Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and the fresh meat that I have killed for my shearers, and give it to men from I know not where?
verses.1 Samuel|25|12: So David's young men turned their way, and went back, and came and told him according to all those sayings.
verses.1 Samuel|25|13: And David said to his men, Let every man gird his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred remained with the baggage.
verses.1 Samuel|25|14: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to greet our master; and he railed at them.
verses.1 Samuel|25|15: But the men were very good to us, and we were not insulted nor did we miss any thing, all the time we went about with them, when we were in the fields:
verses.1 Samuel|25|16: they were a wall to us both by night and day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.
verses.1 Samuel|25|17: Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he is such a base fellow, that no man can speak to him.
verses.1 Samuel|25|18: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready prepared, and five measures of parched corn, and a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
verses.1 Samuel|25|19: And she said to her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.
verses.1 Samuel|25|20: And it was so, as she rode on the ass, that she came down by the covert of the hill, and, behold, David and his men came down against her; and she met them.
verses.1 Samuel|25|21: Now David was saying, Surely in vain have I guarded all that this fellow has in the wilderness, so that nothing of his possessions was missing: and he has rendered me evil for good.
verses.1 Samuel|25|22: So and more also do God to the enemies of David, if I leave alive of all his people by the morning light so much as a single man.
verses.1 Samuel|25|23: And when Abigail saw David, she hastened, and descended from the ass, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,
verses.1 Samuel|25|24: and fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be: and let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thy ears, and hear the words of thy handmaid.
verses.1 Samuel|25|25: Let not my lord, I pray thee, take heed of this worthless fellow, Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I thy handmaid did not see the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.
verses.1 Samuel|25|26: Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord lives, and as thy soul lives, seeing the Lord has prevented thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thy own hand, now let thy enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
verses.1 Samuel|25|27: And now this blessing which thy handmaid has brought to my lord, let it be given to the young men that follow my lord.
verses.1 Samuel|25|28: I pray thee, forgive the trespass of thy handmaid: for the Lord will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fights the battles of the Lord, and evil has not been found in thee all thy days.
verses.1 Samuel|25|29: Though a man rises to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul: yet the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bond of life with the Lord thy God; and the souls of thy enemies, them shall he sling out, as out of the hollow of a sling.
verses.1 Samuel|25|30: And it shall come to pass, when the Lord shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel;
verses.1 Samuel|25|31: that this shall not be a cause of stumbling to thee, nor offence of heart to my lord, that thou hast shed blood causelessly, or that my lord has avenged himself: and the Lord shall deal well with my lord, and thou shalt remember thy handmaid.
verses.1 Samuel|25|32: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who sent thee this day to meet me:
verses.1 Samuel|25|33: and blessed be thy discretion, and blessed be thou who hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with my own hand.
verses.1 Samuel|25|34: For in very deed, as the Lord God of Israel lives, who has kept me back from hurting thee, if thou hadst not hastened and come to meet me, surely there had not been left to Nabal by the morning light so much as a single man!
verses.1 Samuel|25|35: So David received of her hand that which she had brought him, and said to her, Go up in peace to thy house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have granted thy request.
verses.1 Samuel|25|36: And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal's heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk: and so she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.
verses.1 Samuel|25|37: But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
verses.1 Samuel|25|38: And it came to pass about ten days after, that the Lord smote Nabal, and he died.
verses.1 Samuel|25|39: And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be the Lord, that has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept his servant from evil: for the Lord has requited the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and spoke with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.
verses.1 Samuel|25|40: And when the servants of David were come to Abigail to the Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, David sent us to thee, to take thee to him to wife.
verses.1 Samuel|25|41: And she arose, and bowed herself on her face to the earth, and said, Behold, let thy handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.
verses.1 Samuel|25|42: And Abigail hastened, and arose, and rode upon an ass, with five girls of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
verses.1 Samuel|25|43: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they were also both of them his wives.
verses.1 Samuel|25|44: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti, the son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
verses.1 Samuel|26|1: And the Ziphim came to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Does not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the Jeshimon?
verses.1 Samuel|26|2: Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.1 Samuel|26|3: And Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the Jeshimon, by the way. But David abode in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
verses.1 Samuel|26|4: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come for a fact.
verses.1 Samuel|26|5: And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had encamped: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, together with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay within the barricade, and the people were encamped round about him.
verses.1 Samuel|26|6: Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with thee.
verses.1 Samuel|26|7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the barricade and his spear stuck in the ground at his head: and Abner and the people lay round about him.
verses.1 Samuel|26|8: Then said Abishai to David, God has delivered thy enemy into thy hand this day: now therefore let me strike him through with the spear to the earth at one blow, and I will not need to strike him a second time.
verses.1 Samuel|26|9: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch out his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless?
verses.1 Samuel|26|10: And David said, As the Lord lives, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and be swept away.
verses.1 Samuel|26|11: The Lord forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the Lord's anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his head, and the jar of water, and let us go.
verses.1 Samuel|26|12: So David took the spear and the jar of water from Saul's head; and they went away, and no man saw it, or knew it, or awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.
verses.1 Samuel|26|13: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of the hill afar off; a great space being between them:
verses.1 Samuel|26|14: and David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Wilt thou not answer, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who art thou that criest to the king?
verses.1 Samuel|26|15: And David said to Abner, Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? why then hast thou not guarded thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.
verses.1 Samuel|26|16: This thing is not good that thou hast done. As the Lord lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not kept your master, the Lord's anointed. And now see where the king's spear is, and the jar of water that was at his head.
verses.1 Samuel|26|17: And Saul knew David's voice, and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, O my lord, the king.
verses.1 Samuel|26|18: And he said, Why does my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in my hand?
verses.1 Samuel|26|19: Now therefore I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the Lord has stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the Lord; for they have driven me out this day from being joined to the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.
verses.1 Samuel|26|20: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a single flea, as when one hunts the partridge in the mountains.
verses.1 Samuel|26|21: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my life was precious in thy eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
verses.1 Samuel|26|22: And David answered and said, Behold the king's spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.
verses.1 Samuel|26|23: And the Lord requite to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the Lord delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch out my hand against the Lord's anointed.
verses.1 Samuel|26|24: And, behold, as thy life was much esteemed this day in my eyes, so let my life be much esteemed in the eyes of the Lord, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.
verses.1 Samuel|26|25: Then Saul said to David, Blessed be thou, my son David: thou shalt both do great things, and also shalt still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
verses.1 Samuel|27|1: And David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul; there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in the whole territory of Israel: so shall I escape out of his hand.
verses.1 Samuel|27|2: And David arose, and he passed over with the six hundred men that were with him to Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
verses.1 Samuel|27|3: And David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelite, Nabal's wife.
verses.1 Samuel|27|4: And it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him.
verses.1 Samuel|27|5: And David said to Achish, If I have now found favour in thy eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee?
verses.1 Samuel|27|6: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: therefore Ziklag belongs to the king of Judah to this day.
verses.1 Samuel|27|7: And the time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.
verses.1 Samuel|27|8: And David and his men went up, and raided the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekite: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, in the direction of Shur, as far as the land of Egypt.
verses.1 Samuel|27|9: And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel, and returned, and came to Achish.
verses.1 Samuel|27|10: When Achish said, Where did you make a raid today? David would say, Against the south of Judah, or against the south of the Jerahmeelites, or against the south of the Kenites.
verses.1 Samuel|27|11: And David saved neither man or woman alive, to bring tidings to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us, saying, Thus did David, and this was his practice all the time he dwelt in the country of the Philistines.
verses.1 Samuel|27|12: And Achish believed David, saying, He has made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever.
verses.1 Samuel|28|1: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said to David, Thou must know, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men.
verses.1 Samuel|28|2: And David said to Achish, Surely thou shall get to know what thy servant will do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee my bodyguard for ever.
verses.1 Samuel|28|3: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned him, and buried him in Ramah in his own city. And Saul had put away the mediums and the wizards, out of the land.
verses.1 Samuel|28|4: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched on the Gilboa.
verses.1 Samuel|28|5: And when Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.
verses.1 Samuel|28|6: And when Saul inquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by the Urim, nor by prophets.
verses.1 Samuel|28|7: Then said Saul to his servants, Seek me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her, and inquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a medium at En-dor.
verses.1 Samuel|28|8: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other clothes, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine for me by means of the familiar spirit, and bring him up for me, whom I shall name to thee.
verses.1 Samuel|28|9: And the woman said to him, Behold, thou knowst what Saul has done, how he has cut off the diviners, and the wizards, out of the land: why then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
verses.1 Samuel|28|10: And Saul swore to her by the Lord, saying, As the Lord lives, no punishment shall befall thee for this thing.
verses.1 Samuel|28|11: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up to thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.
verses.1 Samuel|28|12: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spoke to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|28|13: And the king said to her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said to Saul, I saw a godlike man ascending out of the earth.
verses.1 Samuel|28|14: And he said to her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man comes up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.
verses.1 Samuel|28|15: And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am greatly distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God has departed from me, and answers me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayst make known to me what I shall do.
verses.1 Samuel|28|16: Then said Samuel, Why then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord has departed from thee, and is become thy enemy?
verses.1 Samuel|28|17: And the Lord has done for himself, as he spoke by me: for the Lord has rent the kingdom out of thy hand, and given it to thy neighbour, to David:
verses.1 Samuel|28|18: because thou wouldst not obey the voice of the Lord nor wouldst execute his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore has the Lord done this thing to thee this day.
verses.1 Samuel|28|19: Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the Lord also shall deliver the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
verses.1 Samuel|28|20: Then Saul quickly fell full-length onto the ground and was greatly afraid at the words of Samuel; nor was there any strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all day and all night.
verses.1 Samuel|28|21: And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was much terrified, and she said to him, Behold, thy handmaid has obeyed thy voice, and I have taken my life in my hand, and have hearkened to thy words which thou didst speak to me.
verses.1 Samuel|28|22: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also to the voice of thy handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayst have strength, when thou goest on thy way.
verses.1 Samuel|28|23: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened to their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.
verses.1 Samuel|28|24: And the woman had a fatted calf in the house; and she hastened, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread of it:
verses.1 Samuel|28|25: and she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.
verses.1 Samuel|29|1: Now the Philistines gathered together all their camps to Aphek: and Israel pitched by the spring which is in Jezreel.
verses.1 Samuel|29|2: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rear with Achish.
verses.1 Samuel|29|3: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What are these Hebrews doing here? And Achish said to the princes of the Philistines, Is not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who has been with me a year, or more, and I have found no fault in him since he came over to me to this day?
verses.1 Samuel|29|4: And the princes of the Philistines were angry with him; and the princes of the Philistines said to him, Make this fellow return, that he may go back to his place which thou hast appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for with what might he reconcile himself to his master? could it not be with the heads of these men?
verses.1 Samuel|29|5: Is not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
verses.1 Samuel|29|6: Then Achish called David, and said to him, Surely, as the Lord lives, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the camp is good in my sight: for I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming to me to this day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not.
verses.1 Samuel|29|7: And now return, and go in peace, that thou displease not the lords of the Philistines.
verses.1 Samuel|29|8: And David said to Achish, But what have I done? and what thou found in thy servant so long as I have been with thee to this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?
verses.1 Samuel|29|9: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou art good in my sight, as an angel of God: but the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.
verses.1 Samuel|29|10: And now rise up early in the morning with thy master's servants that are come with thee: and as soon as you are up early in the morning, and have light, depart.
verses.1 Samuel|29|11: So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.1 Samuel|30|1: And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekite had raided the south, and Ziklag, and had smitten Ziklag, and had burned it with fire;
verses.1 Samuel|30|2: and had taken the women captives, that were there both great and small: they slew not any, but carried them away, and went on their way.
verses.1 Samuel|30|3: So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.
verses.1 Samuel|30|4: Then David and the people that were with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
verses.1 Samuel|30|5: And David's two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.1 Samuel|30|6: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David fortified himself in the Lord his God.
verses.1 Samuel|30|7: And David said to Abiathar, the priest, Ahimelech's son, I pray thee, bring me here the efod. And Abiathar brought the efod of David.
verses.1 Samuel|30|8: And David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
verses.1 Samuel|30|9: So David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the wadi of Besor, where those stayed who were left behind.
verses.1 Samuel|30|10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred, who were too weak to go over the wadi of Besor, remained behind.
verses.1 Samuel|30|11: And they found a Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;
verses.1 Samuel|30|12: and they gave him a slice of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came back to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any water, three days and three nights.
verses.1 Samuel|30|13: And David said to him, To whom dost thou belong? and from where dost thou come? And he said, I am a young Egyptian man, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days ago I fell sick.
verses.1 Samuel|30|14: We made a raid upon the south of the Cherethites, and upon the territory of Judah, and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.
verses.1 Samuel|30|15: And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this troop? And he said, Swear to me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will bring thee down to this troop.
verses.1 Samuel|30|16: And when he had brought him down, behold, they were spread about over the whole area, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
verses.1 Samuel|30|17: And David smote them from the twilight to the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, except four hundred youngsters, who rode upon camels, and fled.
verses.1 Samuel|30|18: And David recovered all that Amalek had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
verses.1 Samuel|30|19: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any thing that they had taken to them: David recovered all.
verses.1 Samuel|30|20: And David took all the flocks and the cattle; they rode before that herd, and declared, This is David's plunder.
verses.1 Samuel|30|21: And David came to the two hundred men, who were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the wadi of Besor: and they went out to meet David, and to meet the people who were with him: and when David came near to the people, he greeted them.
verses.1 Samuel|30|22: Then answered all the bad and worthless men among the men who went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away, and depart.
verses.1 Samuel|30|23: Then said David, You shall not do so, my brothers, with that which the Lord has given us, who has preserved us, and delivered the troop that came against us into our hand.
verses.1 Samuel|30|24: For who will hearken to you in this matter? but as his part is that goes down to the battle, so shall his part be that remains by the baggage: they shall share alike:
verses.1 Samuel|30|25: and it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
verses.1 Samuel|30|26: And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the Lord;
verses.1 Samuel|30|27: to those who were in Beth-el, and to those who were in Ramoth of the south, and to those who were in Jattir,
verses.1 Samuel|30|28: and to those who were in Aroer, and to those who were in Siphmoth, and to those who were in Eshtemoa,
verses.1 Samuel|30|29: and to those who were in Rachal, and to those who were in the cities of the Jerahmeeli, and to those who were in the cities of the Kenites,
verses.1 Samuel|30|30: and to those who were in Hormah, and to those who were in Chor-ashan, and to those who were in Athach,
verses.1 Samuel|30|31: and to those who were in Hebron, and to all the places where David and his men had wandered about.
verses.1 Samuel|31|1: Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.
verses.1 Samuel|31|2: And the Philistines followed closely upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
verses.1 Samuel|31|3: And the battle went hard against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was greatly in dread of the archers.
verses.1 Samuel|31|4: Then Saul said to his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and pierce me with it; lest these uncircumcised come and pierce me, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was very much afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell on it.
verses.1 Samuel|31|5: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise on his sword, and died with him.
verses.1 Samuel|31|6: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.
verses.1 Samuel|31|7: And when the men of Israel that were on the other side of the valley, and they that were on the other side of the Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
verses.1 Samuel|31|8: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on mount Gilboa.
verses.1 Samuel|31|9: And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols, and among the people.
verses.1 Samuel|31|10: And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
verses.1 Samuel|31|11: And when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul;
verses.1 Samuel|31|12: all the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.
verses.1 Samuel|31|13: And they took their bones, and buried them under a tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
verses.2 Samuel|1|1: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of Amalek, and David had remained two days in Ziklag;
verses.2 Samuel|1|2: it came to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and bowed down.
verses.2 Samuel|1|3: And David said to him, From where dost thou come? And he said to him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
verses.2 Samuel|1|4: And David said to him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
verses.2 Samuel|1|5: And David said to the young man that told him, How dost thou know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?
verses.2 Samuel|1|6: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear: and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
verses.2 Samuel|1|7: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, Here I am.
verses.2 Samuel|1|8: And he said to me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
verses.2 Samuel|1|9: He said to me again, Stand, I pray thee, beside me, and slay me: for the agony has seized me, and yet I still have life in me.
verses.2 Samuel|1|10: So I stood beside him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.
verses.2 Samuel|1|11: Then David took hold of his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
verses.2 Samuel|1|12: and they mourned, and wept, and fasted until evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the Lord, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.
verses.2 Samuel|1|13: And David said to the lad that told him, From where art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
verses.2 Samuel|1|14: And David said to him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch out thy hand to destroy the Lord's anointed?
verses.2 Samuel|1|15: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
verses.2 Samuel|1|16: And David said to him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth has testified against thee, saying, I have slain the Lord's anointed.
verses.2 Samuel|1|17: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
verses.2 Samuel|1|18: and he said: (To teach the children of Judah the use of the bow; behold, it is written in the book, Jasher.)
verses.2 Samuel|1|19: The beauty, O Israel, is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
verses.2 Samuel|1|20: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
verses.2 Samuel|1|21: Mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though not anointed with oil.
verses.2 Samuel|1|22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
verses.2 Samuel|1|23: Saul and Jonathan were loved and dear in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
verses.2 Samuel|1|24: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
verses.2 Samuel|1|25: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, slain on thy high places.
verses.2 Samuel|1|26: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very dear hast thou been to me: thy love to me was wonderful, more than the love of women.
verses.2 Samuel|1|27: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war cast away.
verses.2 Samuel|2|1: And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Hebron.
verses.2 Samuel|2|2: So David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail, Nabal's wife, the Carmelite.
verses.2 Samuel|2|3: And David brought up his men that were with him, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
verses.2 Samuel|2|4: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, That the men of Jabesh-gilead were they that buried Saul.
verses.2 Samuel|2|5: And David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said to them, Blessed are you of the Lord, that you have shown this loyal love to your lord, to Saul, and have buried him.
verses.2 Samuel|2|6: And now may the Lord do lovingkindness and truth to you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because you have done this thing.
verses.2 Samuel|2|7: Therefore now let your hands be strong, and be valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
verses.2 Samuel|2|8: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
verses.2 Samuel|2|9: and made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.2 Samuel|2|10: Ish-bosheth Saul's son was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
verses.2 Samuel|2|11: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
verses.2 Samuel|2|12: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.2 Samuel|2|13: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and they met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
verses.2 Samuel|2|14: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
verses.2 Samuel|2|15: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, belonging to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
verses.2 Samuel|2|16: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow's side; so they fell down together: so that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
verses.2 Samuel|2|17: And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
verses.2 Samuel|2|18: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild gazelle.
verses.2 Samuel|2|19: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
verses.2 Samuel|2|20: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Art thou Asahel? And he answered, I am.
verses.2 Samuel|2|21: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
verses.2 Samuel|2|22: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn aside from following me: why should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
verses.2 Samuel|2|23: But he refused to turn aside: so Abner smote him in the belly with the butt end of the spear, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that all those who came to the place where Asahel fell down and died, stood still.
verses.2 Samuel|2|24: Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lies before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.2 Samuel|2|25: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of a hill.
verses.2 Samuel|2|26: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, till thou bid the people return from following their brethren?
verses.2 Samuel|2|27: And Joab said, As God lives, if thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people would have gone up every one from following his brother.
verses.2 Samuel|2|28: So Joab blew the shofar, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
verses.2 Samuel|2|29: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over the Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
verses.2 Samuel|2|30: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there were nineteen of David's servants missing, and Asahel.
verses.2 Samuel|2|31: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, three hundred and sixty men, and they died.
verses.2 Samuel|2|32: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men marched all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.
verses.2 Samuel|3|1: Now there was a long warfare between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David became stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul became weaker and weaker.
verses.2 Samuel|3|2: And to David sons were born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
verses.2 Samuel|3|3: and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
verses.2 Samuel|3|4: and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
verses.2 Samuel|3|5: and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.2 Samuel|3|6: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong among the house of Saul.
verses.2 Samuel|3|7: And Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Why hast thou gone in to my father's concubine?
verses.2 Samuel|3|8: Then was Abner very angry over the words of Ish-bosheth, and said, Am I a dog's head, of Judah? I show kindness this day to the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, by not delivering thee into the hand of David, nevertheless thou chargest me today with a fault concerning this woman.
verses.2 Samuel|3|9: So do God to Abner, and more also, unless I do for David as the Lord has sworn to David;
verses.2 Samuel|3|10: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beer-sheba.
verses.2 Samuel|3|11: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.
verses.2 Samuel|3|12: And Abner sent messengers to David from his place, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring all Israel round to thee.
verses.2 Samuel|3|13: And he said, It is well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
verses.2 Samuel|3|14: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth Saul's son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
verses.2 Samuel|3|15: And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, from Paltiel, the son of Laish.
verses.2 Samuel|3|16: And her husband went along with her weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner to him, Go, return. And he returned.
verses.2 Samuel|3|17: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel saying, You sought for David in times past to be king over you:
verses.2 Samuel|3|18: now then do it: for the Lord has spoken concerning David, saying, It shall be in the hand of my servant David to save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
verses.2 Samuel|3|19: And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and to the whole house of Benjamin.
verses.2 Samuel|3|20: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.
verses.2 Samuel|3|21: And Abner said to David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with thee, and that thou mayst reign over all that thy heart desires. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.
verses.2 Samuel|3|22: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from pursuing a troop, and brought in a great plunder with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.
verses.2 Samuel|3|23: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he has sent him away, and he is gone in peace.
verses.2 Samuel|3|24: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came to thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
verses.2 Samuel|3|25: Thou knowst Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.
verses.2 Samuel|3|26: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
verses.2 Samuel|3|27: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there in the belly, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
verses.2 Samuel|3|28: And afterwards when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before the Lord for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:
verses.2 Samuel|3|29: let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father's house; and let the house of Joab never lack such as are afflicted with an issue, or with zaraat, or that go on crutches, or fall by the sword, or lack bread.
verses.2 Samuel|3|30: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
verses.2 Samuel|3|31: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David himself followed the bier.
verses.2 Samuel|3|32: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
verses.2 Samuel|3|33: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Should Abner die as a churl dies.
verses.2 Samuel|3|34: Thy hands were not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: as a man falls before the wicked thou didst fall. And all the people wept again over him.
verses.2 Samuel|3|35: And all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was yet day, but David swore, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or anything else, till the sun be down.
verses.2 Samuel|3|36: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them: as whatever the king did pleased all the people.
verses.2 Samuel|3|37: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that the slaying of Abner the son of Ner did not come from the king.
verses.2 Samuel|3|38: And the king said to his servants, Know you not that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel.
verses.2 Samuel|3|39: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me: the Lord shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.
verses.2 Samuel|4|1: And when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all Israel were terrified.
verses.2 Samuel|4|2: And Saul's son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin:
verses.2 Samuel|4|3: and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)
verses.2 Samuel|4|4: And Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son whose feet were lame. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
verses.2 Samuel|4|5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, who was lying down for his midday rest.
verses.2 Samuel|4|6: And they came into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him in the belly: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
verses.2 Samuel|4|7: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and went away through the Arabah all night.
verses.2 Samuel|4|8: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul thy enemy, who sought thy life; and the Lord has avenged my lord the king this day of Saul and of his seed.
verses.2 Samuel|4|9: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
verses.2 Samuel|4|10: when one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his tidings:
verses.2 Samuel|4|11: how much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
verses.2 Samuel|4|12: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried it in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.
verses.2 Samuel|5|1: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David to Hebron, and spoke, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.
verses.2 Samuel|5|2: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that didst lead Israel out and didst bring them back; and the Lord said to thee, Thou shalt be a shepherd for my people Israel, and thou shalt be a prince over Israel.
verses.2 Samuel|5|3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord: and they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.2 Samuel|5|4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
verses.2 Samuel|5|5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.2 Samuel|5|6: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem to the Jebusite, the inhabitants of the land: who spoke to David, saying, Unless thou remove even the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in here: thinking, David cannot come in here.
verses.2 Samuel|5|7: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion: that is the city of David.
verses.2 Samuel|5|8: And David said on that day, Whoever smites the Jebusite, and gets up to the aqueduct, and smites the lame and the blind (that are hated of David's soul) – therefore the saying, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.
verses.2 Samuel|5|9: So David dwelt in the stronghold and called it the city of David. And David built round about from the Millo and inward.
verses.2 Samuel|5|10: And David went on, and grew great, and the Lord God of hosts was with him.
verses.2 Samuel|5|11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David a house.
verses.2 Samuel|5|12: And David perceived that the Lord had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel's sake.
verses.2 Samuel|5|13: And David took more concubines and wives of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron: and more sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.2 Samuel|5|14: And these are the names of those that were born to him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan and Solomon,
verses.2 Samuel|5|15: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
verses.2 Samuel|5|16: and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
verses.2 Samuel|5|17: But when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines came up to seek David, and David heard of it, and went down to the stronghold.
verses.2 Samuel|5|18: And the Philistines came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.2 Samuel|5|19: And David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt Thou deliver them into my hand? And the Lord said to David, Go up: for I will surely deliver the Philistines into thy hand.
verses.2 Samuel|5|20: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there, and said, The Lord has broken down my enemies before me, like the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
verses.2 Samuel|5|21: And there they left their images, and David and his men burned them.
verses.2 Samuel|5|22: And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.2 Samuel|5|23: And when David inquired of the Lord, he said, Thou shalt not go up; but make a circuit behind them, and come upon them over against the bakha trees.
verses.2 Samuel|5|24: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the bakha trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the camp of the Philistines.
verses.2 Samuel|5|25: And David did so, as the Lord had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until the approaches of Gezer.
verses.2 Samuel|6|1: Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.2 Samuel|6|2: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him from Baale-jehuda, to bring up from there the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the Lord of hosts who dwells upon the keruvim.
verses.2 Samuel|6|3: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab who was in Gibeah: and Uzza and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.
verses.2 Samuel|6|4: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which was at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
verses.2 Samuel|6|5: And David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on all manner of instruments made of cypress wood, on lyres, and on lutes, and on timbrels, and on rattles, and on cymbals.
verses.2 Samuel|6|6: And when they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, Uzza put out his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it.
verses.2 Samuel|6|7: And the anger of the Lord burned against Uzza; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
verses.2 Samuel|6|8: And David was displeased, because the Lord had burst out against Uzza: and he called the name of the place Perez-uzza to this day.
verses.2 Samuel|6|9: And David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?
verses.2 Samuel|6|10: So David would not remove the ark of the Lord to him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.2 Samuel|6|11: And the ark of the Lord continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the Lord blessed Obed-edom, and all his household.
verses.2 Samuel|6|12: And it was told king David, saying, The Lord has blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that he has, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.
verses.2 Samuel|6|13: And when they that bore the ark of the Lord had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
verses.2 Samuel|6|14: And David leaped about before the Lord with all his might; and David was girded with a linen efod.
verses.2 Samuel|6|15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting, and with the sound of the shofar.
verses.2 Samuel|6|16: And as the ark of the Lord came into the city of David, Michal, Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David dancing and leaping before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart.
verses.2 Samuel|6|17: And they brought in the ark of the Lord, and set it in its place, in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
verses.2 Samuel|6|18: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.
verses.2 Samuel|6|19: And he made a distribution among all the people, among the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, to everyone a cake of bread, and a good piece of meat, and a cake of raisins. So all the people departed everyone to his house.
verses.2 Samuel|6|20: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel today, in that he uncovered himself today in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the low fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!
verses.2 Samuel|6|21: And David said to Michal, It was before the Lord, who chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of the Lord, over Israel. Therefore will I play before the Lord,
verses.2 Samuel|6|22: and I will yet be more lightly esteemed than this, holding myself lowly: and of the maidservants of whom thou hast spoken, of them shall I be had in honour.
verses.2 Samuel|6|23: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.
verses.2 Samuel|7|1: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the Lord had given him rest round about from all his enemies;
verses.2 Samuel|7|2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within curtain.
verses.2 Samuel|7|3: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thy heart; for the Lord is with thee.
verses.2 Samuel|7|4: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
verses.2 Samuel|7|5: Go and tell my servant David, Thus says the Lord, shalt thou build me a house for me to dwell in?
verses.2 Samuel|7|6: For I have not dwelt in any house since that time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but I have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.
verses.2 Samuel|7|7: In all the places where I have walked with all the children of Israel, did I speak a word with any of the rulers of Israel, whom I commanded as shepherds of my people Israel, saying, Why do you not build me a house of cedar?
verses.2 Samuel|7|8: Now therefore so shalt thou say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord of hosts, I took thee from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
verses.2 Samuel|7|9: and I was with thee wherever thou didst go, and have cut off all thy enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like the name of the great men that are on the earth.
verses.2 Samuel|7|10: Moreover I have appointed a place for my people Israel, and planted them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and be troubled no more; neither shall the children of wickedness torment them any more, as at the beginning,
verses.2 Samuel|7|11: and as since the time that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel; but I will give thee rest from all thy enemies, and the Lord tells thee that he will make thee a house.
verses.2 Samuel|7|12: And when the days are fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, who shall issue from thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.2 Samuel|7|13: He shall build a house for my name, and I will make firm the throne of his kingdom for ever.
verses.2 Samuel|7|14: I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with such plagues as befall the sons of Adam:
verses.2 Samuel|7|15: but my covenant love shall not depart away from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before thee.
verses.2 Samuel|7|16: And thy house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be firm for ever.
verses.2 Samuel|7|17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David.
verses.2 Samuel|7|18: Then king David went in, and sat before the Lord, and he said, Who am I, O Lord God? and what is my house, that Thou hast brought me thus far?
verses.2 Samuel|7|19: And this was yet a small thing in Thy sight, O Lord God; but Thou hast also spoken of Thy servant's house continuing for a great while to come. And does any man deserve such a course, O Lord God!
verses.2 Samuel|7|20: And what can David say more to Thee? for Thou, Lord God, knowst Thy servant.
verses.2 Samuel|7|21: For Thy word's sake, and according to Thy own heart, hast Thou done all these great things, to make Thy servant know them.
verses.2 Samuel|7|22: Therefore Thou art great, O Lord God: for there is none like Thee, neither is there any god besides Thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.2 Samuel|7|23: And what one nation in the earth is like Thy people, like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make himself a name, and to do like the great things and terrible which Thou didst for Thy land, by driving out from before Thy people, whom Thou didst redeem to Thee from Egypt, the nations and their gods?
verses.2 Samuel|7|24: For Thou hast confirmed to Thyself Thy people Israel to be a people to Thee for ever: and Thou, Lord, art become their God.
verses.2 Samuel|7|25: And now, O Lord God, the word that Thou hast spoken concerning Thy servant, and concerning his house, establish it for ever, and do as Thou hast said,
verses.2 Samuel|7|26: And let Thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The Lord of hosts is the God over Israel: and let the house of Thy servant David be established before Thee.
verses.2 Samuel|7|27: For Thou, O Lord of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to Thy servant, saying, I will build thee a house: therefore has Thy servant found it in his heart to pray this prayer to Thee.
verses.2 Samuel|7|28: And now, O Lord God, Thou art the God, and let Thy words come true, as Thou hast promised this goodness to Thy servant:
verses.2 Samuel|7|29: therefore now let it please Thee to bless the house of Thy servant, that it may continue for ever before Thee: for Thou, O Lord God, hast spoken it: and with Thy blessing let the house of Thy servant be blessed for ever.
verses.2 Samuel|8|1: And after that it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
verses.2 Samuel|8|2: And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so Moab became David's servants, and brought tribute.
verses.2 Samuel|8|3: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to extend his dominion at the river Euphrates.
verses.2 Samuel|8|4: And David took from him one thousand, seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David lamed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them enough for a hundred chariots.
verses.2 Samuel|8|5: And when Syria of Damascus came to the help of Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of Syria twenty two thousand men.
verses.2 Samuel|8|6: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and Syria became servants to David, and brought tribute. And the Lord gave victory to David wherever he went.
verses.2 Samuel|8|7: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.2 Samuel|8|8: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took very much brass.
verses.2 Samuel|8|9: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the army of Hadadezer,
verses.2 Samuel|8|10: then Toi sent Joram his son to king David, to greet him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
verses.2 Samuel|8|11: which also king David did dedicate to the Lord, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all the nations which he had conquered;
verses.2 Samuel|8|12: from Syria, and Moab, and the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.2 Samuel|8|13: And David got him a name when he returned from smiting Syria in the valley of salt, eighteen thousand men.
verses.2 Samuel|8|14: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he put garrisons, and all Edom became David's servants. And the Lord gave David victory wherever he went.
verses.2 Samuel|8|15: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice to all his people.
verses.2 Samuel|8|16: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
verses.2 Samuel|8|17: and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe;
verses.2 Samuel|8|18: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and the sons of David were ministers of state.
verses.2 Samuel|9|1: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul; that I may show him loyal love for Jonathan's sake?
verses.2 Samuel|9|2: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him to David, the king said to him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
verses.2 Samuel|9|3: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul that I may show the love of God to him? And Ziba said to the king, Jonathan has yet a son, who is lame on his feet.
verses.2 Samuel|9|4: And the king said to him, Where is he? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
verses.2 Samuel|9|5: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
verses.2 Samuel|9|6: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come to David, he fell on his face, and bowed down to the ground. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!
verses.2 Samuel|9|7: And David said to him, Fear not: for I will surely show thee loyal love for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
verses.2 Samuel|9|8: And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldst look upon such a dead dog as I am?
verses.2 Samuel|9|9: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, I have given to thy master's son all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.
verses.2 Samuel|9|10: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the produce, that thy master's son may have food to eat: though Mephibosheth thy master's son shall eat bread always at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.2 Samuel|9|11: Then said Ziba to the king, According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king's sons.
verses.2 Samuel|9|12: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
verses.2 Samuel|9|13: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king's table; and was lame in both his feet.
verses.2 Samuel|10|1: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Samuel|10|2: Then said David, I will show loyal love to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed love to me. And David sent to comfort him for his father's death by the hand of his servants. And David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
verses.2 Samuel|10|3: And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David honours thy father, that he has sent comforters to thee? has not David rather sent his servants to thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?
verses.2 Samuel|10|4: So Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, to their buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.2 Samuel|10|5: When they told it to David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Remain at Jericho until your beards are grown, and then return.
verses.2 Samuel|10|6: And when the children of Ammon saw that they had become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired Syria of Beth-rehob, and Syria of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maachah a thousand men, and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.
verses.2 Samuel|10|7: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the warriors.
verses.2 Samuel|10|8: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and Syria of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ish-tob, and Maachah were by themselves in the open country.
verses.2 Samuel|10|9: When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against Syria:
verses.2 Samuel|10|10: and the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put them in array against the children of Ammon.
verses.2 Samuel|10|11: And he said, If Syria proves too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon are too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
verses.2 Samuel|10|12: Be of good courage, and let us be strong for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the Lord do that which seems good in his eyes.
verses.2 Samuel|10|13: And Joab drew near, and the people that were with him, to the battle against Syria: and they fled before him.
verses.2 Samuel|10|14: And when the children of Ammon saw that Syria were fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
verses.2 Samuel|10|15: And when Syria saw that they were beaten before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
verses.2 Samuel|10|16: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out those of Syria that were beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.
verses.2 Samuel|10|17: And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. And Syria set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
verses.2 Samuel|10|18: And Syria fled before Israel; and David slew the men of seven hundred chariots of Syria, and forty thousand horse-men, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.
verses.2 Samuel|10|19: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were beaten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So Syria feared to help the children of Ammon any more.
verses.2 Samuel|11|1: And it came to pass, at the return of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel, and they ravaged the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
verses.2 Samuel|11|2: And it came to pass one evening, that David arose from his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman bathing; and the woman was very fair to look upon.
verses.2 Samuel|11|3: And David sent and inquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
verses.2 Samuel|11|4: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her; for she had purified herself from her uncleanness, and then she returned to her house.
verses.2 Samuel|11|5: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
verses.2 Samuel|11|6: And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.2 Samuel|11|7: And when Uriah was come to him, David asked how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
verses.2 Samuel|11|8: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king's house, and there followed him a portion of food from the king.
verses.2 Samuel|11|9: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
verses.2 Samuel|11|10: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down to his house, David said to Uriah, Didst thou not come from a journey? why then didst thou not go down to thy house?
verses.2 Samuel|11|11: And Uriah said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, dwell in booths; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul lives, I will not do this thing.
verses.2 Samuel|11|12: And David said to Uriah, Remain here today also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
verses.2 Samuel|11|13: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
verses.2 Samuel|11|14: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.2 Samuel|11|15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and withdraw from him, so that he may be hit, and die.
verses.2 Samuel|11|16: And it came to pass, when Joab besieged the city, that he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew that fighting men were.
verses.2 Samuel|11|17: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and some of the people of the servants of David fell; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
verses.2 Samuel|11|18: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
verses.2 Samuel|11|19: and charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war to the king,
verses.2 Samuel|11|20: and if so be that the king's anger be roused, and he say to thee, Why did you approach so near to the city when you did fight? knew you not that they would shoot from the wall?
verses.2 Samuel|11|21: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast an upper millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why did you go so near the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
verses.2 Samuel|11|22: So the messenger went, and came and told David all that Joab had sent him for.
verses.2 Samuel|11|23: And the messenger said to David, Indeed, the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were engaged with them right up to the entrance of the gate.
verses.2 Samuel|11|24: And the shooters shot from the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king's servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
verses.2 Samuel|11|25: Then David said to the messenger, Thus shalt thou say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devours one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
verses.2 Samuel|11|26: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
verses.2 Samuel|11|27: And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.2 Samuel|12|1: And the Lord sent Nathan to David. And he came to him, and said to him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
verses.2 Samuel|12|2: The rich man had very many flocks and herds:
verses.2 Samuel|12|3: but the poor man had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and reared: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own bread, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.
verses.2 Samuel|12|4: And there came a traveller to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to prepare it for the wayfaring man that was come to him; but took the poor man's lamb, and prepared it for the man that was come to him.
verses.2 Samuel|12|5: And David's anger burned greatly against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the Lord lives, the man that has done this is worthy to die:
