verses.1 Kings|1|34: and let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel and blow with the trumpet, and say, Long live king Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|1|35: Then you shall come up after him, that he may come and sit upon my throne; for he shall be king in my stead: and I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.
verses.1 Kings|1|36: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, and said, Amen: so say the Lord God of my lord the king.
verses.1 Kings|1|37: As the Lord has been with my lord the king, even so let him be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.
verses.1 Kings|1|38: So Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, went down, and caused Solomon to ride on king David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.
verses.1 Kings|1|39: And Zadok the priest took a horn of oil out of the tent, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the shofar; and all the people said, Long live king Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|1|40: And all the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth was split with the sound of them.
verses.1 Kings|1|41: And Adonijah and all the guests that were with him heard it as they made an end of eating. And when Joab heard the sound of the shofar, he said, Why is the city in an uproar?
verses.1 Kings|1|42: And while he yet spoke, behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came: and Adonijah said to him, Come in; for thou art a valiant man, and bringest good tidings.
verses.1 Kings|1|43: And Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, Alas, but our lord king David has made Solomon king.
verses.1 Kings|1|44: And the king has sent with him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and they have caused him to ride upon the king's mule:
verses.1 Kings|1|45: and Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon: and they are come up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. This is the noise that you have heard.
verses.1 Kings|1|46: And also Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.
verses.1 Kings|1|47: And moreover the king's servants have come to bless our lord king David, saying, God make the name of Solomon better than thy name, and make his throne greater than thy throne. And the king did bow himself upon the bed.
verses.1 Kings|1|48: And also thus said the king, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has given one to sit on my throne this day, my own eyes seeing it.
verses.1 Kings|1|49: And all the guests that were with Adonijah trembled, and rose up, and went every man his way.
verses.1 Kings|1|50: And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold of the horns of the altar.
verses.1 Kings|1|51: And it was told Solomon saying, Behold, Adonijah fears king Solomon: for, lo, he has caught hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear to me to day that he will not slay his servant with the sword.
verses.1 Kings|1|52: And Solomon said, If he will show himself a worthy man, no hair of his shall fall to the earth: but if wickedness shall be found in him, he shall die.
verses.1 Kings|1|53: So king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself down to king Solomon: and Solomon said to him, Go to thy house.
verses.1 Kings|2|1: Now the days of David drew near that he should die; and he charged Solomon his son, saying,
verses.1 Kings|2|2: I go the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and show thyself a man;
verses.1 Kings|2|3: and keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayst prosper in all that thou doest, and wherever thou turnest thyself:
verses.1 Kings|2|4: that the Lord may continue his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.
verses.1 Kings|2|5: Moreover thou knowst also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, to Abner the son of Ner, and to Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
verses.1 Kings|2|6: Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to Sheol in peace.
verses.1 Kings|2|7: But show loyal love to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for they came to me when I fled from Absalom thy brother.
verses.1 Kings|2|8: And, behold, thou hast with thee Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite of Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I went to Mahanaim: but he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, I will not put thee to death with the sword.
verses.1 Kings|2|9: Now therefore hold him not guiltless: for thou art a wise man, and knowst what thou oughtest to do to him; but his hoar head bring thou down to Sheol with blood.
verses.1 Kings|2|10: So David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.
verses.1 Kings|2|11: And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years he reigned in Hebron, and thirty three years he reigned in Jerusalem.
verses.1 Kings|2|12: Then Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father; and his kingdom was firmly established.
verses.1 Kings|2|13: And Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bath-sheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.
verses.1 Kings|2|14: He said moreover, I have something to say to thee. And she said, Say on.
verses.1 Kings|2|15: And he said, Thou knowst that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: but the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother's: for it was his from the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|2|16: And now I ask one petition of thee, deny me not. And she said to him, Say on.
verses.1 Kings|2|17: And he said, Speak, I pray thee, to Solomon the king, (for he will not refuse thee,) that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to wife.
verses.1 Kings|2|18: And Bath-sheba said, Well; I will speak for thee to the king.
verses.1 Kings|2|19: Bath-sheba therefore went to king Solomon, to speak to him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself down to her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a seat to be set for the king's mother; and she sat on his right hand.
verses.1 Kings|2|20: Then she said, I desire one small petition of thee; do not deny me. And the king said to her, Ask on, my mother: for I will not deny thee.
verses.1 Kings|2|21: And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to wife.
verses.1 Kings|2|22: And king Solomon answered and said to his mother, And why dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is my elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.
verses.1 Kings|2|23: Then king Solomon swore by the Lord, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah have not spoken this word against his own life.
verses.1 Kings|2|24: Now therefore, as the Lord lives, who has established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house, as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day.
verses.1 Kings|2|25: And king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him that he died.
verses.1 Kings|2|26: And to Abiathar the priest the king said, Get thee to Anathoth, to thy own fields; for thou art worthy of death: but I will not at this time put thee to death, because thou didst bear the ark of the Lord God before David my father, and because thou hast been afflicted in all my father's afflictions.
verses.1 Kings|2|27: So Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest to the Lord; that he might fulfill the word of the Lord, which he spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
verses.1 Kings|2|28: Then tidings came to Joab; for Joab had inclined after Adonijah, though he had not inclined after Absalom. And Joab fled to the tent of the Lord, and caught hold of the horns of the altar.
verses.1 Kings|2|29: And it was told king Solomon, that Joab was fled to the tent of the Lord; and, behold, he was by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall upon him.
verses.1 Kings|2|30: And Benaiah came to the tent of the Lord, and said to him, Thus says the king, Come out. And he said, No; but I will die here. And Benaiah brought the king word back, saying, Thus said Joab, and thus he answered me.
verses.1 Kings|2|31: And the king said to him, Do as he has said, and fall upon him, and bury him; that thou mayst take away the innocent blood, which Joab shed, from me, and from the house of my father.
verses.1 Kings|2|32: And the Lord shall return his blood upon his own head, for he fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and slew them with the sword, my father David not knowing of it, namely, Abner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the host of Judah.
verses.1 Kings|2|33: Their blood shall therefore return upon the head of Joab, and upon the head of his seed for ever: but upon David, and upon his seed, and upon his house, and upon his throne, shall there be peace for ever from the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|2|34: So Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, and fell upon him, and slew him: and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
verses.1 Kings|2|35: And the king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in place of him over the host: and Zadok the priest did the king put in place of Abiathar.
verses.1 Kings|2|36: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, Build thee a house in Jerusalem, and dwell there, and do not go from there anywhere.
verses.1 Kings|2|37: For it shall be, that on the day thou goest out, and passest over the wadi of Kidron, thou shalt know for certain that thou shalt surely die: thy blood shall be upon thy own head.
verses.1 Kings|2|38: And Shimei said to the king, The saying is good: as my lord the king has said, so will thy servant do. And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.
verses.1 Kings|2|39: And it came to pass at the end of three years, that two of the servants of Shimei ran away to Achish son of Maachah king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, Behold, thy servants are in Gath.
verses.1 Kings|2|40: And Shimei arose, and saddled his ass, and went to Gath to Achish to seek his servants: and Shimei went, and brought his servants from Gath.
verses.1 Kings|2|41: And it was told Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and was returned.
verses.1 Kings|2|42: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, Did I not make thee to swear by the Lord, and did I not forewarn thee, saying, Know for certain, on the day thou goest out, and walkest abroad anywhere, that thou shalt surely die? and thou didst say to me, The word that I have heard is good.
verses.1 Kings|2|43: Why then hast thou not kept the oath of the Lord, and the commandment that I have charged thee with?
verses.1 Kings|2|44: And the king said to Shimei, Thou knowst all the wickedness which thy heart is privy to, that thou didst to David my father: therefore the Lord shall return thy wickedness upon thy own head;
verses.1 Kings|2|45: and king Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the Lord for ever.
verses.1 Kings|2|46: So the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; who went out, and fell upon him, that he died. And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|3|1: And Solomon became allied by marriage with Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh's daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem round about.
verses.1 Kings|3|2: Only the people sacrificed in high places, because there was no house built to the name of the Lord, until those days.
verses.1 Kings|3|3: And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father: only he sacrificed and burnt incense in high places.
verses.1 Kings|3|4: And the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar.
verses.1 Kings|3|5: In Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.
verses.1 Kings|3|6: And Solomon said, Thou hast shown great faithful love to Thy servant David my father, according as he walked before Thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with Thee; and Thou hast kept for him this great faithful love, that Thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
verses.1 Kings|3|7: And now, O Lord my God, Thou hast made Thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.
verses.1 Kings|3|8: And Thy servant is in the midst of Thy people which Thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered or counted for multitude.
verses.1 Kings|3|9: Give therefore Thy servant an understanding heart to judge Thy people, that I may discern between good and evil: for who is able to judge this Thy so great a people?
verses.1 Kings|3|10: And it pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.
verses.1 Kings|3|11: And God said to him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast thou asked the life of thy enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;
verses.1 Kings|3|12: behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there has been none like thee before thee, nor after thee shall any arise like thee.
verses.1 Kings|3|13: And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches and honour: so that there shall not be any among the kings like thee all thy days.
verses.1 Kings|3|14: And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days.
verses.1 Kings|3|15: And Solomon awoke; and, behold, it was a dream. And he came to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings, and offered peace offerings, and made a feast to all his servants.
verses.1 Kings|3|16: Then came there two women, that were harlots, to the king, and stood before him.
verses.1 Kings|3|17: And the one woman said, O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house.
verses.1 Kings|3|18: And it came to pass the third day after I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also: and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.
verses.1 Kings|3|19: And this woman's child died in the night; because she lay upon it.
verses.1 Kings|3|20: And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thy handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.
verses.1 Kings|3|21: And when I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold, it was dead: but when I had looked closely at it in the morning, behold, it was not my son, that I did bear.
verses.1 Kings|3|22: And the other woman said, No; but the living child is my son, and the dead one is thy son. And this said, No; but the dead one is thy son, and the living one is my son. Thus they spoke before the king.
verses.1 Kings|3|23: Then said the king, The one says, This is my son that lives, and thy son is the dead: and the other says, No: but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.
verses.1 Kings|3|24: And the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought a sword before the king.
verses.1 Kings|3|25: And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.
verses.1 Kings|3|26: Then spoke the woman whose child was the living one to the king, for her love was enkindled towards her son, and she said, O my lord, give her the living child, but do not slay it. But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.
verses.1 Kings|3|27: Then the king answered and said, Give her the living child, and do not slay it: she is its mother.
verses.1 Kings|3|28: And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment.
verses.1 Kings|4|1: So king Solomon was king over all Israel.
verses.1 Kings|4|2: And these were the princes whom he had; Azariah the son of Zadok the priest,
verses.1 Kings|4|3: Elihoreph and Ahiah the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder.
verses.1 Kings|4|4: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the host: and Zadok and Abiathar were priests:
verses.1 Kings|4|5: and Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers: and Zabud the son of Nathan was the king's private minister of state:
verses.1 Kings|4|6: and Ahishar was over the household: and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the tribute.
verses.1 Kings|4|7: And Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided stores for the king and his household: each man had to make provision for a month in the year.
verses.1 Kings|4|8: And these are their names: The son of Hur, in mount Ephraim:
verses.1 Kings|4|9: the son of Dekar, in Makaz, and in Shaalbim, and Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan:
verses.1 Kings|4|10: the son of Hesed, in Aruboth; to him were assigned Shocho, and all the land of Hepher:
verses.1 Kings|4|11: the son of Abinadab, in all the district of Dor; (he had Taphath daughter of Solomon to wife: )
verses.1 Kings|4|12: Baanah the son of Ahilud; to him belonged Taanach and Megiddo, and of Beth-shean, which is by Zartanah beneath Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, till beyond Jokneam:
verses.1 Kings|4|13: The son of Geber, in Ramoth-gilead; to him were assigned Havoth-jair, the son of Manasseh, which is in Gilead; to him also was assigned the region of Argob, which is in the Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bars of brass:
verses.1 Kings|4|14: Ahinadab son of Iddo had Mahanaim;
verses.1 Kings|4|15: Ahimaaz was in Naphtali; he also took Bashemath daughter of Solomon to wife:
verses.1 Kings|4|16: Baanah the son of Hushai was in Asher and in Aloth:
verses.1 Kings|4|17: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah was in Issachar:
verses.1 Kings|4|18: Shimei the son of Elah was in Benjamin:
verses.1 Kings|4|19: Geber the son of Uri was in the land of Gilead, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorite and Og king of the Bashan; he was the one officer that was in the land.
verses.1 Kings|4|20: Judah and Israel were many, as the sand which by the sea for multitude; they ate, and drank, and were happy.
verses.1 Kings|5|1: And Solomon reigned over all kingdoms from the river to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt: they brought presents, and served Solomon all the days of his life.
verses.1 Kings|5|2: And Solomon's provision for one day was thirty kor of fine flour, and sixty kor of meal,
verses.1 Kings|5|3: ten fat oxen, and twenty oxen out of the pasture, and a hundred sheep, apart from deer, and gazelles, and fallow deer, and geese.
verses.1 Kings|5|4: For he had dominion over all the region on this side the river, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the river: and he had peace on all sides round about him.
verses.1 Kings|5|5: And Judah and Israel dwelt in safety, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|5|6: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
verses.1 Kings|5|7: And those officers provided stores for king Solomon, and for all that came to king Solomon's table, every man in his month: they lacked nothing.
verses.1 Kings|5|8: They brought barley also and straw for the horses and swift steeds to the place where the officers were, every man according to his charge.
verses.1 Kings|5|9: And God gave Solomon very much wisdom and understanding, and largeness of heart, like the sand that is on the sea shore.
verses.1 Kings|5|10: And Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.
verses.1 Kings|5|11: For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.
verses.1 Kings|5|12: And he spoke three thousand proverbs: and his poems were a thousand and five.
verses.1 Kings|5|13: And he spoke of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that comes out of the wall: he spoke also of beasts, and of birds, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
verses.1 Kings|5|14: And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
verses.1 Kings|5|15: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father: for Hiram always loved David.
verses.1 Kings|5|16: And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,
verses.1 Kings|5|17: Thou knowst how David my father could not build a house to the name of the Lord his God on account of the war with the nations which were about him on every side, until the Lord put them under the soles of my feet.
verses.1 Kings|5|18: But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil hindrance.
verses.1 Kings|5|19: And, behold, I purpose to build a house to the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord spoke to David my father, saying, Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy place, he shall build the house to my name.
verses.1 Kings|5|20: Now therefore command thou that they hew for me cedar trees out of the Lebanon; and my servants shall be with thy servants: and to thee will I give hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt say: for thou knowst that there is not among us any that can hew timber like the Zidonians.
verses.1 Kings|5|21: And it came to pass, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, Blessed is the Lord this day, who has given to David a wise son over this great people.
verses.1 Kings|5|22: And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, I have considered the things which thou hast sent to me: and I will do all thy desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of cypress.
verses.1 Kings|5|23: My servants shall bring them down from the Lebanon to the sea: and I will make them into floats to go to the place of which thou shalt send me word, and will cause them to be broken up there, and thou shalt take them away: and thou shalt accomplish my desire, in giving food for my household.
verses.1 Kings|5|24: So Hiram gave Solomon cedar trees and cypress according to all his desire.
verses.1 Kings|5|25: And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kor of wheat for food to his household, and twenty kor of beaten oil: thus Solomon gave to Hiram year by year.
verses.1 Kings|5|26: And the Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him: and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.
verses.1 Kings|5|27: And king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.
verses.1 Kings|5|28: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by turns: a month they were in the Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the levy.
verses.1 Kings|5|29: And Solomon had seventy thousand porters, and eighty thousand stone cutters in the mountains;
verses.1 Kings|5|30: besides Solomon's chief officers who were over the work, three thousand three hundred, who ruled over the people that were employed in the work.
verses.1 Kings|5|31: And the king commanded, and they brought great stones, costly stones to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.
verses.1 Kings|5|32: And Solomon's builders, and Hiram's builders, and the Giblites did hew them: so they prepared timber and stones to build the house.
verses.1 Kings|6|1: And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month Zib, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|6|2: And the house which king Solomon built for the Lord, its length was sixty cubits, and its breadth was twenty cubits, and its height was thirty cubits.
verses.1 Kings|6|3: And the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits was its length, according to the breadth of the house; and ten cubits was its breadth before the house.
verses.1 Kings|6|4: And for the house he made windows wide without, and narrow within.
verses.1 Kings|6|5: And against the wall of the house he built a side structure round about, against the walls of the house round about, both of the temple and of the sanctuary: and he made chambers round about:
verses.1 Kings|6|6: the lowest chamber was five cubits broad, and the middle was six cubits broad, and the third was seven cubits broad: for outside in the wall of the house he made narrowed rests round about, that the beams should not be fastened into the walls of the house.
verses.1 Kings|6|7: And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought there: so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was being built.
verses.1 Kings|6|8: The door for the middle chamber was in the right side of the house: and they went up with winding stairs into the middle chamber, and out of the middle into the third.
verses.1 Kings|6|9: So he built the house, and finished it; and covered the house with beams and boards of cedar.
verses.1 Kings|6|10: And then he built the side structure against all the house, five cubits high: and it rested on the house with timber of cedar.
verses.1 Kings|6|11: And the word of the Lord came to Solomon, saying,
verses.1 Kings|6|12: Concerning this house, which thou art building, if thou wilt follow my statutes, and execute my judgments, and keep all my commandments to walk in them; then will I perform my word with thee, which I spoke to David thy father:
verses.1 Kings|6|13: and I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel.
verses.1 Kings|6|14: So Solomon built the house, and finished it.
verses.1 Kings|6|15: And he built the walls of the house within with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house even to the walls of the ceiling he covered them on the inside with wood, and covered the floor of the house with planks of cypress.
verses.1 Kings|6|16: And he built twenty cubits on the back of the house, from the floor to the top of the walls with boards of cedar: he even built them for it within, for the sanctuary, that is for the most holy place.
verses.1 Kings|6|17: And the house, that is, the temple in front, was forty cubits long.
verses.1 Kings|6|18: And the cedar of the house within was carved with colocynths and open flowers: all was cedar; there was no stone seen.
verses.1 Kings|6|19: And the sanctuary he prepared in the house within, to set there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|6|20: And the space for the sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in its height: and he overlaid it with pure gold; and he covered the altar with cedar.
verses.1 Kings|6|21: So Solomon overlaid the house within with pure gold: and he drew chains of gold across before the sanctuary; and he overlaid it with gold.
verses.1 Kings|6|22: And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until he had finished all the house: also the whole altar that was by the sanctuary he overlaid with gold.
verses.1 Kings|6|23: And within the sanctuary he made two keruvim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
verses.1 Kings|6|24: And five cubits was the one wing of the keruv, and five cubits the other wing of the keruv: from the uttermost part of the one wing to the uttermost part of the other were ten cubits.
verses.1 Kings|6|25: And the other keruv was ten cubits: both the keruvim were of one measure and one form.
verses.1 Kings|6|26: The height of the one keruv was ten cubits, and so was that of the other keruv.
verses.1 Kings|6|27: And he set the keruvim within the inner house: and the wings of the keruvim were spread out, so that the wing of the one touched the one wall, and the wing of the other keruv touched the other wall; and the wings which they stretched towards the midst of the house touched one another.
verses.1 Kings|6|28: And he overlaid the keruvim with gold.
verses.1 Kings|6|29: And he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of keruvim and palm trees and open flowers, both for the inner and outer areas.
verses.1 Kings|6|30: And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, for the inner and outer areas.
verses.1 Kings|6|31: And for the entering of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood: the lintel and side posts forming five sides.
verses.1 Kings|6|32: The two doors also were of olive wood; and he carved upon them carvings of keruvim and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, and spread the gold upon the keruvim and upon the palm trees.
verses.1 Kings|6|33: So also made he for the door of the temple posts of olive wood, in shape foursided.
verses.1 Kings|6|34: And the two doors were of cypress wood: the one door had two folding leaves, and the other door had two folding leaves.
verses.1 Kings|6|35: And he carved on them keruvim and palm trees and open flowers: and covered them with gold fitted upon the carved work.
verses.1 Kings|6|36: And he built the inner court with three rows of hewn stone, and a row of cedar beams.
verses.1 Kings|6|37: In the fourth year was the foundation of the house of the Lord laid, in the month Zib:
verses.1 Kings|6|38: and in the eleventh year, in the month Bul (which is the eighth month), was the house finished throughout all its parts, and according to all the fashion of it. So was he seven years in building it.
verses.1 Kings|7|1: But Solomon spent thirteen years in building his own house, and he finished all his house.
verses.1 Kings|7|2: He built also the house of the forest of the Lebanon; its length was a hundred cubits, and its breadth was fifty cubits, and its height was thirty cubits upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.
verses.1 Kings|7|3: And it was covered with cedar above upon the beams, that lay on forty five pillars, fifteen in a row.
verses.1 Kings|7|4: And there were window spaces in three rows, and light was against light in three ranks.
verses.1 Kings|7|5: And all the doors and posts were square, with the windows: and light was against light in three ranks.
verses.1 Kings|7|6: And he made a porch of pillars; the length of which was fifty cubits, and its breadth, thirty cubits: and a porch was before them: and other pillars and a thick beam were before them.
verses.1 Kings|7|7: Then he made a porch for the throne where he might judge, even the porch of judgment: and it was covered with cedar from floor to floor.
verses.1 Kings|7|8: And his house where he dwelt, in the other court within the porch, was of the like work. Solomon made also a house for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had taken to wife, like this porch.
verses.1 Kings|7|9: All these were of costly stones, according to the measures of hewn stones, sawed with saws, within and without, from the foundation to the coping, and on the outside toward the great court.
verses.1 Kings|7|10: And the foundation was of costly stones, great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
verses.1 Kings|7|11: And above were costly stones, after the measures of hew stones, and cedars.
verses.1 Kings|7|12: And the great court round about was with three rows of hewn stones, and a row of cedar beams, both for the inner court of the house of the Lord, and for the porch of the house.
verses.1 Kings|7|13: And king Solomon sent and fetched Hiram from Tyre.
verses.1 Kings|7|14: He was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass: and he was filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and wrought all his work.
verses.1 Kings|7|15: For he cast two pillars of brass, of eighteen cubits high each pillar: and a line of twelve cubits did circle either of them about.
verses.1 Kings|7|16: And he made two capitals of molten brass, to set upon the tops of the pillars: the height of the one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits:
verses.1 Kings|7|17: and nets of checker work, and wreaths of chain work, for the capitals which were upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one capital, and seven for the other capital.
verses.1 Kings|7|18: And he made the pillars, and two rows round about upon the one network, to cover the capitals that were on the top of the pomegranates: and so did he for the other capital.
verses.1 Kings|7|19: And the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars in the porch, were of lily work, four cubits.
verses.1 Kings|7|20: And there were capitals upon the two pillars also above, over against the protuberance which was by the network: and the pomegranates were two hundred in rows round about upon the other capital.
verses.1 Kings|7|21: And he set up the pillars in the porch of the temple: and he set up the right pillar, and called its name Jachin: and he set up the left pillar, and called its name Boaz.
verses.1 Kings|7|22: And upon the top of the pillars was lily work: so was the work of the pillars finished.
verses.1 Kings|7|23: And he made a molten sea, ten cubits from the one brim to the other: it was round all about, and its height was five cubits: and a line of thirty cubits did circle it round about.
verses.1 Kings|7|24: And under the brim of it round about there were colocynths compassing it, ten cubits, compassing the sea round about: the colocynths were in two rows, cast with it in the same casting.
verses.1 Kings|7|25: It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking towards the north, and three looking towards the west, and three looking towards the south, and three looking towards the east: and the sea was set above upon them, and all their hinder parts were inward.
verses.1 Kings|7|26: And it was a hand breadth thick, and its brim was wrought like the brim of a cup, like the petals of a lily: it contained two thousand bat.
verses.1 Kings|7|27: And he made ten bases of brass; four cubits was the length of one base, and four cubits its breadth, and three cubits the height of it.
verses.1 Kings|7|28: And the work of the bases was of this manner: they had borders, and the borders were between the ledges:
verses.1 Kings|7|29: and on the borders that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and keruvim: (and upon the ledges there was a base above:) and beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
verses.1 Kings|7|30: And every base had four wheels of brass, and plates of brass: and the four corners thereof had shoulders: under the laver the shoulders were cast on, at the side of each were wreaths.
verses.1 Kings|7|31: And the mouth of it within the capital and above was a cubit: and its mouth was found after the work of the base, a cubit and a half: and also upon the mouth of it were engravings with their borders, foursquare, not round.
verses.1 Kings|7|32: And under the borders were four wheels; and the axles of the wheels were joined to the base: and the height of a wheel was a cubit and half a cubit.
verses.1 Kings|7|33: And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axles, and their rims, and their hoops, and their hubs, were all molten.
verses.1 Kings|7|34: And there were four shoulders to the four corners of one base: and the shoulders were of the very base itself.
verses.1 Kings|7|35: And in the top of the base was there a round compass of half a cubit high: and on the top of the base its stays and its borders were of one piece with it.
verses.1 Kings|7|36: For on the plates, on its stays and on its borders, he engraved keruvim, lions, and palm trees, according to the space between each one; and the wreaths were round about.
verses.1 Kings|7|37: After this manner he made the ten bases: all of them of the same casting, the same measure, and the same shape.
verses.1 Kings|7|38: Then he made ten lavers of brass: one laver contained forty bats: and every laver was four cubits: and upon every one of the ten bases one laver.
verses.1 Kings|7|39: And he put five bases on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house: and he set the sea on the right side of the house eastward towards the south.
verses.1 Kings|7|40: And Hiram made the lavers, and the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram made an end of doing all the work that he did for king Solomon, in the house of the Lord:
verses.1 Kings|7|41: the two pillars, and the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the two pillars; and the two networks, to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were upon the top of the pillars;
verses.1 Kings|7|42: and four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars;
verses.1 Kings|7|43: and the ten bases, and ten lavers on the bases;
verses.1 Kings|7|44: and one sea, and twelve oxen under the sea;
verses.1 Kings|7|45: and the pans, and the shovels, and the basins: and all these vessels, which Hiram made for king Solomon for the house of the Lord, were of burnished brass.
verses.1 Kings|7|46: In the plain of the Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zaretan.
verses.1 Kings|7|47: And Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because they were very very many: the weight of the brass was not found out.
verses.1 Kings|7|48: And Solomon made all the vessels that belonged to the house of the Lord: the altar of gold, and the table of gold, upon which the showbread was,
verses.1 Kings|7|49: and the candlesticks of pure gold, five on the right side, and five on the left, before the inner sanctuary, with the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs of gold,
verses.1 Kings|7|50: and the bowls, and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the firepans of pure gold; and the hinges of gold, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the outer house, namely, the temple.
verses.1 Kings|7|51: So was ended all the work that king Solomon made for the house of the Lord. And Solomon brought in the things which David his father had dedicated; the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, he did put in the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|8|1: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chiefs of the fathers of the children of Israel, to king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.
verses.1 Kings|8|2: And all the men of Israel assembled themselves to king Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
verses.1 Kings|8|3: And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
verses.1 Kings|8|4: And they brought up the ark of the Lord, and the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent, even those did the priests and the Levites bring up.
verses.1 Kings|8|5: And king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled to him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be told nor numbered for multitude.
verses.1 Kings|8|6: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, into the sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, under the wings of the keruvim.
verses.1 Kings|8|7: For the keruvim spread out their two wings over the place of the ark, and the keruvim covered the ark and its poles above.
verses.1 Kings|8|8: And they drew out the poles, so that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place, before the sanctuary, though they were not seen outside: and there they are to this day.
verses.1 Kings|8|9: There was nothing in the ark save the two tablets of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.
verses.1 Kings|8|10: And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the Lord,
verses.1 Kings|8|11: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|8|12: Then spoke Solomon, The Lord said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.
verses.1 Kings|8|13: I have surely built Thee a house to dwell in, a settled place for Thee to abide in for ever.
verses.1 Kings|8|14: And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the congregation of Israel: (and all the congregation of Israel stood:)
verses.1 Kings|8|15: and he said, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father, and has with his hand fulfilled it, saying,
verses.1 Kings|8|16: Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.
verses.1 Kings|8|17: And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
verses.1 Kings|8|18: And the Lord said to David my father, Whereas it was in thy heart to build a house to my name, thou didst well that it was in thy heart.
verses.1 Kings|8|19: Yet thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house to my name.
verses.1 Kings|8|20: And the Lord has performed his word that he spoke, and I am risen up in the place of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and have built a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
verses.1 Kings|8|21: And I have set there a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord, which he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
verses.1 Kings|8|22: And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel and spread out his hands towards heaven:
verses.1 Kings|8|23: and he said, Lord God of Israel, there is no God like Thee, in the heaven above, or on the earth beneath, who keepest covenant and troth with Thy servants who walk before Thee with all their heart:
verses.1 Kings|8|24: who hast kept with Thy servant David my father that which Thou didst promise him: Thou didst also with Thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it with Thy hand, as it is this day.
verses.1 Kings|8|25: Therefore now, Lord God of Israel, keep with Thy servant David my father that which Thou didst promise him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel; provided that thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me as thou hast walked before me.
verses.1 Kings|8|26: And now, O God of Israel, let Thy word, I pray Thee, be verified, which Thou didst speak to Thy servant David my father.
verses.1 Kings|8|27: For will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have built?
verses.1 Kings|8|28: Have consideration therefore to the prayer of Thy servant, and to his supplication, O Lord my God, to hearken to the cry and to the prayer, which Thy servant prays before Thee to day:
verses.1 Kings|8|29: that Thy eyes may be open towards this house night and day, towards the place of which Thou hast said, My name shall be there: that Thou mayst hearken to the prayer which Thy servant shall make toward this place.
verses.1 Kings|8|30: And hearken Thou to the supplication of Thy servant, and of Thy people Israel, when they shall pray towards this place: and hear Thou in heaven Thy dwelling place: and when Thou hearest, forgive.
verses.1 Kings|8|31: If any man trespass against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and the oath come before Thy altar in this house:
verses.1 Kings|8|32: then hear Thou in heaven, and do, and judge Thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
verses.1 Kings|8|33: When Thy people Israel are smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against Thee, and shall turn again to Thee, and confess Thy name, and pray, and make supplication to Thee in this house:
verses.1 Kings|8|34: then hear Thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of Thy people Israel, and bring them back to the land which Thou didst give to their fathers.
verses.1 Kings|8|35: When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against Thee; if they pray towards this place, and confess Thy name, and turn from their sin, when Thou dost afflict them:
verses.1 Kings|8|36: then hear Thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of Thy servants, and of Thy people Israel, that Thou teach them the good way in which they should walk, and give rain upon Thy land, which Thou hast given to Thy people for an inheritance.
verses.1 Kings|8|37: If there be famine in the land, if there be pestilence, blasting, mildew, locust, or if there be caterpillar; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; whatever plague, whatever sickness there be:
verses.1 Kings|8|38: Whatever prayer and whatever supplication is made by any man, or by all Thy people Israel, (who shall know every man the plague of his own heart) and he spread forth his hands towards this house:
verses.1 Kings|8|39: then hear Thou in heaven Thy dwelling place, and forgive, and do, and give to every man according to his ways, whose heart Thou knowst; (for Thou, Thou only, knowst the hearts of all the children of men;)
verses.1 Kings|8|40: that they may fear Thee all the days that they live in the land which Thou didst give to our fathers.
verses.1 Kings|8|41: Moreover concerning a stranger, that is not of Thy people Israel, but comes out of a far country for Thy name's sake:
verses.1 Kings|8|42: (for they shall hear of Thy great name, and of Thy strong hand, and of Thy stretched out arm;) when he shall come and pray towards this house;
verses.1 Kings|8|43: hear Thou in heaven Thy dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calls to Thee for: that all people of the earth may know Thy name, to fear Thee, as do Thy people Israel; and that they may know that this house, which I have built is called by Thy name.
verses.1 Kings|8|44: If Thy people go out to battle against their enemy, wherever Thou shalt send them, and shall pray to the Lord towards the city which Thou hast chosen, and towards the house that I have built for Thy name:
verses.1 Kings|8|45: then hear Thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.
verses.1 Kings|8|46: If they sin against Thee, (for there is no man who does not sin) and Thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives to the land of the enemy, far or near;
verses.1 Kings|8|47: yet if they take thought in the land where they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication to Thee in the land of their captors, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;
verses.1 Kings|8|48: and so they return to Thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, who led them away captive, and pray to Thee towards their land, which Thou didst give to their fathers, the city which Thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for Thy name:
verses.1 Kings|8|49: then hear Thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven Thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause,
verses.1 Kings|8|50: and forgive Thy people that have sinned against Thee, and all their transgressions in which they have transgressed against Thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them:
verses.1 Kings|8|51: for they are Thy people, and Thy inheritance, whom Thou didst bring out of Egypt, out of the midst of the iron furnace:
verses.1 Kings|8|52: that Thy eyes may be open to the supplication of Thy servant, and to the supplication of Thy people Israel, to hearken to them in all that they call for to Thee.
verses.1 Kings|8|53: For Thou didst separate them from among all the people of the earth, to be Thy inheritance, as Thou didst speak by the hand of Moses Thy servant, when Thou didst bring our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord God.
verses.1 Kings|8|54: And it was so, that when Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication to the Lord, he arose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to heaven.
verses.1 Kings|8|55: And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
verses.1 Kings|8|56: Blessed is the Lord that has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there has not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.
verses.1 Kings|8|57: The Lord our God be with us, as he was with our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us:
verses.1 Kings|8|58: that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers.
verses.1 Kings|8|59: And let these my words, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel at all times, as each day may require,
verses.1 Kings|8|60: that all the people of the earth may know that the Lord is God, and that there is no other.
verses.1 Kings|8|61: Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.
verses.1 Kings|8|62: And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|8|63: And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered to the Lord, twenty two thousand oxen, and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|8|64: On the same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that was before the house of the Lord: for there he offered burnt offerings, and meal offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings: because the altar of brass that was before the Lord was too little to receive the burnt offerings, and meal offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.
verses.1 Kings|8|65: And at that time Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath to the wadi of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, namely fourteen days.
verses.1 Kings|8|66: On the eighth day he sent the people away: and they blessed the king, and went to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the Lord had done for David his servant, and for Israel his people.
verses.1 Kings|9|1: And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished the building of the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all Solomon's desire which he was pleased to do,
verses.1 Kings|9|2: that the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.
verses.1 Kings|9|3: And the Lord said to him, I have heard thy prayer and thy supplication, that thou hast made before me: I have hallowed this house, which thou hast built, to put my name there for ever; and my eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually.
verses.1 Kings|9|4: And if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and my judgments:
verses.1 Kings|9|5: then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Israel for ever, as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel.
verses.1 Kings|9|6: But if you shall turn from following me, you or your children, and will not keep my commandments and my statutes which I have set before you, but go and serve other gods, and worship them:
verses.1 Kings|9|7: then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people:
verses.1 Kings|9|8: and at this house, which is high, every one that passes by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss; and they shall say, Why has the Lord done thus to this land, and to this house?
verses.1 Kings|9|9: And they shall answer, Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold of other gods, and have worshipped them, and served them: therefore has the Lord brought upon them all this evil.
verses.1 Kings|9|10: And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, when Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the Lord, and the king's house.
verses.1 Kings|9|11: (Now Hiram the king of Tyre had helped Solomon with cedar trees and cypress trees, and with gold, according to all his desire,) that then king Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of the Galilee.
verses.1 Kings|9|12: And Hiram came out of Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him; and they pleased him not.
verses.1 Kings|9|13: And he said, What cities are these which thou hast given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Cabul to this day.
verses.1 Kings|9|14: And Hiram sent to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
verses.1 Kings|9|15: And this is the manner of the levy which king Solomon raised; to build the house of the Lord, and his own house, and the Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, and Megiddo, and Gezer.
verses.1 Kings|9|16: For Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it with fire, and slain the Canaanite that dwelt in the city, and given it for a present to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
verses.1 Kings|9|17: And Solomon built Gezer, and the lower Beth-horon,
verses.1 Kings|9|18: and Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,
verses.1 Kings|9|19: and all the store-cities that Solomon had, and cities for his chariots, and cities for his horsemen, and that which Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
verses.1 Kings|9|20: Of all the people that were left of the Amorite, Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, who were not of the children of Israel,
verses.1 Kings|9|21: their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel were not able to wipe out, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice to this day.
verses.1 Kings|9|22: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen: but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen.
verses.1 Kings|9|23: These were the chief officers that were over Solomon's work, five hundred and fifty, who bore rule over the people that did the work.
verses.1 Kings|9|24: But Pharaoh's daughter came up out of the city of David to her house which he had built for her: then did he build the Millo.
verses.1 Kings|9|25: And three times a year did Solomon offer burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar which he built to the Lord, and he burnt incense upon the altar that was before the Lord. So he finished the house.
verses.1 Kings|9|26: And king Solomon made a ship in Ezion-geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom.
verses.1 Kings|9|27: And Hiram sent in the ship his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|9|28: And they came to Ophir, and fetched from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold, and brought it to king Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|10|1: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, and what he had done in the name of the Lord, she came to prove him with riddles.
verses.1 Kings|10|2: And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bore spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she spoke to him of all that was in her heart,
verses.1 Kings|10|3: and Solomon answered her all her questions: there was not anything hid from the king, which he told her not.
verses.1 Kings|10|4: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built,
verses.1 Kings|10|5: and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the Lord; there was no more spirit in her.
verses.1 Kings|10|6: And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in my own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom.
verses.1 Kings|10|7: But I believed not the words, until I came, and my eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceed the fame which I heard.
verses.1 Kings|10|8: Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, who stand continually before thee, and who hear thy wisdom.
verses.1 Kings|10|9: May the Lord thy God, be blessed, who delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore he made thee king, to do justice and righteousness.
verses.1 Kings|10|10: And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|10|11: And also the ship of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir a great amount of almug wood, and precious stones.
verses.1 Kings|10|12: And the king made of the almug wood a railing for the house of the Lord, and for the king's house, lyres also and lutes for singers: there came no such almug wood, nor were seen to this day.
verses.1 Kings|10|13: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, besides that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.
verses.1 Kings|10|14: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty six talents of gold,
verses.1 Kings|10|15: besides what he had of the merchantmen, and of the traffic of the merchants, and of all the kings of the Arabia, and of the governors of the country.
verses.1 Kings|10|16: And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of gold went to one target.
verses.1 Kings|10|17: And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pound of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of the Lebanon.
verses.1 Kings|10|18: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.
verses.1 Kings|10|19: The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round behind: and there were arm rests on either side on the seat, and two lions stood beside the arm rests.
verses.1 Kings|10|20: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.
verses.1 Kings|10|21: And all king Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; none were of silver: that was considered nothing in the days of Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|10|22: For the king had at sea a ship of Tarshish with a ship of Hiram: once in three years the ship of Tarshish came, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
verses.1 Kings|10|23: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.
verses.1 Kings|10|24: And all the earth sought of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
verses.1 Kings|10|25: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, and so it was year by year.
verses.1 Kings|10|26: And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he placed in the cities for chariots, and with the king at Jerusalem.
verses.1 Kings|10|27: And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem like stones, and he made cedars to be like the sycamore trees that are in the lowlands for abundance.
verses.1 Kings|10|28: And Solomon had horses brought from Egypt and from Kue; the king's merchants took the horses from Kue at a fixed price.
verses.1 Kings|10|29: And a chariot going out of Egypt would cost six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse, a hundred and fifty: and so by their means they brought them out also for all the kings of Hittites and the kings of Syria.
verses.1 Kings|11|1: But king Solomon loved many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, Moabitess, Ammonite, Edomite, Zidonians, and Hittite women;
verses.1 Kings|11|2: of the nation concerning whom the Lord said to the children of Israel, you shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in to you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon attached himself to these in love.
verses.1 Kings|11|3: And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.
verses.1 Kings|11|4: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.
verses.1 Kings|11|5: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
verses.1 Kings|11|6: And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father.
verses.1 Kings|11|7: Then did Solomon build a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.
verses.1 Kings|11|8: And likewise did he for all his foreign wives, who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods.
verses.1 Kings|11|9: And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, who had twice appeared to him.
verses.1 Kings|11|10: And had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.
verses.1 Kings|11|11: So that the Lord said to Solomon, Since this is your mind, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.
verses.1 Kings|11|12: Yet in thy days I will not do it for David thy father's sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.
verses.1 Kings|11|13: Nevertheless, I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake, and for the sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen.
verses.1 Kings|11|14: And the Lord stirred up an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomitess: he was of the king's seed in Edom.
verses.1 Kings|11|15: For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain, after he had smitten every male in Edom;
verses.1 Kings|11|16: (for six months did Joab remain there with all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom: )
verses.1 Kings|11|17: that Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father's servants with him, to go into Egypt; Hadad being yet a little child.
verses.1 Kings|11|18: And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran: and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt; who gave him a house, and bread, and gave him land.
verses.1 Kings|11|19: And Hadad found great favour in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
verses.1 Kings|11|20: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house: and Genubath was in Pharaoh's household among the sons of Pharaoh.
verses.1 Kings|11|21: And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to my own country.
verses.1 Kings|11|22: Then Pharaoh said to him, But what hast thou lacked with me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thy own country? And he answered, Nothing: but let me go.
verses.1 Kings|11|23: And God stirred him up another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah:
verses.1 Kings|11|24: and he gathered men to him, and became captain over a band, when David slew them of Zobah: and they went to Damascus, and dwelt there, and reigned in Damascus.
verses.1 Kings|11|25: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, besides the mischief that Hadad did: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
verses.1 Kings|11|26: And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite, of Zereda, Solomon's servant, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow woman, he lifted up his hand against the king.
verses.1 Kings|11|27: And this was the cause that he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo, and repaired the breaches of the city of David his father.
verses.1 Kings|11|28: And the man Jeroboam was a mighty warrior: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the labour of the house of Joseph.
verses.1 Kings|11|29: And it came to pass at that time when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field:
verses.1 Kings|11|30: and Ahijah caught the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces:
verses.1 Kings|11|31: and he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:
verses.1 Kings|11|32: (but he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)
verses.1 Kings|11|33: because they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in my eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments, as did David his father.
verses.1 Kings|11|34: Yet I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand: but I will make him prince all the days of his life for David my servant's sake, whom I chose, because he kept my commandments and my statutes:
verses.1 Kings|11|35: but I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand, and will give it to thee, that is the ten tribes.
verses.1 Kings|11|36: And to his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a lamp always before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there.
verses.1 Kings|11|37: And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desires, and shalt be king over Israel.
verses.1 Kings|11|38: And it shall be, if thou wilt hearken to all that I command thee, and will walk in my ways, and do what is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to thee.
verses.1 Kings|11|39: And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.
verses.1 Kings|11|40: Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. And Jeroboam arose, and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|11|41: And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
verses.1 Kings|11|42: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
verses.1 Kings|11|43: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.
verses.1 Kings|12|1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem, to make him king.
verses.1 Kings|12|2: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who was yet in Egypt, heard of it, (for he was fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt;)
verses.1 Kings|12|3: that they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.1 Kings|12|4: Thy father made our yoke hard: now therefore make thou the hard service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.
verses.1 Kings|12|5: And he said unto them, Depart for three more days, then come back to me.
verses.1 Kings|12|6: And the people departed. And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do you advise that I answer this people?
verses.1 Kings|12|7: And they spoke to him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant to this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words of them, then they will be thy servants for ever.
verses.1 Kings|12|8: But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that had grown up with him, and who stood before him:
verses.1 Kings|12|9: and he said to them, What counsel give you that we answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make lighter the yoke which thy father did put upon us?
verses.1 Kings|12|10: And the young men that had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak to this people that spoke to thee, saying,
verses.1 Kings|12|11: Thy father made our yoke heavy, but thou make it lighter to us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. And now whereas my father did burden you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
verses.1 Kings|12|12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.
verses.1 Kings|12|13: And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the counsel that the old men had counselled him;
verses.1 Kings|12|14: and spoke to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
verses.1 Kings|12|15: So that the king hearkened not to the people; for it was so brought about from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.1 Kings|12|16: So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not to them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thy own house, David. So Israel departed to their tents.
verses.1 Kings|12|17: But as for the children of Israel who dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
verses.1 Kings|12|18: Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute; and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. Therefore king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.1 Kings|12|19: So Israel rebelled against the house of David to this day.
verses.1 Kings|12|20: And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come back, that they sent and called him to the congregation, and made him king over all Israel, there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.
verses.1 Kings|12|21: And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, who were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
verses.1 Kings|12|22: But the word of God came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,
verses.1 Kings|12|23: Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah, and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying,
verses.1 Kings|12|24: Thus says the Lord, You shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of the Lord, and turned and went their way, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|12|25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim, and dwelt there; and went out from there, and built Penuel.
verses.1 Kings|12|26: And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David:
verses.1 Kings|12|27: if this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again to their lord, namely to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me, and go back to Rehoboam king of Judah.
verses.1 Kings|12|28: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said to them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem; behold thy gods, O Israel, who brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.1 Kings|12|29: And he set the one in Beth-el, and the other put he in Dan.
verses.1 Kings|12|30: And this thing became a sin: for the people went as far as Dan, to worship before that one.
verses.1 Kings|12|31: And he made a house of high places, and made priests from all ranks of the people, who were not of the sons of Levi.
verses.1 Kings|12|32: And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Beth-el, sacrificing to the calves that he had made: and in Beth-el he placed the priests of the high places which he had made.
verses.1 Kings|12|33: So he offered upon the altar which he had made in Beth-el on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and ordained a feast to the children of Israel: and he went up to the altar to burn incense.
verses.1 Kings|13|1: And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the Lord to Beth-el: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense.
verses.1 Kings|13|2: And he cried against the altar by the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus says the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born to the house of David (Josiah by name;) and upon thee shall he slay the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men's bones shall they burn upon thee.
verses.1 Kings|13|3: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the Lord has spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.
verses.1 Kings|13|4: And it came to pass, when the king heard the saying of the man of God, who had cried against the altar in Beth-el, that he put out his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put out against him, dried up, so that he could not draw it back to him.
verses.1 Kings|13|5: The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.
verses.1 Kings|13|6: And the king answered and said to the man of God, Entreat now the face of the Lord thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God entreated the Lord, and the king's hand was restored him again, and became as it was before.
verses.1 Kings|13|7: And the king said to the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a present.
verses.1 Kings|13|8: And the man of God said to the king, If thou wilt give me half thy house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place:
verses.1 Kings|13|9: for so was it charged me by the word of the Lord, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor return by the same way that thou camest.
verses.1 Kings|13|10: So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Beth-el.
verses.1 Kings|13|11: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beth-el; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Beth-el: the words which he had spoken to the king, them they told also to their father.
verses.1 Kings|13|12: And their father said to them, Which way did he go? For his sons had seen which way the man of God went, who came from Judah.
verses.1 Kings|13|13: And he said to his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode on it,
verses.1 Kings|13|14: and went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said to him, Art thou the man of God that didst come from Judah? And he said, I am.
verses.1 Kings|13|15: Then he said to him, Come home with me, and eat bread.
verses.1 Kings|13|16: And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:
verses.1 Kings|13|17: for it was said to me by the word of the Lord, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.
verses.1 Kings|13|18: He said to him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thy house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied to him.
verses.1 Kings|13|19: So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
verses.1 Kings|13|20: And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the Lord came to the prophet that brought him back:
verses.1 Kings|13|21: and he cried to the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus says the Lord, Since thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee,
verses.1 Kings|13|22: but camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which he did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcass shall not come to the tomb of thy fathers.
verses.1 Kings|13|23: And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled the ass for him, that is for the prophet whom he had brought back.
verses.1 Kings|13|24: And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcass was thrown down on the road, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcass.
