verses.2 Kings|5|8: And when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, Why hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.
verses.2 Kings|5|9: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
verses.2 Kings|5|10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall be restored to thee, and thou shalt be clean.
verses.2 Kings|5|11: But Naaman was angry, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the Lord his God, and wave his hand over the place, and so heal the infected person.
verses.2 Kings|5|12: Are not Amana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.
verses.2 Kings|5|13: And his servants came near, and spoke to him, and said, My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldst thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he says to thee, Wash, and be clean?
verses.2 Kings|5|14: Then he went down, and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
verses.2 Kings|5|15: And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.
verses.2 Kings|5|16: But he said, As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it; but he refused.
verses.2 Kings|5|17: And Naaman said, If not, let then, I pray thee, be given to thy servant two mules' burden of earth; for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods, but to the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|5|18: In this thing the Lord pardon thy servant, that when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow myself down in the house of Rimmon, the Lord pardon thy servant in this thing.
verses.2 Kings|5|19: And he said to him, Go in peace. So he departed from him a little way.
verses.2 Kings|5|20: But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, Behold, my master has spared Naaman this Syrian, in not receiving at his hand that which he bought: but, as the Lord lives, I will run after him, and take something of him.
verses.2 Kings|5|21: So Gehazi followed after Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he came down from the chariot to meet him, and said, Is all well?
verses.2 Kings|5|22: And he said, All is well. My master has sent me, saying, Behold, even now there be come to me from mount Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.
verses.2 Kings|5|23: And Naaman said, Be pleased to take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and laid them upon two of his servants; and they bore them before him.
verses.2 Kings|5|24: And when he came to the hill, he took them from their hand, and deposited them in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.
verses.2 Kings|5|25: But he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said to him, Where from, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went nowhere at all.
verses.2 Kings|5|26: And he said to him, Went not my heart with thee, when the man turned back from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?
verses.2 Kings|5|27: So let the disease of Naaman cleave to thee, and to thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence stricken as white as snow.
verses.2 Kings|6|1: And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, Behold now, the place where we dwell with thee is too small for us.
verses.2 Kings|6|2: Let us go, we pray thee, to the Jordan, and take from there every man a beam, and let us make us a place there, where we may dwell. And he answered, Go.
verses.2 Kings|6|3: And one said, Be pleased to go with thy servants. And he answered, I will go.
verses.2 Kings|6|4: So he went with them, And when they came to the Jordan, they cut down wood.
verses.2 Kings|6|5: But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water: and he cried, and said, Alas, master! for it was borrowed.
verses.2 Kings|6|6: And the man of God said, Where fell it? And he showed him the place. And he cut off a stick, and threw it in there; and made the iron float.
verses.2 Kings|6|7: Then he said, Take it up to thee. And he put out his hand, and took it.
verses.2 Kings|6|8: Then the king of Syria warred against Israel, and took counsel with his servants, saying, In such and such a place shall be my camp.
verses.2 Kings|6|9: And the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, Beware that thou pass not such a place; for there Syria are hidden.
verses.2 Kings|6|10: And the king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God told him and warned him of, and saved himself there, not once nor twice.
verses.2 Kings|6|11: Therefore the heart of the king of Syria was sore troubled for this thing; and he called his servants, and said to them, Will you not show me which of us is for the king of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|6|12: And one of his servants said, No, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber.
verses.2 Kings|6|13: And he said, Go and see where he is, that I may send and fetch him. And it was told him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothan.
verses.2 Kings|6|14: Therefore he sent there horses, and chariots, and a great host: and they came by night, and surrounded the city.
verses.2 Kings|6|15: And the servant of the man of God rose early, and went out, and behold, an army surrounded the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said to him, Alas, my master! what shall we do?
verses.2 Kings|6|16: And he answered, Fear not: for they that are with us are more than they that are with them.
verses.2 Kings|6|17: And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray Thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.
verses.2 Kings|6|18: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the Lord, and said, Smite this people, I pray Thee, with blindness. And he smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
verses.2 Kings|6|19: And Elisha said to them, This is not the way, neither is this the city: follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek. But he led them to Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|6|20: And it came to pass, when they were come to Samaria, that Elisha said, Lord, open the eyes of these men, that they may see. And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw; and, behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|6|21: And the king of Israel said to Elisha, when he saw them, My father, shall I smite them? shall I smite them?
verses.2 Kings|6|22: And he answered, Thou shalt not smite them: wouldst thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.
verses.2 Kings|6|23: And he prepared a great feast for them: and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|6|24: And it came to pass after this, that Ben-hadad king of Syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|6|25: And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a qav of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.
verses.2 Kings|6|26: And as the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, a woman cried to him, saying, Help, my lord, O king.
verses.2 Kings|6|27: And he said, If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?
verses.2 Kings|6|28: And the king said to her, What ails thee? And she answered, This woman said to me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow.
verses.2 Kings|6|29: So we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said to her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she has hid her son.
verses.2 Kings|6|30: And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he rent his clothes; and he passed by upon the wall, and the people looked, and, behold, he had sackcloth within upon his flesh.
verses.2 Kings|6|31: Then he said, God do so and more also to me, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat, shall stand on him this day.
verses.2 Kings|6|32: But Elisha sat in his house, and the elders sat with him; and the king sent a man from before him: but before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? look, when the messenger comes, shut the door, and hold him fast at the door: is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?
verses.2 Kings|6|33: And while he yet talked with them, behold, the messenger came down to him: and he said, Behold, this evil is of the Lord; why should I wait for the Lord any longer?
verses.2 Kings|7|1: Then Elisha said, Hear the word of the Lord; Thus says the Lord, To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|7|2: Then the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, and said, Behold, if the Lord would make windows in heaven, might this thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thy eyes, but thou shalt not eat of it.
verses.2 Kings|7|3: And there were four men afflicted with zaraat at the entrance of the gate: and they said to one another, Why do we sit here until we die?
verses.2 Kings|7|4: If we say, We will enter the city, then the famine is in the city, and we shall die there: and if we sit still here, we will die also. Now therefore come, and let us go over to the camp of Syria: if they save us alive, we shall live; and if they kill us, we shall but die.
verses.2 Kings|7|5: And they rose up in the twilight, to go to the camp of Syria: and when they were come to the outer edge of the camp of Syria, behold, there was no man there.
verses.2 Kings|7|6: For the Lord had made the camp of Syria to hear a noise of chariots, and a noise of horses, the noise of a great host: and they said to one another, Lo, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of Egypt, to come upon us.
verses.2 Kings|7|7: So they arose and fled in the twilight, and left their tents, and their horses, and their asses, even the camp as it was, and fled for their life.
verses.2 Kings|7|8: And when these diseased men came to the outer edge of the camp, they went into one tent, and did eat and drink, and carried from there silver, and gold, and raiment, and went and hid it; and came back, and entered into another tent, and carried from there also, and went and hid it.
verses.2 Kings|7|9: Then they said to one another, We do not behave correctly: this day is a day of good tidings, and we hold our peace: if we tarry till the morning light, punishment will come upon us: now therefore come, that we may go and tell the king's household.
verses.2 Kings|7|10: So they came and called to the gatekeepers of the city: and they told them, saying, We came to the camp of Syria, and, behold, there was no man there, neither voice of man, but horses tied, and asses tied, and the tents as they were.
verses.2 Kings|7|11: And he called the gatekeepers; and they told it to the king's house within.
verses.2 Kings|7|12: And the king arose in the night, and said to his servants, I will now tell you what Syria has done to us. They know that we are hungry; therefore are they gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, When they come out of the city, we shall catch them alive, and get into the city.
verses.2 Kings|7|13: And one of his servants answered and said, Let some take, I pray thee, five of the horses that remain, which are left in the city, (behold, they are as all the multitude of Israel that are left in it: behold, I say, they are even as all the multitude of Israel that are consumed:) and let us send and see.
verses.2 Kings|7|14: They took therefore two chariot horses; and the king sent after the camp of Syria, saying, Go and see.
verses.2 Kings|7|15: And they went after them to the Jordan: and, lo, all the way was full of garments and vessels, which Syria had cast away in their haste. And the messengers returned, and told the king.
verses.2 Kings|7|16: And the people went out, and plundered the camp of Syria. So a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|7|17: And the king appointed the officer on whose hand he had leaned to have the charge of the gate: and the people trampled upon him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God had said, who spoke when the king came down to him.
verses.2 Kings|7|18: And it came to pass when the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be to morrow about this time in the gate of Samaria,
verses.2 Kings|7|19: that that officer answered the man of God, and said, Now, behold, if the Lord should make windows in heaven, might such a thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thy eyes, but shalt not eat of it.
verses.2 Kings|7|20: And so it happened to him: for the people trampled upon him in the gate, and he died.
verses.2 Kings|8|1: Then Elisha spoke to the woman, whose son he had restored to life, saying, Arise, and go thou and thy household, and sojourn wherever thou canst sojourn: for the Lord has called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land for seven years.
verses.2 Kings|8|2: And the woman arose, and did according to the saying of the man of God: and she went with her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
verses.2 Kings|8|3: And it came to pass at the end of seven years; that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went out to cry to the king for her house and for her land.
verses.2 Kings|8|4: And the king talked with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things that Elisha has done.
verses.2 Kings|8|5: And it came to pass, as he was telling the king how he had restored a dead body to life, that, behold, the woman, whose son he had restored to life, cried to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said, My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.
verses.2 Kings|8|6: And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed to her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the produce of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.
verses.2 Kings|8|7: And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben-hadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come here.
verses.2 Kings|8|8: And the king said to Hazael, Take a present in thy hand, and go, meet the man of God, and inquire of the Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
verses.2 Kings|8|9: So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, and every good thing of Damascus, forty camels' burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben-hadad king of Syria has sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
verses.2 Kings|8|10: And Elisha said to him, Go, say to him, Thou mayst certainly recover (nonetheless, the Lord has shown me that he shall surely die.)
verses.2 Kings|8|11: And he settled his countenance steadfastly, as long as he could; then the man of God wept.
verses.2 Kings|8|12: And Hazael said, Why does my lord weep? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do to the children of Israel: their strongholds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their infants, and rip up their women with child.
verses.2 Kings|8|13: And Hazael said, But what is thy servant, who is but a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The Lord has shown me that thou shalt be king over Syria.
verses.2 Kings|8|14: So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldst surely recover.
verses.2 Kings|8|15: And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took the coverlet, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|8|16: And in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.
verses.2 Kings|8|17: Thirty two years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned for eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.2 Kings|8|18: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|8|19: Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah for David his servant's sake, as he promised him to give him and to his children a lamp for all time.
verses.2 Kings|8|20: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.
verses.2 Kings|8|21: So Joram went over to Zair, and all the chariots with him: and he rose by night, and smote the men of Edom who surrounded him, and the captains of the chariots: and the people fled into their tents.
verses.2 Kings|8|22: Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time.
verses.2 Kings|8|23: And the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.2 Kings|8|24: And Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|8|25: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel did Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram king of Judah begin to reign.
verses.2 Kings|8|26: Ahaziah was twenty two years old when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|8|27: And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.
verses.2 Kings|8|28: And he went with Joram the son of Ahab to the war against Hazael king of Syria in Ramoth-gilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram.
verses.2 Kings|8|29: And the king Joram went back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
verses.2 Kings|9|1: And Elisha the prophet called one of the children of the prophets, and said to him, Gird up thy loins, and take this flask of oil in thy hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead:
verses.2 Kings|9|2: and when thou comest there, look out there Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in, and make him rise up from among his brethren, and carry him to an inner chamber;
verses.2 Kings|9|3: then take the flask of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed thee king over Israel. Then open the door, and flee, and do not wait.
verses.2 Kings|9|4: So the young man, namely, the young man, the prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.2 Kings|9|5: And when he came, behold, the captains of the host were sitting; and he said, I have an errand to thee, O captain. And Jehu said, To which of us all? And he said, To thee, O captain.
verses.2 Kings|9|6: And he arose, and went into the house; and he poured the oil on his head, and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.
verses.2 Kings|9|7: And thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord, at the hand of Jezebel.
verses.2 Kings|9|8: For the whole house of Ahab shall perish: and I will cut off from Ahab every male person, and him that is shut up and him that is left free in Israel:
verses.2 Kings|9|9: and I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah:
verses.2 Kings|9|10: and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled.
verses.2 Kings|9|11: Then Jehu came out to the servants of his lord: and one said to him, Is all well? why did this mad fellow come to thee? And he said to them, you know the man, and his way of talking.
verses.2 Kings|9|12: And they said, It is false; tell us now. And he said, Thus and thus spoke he to me, saying, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed thee king over Israel.
verses.2 Kings|9|13: Then they hastened, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew with the shofar, saying, Jehu is king.
verses.2 Kings|9|14: So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. (Now Joram had been guarding Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria.
verses.2 Kings|9|15: But king Joram was returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria.) And Jehu said, If this be your mind, then let none go out or escape from the city to go to tell it in Jezreel.
verses.2 Kings|9|16: So Jehu rode in a chariot, and went to Jezreel; for Joram lay there. And Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see Joram.
verses.2 Kings|9|17: And there stood a watchman on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the company of Jehu as he came, and said, I see a company. And Jehoram said, Take a horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, Is it peace?
verses.2 Kings|9|18: So there went one on horseback to meet him, and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What hast thou to do with peace? turn round and ride behind me. And the watchman told, saying, The messenger came to them, but he does not return.
verses.2 Kings|9|19: Then he sent out a second on horseback, who came to them, and said, Thus say the king, Is it peace? And Jehu answered, What hast thou to do with peace? turn round and ride behind me.
verses.2 Kings|9|20: And the watchman told, saying, He came to them, and does not return: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he drives furiously.
verses.2 Kings|9|21: And Jehoram said, Harness. And they harnessed his chariot. And Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went out against Jehu, and met him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
verses.2 Kings|9|22: And it came to pass, when Jehoram saw Jehu, that he said, Is it peace, Jehu? And he answered, What peace can there be, so long as the lewd practices of thy mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts are so many?
verses.2 Kings|9|23: And Jehoram turned his hands, and fled, and said to Ahaziah, Treachery, Ahaziah.
verses.2 Kings|9|24: And Jehu drew a bow with his full strength, and smote Jehoram between his arms, and the arrows went out at his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.
verses.2 Kings|9|25: Then said Jehu to Bidkar his captain, Take him up, and cast him in the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite: for remember how that, when I and thou rode together after Ahab his father, the Lord pronounced this burden upon him;
verses.2 Kings|9|26: Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons, says the Lord; and I will repay thee in this plot of ground says the Lord. Now therefore take him and cast him into the plot of ground, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|9|27: But when Ahaziah the king of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of Bet-haggan, And Jehu followed after him, and said, Smite him also in the chariot. And they did so at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo, and died there.
verses.2 Kings|9|28: And his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.2 Kings|9|29: And in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab had Ahaziah begun to reign over Judah.
verses.2 Kings|9|30: And when Jehu was come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her eyes, and adorned her head, and looked out at the window.
verses.2 Kings|9|31: And as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Is it peace? thou Zimri, who murdered his master.
verses.2 Kings|9|32: And he lifted up his face to the window, and said, Who is on my side? who? And there looked out to him two or three eunuchs.
verses.2 Kings|9|33: And he said, Throw her down. So they threw her down: and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses: and he trampled her under foot.
verses.2 Kings|9|34: And when he was come in, he did eat and drink, and said, Go, see now to this cursed woman, and bury her: for she is a king's daughter.
verses.2 Kings|9|35: And they went to bury her: but they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.
verses.2 Kings|9|36: So they came back, and told him. And he said, This is the word of the Lord, which he spoke by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel, shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel:
verses.2 Kings|9|37: And the carcass of Jezebel shall be as dung upon the open field in the portion of Jezreel; so that they shall not be able to say, This is Jezebel.
verses.2 Kings|10|1: And Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters, and sent to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders, and to those who brought up Ahab's children, saying,
verses.2 Kings|10|2: Now as soon as this letter comes to you, seeing your master's sons are with you, and there are with you chariots and horses, a fortified city also, and armour;
verses.2 Kings|10|3: select then the best and fittest of your master's sons, and set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house.
verses.2 Kings|10|4: But they were exceedingly afraid, and said, Behold, two kings could not stand before him: how then shall we stand?
verses.2 Kings|10|5: And he that was over the house, and he that was over the city, the elders also, and the guardians, sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants, and will do all that thou shalt bid us; we will not make anyone king: do thou that which is good in thy eyes.
verses.2 Kings|10|6: Then he wrote a letter the second time to them, saying, If you are mine, and if you will hearken to my voice, take the heads of the men your master's sons, and come to me to Jezreel by to morrow this time. Now the king's sons, being seventy persons, were with the notables of the city, who brought them up.
verses.2 Kings|10|7: And it came to pass, when the letter came to them, that they took the king's sons, and slew seventy persons, and put their heads in baskets, and sent him them to Jezreel.
verses.2 Kings|10|8: And there came a messenger, and told him, saying, They have brought the heads of the king's sons. And he said, Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until the morning.
verses.2 Kings|10|9: And it came to pass in the morning, that he went out, and stood, and said to all the people, You are just men: behold, I conspired against my master, and slew him: but who slew all these?
verses.2 Kings|10|10: Know now that nothing shall fall to the earth of the word of the Lord, which the Lord spoke concerning the house of Ahab: for the Lord has done that which he spoke by his servant Elijah.
verses.2 Kings|10|11: So Jehu slew all that remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his familiar friends, and his priests, until he left him none remaining.
verses.2 Kings|10|12: And he arose and departed, and came to Samaria. And as he was at the shepherds' meeting house in the way,
verses.2 Kings|10|13: Jehu met with the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and said, Who are you? And they answered, We are the brothers of Ahaziah: and we are going down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother.
verses.2 Kings|10|14: And he said, Take them alive. And they took them alive, and slew them at the pit of the meeting house, forty two men; neither left he any of them.
verses.2 Kings|10|15: And when he was departed from there, he came across Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him: and he greeted him, and said to him, Is thy heart right, as my heart is with thy heart? And Jehonadab answered, It is. If it be, said Jehu, give me thy hand. And he gave him his hand; and he took him up to him into the chariot.
verses.2 Kings|10|16: And he said, Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord. So they made him ride in his chariot.
verses.2 Kings|10|17: And when he came to Samaria, he slew all that remained to Ahab in Samaria, till he had destroyed him, according to the saying of the Lord, which he spoke to Elijah.
verses.2 Kings|10|18: And Jehu gathered all the people together, and said to them, Ahab served the Baal a little; but Jehu shall serve him much.
verses.2 Kings|10|19: Now therefore call to me all the prophets of the Baal, all his servants, and all his priests; let none be wanting: for I have a great sacrifice to do to the Baal; whoever shall be missing, he shall not live. But Jehu did it in subtlety, to the intent that he might destroy the worshippers of the Baal.
verses.2 Kings|10|20: And Jehu said, Sanctify a solemn assembly for the Baal. And they proclaimed the day.
verses.2 Kings|10|21: And Jehu sent through all Israel: and all the worshippers of the Baal came, so that there was not a man left that came not. And they came to the house of the Baal; and the house of the Baal was full from one end to another.
verses.2 Kings|10|22: And he said to him that was over the wardrobe, Bring forth garments for all the worshippers of the Baal. And he brought out garments for them.
verses.2 Kings|10|23: And Jehu went, and Jehonadab the son of Rechab, into the house of the Baal, and said to the worshippers of the Baal, Search, and look that there be here with you none of the servants of the Lord, but the worshippers of the Baal only.
verses.2 Kings|10|24: And when they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings, Jehu appointed eighty men outside, and said, If any of the men whom I have brought into your hands escape, his life shall be for the life of him.
verses.2 Kings|10|25: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guard and to the captains, Go in, and slay them; let none come out. And they smote them with the edge of the sword; and the guard and the captains cast them out, and went to the city of the house of the Baal.
verses.2 Kings|10|26: And they brought out the pillars of the house of the Baal, and burned them.
verses.2 Kings|10|27: And they pulled down the pillar of the Baal, and pulled down the house of the Baal, and made it a latrine unto this day.
verses.2 Kings|10|28: Thus Jehu destroyed the Baal out of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|10|29: Nevertheless, from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, namely, the golden calves that were in Beth-el, and that were in Dan.
verses.2 Kings|10|30: And the Lord said to Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in my eyes, and hast done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in my heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|10|31: But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, who made Israel to sin.
verses.2 Kings|10|32: In those days the Lord began to cut off parts of Israel: and Hazael smote them in all the borders of Israel,
verses.2 Kings|10|33: from the Jordan eastwards, all the land of the Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the wadi Arnon, and the Gilead and the Bashan.
verses.2 Kings|10|34: Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|10|35: And Jehu slept with his fathers: and they buried him in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|10|36: And the time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty eight years.
verses.2 Kings|11|1: And when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal seed.
verses.2 Kings|11|2: But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons who were slain, and put him and his nurse in the bed chamber, and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
verses.2 Kings|11|3: And he was with her hid in the house of the Lord six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land.
verses.2 Kings|11|4: And in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the rulers over hundreds of the Carites, with the runners, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord, and made a covenant with them, and laid an oath on them in the house of the Lord, and showed them the king's son.
verses.2 Kings|11|5: And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that you shall do; the third part of you that come in on the sabbath shall be keepers of the watch of the king's house;
verses.2 Kings|11|6: and a third part shall be at the gate of Sur; and a third part at the gate behind the runners: so shall you keep the watch of the house, as a defence.
verses.2 Kings|11|7: And the two divisions of all you that go out on the sabbath, they shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord about the king.
verses.2 Kings|11|8: And you shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand: and he that comes within the ranks, let him be slain: and be with the king as he goes out and as he comes in.
verses.2 Kings|11|9: And the captains over the hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded: and they took every man his men that were to come in on the sabbath, with them that should go out on the sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.2 Kings|11|10: And to the captains over hundreds did the priest give king David's spear and shields, that were in the temple of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|11|11: And the guard stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, round about the king, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and within.
verses.2 Kings|11|12: And he brought out the king's son, and put the crown upon him, and gave him the testimony; and they made him king, and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, Long live the king.
verses.2 Kings|11|13: And when Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she came to the people into the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|11|14: And when she looked, behold, the king stood by a pillar, according to the custom, and the princes and the trumpeters by the king, and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded trumpets: and Athaliah rent her clothes, and cried, Treason, Treason.
verses.2 Kings|11|15: But Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of the hundreds, the officers of the host and said to them, Bring her out between the ranks: and him that follows her kill with the sword. For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|11|16: And they laid hands on her; and she went by the way of the Horse Gate into the king's house: and there was she slain.
verses.2 Kings|11|17: And Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be the Lord's people; between the king also and the people.
verses.2 Kings|11|18: And all the people of the land went into the house of the Baal, and pulled it down; his altars and his images they broke in pieces thoroughly, and slew Mattan the priest of the Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed officers over the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|11|19: And he took the rulers over hundreds, and the Carites, and the runners, and all the people of the land; and they brought down the king from the house of the Lord, and came by the way of the gate of the runners to the king's house. And he sat on the throne of the kings.
verses.2 Kings|11|20: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was in quiet: and they slew Athaliah with the sword in the king's house.
verses.2 Kings|12|1: Seven years old was Jehoash when he began to reign.
verses.2 Kings|12|2: In the seventh year of Jehu Jehoash began to reign; and forty years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zibiah of Beer-sheba.
verses.2 Kings|12|3: And Jehoash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all his days as Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
verses.2 Kings|12|4: But the high places were not taken away: the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
verses.2 Kings|12|5: And Jehoash said to the priests, All the money of the dedicated things which is brought into the house of the Lord, in current money, and the money of persons, by assesment of every man, and all the money that any man is prompted by his heart to bring into the house of the Lord,
verses.2 Kings|12|6: let the priests take it to them, every man from his acquaintance: and let them repair the breaches of the house, wherever any breach shall be found.
verses.2 Kings|12|7: But it happened in the twenty third year of king Jehoash, that the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.
verses.2 Kings|12|8: Then king Jehoash called for Jehoiada the priest, and the other priests, and said to them, Why do you not repair the breaches of the house? now therefore receive no more money of your acquaintances, but deliver it for the breaches of the house.
verses.2 Kings|12|9: And the priests consented to receive no more money of the people, nor to repair the breaches of the house.
verses.2 Kings|12|10: But Jehoiada the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the house of the Lord: and the priests that kept the door put in it all the money that was brought into the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|12|11: And when they saw that there was much money in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest came up, and they tied it in bags, and counted the money that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|12|12: And they gave the money, that was counted, into the hands of them that did the work, that had the oversight of the house of the Lord: and they disbursed it to the carpenters and builders, that worked upon the house of the Lord,
verses.2 Kings|12|13: and to masons, and hewers of stone, and to buy timber and hewn stone to repair the breaches of the house of the Lord, and for all that was laid out for the house to repair it.
verses.2 Kings|12|14: But there were not made for the house of the Lord bowls of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, or any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, from the money that was brought into the house of the Lord:
verses.2 Kings|12|15: for they gave that to the workmen, and they repaired with it the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|12|16: Moreover they did not keep accounts with the men, into whose hand they delivered the money to pay out to the workmen: for they dealt in good faith.
verses.2 Kings|12|17: The money for guilt offerings and the money for sin offerings was not brought into the house of the Lord: it was delivered to the priests.
verses.2 Kings|12|18: Then Hazael king of Syria went up, and fought against Gath, and took it: and Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.2 Kings|12|19: And Jehoash king of Judah took all the hallowed things that Jehoshaphat, and Jehoram and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own hallowed things, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and in the king's house, and sent it to Hazael king of Syria: and he went away from Jerusalem.
verses.2 Kings|12|20: And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.2 Kings|12|21: And his servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and slew Joash in the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.
verses.2 Kings|12|22: For Jozachar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, smote him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|13|1: In the twenty third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned for seventeen years.
verses.2 Kings|13|2: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin; he departed not from that.
verses.2 Kings|13|3: And the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, all their days.
verses.2 Kings|13|4: And Jehoahaz entreated the Lord, and the Lord hearkened to him: for he saw the oppression of Israel because the king of Syria oppressed them.
verses.2 Kings|13|5: (And the Lord gave Israel a deliverer, so that they went out from under the hand of Syria: and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents, as in earlier times.
verses.2 Kings|13|6: Nevertheless they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel to sin, but continued in that; and the ashera remained also in Samaria.)
verses.2 Kings|13|7: Neither did he leave for Jehoahaz a following, except for fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria had destroyed them, and had made them like the dust in threshing.
verses.2 Kings|13|8: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|13|9: And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers; and they buried him in Samaria: and Joash his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|13|10: In the thirty seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned for sixteen years.
verses.2 Kings|13|11: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord; he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin: he continued in that.
verses.2 Kings|13|12: And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|13|13: And Joash slept with his fathers; and Jeroboam sat upon his throne: and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|13|14: Now Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness of which he was to die. And Joash the king of Israel came down to him, and wept over his face, and said, O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
verses.2 Kings|13|15: And Elisha said to him, Take a bow and arrows. And he took for himself a bow and arrows.
verses.2 Kings|13|16: And he said to the king of Israel, Put thy hand upon the bow. And he put his hand upon it: and Elisha put his hands upon the king's hands.
verses.2 Kings|13|17: And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, The arrow of the Lord's deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria: for thou shalt smite Syria in Aphek, till thou have consumed them.
verses.2 Kings|13|18: And he said, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, Smite upon the ground. And he smote three times, and stopped.
verses.2 Kings|13|19: And the man of God was angry with him, and said, Thou shouldst have struck five or six times; then hadst thou smitten Syria till they had been consumed: whereas now thou shalt smite Syria three times.
verses.2 Kings|13|20: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the bands of Moab invaded the land at the coming in of the year.
verses.2 Kings|13|21: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a raiding party; and they cast the man into the tomb of Elisha: and as the man came there, he touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
verses.2 Kings|13|22: And Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.2 Kings|13|23: And the Lord was gracious to them, and had compassion on them, and turned towards them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them; neither has he till now cast them away from his presence.
verses.2 Kings|13|24: So Hazael king of Syria died; and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|13|25: And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took back out of the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael the cities which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Three times did Joash beat him, and recovered the cities of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|14|1: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah reigned.
verses.2 Kings|14|2: He was twenty five years old when he began to reign, and reigned twenty nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
verses.2 Kings|14|3: And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, yet not like David his father: he did according to all things as Joash his father had done.
verses.2 Kings|14|4: But the high places were not taken away: as yet the people sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places.
verses.2 Kings|14|5: And it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in his hand, that he slew his servants who had slain the king his father.
verses.2 Kings|14|6: But the children of the murderers he slew not: according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, wherein the Lord commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
verses.2 Kings|14|7: He slew of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took Selah by war, and called the name of it Joktheel to this day.
verses.2 Kings|14|8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.
verses.2 Kings|14|9: And Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that was in the Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in the Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in the Lebanon, and trampled down the thistle.
verses.2 Kings|14|10: Thou hast indeed smitten Edom, and thy heart has lifted thee up: keep thy glory and stay at home: for why shouldst thou meddle with evil, that thou shouldst fall, thou, and Judah with thee?
verses.2 Kings|14|11: But Amaziah would not hear. Therefore Jehoash king of Israel went up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.2 Kings|14|12: And Judah was beaten before Israel; and they fled every man to their tents.
verses.2 Kings|14|13: And Jehoash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
verses.2 Kings|14|14: And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|14|15: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|14|16: And Jehoash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|14|17: And Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.
verses.2 Kings|14|18: And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.2 Kings|14|19: Now they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem: and he fled to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish, and slew him there.
verses.2 Kings|14|20: And they brought him on horses: and he was buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.2 Kings|14|21: And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amaziah.
verses.2 Kings|14|22: He built Elath, and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.2 Kings|14|23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and he reigned forty one years.
verses.2 Kings|14|24: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
verses.2 Kings|14|25: He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was of Gath-hepher.
verses.2 Kings|14|26: For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel that it was very bitter: for there was not any shut up, nor any left free, nor any helper for Israel.
verses.2 Kings|14|27: For the Lord had not said that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven: but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.
verses.2 Kings|14|28: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath (which had belonged to Judah) for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|14|29: And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel, and Zechariah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|15|1: In the twenty seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah began to reign.
verses.2 Kings|15|2: Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty two years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.
verses.2 Kings|15|3: And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah had done;
verses.2 Kings|15|4: except that the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burnt incense still on the high places.
verses.2 Kings|15|5: And the Lord smote the king, so that he was afflicted with zaraat until the day of his death, and dwelt in the house of immunity. And Jotham the king's son was over the house, judging the people of the land.
verses.2 Kings|15|6: And the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.2 Kings|15|7: So Azariah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|15|8: In the thirty eighth year of Azariah king of Judah did Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six months.
verses.2 Kings|15|9: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
verses.2 Kings|15|10: And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|15|11: And the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|15|12: This was the word of the Lord which he spoke to Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.
verses.2 Kings|15|13: Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|15|14: For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|15|15: And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|15|16: Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and its borders from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the women that were there with child he ripped up.
verses.2 Kings|15|17: In the thirty ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi began to reign over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.
verses.2 Kings|15|18: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
verses.2 Kings|15|19: And Pul the king of Assyria came against the land: and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.
verses.2 Kings|15|20: And Menahem exacted the money from Israel, from all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and stayed not there in the land.
verses.2 Kings|15|21: And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2 Kings|15|22: And Menahem slept with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|15|23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel on Samaria, and reigned two years.
verses.2 Kings|15|24: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
verses.2 Kings|15|25: But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria, in the palace of the king's house, (by Argob and the Arye) and with him fifty men of the Giladim: and he killed him, and reigned in his place.
verses.2 Kings|15|26: And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|15|27: In the fifty second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned twenty years.
verses.2 Kings|15|28: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
verses.2 Kings|15|29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king Assyria came and took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and the Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.
verses.2 Kings|15|30: And Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and smote him, and slew him, and reigned in his stead, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
verses.2 Kings|15|31: And the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|15|32: In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah began to reign.
verses.2 Kings|15|33: He was twenty five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.
verses.2 Kings|15|34: And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord: he did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
verses.2 Kings|15|35: Yet the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burned incense still on the high places. He built the higher gate of the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|15|36: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.2 Kings|15|37: In those days the Lord began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah.
verses.2 Kings|15|38: And Jotham slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|16|1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.
verses.2 Kings|16|2: Twenty years old was Ahaz when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and did not do that which was right in the sight of the Lord his God, like David his father.
verses.2 Kings|16|3: But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and even made his son pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel.
verses.2 Kings|16|4: And he sacrificed and burnt incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.
verses.2 Kings|16|5: Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to war: and they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.
verses.2 Kings|16|6: At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drove the men of Judah from Elath: and the Edomites came to Elath, and dwelt there to this day.
verses.2 Kings|16|7: So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, who have risen against me.
verses.2 Kings|16|8: And Ahaz took the silver and gold that was in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the king's house, and sent it for a present to the king of Assyria.
verses.2 Kings|16|9: And the king of Assyria hearkened to him: for the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, and took it, and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin.
verses.2 Kings|16|10: And king Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and saw an altar that was at Damascus: and king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all its workmanship.
verses.2 Kings|16|11: And Urijah the priest built an altar according to all that king Ahaz had sent from Damascus: so Urijah the priest made it before king Ahaz arrived from Damascus.
verses.2 Kings|16|12: And when the king was come from Damascus, the king saw the altar: and the king drew near to the altar, and offered on it.
verses.2 Kings|16|13: And he burnt his burnt offering and his meal offering, and poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings upon the altar.
verses.2 Kings|16|14: And he brought also the brazen altar, which was before the Lord, from the forefront of the house, from between his altar and the house of the Lord, and put it on the north side of his altar.
verses.2 Kings|16|15: And king Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, Upon the great altar burn the morning burnt offering, and the evening meal offering, and the king's burnt sacrifice, and his meal offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their meal offering, and their drink offerings; and sprinkle upon it all the blood of the burnt offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice: and the brazen altar shall be for me to visit.
verses.2 Kings|16|16: Thus did Urijah the priest, according to all that king Ahaz commanded.
verses.2 Kings|16|17: And king Ahaz cut off the borders of the bases, and removed the laver from off them; and took down the sea from off the brazen oxen that were under it, and put it upon a pavement of stones.
verses.2 Kings|16|18: And the covered passage for the sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king's outer entry, he turned to the house of the Lord because of the king of Assyria.
verses.2 Kings|16|19: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.2 Kings|16|20: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.2 Kings|17|1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in Samaria over Israel, reigning for nine years.
verses.2 Kings|17|2: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him.
verses.2 Kings|17|3: Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents.
verses.2 Kings|17|4: And the king of Assyria found treachery in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.
verses.2 Kings|17|5: Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
verses.2 Kings|17|6: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
verses.2 Kings|17|7: For so it was, when the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
verses.2 Kings|17|8: and walked in the statutes of the nations, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they practised;
verses.2 Kings|17|9: and the children of Israel fabricated matters that were not right against the Lord their God, and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city;
verses.2 Kings|17|10: and they set them up pillars and asherim on every high hill, and under every green tree;
verses.2 Kings|17|11: and there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the heathen whom the Lord carried away before them; and did wicked things to provoke the Lord to anger;
verses.2 Kings|17|12: for they served idols, concerning which the Lord had said to them, You shall not do this thing;
verses.2 Kings|17|13: then the Lord testified against Israel, and against Judah, by all the prophets, and by all the seers, saying, Turn from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets.
verses.2 Kings|17|14: Yet they would not hear, but hardened their necks, like the neck of their fathers, that did not believe in the Lord their God.
verses.2 Kings|17|15: And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified against them; and they followed worthless paths, and became themselves worthless, and went after the nations that were round about them, concerning whom the Lord had charged them, that they should not do like them.
verses.2 Kings|17|16: And they left all the commandments of the Lord their God, and made them molten images, two calves, and made an ashera, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served the Baal.
verses.2 Kings|17|17: And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and gave themselves up to do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
verses.2 Kings|17|18: Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.2 Kings|17|19: Also Judah did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they practised.
verses.2 Kings|17|20: And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out from his face.
verses.2 Kings|17|21: For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drove Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.
verses.2 Kings|17|22: For the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; they departed not from them;
verses.2 Kings|17|23: until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria to this day.
verses.2 Kings|17|24: And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria, in place of the children of Israel: and they took possession of Samaria and dwelt in its cities.
verses.2 Kings|17|25: And at the beginning of their dwelling there, they did not fear the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them, which slew some of them.
verses.2 Kings|17|26: Then they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, The nations which thou hast removed, and placed in the cities of Samaria, know not the law of the God of the land: therefore he has sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they know not the law of the God of the land.
verses.2 Kings|17|27: Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, Carry there one of the priests whom you brought from there; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the law of the God of the land.
verses.2 Kings|17|28: Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Beth-el, and taught them how they should fear the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|17|29: Yet every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities in which they dwelt.
verses.2 Kings|17|30: And the men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,
verses.2 Kings|17|31: and the Avim made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvaim burnt their sons in fire to Adrammelech, and Anammelech, god of Sepharvaim.
verses.2 Kings|17|32: So they feared the Lord, and made to themselves from all ranks of them priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places.
verses.2 Kings|17|33: They feared the Lord, and served their own gods, after the manner of the nations of the countries from which they were carried away.
verses.2 Kings|17|34: Unto this day they do after the former manners: they fear not the Lord, neither do they follow the statutes or the ordinances, or the law and the commandment which the Lord commanded the children of Jacob, whom he named Israel;
verses.2 Kings|17|35: with whom the Lord had made a covenant, and charged them, saying, you shall not fear other gods, nor bow yourselves down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them:
verses.2 Kings|17|36: but the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and a stretched out arm, him shall you fear, and him shall you worship, and to him shall you do sacrifice.
verses.2 Kings|17|37: And the statutes, and the ordinances, and the law, and the commandment, which he wrote for you, you shall be careful to do for all time; and you shall not fear other gods.
verses.2 Kings|17|38: And the covenant that I have made with you shall you not forget; neither shall you fear other gods.
verses.2 Kings|17|39: But the Lord your God shall you fear; and he shall deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.
verses.2 Kings|17|40: Yet they did not hearken, but they did after their former manner.
verses.2 Kings|17|41: So these nations feared the Lord, and served their carved idols, both their children, and their children's children: as their fathers did, so they do to this day.
verses.2 Kings|18|1: Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.
verses.2 Kings|18|2: Twenty five years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name also was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.2 Kings|18|3: And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father did.
verses.2 Kings|18|4: He removed the high places, and broke the pillars, and cut down the ashera, and broke in pieces the brazen serpent that Moses had made: for until that time the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.
verses.2 Kings|18|5: He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those that were before him.
verses.2 Kings|18|6: For he held fast to the Lord, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.2 Kings|18|7: And the Lord was with him; and he prospered wherever he went out: and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not.
verses.2 Kings|18|8: He smote the Philistines, as far as Gaza and its borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
verses.2 Kings|18|9: And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria, and besieged it.
verses.2 Kings|18|10: And at the end of three years they took it: in the sixth year of Hezekiah, that is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
verses.2 Kings|18|11: And the king of Assyria did carry away Israel to Assyria, and put them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes:
verses.2 Kings|18|12: because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord their God, but transgressed his covenant, and all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and would not hear them, nor do them.
verses.2 Kings|18|13: Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.
verses.2 Kings|18|14: And Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, I have offended; withdraw from me: that which thou wilt impose on me I will bear. And the king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah a payment of three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.2 Kings|18|15: And Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the king's house.
verses.2 Kings|18|16: At that time did Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of the Lord, and the pilasters which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid with gold, and gave them to the king of Assyria.
verses.2 Kings|18|17: And the king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great host against Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem. And when they were come up, they came and stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the washers' field.
verses.2 Kings|18|18: And when they had called to the king, there came out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder.
verses.2 Kings|18|19: And Rabshakeh said to them, Speak now to Hezekiah, Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this in which thou trustest?
verses.2 Kings|18|20: Thou sayst, A mere word with the lips will serve as counsel and strength for the war. Now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?
verses.2 Kings|18|21: Now, behold, thou trustest upon the staff of this broken reed, upon Egypt, on which if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him.
verses.2 Kings|18|22: But if you say to me, We trust in the Lord our God: is not that he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has said to Judah and Jerusalem, You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem?
verses.2 Kings|18|23: Now therefore, I pray thee, make a wager with my lord the king of Assyria, and I will deliver thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.
verses.2 Kings|18|24: Why then wilt thou turn away the face of one officer of the least of my master's servants, and put thy trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
verses.2 Kings|18|25: Am I now come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? It is the Lord who said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.
verses.2 Kings|18|26: Then said Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and Shebna, and Joah, to Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, to thy servants in the tongue of Syria; for we understand it: and talk not with us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people that are on the wall.
verses.2 Kings|18|27: But Rabshakeh said to them, Has my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these words? has he not sent me to the men who sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own urine with you?
verses.2 Kings|18|28: Then Rabshakeh stood and cried with a loud voice in the language of Judah, and spoke, saying, Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria:
verses.2 Kings|18|29: thus says the king, Let not Hezekiah deceive you: for he shall not be able to deliver you out of his hand:
verses.2 Kings|18|30: neither let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord, saying, The Lord will surely deliver us, and this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.
verses.2 Kings|18|31: Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus says the king of Assyria, Make an agreement with me and come out to me, and then you may eat every man of his own vine, and every one of his fig tree, and drink every one the waters of his cistern:
verses.2 Kings|18|32: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of oil olive and of honey, that you may live, and not die; and do not hearken to Hezekiah when he entices you, saying, The Lord will deliver us.
verses.2 Kings|18|33: Has any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
verses.2 Kings|18|34: Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? where are the gods Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
verses.2 Kings|18|35: Which of all the gods of the countries, have delivered their country out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?
verses.2 Kings|18|36: But the people held their peace, and answered him not a word: for the king's commandment was, saying, Answer him not.
verses.2 Kings|18|37: Then came Eliakim the son of Hilkiah who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
verses.2 Kings|19|1: And it came to pass, when king Hezekiah heard it, that he rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|19|2: And he sent Eliakim who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
verses.2 Kings|19|3: And they said to him, Thus says Hezekiah, This day is a day of trouble, and of reviling, and blasphemy: for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth.
verses.2 Kings|19|4: It may be the Lord thy God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to taunt the living God; and to revile with words as the Lord thy God has heard: wherefore send up a prayer for the remnant that are left.
verses.2 Kings|19|5: So the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.2 Kings|19|6: And Isaiah said to them, Thus shall you say to your master, Thus says the Lord, Be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
verses.2 Kings|19|7: Behold, I will send another spirit in him, and he shall hear a rumour, and shall return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.
verses.2 Kings|19|8: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah: for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.
verses.2 Kings|19|9: And when he heard say of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, Behold, he is come out to fight against thee: he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.2 Kings|19|10: Thus shall you speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not thy God in whom thou trustest deceive thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.
verses.2 Kings|19|11: Behold, Thou hast heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, by destroying them utterly: and shalt thou be delivered?
verses.2 Kings|19|12: Have their gods delivered those nations which my fathers have destroyed; Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph and the children of Eden who were in Telassar?
verses.2 Kings|19|13: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivah?
verses.2 Kings|19|14: And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them: and Hezekiah went up into the house of the Lord, and spread them before the Lord.
verses.2 Kings|19|15: And Hezekiah prayed before the Lord, and said, O Lord God of Israel who sittest upon the keruvim, Thou art the God, even Thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; Thou hast made heaven and earth.
verses.2 Kings|19|16: Lord, bend Thy ear, and hear: open, Lord, Thy eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, and him he has sent to taunt the living God.
verses.2 Kings|19|17: Of a truth, Lord, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands,
verses.2 Kings|19|18: and have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them.
verses.2 Kings|19|19: Now therefore, O Lord our God, I beseech Thee, save Thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that Thou art the Lord God, even Thou only.
verses.2 Kings|19|20: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.
