verses.Ecclesiastes|1|15: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
verses.Ecclesiastes|1|16: I spoke to my own heart, saying, See, I have acquired great wisdom, surpassing all those who were before me in Jerusalem: for my heart has seen much of wisdom and knowledge.
verses.Ecclesiastes|1|17: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also was a striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|1|18: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increases knowledge increases sorrow.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|1: I said in my heart, Come now, I will try thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also was vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|2: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What does it achieve?
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|3: I sought in my heart to stimulate my body with wine (yet guiding my heart with wisdom;) and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|4: I made great works for myself; I built houses; I planted vineyards:
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|5: I made gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|6: I made pools of water, from which to water a forest of growing trees:
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|7: I acquired male and female servants, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of herds and flocks, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me:
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|8: I gathered also silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces: I acquired men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, women very many.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|9: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|10: And whatever my eyes desired I did not withhold from them; I did not restrain my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|11: Then I looked at all the works that my hands had wrought, and at the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and a striving after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|12: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do who comes after the king? even that which has been already done.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|13: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|14: The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walks in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happens to them all.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|15: Then I said in my heart, As it happens to the fool, so it happens even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|16: For of the wise man as of the fool there is no enduring remembrance; seeing that which now is, shall, in the days to come, be entirely forgotten. And how does the wise man die? just like the fool.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|17: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me: for all is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|18: And I hated all my labour in which I had laboured under the sun: because I must leave it to the man who shall come after me.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|19: And who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour in which I have laboured, and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|20: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|21: For there is a man whose labour is with wisdom, and with knowledge, and with skill; yet he must leave it for a portion to a man who has not laboured in it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|22: For what has a man of all his labour, and of the striving of his heart, in which he labours under the sun?
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|23: For all his days are pains, and his work is a vexation; even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|24: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour; but this also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|25: For who can eat, or who can enjoy pleasure, more than I?
verses.Ecclesiastes|2|26: Surely he gives to a man that is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and heaping up, that he may give it to one who is good before God. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|1: To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|2: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|3: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|4: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|5: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|6: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|7: a time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|8: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|9: What profit has the worker from his toil?
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|10: I have seen the task, which God has given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|11: He has made every thing beautiful in his time: also he has set the mystery of the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work which God has made from the beginning to the end.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|12: I know that there is nothing better for them, than to rejoice, and to do good in his life:
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|13: also that it is the gift of God that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|14: I know that, whatever God does, it shall be forever: nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it: and God does it, so that men should fear before him.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|15: That which is, already has been; and that which is to be has already been; and only God can find the fleeting moment.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|16: And moreover I saw under the sun in the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|17: I said in my heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|18: I said in my heart, after the speech of the sons of men, that God has chosen them out, but only to see that they themselves are but as beasts;
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|19: that that which befalls the sons of men befalls the beasts; even one thing befalls them both: as the one dies, so the other dies; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man has no preeminence over a beast: for all is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|20: All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust.
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|21: Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upwards, and the spirit of the beast goes downwards to the earth?
verses.Ecclesiastes|3|22: So I saw that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his work; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|1: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|2: So I praised the dead that are already dead more than the living that are yet alive;
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|3: but better than both of them is he who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|4: Again, I considered all labour, and every skill in work, that it comes from a man's rivalry with his neighbour. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|5: The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|6: Better is a handful with quietness, than both the hands full of labour and striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|7: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|8: There is one alone, without a companion; yea, he has neither son nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches: he may say, For whom then do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity; indeed, it is a sorry business.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|9: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|10: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls; for he has not another to help him up.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|11: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth: but how can one be warm alone?
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|12: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; but a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|13: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who no longer knows how to take care of himself.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|14: For out of prison one came forth to reign; whilst another in his royal power may become poor.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|15: I saw all the living who wander under the sun – they were with the second child who was to rise up in his stead.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|16: There is no end of all the people who come to acclaim the one who goes before them: yet they who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|4|17: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; to draw near to hearken is better than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|1: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|2: For a dream comes through a multitude of business; and a fool's voice is known by a multitude of words.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|3: When thou vowest a vow to God, do not defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|4: Better is it that thou shouldst not vow, than that thou shouldst vow and not pay.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|5: Do not let thy mouth cause thy flesh to sin; nor say before the angel, that it was an error: why should God be angry at thy voice and destroy the work of thy hands?
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|6: For this comes from the multitude of dreams and vanities and many words: but fear thou God.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|7: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and the violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel at the matter: for there is a high one who watches over him that is high; and there are yet higher ones over them.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|8: Moreover, land has an advantage for everyone: he who tills a field is a king.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|9: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|10: When goods increase, they who eat them are increased: and what good is there to their owner, saving the beholding of them with his eyes?
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|11: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the repletion of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|12: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for their owner to his hurt.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|13: But those riches perish by evil adventure: and he begets a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|14: As he came forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and he shall take nothing for his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|15: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit has he that labours for the wind?
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|16: All his days also he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and sickness and wrath.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|17: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour in which he toils under the sun all the days of his life, which God gives him: for it is his portion.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|18: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.
verses.Ecclesiastes|5|19: For he shall remember that the days of his life are not many, in which God provides him with the joy of his heart.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|1: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon men:
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|2: a man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God does not give him power to eat of it but a stranger eats it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|3: If a man begets a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not content with the good, and also that he has no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|4: For it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|5: Moreover it has not seen the sun, nor known anything: this has more comfort than the other.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|6: For though he live a thousand years twice told, yet he has seen no good: do not all go to one place?
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|7: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|8: For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? what has the poor man who knows how to make his way among the living?
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|9: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|10: That which has been was named long ago, and it is known that it is but man: nor may he contend with one who is mightier than he.
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|11: Seeing there are many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
verses.Ecclesiastes|6|12: For who knows what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|1: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|2: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|3: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made glad.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|7: Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; and a bribe destroys the heart.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|8: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning of it: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|9: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|10: Do not say, How was it that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|12: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom gives life to those who have it.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|13: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|15: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his wickedness.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|16: Be not righteous overmuch; nor make thyself overwise: why shouldst thou destroy thyself?
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|17: Be not wicked overmuch, nor be foolish: why shouldst thou die before thy time?
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|18: It is good that thou shouldst take hold of this; but do not withdraw thy hand from that either: for he that fears God performs them all.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|19: Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten rulers who are in a city.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|20: For there is not a just man upon earth, that does good, and sins not.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|21: Also take no heed to all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|22: for oftentimes also thy own heart knows that thou thyself hast likewise cursed others.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|23: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|24: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|25: I cast about in my mind to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly and foolishness which is madness:
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|26: and I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands are fetters: he who pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|27: Behold, this have I found, says Koheleth, counting one thing to another, to find out the sum,
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|28: which yet my soul seeks, but I have not found it: One man among a thousand I have found; but a woman among all those I have not found.
verses.Ecclesiastes|7|29: Lo, this only have I found, that God has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|1: Who is like the wise man? and who knows the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face is changed.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|2: I counsel thee to keep the king's commandment, and that in the manner of an oath of God.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|3: Be not hasty to go out of his presence: stand not in an evil thing; for he does whatever pleases him.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|4: For the word of a king has authority: and who may say to him, What doest thou?
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|5: He who keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerns both time and method.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|6: For every matter has its time and method, though the misery of man is great upon him.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|7: For he knows not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|8: There is no man who has power over the wind to retain the wind; nor has he power over the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; nor shall wickedness deliver those who are given up to it.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|9: All this have I seen, and have appointed my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when one man rules over another to his own hurt.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|10: And so I saw the wicked buried, and come to their rest; but those who had done right were gone from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city: this also is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|11: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|12: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with those who fear God, who fear before him:
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|13: but it shall not be well with the wicked, and, like the shadow, he will not prolong his days; because he does not fear before God.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|14: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are just men, to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked; again, there are wicked men, to whom it happens according to the deeds of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|15: So I commend mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall accompany him in his labour during the days of his life, which God gives him under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|16: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (how one sees no sleep with one's eyes either by day or by night;)
verses.Ecclesiastes|8|17: then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; furthermore; though a wise man think to know it, yet he shall not be able to find it.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|1: For all this I laid to my heart, and sought to clarify all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their deeds, are in the hand of God: no man knows whether love or hatred is in store: all is before them.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|2: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him who sacrifices, and to him who does not sacrifice: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he who swears, as he who fears an oath.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|3: This is an evil in all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|4: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|5: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know nothing, nor do they have any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|6: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now long perished; nor have they any more a portion forever in any thing that is done under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|7: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted thy works.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|8: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no oil.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|9: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he has given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labour in which thou dost labour under the sun.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|10: Whatever thy hand finds to do, do it with thy strength, for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, whither thou goest.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|11: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happens to them all.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|12: For man also knows not his time: like the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and like the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|13: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|14: there was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great siegeworks against it:
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|15: now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom saved the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|16: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|17: The words of wise men heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.
verses.Ecclesiastes|9|18: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|1: Dead flies cause the perfumer's ointment to give off a foul odour: so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honour.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|2: A wise man's heart inclines him to his right hand: but a fool's heart to his left.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|3: Yea also, when a fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he reveals to everyone that he is a fool.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|4: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, do not leave thy place; for deference appeases great offences.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|5: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, when an error proceeds from the ruler:
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|6: folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|7: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|8: He who digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoever breaks through a hedge, a snake shall bite him.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|9: He who removes stones shall be hurt by them; and he who chops wood shall be endangered by that.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|10: If the iron is blunt, and one does not whet the edge, then he must put to more strength: but wisdom increases skill.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|11: If the serpent bites and cannot be charmed, then there is no advantage in a charmer.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|12: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is grievous madness.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|14: A fool also multiplies words: yet no man can tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|15: The labour of fools wearies himself; for he does not know to get to the city.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|16: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes dine in the morning!
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|17: Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is a man of dignity, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|18: By much slothfulness the beams collapse; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|19: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life joyful: and money answers all things.
verses.Ecclesiastes|10|20: Do not curse the king, no, not even in thy thought; and do not curse the rich even in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the sky shall carry the sound, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|1: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|2: Give a portion to seven, and even to eight; for thou knowst not what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|3: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree falls towards the south, or towards the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|4: He who observes the wind shall not sow; and he who regards the clouds shall not reap.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|5: As thou knowst not what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowst not the works of God who makes all.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|6: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening do not withhold thy hand: for thou knowst not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|7: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|8: for if a man live many years, let him rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|9: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thy eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.Ecclesiastes|11|10: Therefore remove vexation from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|1: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|2: before the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain:
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|3: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows are dimmed,
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|4: and the doors are shut in the street, when the sound of the grinding is low, and one starts up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music are brought low;
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|5: when they are also afraid of that which is high, and terrors are in the way, and the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caperberry fails; because the man goes to his eternal home, and the mourners go about the streets;
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|6: before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is shattered, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern;
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|7: and the dust returns to the earth as it was: and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|8: Vanity of vanities, says Koheleth; all is vanity.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|9: And besides being wise, Koheleth also taught the people knowledge; for he weighed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|10: Koheleth sought to find out acceptable words: and words of truth written in proper form.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|11: The words of the wise are like spurs, and like nails well driven in are the sayings of the masters of collections; they are given by one shepherd.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|12: And furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|13: The end of the matter, when all is said and done: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for that is the whole duty of man.
verses.Ecclesiastes|12|14: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
verses.Song of Songs|1|1: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
verses.Song of Songs|1|2: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.
verses.Song of Songs|1|3: Thy ointments are fragrant; for thy flowing oil thou art renowned: therefore do the virgins love thee.
verses.Song of Songs|1|4: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king has brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will praise thy love more than wine: sincerely they love thee.
verses.Song of Songs|1|5: I am black, but comely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
verses.Song of Songs|1|6: Do not gaze upon me, because I am black, because the sun has scorched me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but my own vineyard I have not kept.
verses.Song of Songs|1|7: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loves, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be like one who cloaks himself by the flocks of thy companions?
verses.Song of Songs|1|8: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids besides the shepherds' tents.
verses.Song of Songs|1|9: I compare thee, O my love, to a mare of the chariots of Pharaoh.
verses.Song of Songs|1|10: Thy cheeks would be comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with strings of beads.
verses.Song of Songs|1|11: We will make thee necklets of gold studded with silver.
verses.Song of Songs|1|12: While the king was reclining at his board, my nard sent forth its fragrance.
verses.Song of Songs|1|13: My wellbeloved is to me a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts.
verses.Song of Songs|1|14: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna in the vineyards of En-gedi.
verses.Song of Songs|1|15: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.
verses.Song of Songs|1|16: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our couch is green.
verses.Song of Songs|1|17: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters are of cypress.
verses.Song of Songs|2|1: I am the tulip of the Sharon; the daffodil of the vallies.
verses.Song of Songs|2|2: Like the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
verses.Song of Songs|2|3: Like the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.Song of Songs|2|4: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
verses.Song of Songs|2|5: Let me lean against the stout trunks, let me couch among the apple trees: for I am sick with love.
verses.Song of Songs|2|6: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
verses.Song of Songs|2|7: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till it please.
verses.Song of Songs|2|8: The voice of my beloved! behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
verses.Song of Songs|2|9: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young hart: behold, he stands behind our wall, he looks in at the windows; he peers through the lattice.
verses.Song of Songs|2|10: My beloved spoke, and said to me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.Song of Songs|2|11: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
verses.Song of Songs|2|12: the flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing bird is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
verses.Song of Songs|2|13: the fig tree puts forth her green figs, and the vines in blossom give their scent. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.Song of Songs|2|14: O my dove, who art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the cliff, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
verses.Song of Songs|2|15: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vineyards: for our vineyards are in blossom.
verses.Song of Songs|2|16: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feeds among the lilies.
verses.Song of Songs|2|17: Before the day cools, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a gazelle or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
verses.Song of Songs|3|1: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.Song of Songs|3|2: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.Song of Songs|3|3: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Have you seen him whom my soul loves?
verses.Song of Songs|3|4: Scarce had I passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her who conceived me.
verses.Song of Songs|3|5: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till it please.
verses.Song of Songs|3|6: Who is this coming out of the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
verses.Song of Songs|3|7: Behold it is his litter, that of Solomon! sixty valiant men are round about it, of the mighty men of Israel.
verses.Song of Songs|3|8: All girt with swords, and expert in war: every man has his sword upon his thigh because of the fear by night.
verses.Song of Songs|3|9: King Solomon made himself a palanquin of the timbers of the Lebanon.
verses.Song of Songs|3|10: He made its pillars of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple, the midst of it being inlaid lovingly, by the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.Song of Songs|3|11: Go forth, O daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, and on the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.Song of Songs|4|1: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes behind thy veil: thy hair is like a flock of goats, that cascade down from mount Gilead.
verses.Song of Songs|4|2: Thy teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes, which came up from the washing; all of which bear twins, and none of them miscarries.
verses.Song of Songs|4|3: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy mouth is comely: thy cheek is like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.
verses.Song of Songs|4|4: Thy neck is like the tower of David built with turrets, on which there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
verses.Song of Songs|4|5: Thy two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, which feed among the lilies.
verses.Song of Songs|4|6: Before the day cools, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
verses.Song of Songs|4|7: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no blemish in thee.
verses.Song of Songs|4|8: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
verses.Song of Songs|4|9: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my bride; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thy eyes, with one link of thy necklace.
verses.Song of Songs|4|10: How fair is thy love, my sister, my bride! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thy ointments than all spices!
verses.Song of Songs|4|11: Thy lips, O my bride, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the scent of thy garments is like the scent of Lebanon.
verses.Song of Songs|4|12: A garden enclosed is my sister, my bride; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
verses.Song of Songs|4|13: Thy shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits, henna and nard.
verses.Song of Songs|4|14: Nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
verses.Song of Songs|4|15: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
verses.Song of Songs|4|16: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat its choicest fruits.
verses.Song of Songs|5|1: I am come into my garden, my sister, my bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O dear ones, and drink; drink deep, O loving companions.
verses.Song of Songs|5|2: I sleep, but my heart wakes: hark, my beloved is knocking, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
verses.Song of Songs|5|3: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I soil them?
verses.Song of Songs|5|4: My beloved put in his hand by the latchet of the door, and my heart was thrilled for him.
verses.Song of Songs|5|5: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with flowing myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
verses.Song of Songs|5|6: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had turned away, and was gone: my soul failed when he spoke: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
verses.Song of Songs|5|7: The watchmen who went about the city found me, they struck me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.Song of Songs|5|8: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him, that I am sick with love.
verses.Song of Songs|5|9: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
verses.Song of Songs|5|10: My beloved is white and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.
verses.Song of Songs|5|11: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are wavy, and black as a raven.
verses.Song of Songs|5|12: His eyes are like doves by the water courses, washed with milk, and fitly set.
verses.Song of Songs|5|13: His cheeks are like a bed of spices, like banks of fragrant flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping flowing myrrh.
verses.Song of Songs|5|14: His hands are like rods of gold set with emeralds: his belly is polished ivory overlaid with sapphires.
verses.Song of Songs|5|15: His legs are pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is like the Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.Song of Songs|5|16: His mouth is most sweet: and he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.Song of Songs|6|1: Where is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? where has thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
verses.Song of Songs|6|2: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.Song of Songs|6|3: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feeds among the lilies.
verses.Song of Songs|6|4: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
verses.Song of Songs|6|5: Turn away thy eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is like a flock of goats cascading down from Gilead.
verses.Song of Songs|6|6: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, of which all bear twins, and not one of them miscarries.
verses.Song of Songs|6|7: As a piece of a pomegranate is thy cheek within thy veil.
verses.Song of Songs|6|8: There are sixty queens, and eighty concubines and young women without number.
verses.Song of Songs|6|9: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her happy; and the queens and the concubines praised her.
verses.Song of Songs|6|10: Who is she that looks out like the dawn, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
verses.Song of Songs|6|11: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine had blossomed, whether the pomegranates were in flower.
verses.Song of Songs|6|12: Without my knowing it, my soul set me among the chariots of a princely people.
verses.Song of Songs|7|1: Return return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will you see in the Shulamite? as it were the dance at Mahanaim.
verses.Song of Songs|7|2: How beautiful are thy feet in sandals, O prince's daughter! thy rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of an artist.
verses.Song of Songs|7|3: Thy navel is like a round goblet, that never lacks blended wine: thy belly is like a heap of wheat set about with lilies.
verses.Song of Songs|7|4: Thy two breasts are like two fawns, the twins of a gazelle.
verses.Song of Songs|7|5: Thy neck is like a tower of ivory; thy eyes like the pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose is like the tower of the Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
verses.Song of Songs|7|6: Thy head upon thee is like the Carmel, and the hair of thy head like purple: a king is caught in its tresses.
verses.Song of Songs|7|7: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
verses.Song of Songs|7|8: This thy stature is like a palm tree, and thy breasts are like clusters of grapes.
verses.Song of Songs|7|9: I said, I will go up into the palm tree, I will take hold of its boughs: may thy breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the scent of thy countenance like apples;
verses.Song of Songs|7|10: and the roof of thy mouth like the best wine, that goes down sweetly for my beloved, causing the sleepers' lips to murmur.
verses.Song of Songs|7|11: I am my beloved's, and his desire is towards me.
verses.Song of Songs|7|12: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
verses.Song of Songs|7|13: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine has flowered, if the grape blossoms have opened, if the pomegranates are in flower: there will I give thee my loves.
verses.Song of Songs|7|14: The mandrakes give a fragrance, and at our gates are all manner of choice fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
verses.Song of Songs|8|1: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee outside, I would kiss thee; and none would scorn me.
verses.Song of Songs|8|2: I would lead thee, and bring thee into the house of my mother who brought me up: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.
verses.Song of Songs|8|3: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
verses.Song of Songs|8|4: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that you stir not up, nor awaken my love, until it please.
verses.Song of Songs|8|5: Who is that, coming up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I roused thee under the apple tree: there thy mother was in travail with thee: there she who bore thee was in travail.
verses.Song of Songs|8|6: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as Sheol: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which have a most vehement flame.
verses.Song of Songs|8|7: Many waters cannot quench love, nor can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would be utterly scorned.
verses.Song of Songs|8|8: We have a little sister, and she has no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
verses.Song of Songs|8|9: If she be a wall, we will build upon her a battlement of silver: and if she be a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
verses.Song of Songs|8|10: I was a wall, and my breasts were like towers: then was I in his eyes as one who finds content.
verses.Song of Songs|8|11: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard to keepers; everyone for its fruit was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.
verses.Song of Songs|8|12: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: thou, O Solomon, may have the thousand, and those that keep its fruit two hundred.
verses.Song of Songs|8|13: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken for thy voice: cause me to hear it.
verses.Song of Songs|8|14: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like a gazelle or a young hart upon the mountains of spices.
verses.Isaiah|1|1: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.Isaiah|1|2: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: I have reared and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
verses.Isaiah|1|3: The ox knows his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel does not know, my people does not consider.
verses.Isaiah|1|4: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that deal corruptly: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger, they are gone away backward.
verses.Isaiah|1|5: Where could you still be smitten, that you revolt again: every head is sick, and every heart faint.
verses.Isaiah|1|6: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrefying sores: they have not been pressed, neither bound up, nor mollified with oil.
verses.Isaiah|1|7: Your country is desolate, your cities are burned with fire: as for your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as though overthrown by strangers.
verses.Isaiah|1|8: And the daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, like a besieged city.
verses.Isaiah|1|9: If the Lord of hosts had not left us a very small remnant, we should have been like Sodom, and we should have been like Gomorrah.
verses.Isaiah|1|10: Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; give ear to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah.
verses.Isaiah|1|11: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? says the Lord: I am sated with the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.
verses.Isaiah|1|12: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?
verses.Isaiah|1|13: Bring no more vain offerings; incense of abomination they are to me; as for new moons and sabbaths and the calling of assemblies, I cannot bear iniquity along with solemn meeting.
verses.Isaiah|1|14: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates: they are a trouble to me; I am weary of enduring them.
verses.Isaiah|1|15: And when you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you: even when you make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.
verses.Isaiah|1|16: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil;
verses.Isaiah|1|17: learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
verses.Isaiah|1|18: Come now, and let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins be like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be white as wool.
verses.Isaiah|1|19: If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land:
verses.Isaiah|1|20: but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it.
verses.Isaiah|1|21: How is the faithful city become a harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.
verses.Isaiah|1|22: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine is mixed with water:
verses.Isaiah|1|23: thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loves bribes, and follows after rewards: they judge not the fatherless neither does the cause of the widow reach them.
verses.Isaiah|1|24: Therefore says the Master, the Lord of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of my adversaries, and avenge me of my enemies:
verses.Isaiah|1|25: and I will turn my hand against thee, and purge away thy dross as with lye, and take away all thy base alloy.
verses.Isaiah|1|26: And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterwards thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, a faithful city.
verses.Isaiah|1|27: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and those that return to her with righteousness.
verses.Isaiah|1|28: And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.
verses.Isaiah|1|29: For they shall be ashamed of the sacred oaks on which you set your desire, and you shall be confounded on account of the gardens of idolatry that you did choose.
verses.Isaiah|1|30: For you shall be like an oak whose leave are fading, and like a garden that has no water.
verses.Isaiah|1|31: And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.
verses.Isaiah|2|1: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|2|2: And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all the nations shall flow unto it.
verses.Isaiah|2|3: And many people shall go and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|2|4: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall decide among many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
verses.Isaiah|2|5: O house of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.
verses.Isaiah|2|6: For thou hast abandoned thy people, the house of Jacob; for they are replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers.
verses.Isaiah|2|7: Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots:
verses.Isaiah|2|8: their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made:
verses.Isaiah|2|9: and the mean man is bowed down, and the great man is brought low; forgive them not.
verses.Isaiah|2|10: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty.
verses.Isaiah|2|11: The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day.
verses.Isaiah|2|12: For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up that he shall be brought low:
verses.Isaiah|2|13: and upon all the cedars of the Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of the Bashan,
verses.Isaiah|2|14: and upon all the high mountains, and upon all the lofty hills,
verses.Isaiah|2|15: and upon every high tower, and upon every fortified wall,
verses.Isaiah|2|16: and upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all delightful craftsmanship.
verses.Isaiah|2|17: And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be made low: and the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day.
verses.Isaiah|2|18: And the idols shall utterly be abolished.
verses.Isaiah|2|19: And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth terribly.
verses.Isaiah|2|20: In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which had been made for him to worship, to the moles and to the bats;
verses.Isaiah|2|21: to go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the crevices of the ragged rocks, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth terribly.
verses.Isaiah|2|22: Cease from man, though his breath be in his nostrils: for in what is he to be accounted of?
verses.Isaiah|3|1: For, behold, the Master, the Lord of hosts, takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water,
verses.Isaiah|3|2: the mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the diviner, and the elder,
verses.Isaiah|3|3: the captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.
verses.Isaiah|3|4: And I will make youngsters their princes, and babes shall rule over them.
verses.Isaiah|3|5: And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the elder, and the base against the honourable.
verses.Isaiah|3|6: When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand:
verses.Isaiah|3|7: in that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.
verses.Isaiah|3|8: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his glory.
verses.Isaiah|3|9: The show of their countenance witnesses against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they cannot hide it. Woe to their soul! for they have requited evil to themselves.
verses.Isaiah|3|10: Say of the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.
verses.Isaiah|3|11: Alas! it shall be ill with the wicked: for according to the deserving of his hands shall be done to him.
verses.Isaiah|3|12: As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they that lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.
verses.Isaiah|3|13: The Lord stands up to plead, and stands to judge the people.
verses.Isaiah|3|14: The Lord will enter into judgment with the elders of his people, and its princes, saying, It is you who have eaten up the vineyard; the robbery of the poor is in your houses.
verses.Isaiah|3|15: What mean you by crushing my people to pieces, and grinding the faces of the poor? says the Lord God of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|3|16: Moreover the Lord says, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with outstretched necks and ogling eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:
verses.Isaiah|3|17: therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will lay bare their secret parts.
verses.Isaiah|3|18: In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of the anklets, and the tiaras, and the necklaces,
verses.Isaiah|3|19: the eardrops, and the bracelets, and the scarves,
verses.Isaiah|3|20: the bonnets, and the armbands, and the belts, and the perfume boxes, and the amulets,
verses.Isaiah|3|22: the cloaks, and the mantles, and the gowns, and the handbags,
verses.Isaiah|3|23: the gauze, and the fine linen, and the hoods, and the veils.
verses.Isaiah|3|24: And it shall come to pass, that instead of a sweet smell there shall be a stench; and instead of a girdle a rope; and instead of well set hair, baldness; and instead of a fine dress a girding of sackcloth; instead of beauty, a brand.
verses.Isaiah|3|25: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war,
verses.Isaiah|3|26: and her gates shall both lament and mourn; and she being desolate shall sit upon the ground.
verses.Isaiah|4|1: And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name; take away our reproach.
verses.Isaiah|4|2: In that day shall the plant of the Lord be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|4|3: And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, every one in Jerusalem that is written to life:
verses.Isaiah|4|4: when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
verses.Isaiah|4|5: And the Lord will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall there be a canopy.
verses.Isaiah|4|6: And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain.
verses.Isaiah|5|1: Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved concerning his vineyard. My wellbeloved had a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:
verses.Isaiah|5|2: and he dug it, and cleared away its stones, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also hewed out a wine vat in it: and he looked that it should bring forth good grapes, but it brought forth bad grapes.
verses.Isaiah|5|3: And now, O inhabitant of Jerusalem, and man of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard.
verses.Isaiah|5|4: What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done it? why was it, when I looked that it should bring forth good grapes, that it brought forth bad grapes?
verses.Isaiah|5|5: And now; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it shall be eaten up; and break down its wall, and it shall be trodden down:
verses.Isaiah|5|6: and I will lay it waste: it shall be neither pruned, nor hoed; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they drop no rain upon it.
verses.Isaiah|5|7: For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.
verses.Isaiah|5|8: Woe to them that join house to house, that lay field to field till there is no room, that you may dwell alone in the midst of the earth!
verses.Isaiah|5|9: In my ears said the Lord of hosts, Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, great and fair, without inhabitant.
verses.Isaiah|5|10: For ten acres of vineyard shall yield the measure of a bat, and the seed of a homer shall yield one efa.
verses.Isaiah|5|11: Woe to them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!
verses.Isaiah|5|12: And the lyre, and the lute, the tambourine, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the Lord, neither consider the operation of his hands.
verses.Isaiah|5|13: Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst.
verses.Isaiah|5|14: Therefore Sheol has enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that is joyful, shall go down into it.
verses.Isaiah|5|15: And the mean man shall be brought down, and the mighty man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be brought low.
verses.Isaiah|5|16: But the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in the judgment, and God that is holy shall be sanctified in righteousness.
verses.Isaiah|5|17: Then shall the lambs feed as in their pasture, and fat ones and strangers shall feed in the ruins.
verses.Isaiah|5|18: Woe to them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope:
verses.Isaiah|5|19: that say, Let him make speed, and hasten his work, that we may see it: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!
verses.Isaiah|5|20: Woe to them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
verses.Isaiah|5|21: Woe to them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
verses.Isaiah|5|22: Woe to them that are mighty to drink wine, and warriors to mingle strong drink:
verses.Isaiah|5|23: who justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!
verses.Isaiah|5|24: Therefore as the fire devours the stubble, and as the chaff is consumed on the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they have cast away the law of the Lord of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|5|25: Therefore the anger of the Lord burns against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against them, and has smitten them; and the hills did tremble, and their dead bodies, were as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.Isaiah|5|26: And he will lift up a banner to the nations from far, and will whistle to them from the ends of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly:
verses.Isaiah|5|27: none shall be weary or stumble among them; none shall slumber or sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:
verses.Isaiah|5|28: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like the whirlwind:
verses.Isaiah|5|29: their roaring shall be like a lion, they shall shout and roar like young lions: and shall lay hold of the prey, and carry it away safe, and none shall deliver it.
verses.Isaiah|5|30: And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea: and if one look to the land, behold narrow darkness: the light also is darkened in its heavens.
verses.Isaiah|6|1: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
verses.Isaiah|6|2: seraphim stood above him: each one had six wings; with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he did fly.
verses.Isaiah|6|3: And one cried to another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
verses.Isaiah|6|4: And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
verses.Isaiah|6|5: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am ruined; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|6|6: Then one of the serafim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with tongs from off the altar:
verses.Isaiah|6|7: and he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this has touched thy lips; and thy iniquity is taken away, and thy sin is purged.
verses.Isaiah|6|8: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
verses.Isaiah|6|9: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear indeed, but understand not; and see indeed, but perceive not.
verses.Isaiah|6|10: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and smear over their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and return, and be healed.
verses.Isaiah|6|11: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate,
verses.Isaiah|6|12: and the Lord has removed men far away, and there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.
verses.Isaiah|6|13: And if one tenth remain in it, then that shall again be consumed: but like a terebinth and like an oak, whose stump remains when they cast their leaves, so the holy seed is its immovable stump.
verses.Isaiah|7|1: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
verses.Isaiah|7|2: And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest are moved with the wind.
verses.Isaiah|7|3: Then said the Lord to Isaiah, Go out now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy son, at the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool in the highway of the washers' field;
verses.Isaiah|7|4: and say to him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted on account of the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
verses.Isaiah|7|5: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee, saying,
verses.Isaiah|7|6: Let us go up against Judah, and harass it, and let us make a breach in it for us, and set a king in the midst of it, namely the son of Tabeal:
verses.Isaiah|7|7: thus says the Lord God, It shall not stand; neither shall it come to pass.
verses.Isaiah|7|8: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within sixty five years Ephraim shall be broken in pieces, and no more a people.
verses.Isaiah|7|9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you have no faith you shall not be established.
verses.Isaiah|7|10: Moreover the Lord spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
verses.Isaiah|7|11: Ask a sign of the Lord thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.
verses.Isaiah|7|12: But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I try the Lord.
verses.Isaiah|7|13: And he said, Hear now, O house of David; Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will you weary my God also?
verses.Isaiah|7|14: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, the virgin is with child, and she will bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
verses.Isaiah|7|15: Butter and honey shall he eat, when he shall know how to refuse the evil, and choose the good.
verses.Isaiah|7|16: For before the child shall know how to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land whose two kings thou dreadest shall be deserted.
verses.Isaiah|7|17: The Lord shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father's house, days that have not come since the day that Ephraim departed from Judah; namely the king of Assyria.
verses.Isaiah|7|18: And it shall come to pass on that day, that the Lord shall whistle to the fly that is in the uttermost end of the canals of Egypt, and to the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
verses.Isaiah|7|19: And they shall come, and shall rest all of them in the desolate wadis, and in the holes of the rocks, and upon all thorns, and upon all branches.
verses.Isaiah|7|20: On the same day shall the Lord shave with a hired razor that is hired (namely with them beyond the river with the king of Assyria) the head, and the hair of the legs: and it shall also sweep away the beard.
verses.Isaiah|7|21: And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man shall nourish a young cow, and two sheep;
verses.Isaiah|7|22: and it shall come to pass, from the abundance of milk that they shall give he shall eat butter: for butter and honey shall every one eat that is left in the land.
verses.Isaiah|7|23: And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place shall be, where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand silver shekels, it shall be for briers and thorns.
verses.Isaiah|7|24: With the arrows and with the bow shall men come there; because all the land shall become briers and thorns.
verses.Isaiah|7|25: And on all hills that are hoed with the hoe, thou shalt not come there for fear of briers and thorns: but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of sheep.
verses.Isaiah|8|1: Moreover the Lord said to me, Take a great roll, and write on it with a common pen, The spoil speeds; the prey hastens.
verses.Isaiah|8|2: And I took to myself faithful witnesses namely Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.
verses.Isaiah|8|3: And I came near to the prophetess; and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz (the spoil speeds; the prey hastens).
verses.Isaiah|8|4: For before the child shall know how to cry, My father, and my mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.
verses.Isaiah|8|5: And the Lord spoke to me again, saying,
verses.Isaiah|8|6: Since this people refuses the water of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoices in Rezin and the son of Remaliah.
verses.Isaiah|8|7: Now therefore, behold, the Lord brings up upon them the waters of the river, strong and abundant, namely the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks:
verses.Isaiah|8|8: and he shall sweep through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.
verses.Isaiah|8|9: Be broken up you peoples, and be dismayed; and give ear, all you of far countries: gird yourselves, and you shall be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, and you shall be broken in pieces.
verses.Isaiah|8|10: Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.
verses.Isaiah|8|11: For the Lord spoke thus to me with a strong hand, and warned me that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying,
verses.Isaiah|8|12: Say not, it is a conspiracy, to all of which this people shall say, call a conspiracy; neither hear their fear, nor be afraid.
verses.Isaiah|8|13: Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.
verses.Isaiah|8|14: And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a trap and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|8|15: And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.
verses.Isaiah|8|16: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.
verses.Isaiah|8|17: And I will wait upon the Lord, that hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope for him.
verses.Isaiah|8|18: Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me are for signs and for portents in Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwells in mount Zion.
verses.Isaiah|8|19: And when they shall say to you, Consult the mediums, and the wizards that chirp, and that mutter: shall not a people seek their God? why seek the living among the dead,
verses.Isaiah|8|20: for law and for testimony? Surely they will speak according to this word which has no profit in it.
verses.Isaiah|8|21: And they shall pass through it, greatly distressed and hungry: and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, and look upward.
verses.Isaiah|8|22: And they shall look to the earth; and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish; and they shall be driven into darkness.
verses.Isaiah|8|23: For there is no weariness to him that is set against her; at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun, and the land of Naphtali and afterwards he afflicted her more grievously by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan in the Galilee of the nations.
verses.Isaiah|9|1: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, upon them has the light shone.
verses.Isaiah|9|2: Thou hast multiplied the nation, and increased their joy: they joy before Thee according to the joy in harvest, and as men rejoice when they divide the spoil.
verses.Isaiah|9|3: For Thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian.
verses.Isaiah|9|4: For every shoe of the stormy warrior and every garment rolled in blood shall be burnt as fuel of fire.
verses.Isaiah|9|5: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given: and the government is upon his shoulder: and his name is called Wonderful Counselor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
verses.Isaiah|9|6: for the increase of the realm and for peace without end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice: from henceforth for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts performs this.
verses.Isaiah|9|7: The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it will descend upon Israel.
verses.Isaiah|9|8: And all the people shall know, Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in pride and arrogancy of heart,
verses.Isaiah|9|9: The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycamores are cut down, but we will change them for cedars.
verses.Isaiah|9|10: Therefore the Lord sets up the adversaries of Rezin against him, and goads his enemies;
verses.Isaiah|9|11: Syria before, and Philistines behind; and they devoured Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.Isaiah|9|12: For the people turned not unto him that smote them, neither do they seek the Lord of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|9|13: Therefore the Lord cut off from Israel, head and tail, branch and rush, in one day.
verses.Isaiah|9|14: The elder and the honourable man, he is the head; and the prophet that teaches lies, he is the tail.
verses.Isaiah|9|15: For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led by them are destroyed.
verses.Isaiah|9|16: Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men, neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows: for everyone is a flatterer and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.Isaiah|9|17: For wickedness burns like the fire: it devours the briers and thorns, and kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they mount up in a billow of smoke.
verses.Isaiah|9|18: Through the wrath of the Lord of hosts is the land darkened, and the people are as the fuel of the fire: no man spares his brother.
verses.Isaiah|9|19: And he snatches on the right hand, and is hungry; and he eats on the left hand, and they are not satisfied: they eat every man the flesh of his own arm:
verses.Isaiah|9|20: Manasseh against Ephraim; and Ephraim against Manasseh: and they together are against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.Isaiah|10|1: Woe them that decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers that prescribe oppression.
verses.Isaiah|10|2: To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless!
verses.Isaiah|10|3: And what will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will you flee for help? and where will you leave your glory?
verses.Isaiah|10|4: There is nothing to be done except to crouch among the prisoners, and fall among the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.Isaiah|10|5: Woe to Assyria the rod of my anger; for the staff in their hand is my indignation.
verses.Isaiah|10|6: I will send him against a hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
