verses.Isaiah|10|7: Howbeit he means not so, neither does his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.
verses.Isaiah|10|8: For he says, Are not my princes all of them kings?
verses.Isaiah|10|9: Is not Calno as Carchemish? is not Hamath as Arpad? is not Samaria as Damascus?
verses.Isaiah|10|10: As my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved idols did exceed those of Jerusalem and of Samaria,
verses.Isaiah|10|11: shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?
verses.Isaiah|10|12: Wherefore it shall come to pass, that when the Lord has performed his whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks.
verses.Isaiah|10|13: For he says, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the mighty number of their inhabitants.
verses.Isaiah|10|14: And my hand has found as a nest the riches of the people: and as one gathers eggs that are left, have I gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or chirped.
verses.Isaiah|10|15: Shall the ax boast itself against him that hews with it? or shall the saw magnify itself against him that wields it? as if the rod should shake them that lift it up, or as if the staff should lift up them that are no wood!
verses.Isaiah|10|16: Therefore shall the Master, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory shall be kindled a burning like the burning of a fire.
verses.Isaiah|10|17: And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame: and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day;
verses.Isaiah|10|18: and shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body: and they shall be as when a sick person wastes away.
verses.Isaiah|10|19: And the rest of the trees of his forest shall be few, that a child may write them down.
verses.Isaiah|10|20: And it shall come to pass on that day, that the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again rely upon him that smote them; but shall rely upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel in truth.
verses.Isaiah|10|21: A remnant shall return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.
verses.Isaiah|10|22: For though Thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: total destruction is decreed but overflowing with righteousness.
verses.Isaiah|10|23: For it is determined and decreed; the Lord God of hosts shall do it.
verses.Isaiah|10|24: Therefore thus says the Lord God of hosts, O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of Assyria: he shall smite thee with a rod, and shall lift up his staff against thee, after the manner of Egypt.
verses.Isaiah|10|25: But yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease, and my anger shall be turned to their destruction.
verses.Isaiah|10|26: And the Lord of hosts shall stir up a whip for him according to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb: and as his rod was upon the sea, so shall he lift it up after the manner of Egypt.
verses.Isaiah|10|27: And it shall come to pass on that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the fatness.
verses.Isaiah|10|28: He is come to Aiath, he is passed to Migron; at Michmash he has left his baggage:
verses.Isaiah|10|29: they are gone over the pass: they have taken up their lodging at Geba; Ramah is afraid; Gibeah of Saul is fled.
verses.Isaiah|10|30: Lift up thy voice, O Gallim: hearken Laish, O poor Anathoth.
verses.Isaiah|10|31: Madmenah is removed; the inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.
verses.Isaiah|10|32: This very day he will halt at Nob: he will shake his hands against the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|10|33: Behold, the Master, the Lord of hosts, shall lop the bough with terror: and the high ones of stature shall be hewn down, and the haughty shall be humbled.
verses.Isaiah|10|34: And he shall cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one.
verses.Isaiah|11|1: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots:
verses.Isaiah|11|2: and the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord;
verses.Isaiah|11|3: and his delight shall be in the fear of the Lord: and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither decide after the hearing of his ears:
verses.Isaiah|11|4: but with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and decide with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.
verses.Isaiah|11|5: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.
verses.Isaiah|11|6: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
verses.Isaiah|11|7: And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
verses.Isaiah|11|8: And the sucking child play on the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the viper's nest.
verses.Isaiah|11|9: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.
verses.Isaiah|11|10: And in that day it shall be, that the root of Jesse, that stands for a banner of the peoples, to it shall the nations seek: and his resting place shall be glorious.
verses.Isaiah|11|11: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, that shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, from Pathros, and from Ethiopia, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
verses.Isaiah|11|12: And he shall set up a banner for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
verses.Isaiah|11|13: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.
verses.Isaiah|11|14: But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the sea; they shall spoil the children of the east together: they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.
verses.Isaiah|11|15: And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the sea of Egypt; and with his scorching wind he shall shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in seven streams, and make men go over dryshod.
verses.Isaiah|11|16: And there shall be a highway for the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria; as there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.Isaiah|12|1: And in that day thou shalt say, O Lord, I will praise Thee: though wast angry with me, Thy anger is turned away, and Thou dost comfort me.
verses.Isaiah|12|2: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the Lord God is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.
verses.Isaiah|12|3: Therefore with joy shall you draw water out of the wells of salvation.
verses.Isaiah|12|4: And in that day shall you say, Praise the Lord, call upon his name, declare his doings among the people, make mention that his name is exalted.
verses.Isaiah|12|5: Sing to the Lord; for he has done excellent things: this is known in all the earth.
verses.Isaiah|12|6: Cry out and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion: for great is the Holy One of Israel in the midst of thee.
verses.Isaiah|13|1: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.
verses.Isaiah|13|2: Lift up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, wave the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.
verses.Isaiah|13|3: I have commanded my sanctified ones, I have also called my warriors for my anger, my proudly exalting ones.
verses.Isaiah|13|4: The noise of a multitude in the mountains, like as of a great people; a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together: the Lord of hosts musters the host of the battle.
verses.Isaiah|13|5: They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, the Lord, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.
verses.Isaiah|13|6: Howl; for the day of the Lord is at hand; it shall come as a destruction from the Almighty.
verses.Isaiah|13|7: Therefore shall all hands be slack, and every man's heart shall melt:
verses.Isaiah|13|8: and they shall be afraid: pangs and sorrows shall take hold of them; they shall be in pain as a woman in travail: they shall be amazed at one another; their faces shall be as flames.
verses.Isaiah|13|9: Behold, the day of the Lord comes, a day of cruelty, wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy its sinners from out of it.
verses.Isaiah|13|10: For the stars of heaven and its constellations shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not shed her light.
verses.Isaiah|13|11: And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the tyrants.
verses.Isaiah|13|12: I will make men more rare than fine gold; and mankind, than the pure gold of Ophir.
verses.Isaiah|13|13: Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth shall remove out of her place, by the wrath of the Lord of host, and on the day of his fierce anger.
verses.Isaiah|13|14: And it shall be like the outcast gazelle, and the sheep that no man takes up; they shall every man turn to his own people, and flee every one into his own land.
verses.Isaiah|13|15: Every one that is found shall be thrust through; and every one that is caught shall fall by the sword.
verses.Isaiah|13|16: Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished.
verses.Isaiah|13|17: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.
verses.Isaiah|13|18: Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.
verses.Isaiah|13|19: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the pride of the Chaldeans, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
verses.Isaiah|13|20: It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their flock lie down there.
verses.Isaiah|13|21: But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of owls; and ostriches shall dwell there, and the scops owl shall hop about there.
verses.Isaiah|13|22: And jackals shall cry in their castles, and wild dogs in their pleasant palaces: and her time is near at hand, and her days shall not be prolonged.
verses.Isaiah|14|1: For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the stranger shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.
verses.Isaiah|14|2: And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.
verses.Isaiah|14|3: And it shall come to pass on the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage in which thou wast made to serve,
verses.Isaiah|14|4: that thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How has the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!
verses.Isaiah|14|5: The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked, the sceptre of the rulers,
verses.Isaiah|14|6: that smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, that ruled the nations in anger with unrelenting persecution.
verses.Isaiah|14|7: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.
verses.Isaiah|14|8: Yea, the cypresses rejoice at thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us.
verses.Isaiah|14|9: Sheol from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirs up the shades for thee, all the chief ones of the earth; it has raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
verses.Isaiah|14|10: They all shall speak and say to thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like us?
verses.Isaiah|14|11: Thy pomp is brought down to Sheol, and the noise of thy lutes: worms are spread under thee, and worms cover thee.
verses.Isaiah|14|12: How art thou fallen from heaven, O bright star, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, that didst rule over the nations!
verses.Isaiah|14|13: For thou hast said in thy heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the farthest north:
verses.Isaiah|14|14: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.
verses.Isaiah|14|15: Yet thou shalt be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
verses.Isaiah|14|16: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms;
verses.Isaiah|14|17: that made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed its cities; that opened not the house of his prisoners?
verses.Isaiah|14|18: All the kings of the nations, even all of them, lie in glory, every one in his own house.
verses.Isaiah|14|19: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abhorred branch, dressed in the garment of the slain, thrust through with a sword; like them that go down to the stones of the pit as a carcass trodden under feet.
verses.Isaiah|14|20: Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial, because thou hast destroyed thy land, and slain thy people: may the seed of evildoers nevermore be named.
verses.Isaiah|14|21: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land; for the face of the world would be filled with enemies.
verses.Isaiah|14|22: For I will rise up against them, says the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon name, and remnant, and offspring and posterity, says the Lord.
verses.Isaiah|14|23: I will also make it a possession for wild birds, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction, says the Lord of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|14|24: The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying, Surely as I have thought, so has it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand:
verses.Isaiah|14|25: that I will break Assyria in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders.
verses.Isaiah|14|26: This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations.
verses.Isaiah|14|27: For the Lord of hosts has purposed, and who shall annul it? and his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?
verses.Isaiah|14|28: In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden.
verses.Isaiah|14|29: Rejoice not thou, O Philistia entire, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a viper, and his fruit shall be a venomous flying serpent.
verses.Isaiah|14|30: And the firstborn of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety: and I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant.
verses.Isaiah|14|31: Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, entire Philistia, melt in fear: for there shall come from the north a smoke, and there shall be no straggler in his ranks.
verses.Isaiah|14|32: What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord has founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall shelter in it.
verses.Isaiah|15|1: The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and ruined; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and ruined;
verses.Isaiah|15|2: he is gone up to the shrine, and Dibon to the high places, to weep: Moab shall howl over Nebo, and over Medeba: on all their heads is baldness, and every beard is cut off.
verses.Isaiah|15|3: In their streets they gird themselves with sackcloth: on the tops of their houses, and in their streets, every one howls, weeping abundantly.
verses.Isaiah|15|4: And Heshbon cries, and Elealeh: their voice is heard as far as Jahaz: therefore the armed soldiers of Moab cry out; his soul trembles.
verses.Isaiah|15|5: My heart cries out for Moab; his fugitives shall flee to Zoar, a heifer of three years old: for by the ascent of Luhith, with weeping shall they ascend it; for in the way of Horonaim they shall raise up a cry of destruction.
verses.Isaiah|15|6: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate: for the nay is withered away, the grass fails, there is no green thing.
verses.Isaiah|15|7: Therefore the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall the enemy carry away past the wadi of the willows.
verses.Isaiah|15|8: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; its howling as far as Eglaim, and its roaring to Beer-elim.
verses.Isaiah|15|9: For the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood: for I will bring yet more upon Dimon: a lion will I bring upon him that escapes of Moab, and upon the remnant of the land.
verses.Isaiah|16|1: Send the lamb to the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mount of the daughter of Zion.
verses.Isaiah|16|2: For it shall be, that, as a wandering bird, as a scattered nest, the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon.
verses.Isaiah|16|3: Take counsel, execute judgment; make thy shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday; hide the outcasts; betray not the wanderer.
verses.Isaiah|16|4: Let my outcasts, the outcasts of Moab, dwell with thee; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler: for the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceases, the oppressors are consumed out of the land.
verses.Isaiah|16|5: And in mercy a throne was established: and he sat upon it in truthfulness in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and quick to do righteousness.
verses.Isaiah|16|6: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: even of his haughtiness, and his pride, and his wrath: false are his pratings.
verses.Isaiah|16|7: Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir-haraseth shall you mourn; surely they are stricken.
verses.Isaiah|16|8: For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah: have broken down its choice branches, they reached to Jazer, they wandered into the wilderness: her offshoots were stretched out, they went over the sea.
verses.Isaiah|16|9: Therefore I will bewail with the weeping of Jazer the vine of Sibmah: I will water thee with my tears, O Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on thy summer fruits and on thy harvest the battle cry has fallen.
verses.Isaiah|16|10: And gladness is taken away, and joy out of the plentiful field; and in the vineyards there shall be no singing, neither shall there be shouting: the treaders shall tread out no wine in their presses; I have made shouting at the vintage to cease.
verses.Isaiah|16|11: Wherefore my heart shall moan like a lyre for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir-hareseth.
verses.Isaiah|16|12: And it shall come to pass, when it is seen that Moab is weary on the high place, that he shall come to his sanctuary to pray; but he shall not prevail.
verses.Isaiah|16|13: This is the word that the Lord has spoken concerning Moab long ago.
verses.Isaiah|16|14: But now the Lord has spoken, saying, Within three years, as the years of a hireling, and the glory of Moab shall be contemned, with all that great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and powerless.
verses.Isaiah|17|1: The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a heap of ruins.
verses.Isaiah|17|2: The cities of Aroer are forsaken: they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
verses.Isaiah|17|3: The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, says the Lord of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|17|4: And on that day it shall come to pass, that the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall become lean.
verses.Isaiah|17|5: And it shall be as when the harvester gathers the standing corn, and reaps the ears with his arm; and it shall be as he that gathers ears in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.Isaiah|17|6: And gleanings shall be left of him, as in the beating of an olive tree, two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in its fruitful branches, says the Lord God of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|17|7: At that day shall a man look to his Maker, and his eyes shall have regard to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|17|8: And he shall not look to the altars, the work of his hands, neither shall he regard that which his fingers have made, either the asherim or the sun images.
verses.Isaiah|17|9: On that day shall his strong cities be as the forsaken portion of the thicket and the uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Israel: and there shall be desolation.
verses.Isaiah|17|10: Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength, therefore though thou plant pleasant plants, and set it with slips of a strange god:
verses.Isaiah|17|11: though in the day of thy planting thou make it grow, and in the morning thou make thy seed to flourish: yet the harvest shall disappear in the day of grief and of desperate pain.
verses.Isaiah|17|12: Woe to the multitude of many people, who make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!
verses.Isaiah|17|13: The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but he shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like whirling dust before the storm.
verses.Isaiah|17|14: And behold at evening, trouble; and before the morning they are no more. This is the portion of them that spoil us, and the lot of them that rob us.
verses.Isaiah|18|1: O land of buzzing wings, which fly beyond the rivers of Ethiopia:
verses.Isaiah|18|2: that sendest ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus upon the waters: Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people terrible from their beginning onward; a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers have divided!
verses.Isaiah|18|3: All you inhabitants of the world, and dwellers on the earth, see, when he lifts up a banner on the mountains; and when he blows a shofar, hear!
verses.Isaiah|18|4: For so the Lord said to me, I will take my rest, and I will look on in my dwelling place, like the clear heat in sunlight; and like the cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
verses.Isaiah|18|5: For before the harvest, when the blossom is past, and the bud is ripening into young grapes, he shall both cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and take away and cut down the branches.
verses.Isaiah|18|6: They shall be left together to the predatory birds of the mountains, and to the beasts of the earth: and the birds shall summer upon them, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter upon them.
verses.Isaiah|18|7: In that time shall a present be brought to the Lord of hosts, by a people tall and smooth, even by a people terrible from their beginning onward; a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers have divided, to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, the mount Zion.
verses.Isaiah|19|1: The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.
verses.Isaiah|19|2: And I will set Egypt against Egypt: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
verses.Isaiah|19|3: And the spirit of Egypt shall be emptied in his midst; and I will destroy his counsel: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the necromancers, and to the mediums, and to the wizards.
verses.Isaiah|19|4: And I will give over Egypt to the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, says the Master, the Lord of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|19|5: And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and dried up.
verses.Isaiah|19|6: And the rivers shall become foul; and the canals of Egypt shall be diminished and dried up: the reeds and rushes shall wither.
verses.Isaiah|19|7: The meadows by the River, by the mouth of the River, and every thing sown by the River, shall wither, be driven away, and be no more.
verses.Isaiah|19|8: The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the River shall lament, and they that spread nets upon the waters shall be wretched.
verses.Isaiah|19|9: Moreover they that work in combed flax, and they that weave white cotton, shall be confounded.
verses.Isaiah|19|10: And its foundations shall be broken; all that make dams shall be sad in their soul.
verses.Isaiah|19|11: Surely the princes of Zoan are fools, the counsel of the wise counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish: how can you say to Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?
verses.Isaiah|19|12: Where are they? where are thy wise men? and let them tell thee now, and let them know what the Lord of hosts has purposed concerning Egypt.
verses.Isaiah|19|13: The princes of Zoan are become fools, the princes of Noph are deceived; they have also made Egypt go astray, those that are the stay of its tribes.
verses.Isaiah|19|14: The Lord has mingled a spirit of confusion in the midst of her: and they have caused Egypt to err in all its work, as a drunken man staggers in his vomit.
verses.Isaiah|19|15: Neither shall there be any work for Egypt which the head or tail, branch or rush, may do.
verses.Isaiah|19|16: In that day shall Egypt be like women: and it shall be afraid and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he shakes over it.
verses.Isaiah|19|17: And the land of Judah shall be a trembling to Egypt, every one to whom one makes mention of that shall be afraid, because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he has determined against it.
verses.Isaiah|19|18: In that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt, speaking the language of Canaan and swearing by the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.
verses.Isaiah|19|19: In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at its border to the Lord.
verses.Isaiah|19|20: And it shall be for a sign and for a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry to the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them one that shall save them and plead for them, and he shall deliver them.
verses.Isaiah|19|21: And the Lord shall be known to Egypt, and Egypt shall know the Lord on that day, and shall do sacrifice and meal offering; and they shall vow a vow to the Lord, and perform it.
verses.Isaiah|19|22: And the Lord shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal: and they shall return to the Lord, and he shall be entreated of them, and shall heal them.
verses.Isaiah|19|23: In that day there shall be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and Assyria shall come into Egypt, and Egypt to Assyria, and Egypt shall worship with Assyria.
verses.Isaiah|19|24: In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land:
verses.Isaiah|19|25: whom the Lord of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.
verses.Isaiah|20|1: In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,) and fought against Ashdod, and took it;
verses.Isaiah|20|2: at the same time the Lord spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz saying, Go and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put off thy shoe from thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.
verses.Isaiah|20|3: And the Lord said, Just as my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a portent upon Egypt and upon Ethiopia;
verses.Isaiah|20|4: so shall the king of Assyria lead away the prisoners of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, even with their buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
verses.Isaiah|20|5: And they shall be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.
verses.Isaiah|20|6: And the inhabitant of this coast land shall say on that day, Behold, such is our expectation, whither we flee for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria: and how shall we escape?
verses.Isaiah|21|1: The burden of the desert of the sea. As storms in the south sweep on; so it comes from the desert, from a terrible land.
verses.Isaiah|21|2: A grievous vision is declared to me; He who desires to be treacherous may be treacherous, and he who desires to spoil may spoil, Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Medes; all its sighing have I made to cease.
verses.Isaiah|21|3: Therefore are my loins filled with anguish: pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman in travail: I was bowed down so that I could not hear; I was dismayed so that I could not see.
verses.Isaiah|21|4: My heart reeled, fearfulness affrighted me: the night of my pleasure has he turned for me into terror.
verses.Isaiah|21|5: Prepare the table, spread the carpet, eat, drink: arise, princes, and anoint the shield.
verses.Isaiah|21|6: For thus has the Lord said to me, Go, set a watchman, let him declare what he sees.
verses.Isaiah|21|7: And if he should see riders, pairs of horsemen, riders on asses, riders on camels; he should hearken diligently with much heed:
verses.Isaiah|21|8: and he cried like a lion: My Lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I stand on guard whole nights:
verses.Isaiah|21|9: and, behold, here come men riding, pairs of horsemen. And he answered and said, Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the carved images of her gods he has broken to the ground.
verses.Isaiah|21|10: O my trodden one, and child of my threshing floor; that which I have heard of the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, have I declared to you.
verses.Isaiah|21|11: The burden of Dumah. One calls to me out of Seir, Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?
verses.Isaiah|21|12: The watchman said, The morning comes, and also the night: if you will inquire, inquire: return, come.
verses.Isaiah|21|13: The burden upon Arabia. In the forest, in Arabia shall you lodge, O travelling companies of Dedanim.
verses.Isaiah|21|14: O inhabitants of the land of Tema, bring water to him that is thirsty, meet the fugitive with bread.
verses.Isaiah|21|15: For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grievousness of war.
verses.Isaiah|21|16: For thus the Lord said to me, Within a year, according to the years of a hireling, and all the glory of Kedar shall fail:
verses.Isaiah|21|17: And the residue of the number of archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, shall be diminished: for the Lord God of Israel has spoken it.
verses.Isaiah|22|1: The burden of the Valley of Vision. What ails thee now, that thou art wholly gone up to the housetops?
verses.Isaiah|22|2: Thou that art full of uproar, a tumultuous city, a joyous city: thy slain men are not slain with the sword, nor dead in battle.
verses.Isaiah|22|3: All thy rulers are fled together, they are bound by the bowmen: all that are found in thee are bound together; they have fled from far.
verses.Isaiah|22|4: Therefore said I, Look away from me; I will weep bitterly, labour not to comfort me, because of the spoiling of the daughter of my people.
verses.Isaiah|22|5: For it is a day of trouble, and of trampling, and of confusion by the Lord God of hosts in the Valley of Vision, a breaking down of walls and a shouting to the mountains.
verses.Isaiah|22|6: And Elam bore the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.
verses.Isaiah|22|7: And it came to pass, when thy choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate,
verses.Isaiah|22|8: and he stripped the covering of Judah, that thou didst look on that day to the armour of the house of the forest.
verses.Isaiah|22|9: You saw also the breaches of the city of David, that they are many: and you gathered together the waters of the lower pool.
verses.Isaiah|22|10: And you numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses you broke down to fortify the wall.
verses.Isaiah|22|11: You made also a pond between the two walls for the water of the old pool: but you did not look to him who made it, nor did you see him that fashioned it long ago.
verses.Isaiah|22|12: And on that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:
verses.Isaiah|22|13: and behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating meat, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
verses.Isaiah|22|14: And it was revealed in my ears, by the Lord of hosts: Surely this iniquity shall not be forgiven you till you die, says the Lord God of hosts.
verses.Isaiah|22|15: Thus says the Lord God of hosts, Go, get thee to this steward, to Shebna who is over the house.
verses.Isaiah|22|16: Say to him, What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewn thee out a tomb here, hewing out a tomb on high, carving a habitation for himself in a rock?
verses.Isaiah|22|17: Behold, the Lord will thrust thee about with a mighty throw, and will seize thee firmly.
verses.Isaiah|22|18: He will violently roll and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there shall be the chariots of thy glory, O shame of thy master's house.
verses.Isaiah|22|19: And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.
verses.Isaiah|22|20: And it shall come to pass on that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah.
verses.Isaiah|22|21: And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
verses.Isaiah|22|22: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut: and he shall shut, and none shall open.
verses.Isaiah|22|23: And I will fasten him as a tent peg in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father's house.
verses.Isaiah|22|24: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups, even to all the vessels of flagons.
verses.Isaiah|22|25: On that day, says the Lord of hosts, shall the tent peg that is fastened in the sure place be removed, and be cut down, and fall; and the burden that was upon it shall be cut off: for the Lord has spoken it.
verses.Isaiah|23|1: The burden of Tyre. Howl, O ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them.
verses.Isaiah|23|2: Be still, O inhabitants of the coastland; thou whom the merchants of Zidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.
verses.Isaiah|23|3: And by great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the River, is her revenue; and she is a mart of nations.
verses.Isaiah|23|4: Be thou ashamed, O Zidon: for the sea has spoken, even the strength of the sea, saying, I have not travailed, nor brought forth children, nor did I nourish up young men, nor bring up virgins.
verses.Isaiah|23|5: When the report comes to Egypt, they shall tremble at the report of Tyre.
verses.Isaiah|23|6: Pass over to Tarshish; howl, inhabitants of the coastland.
verses.Isaiah|23|7: Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days? her own feet shall carry her afar off to sojourn.
verses.Isaiah|23|8: Who has taken this counsel against Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honourable men of the earth?
verses.Isaiah|23|9: The Lord of hosts has purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.
verses.Isaiah|23|10: Overflow thy land like the River, O daughter of Tarshish: there is no wharf any more.
verses.Isaiah|23|11: He stretched out his hand over the sea, he shook the kingdoms: the Lord has given a commandment against the merchant city, to destroy its strongholds.
verses.Isaiah|23|12: And he said, Thou shalt no more rejoice, O thou oppressed virgin, daughter of Zidon: arise, pass over to Chittim; there also shalt thou have no rest.
verses.Isaiah|23|13: (Behold the land of Chaldeans; this people was not till Assyria founded it for desert dwellers; they set up its towers, they destroyed its palaces; they have brought it to ruin.)
verses.Isaiah|23|14: Howl, O ships of Tarshish: for your strength is laid waste.
verses.Isaiah|23|15: And it shall come to pass on that day, that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king: after the end of years, according to the days of one king: after the end of seventy years, it shall fare with Tyre as in the song of the harlot.
verses.Isaiah|23|16: Take a lyre, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that thou mayst be remembered.
verses.Isaiah|23|17: And it shall come to pass after the end of seventy years, that the Lord will visit Tyre, and she shall turn to her hire, and shall play the harlot with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth.
verses.Isaiah|23|18: And her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the Lord: it shall not be treasured nor laid up; for her gain shall be for them that dwell before the Lord, to eat sufficiently, and for stately clothing.
verses.Isaiah|24|1: Behold, the Lord makes the earth empty, and makes it waste, and turns it upside down, and scatters abroad its inhabitants.
verses.Isaiah|24|2: And it shall be as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower, as with the creditor, so with the debtor.
verses.Isaiah|24|3: The land shall be utterly emptied, and utterly spoiled: for the Lord has spoken this word.
verses.Isaiah|24|4: The earth mourns and fades away, the world languishes and fades away, the lofty people of the earth languish.
verses.Isaiah|24|5: The earth also is defiled under its inhabitants; because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinance, broken the everlasting covenant.
verses.Isaiah|24|6: Therefore has a curse devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are found guilty: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are parched, and few men left.
verses.Isaiah|24|7: The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, all the merryhearted do sigh.
verses.Isaiah|24|8: The mirth of tambourines ceases, the noise of them that rejoice ends, the joy of the lyre is stilled.
verses.Isaiah|24|9: They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it.
verses.Isaiah|24|10: The city of confusion is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in.
verses.Isaiah|24|11: There is a crying for wine in the streets; all joy is darkened, the mirth of the land is gone.
verses.Isaiah|24|12: In the city is left desolation, and the gate is smitten with destruction.
verses.Isaiah|24|13: For thus it shall be in the midst of the land among the people, even as the beating of an olive tree, and as the gleaning grapes when the vintage is done.
verses.Isaiah|24|14: They shall lift up their voice, they shall sing; for the majesty of the Lord shall they shout more than at the sea.
verses.Isaiah|24|15: Wherefore glorify the Lord in the regions of light, even the name of the Lord God of Israel in the isles of the sea.
verses.Isaiah|24|16: From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs, glory to the righteous. But I said, My leanness, my leanness, woe to me! traitors have dealt treacherously; traitors have dealt very treacherously.
verses.Isaiah|24|17: Fear, and the pit, and the trap, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the land.
verses.Isaiah|24|18: And it shall come to pass, that he who flees from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that comes up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the trap: for the windows from on high are open, and the foundations of the earth do shake.
verses.Isaiah|24|19: The earth is utterly broken down, the earth crumbles away, the earth is violently shaken.
verses.Isaiah|24|20: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a frail hut; and its transgression is heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again.
verses.Isaiah|24|21: And it shall come to pass on that day, that the Lord shall punish the host of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth.
verses.Isaiah|24|22: And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be punished.
verses.Isaiah|24|23: Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his elders will be his glory.
verses.Isaiah|25|1: O Lord, Thou art my God; I will exalt Thee, I will praise Thy name; for Thou hast done wonderful things – counsels of old in faithfulness and truth.
verses.Isaiah|25|2: For thou hast made of a city a heap; of a fortified city a ruin: a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built.
verses.Isaiah|25|3: Therefore shall the strong people glorify Thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear Thee.
verses.Isaiah|25|4: For Thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of tyrants was like a storm against the wall.
verses.Isaiah|25|5: Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, as the heat in a dry place; as the heat is removed by the shadow of a cloud, so the song of tyrants shall be brought low.
verses.Isaiah|25|6: And in this mountain shall the Lord of hosts make to all the peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.
verses.Isaiah|25|7: And he will destroy in this mountain the covering that is cast over all the people, and the veil that is spread over all the nations.
verses.Isaiah|25|8: He will destroy death for ever; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the insult of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the Lord has spoken it.
verses.Isaiah|25|9: And it shall be said on that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, that he should save us: this is the Lord; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.
verses.Isaiah|25|10: For in this mountain shall the hand of the Lord rest, and Moab shall be trodden down in his own place, even as straw is trodden down in the dunghill.
verses.Isaiah|25|11: And he shall spread out his hands in the midst of it, as he that swims spreads out his hands to swim: and he shall bring down his pride together with the spoils of his hands.
verses.Isaiah|25|12: And the lofty fortress of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust.
verses.Isaiah|26|1: On that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city; he sets up salvation as walls and bulwarks.
verses.Isaiah|26|2: Open the gates, that the righteous nation that keeps faithfulness may enter in:
verses.Isaiah|26|3: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on Thee: because he trusts in Thee.
verses.Isaiah|26|4: Trust in the Lord for ever: for the Lord God is an eternal Rock.
verses.Isaiah|26|5: For he brings down them that dwell on high; the lofty city, he lays it low; he lays it low, even to the ground; he brings it to the dust.
verses.Isaiah|26|6: The foot shall trample it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy.
verses.Isaiah|26|7: The way of the just is uprightness: Thou, most upright, dost make level the path of the just.
verses.Isaiah|26|8: Indeed, in the way of Thy judgments, O Lord, have we waited for Thee; the desire of our soul is to Thy name, and to the remembrance of Thee.
verses.Isaiah|26|9: With my soul have I desired Thee in the night; with my spirit within me I seek Thee: for when Thy judgments are on the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
verses.Isaiah|26|10: Let favour be shown to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the Lord.
verses.Isaiah|26|11: Lord, when Thy hand is lifted up, they will not see; but they shall see with shame Thy zeal for the people, the fire which shall devour Thy enemies.
verses.Isaiah|26|12: Lord, Thou wilt ordain peace for us: for Thou also hast performed all our works for us.
verses.Isaiah|26|13: O Lord our God, other masters besides Thee have had dominion over us: but by Thee only will we make mention of Thy name.
verses.Isaiah|26|14: They are dead, they shall not live; the shades of the dead shall not rise: therefore hast Thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.
verses.Isaiah|26|15: Thou hast increased the nation, O Lord, Thou hast increased the nation: Thou art glorified: Thou hast enlarged all the borders of the land.
verses.Isaiah|26|16: Lord, in trouble have they besought Thee, they poured out a silent prayer when Thy chastening was upon them.
verses.Isaiah|26|17: Like a woman with child, that draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and cries out in her pangs; so have we been in Thy sight, O Lord.
verses.Isaiah|26|18: We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth; and the inhabitants of the world have not fallen.
verses.Isaiah|26|19: The dead men of Thy people shall live, my dead body shall arise. Awake and sing, you that dwell in dust: for Thy dew is as the dew on herbs, and the earth shall cast out the shades of the dead.
verses.Isaiah|26|20: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast.
verses.Isaiah|26|21: For, behold, the Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.
verses.Isaiah|27|1: On that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the flying serpent, and leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the crocodile that is in the sea.
verses.Isaiah|27|2: On that day sing to her, A vineyard of foaming wine.
verses.Isaiah|27|3: I the Lord do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day.
verses.Isaiah|27|4: Fury is not in me: who would set the thorns and weeds against me in battle? I would go through them, I would burn them together.
verses.Isaiah|27|5: Or let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me.
verses.Isaiah|27|6: In days to come Jacob shall take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and the face of the world shall be filled with fruit.
verses.Isaiah|27|7: Has he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him? or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him?
verses.Isaiah|27|8: By measure, by exile, thou didst contend with them; he removed her by his rough blast in the day of the east wind.
verses.Isaiah|27|9: By this therefore shall the iniquity of Jacob be atoned; and this is all the fruit to take away his sin; when he makes all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the asherim and sun images shall not remain standing.
verses.Isaiah|27|10: Yet the fortified city shall be solitary, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume its branches.
verses.Isaiah|27|11: When its boughs are withered, they shall be broken off: the women shall come, and set them on fire: for it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them, and he that formed them will show them no favour.
verses.Isaiah|27|12: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat out his harvest from the strongly flowing river as far as the wadi of Egypt, and you shall be gathered up one by one, O children of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|27|13: And it shall come to pass on that day, that a great shofar shall be blown, and they shall come who were lost in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the Lord in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|28|1: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty which is at the head of the rich valley of those who are overcome with wine!
verses.Isaiah|28|2: Behold, the Lord has one who is mighty and strong, as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm, as a flood of mighty waters overflowing; he will cast down to the earth with might.
verses.Isaiah|28|3: The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim shall be trodden under feet:
verses.Isaiah|28|4: and the fading flower of the glorious beauty, which is at the head of the rich valley, shall be as the first ripe fig before the summer; which when one sees, while it is yet in his hand he swallows it up.
verses.Isaiah|28|5: In that day shall the Lord of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, to the residue of his people,
verses.Isaiah|28|6: and for a spirit of judgment to him that sits in judgment, and for strength to them that turn back the battle to the gate.
verses.Isaiah|28|7: But they also reel through wine, and stagger through strong drink; the priest and the prophet reel through strong drink, they are confused by wine, they stagger through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment.
verses.Isaiah|28|8: For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place clean.
verses.Isaiah|28|9: Whom shall one teach knowledge? and whom shall one make to understand doctrine? those that are weaned from the milk, and removed from the breasts?
verses.Isaiah|28|10: For it is precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little:
verses.Isaiah|28|11: for with stammering lips and another tongue shall one speak to this people.
verses.Isaiah|28|12: When he said to them, This is the rest; cause the weary to rest and this is the refreshing: they would not hear.
verses.Isaiah|28|13: Therefore the word of the Lord was to them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little; that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.
verses.Isaiah|28|14: Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|28|15: Because you have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come to us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:
verses.Isaiah|28|16: therefore thus says the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believes shall not make haste.
verses.Isaiah|28|17: Judgment also will I lay by a line, and righteousness by a plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and waters shall overflow the hiding place.
verses.Isaiah|28|18: And your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then you shall be trodden down by it.
verses.Isaiah|28|19: As often as it goes forth it shall take you: for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and the mere understanding of the report shall bring terror.
verses.Isaiah|28|20: For the bed is too short for a man to stretch himself; and the covering too narrow for him to wrap himself up.
verses.Isaiah|28|21: For the Lord shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be full of anger as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, though strange be his work; and bring to pass his act, though strange be his act.
verses.Isaiah|28|22: Now therefore be not mockers, lest your bands be made strong: for I have heard from the Lord God of hosts that destruction is decreed upon the whole land.
verses.Isaiah|28|23: Give ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech.
verses.Isaiah|28|24: Does the plowman all day plow to sow? open and harrow his ground?
verses.Isaiah|28|25: When he has prepared a smooth surface, does he not then scatter the black seeds, and cast the cummin, and throw in wheat by rows, and barley in the marked spot, and spelt along its border.
verses.Isaiah|28|26: And he strictly raises it according to the method prescribed; his God instructs him.
verses.Isaiah|28|27: For the black seeds are not threshed with a threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the black crop is beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod.
verses.Isaiah|28|28: Is the bread corn crushed? No, he will not ever be threshing it; and when he drives the wheel of his cart and his horses over it, he does not crush it.
verses.Isaiah|28|29: This also came from the Lord of hosts. He is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.
verses.Isaiah|29|1: Ho Ariel, Ariel, the city where David encamped! add year to year; let the feasts come round.
verses.Isaiah|29|2: Yet I will distress Ariel, and there shall be heaviness and sorrow: yet it shall be to me as an Ariel (altar hearth).
verses.Isaiah|29|3: And I will camp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with a mound, and I will raise siege works against thee.
verses.Isaiah|29|4: And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be, as of a medium, out of the ground, and thy speech shall chirp out of the dust.
verses.Isaiah|29|5: Yet the multitude of thy strangers shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones shall be like chaff that passes away: and it shall be in an instant suddenly.
verses.Isaiah|29|6: Thou shalt be visited by the Lord of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.
verses.Isaiah|29|7: And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all that fight against her and her stronghold, and that distress her, shall be as a dream of a night vision.
verses.Isaiah|29|8: It shall even be as when a hungry man dreams, and, behold, he eats; but he awakes, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreams, and, behold, he drinks; but he awakes, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul longs for water: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion.
verses.Isaiah|29|9: Amaze yourselves and be amazed; blind yourselves and be blind; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not with strong drink.
verses.Isaiah|29|10: For the Lord has poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes, the prophets, and has covered your heads, the seers.
verses.Isaiah|29|11: And the vision of all this is become to you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he says, I cannot; for it is sealed:
verses.Isaiah|29|12: and the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he says, I am not learned.
verses.Isaiah|29|13: And the Lord said, Since this people draw near, and with their mouth and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear towards me is as a commandment of men learned by rote;
verses.Isaiah|29|14: therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.
verses.Isaiah|29|15: Woe to them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord, and their works are in the dark, and they say, Who sees us? and who knows us?
verses.Isaiah|29|16: O your perverseness! shall the potter be esteemed as the clay? for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?
verses.Isaiah|29|17: Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be regarded as a forest?
verses.Isaiah|29|18: And on that day shall the deaf hear the words of a book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness.
verses.Isaiah|29|19: The meek also shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poorest among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|29|20: For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off:
verses.Isaiah|29|21: that make a man an offender for a word, and ensnare the mentor in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought.
verses.Isaiah|29|22: Therefore thus says the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now grow pale;
verses.Isaiah|29|23: when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in the midst of him, sanctifying my name; for they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall reverence the God of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|29|24: They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine.
verses.Isaiah|30|1: Woe to the rebellious children, says the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that prepare a plan but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin:
verses.Isaiah|30|2: that walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!
verses.Isaiah|30|3: Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.
verses.Isaiah|30|4: For his princes were at Zoan, and his ambassadors came to Hanes.
verses.Isaiah|30|5: They were all ashamed of a people that could not profit them, nor be a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach.
verses.Isaiah|30|6: The burden of the beasts of the south: into the land of trouble and anguish, from whence come the young and old lion, the viper and the venomous flying serpent, they will carry their riches upon the shoulders of young asses, and their treasurers upon the humps of camels, to a people that shall not profit them.
verses.Isaiah|30|7: For Egypt shall help in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I called this people, Boasters in sitting still.
verses.Isaiah|30|8: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever:
verses.Isaiah|30|9: that this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord:
verses.Isaiah|30|10: who say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not to us right things, speak to us smooth things, prophesy delusions:
verses.Isaiah|30|11: get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.
verses.Isaiah|30|12: Wherefore thus says the Holy One of Israel, Because you despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and depend on that:
verses.Isaiah|30|13: therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, bulging out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.
verses.Isaiah|30|14: And he shall break it as the breaking of the potters' vessel that is broken in pieces; he shall not spare: so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it a shred sufficient for taking fire from the hearth, or for taking water out of the cistern.
verses.Isaiah|30|15: For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel; In ease and rest shall you be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and you did not wish it.
verses.Isaiah|30|16: But you said, No; for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall you flee; and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift.
verses.Isaiah|30|17: One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one; at the rebuke of five shall you flee: till you be left like a flagstaff upon the top of a mountain, and as a banner on a hill.
verses.Isaiah|30|18: And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious to you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the Lord is a God of judgment: happy are all they that wait for him.
verses.Isaiah|30|19: For a people that dwell in Zion, even in Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be very gracious to thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee.
verses.Isaiah|30|20: And the Lord shall give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction; yet thy teacher shall not withdraw himself any more, but thy eyes shall see thy teacher:
verses.Isaiah|30|21: and thy ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk in it, when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left.
verses.Isaiah|30|22: You shall defile also the silver plating of thy carved idols, and the gold binding of thy molten images: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous thing; thou shalt say to it, Get thee hence.
verses.Isaiah|30|23: Then shall he give the rain for thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground with that; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures.
verses.Isaiah|30|24: The oxen likewise and the young asses that till the ground shall eat clean provender, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan.
verses.Isaiah|30|25: And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, rivers and streams of waters on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
verses.Isaiah|30|26: Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, on the day that the Lord binds up the breach of his people, and heals the stroke of their wound.
verses.Isaiah|30|27: Behold the name of the Lord comes from far; burning with his anger and in a thick column of smoke: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire:
verses.Isaiah|30|28: and his breath is as an overflowing stream, that reaches to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and to put a bridle on the jaws of the people, causing them to err.
verses.Isaiah|30|29: You shall have a song, as in the night when a holy solemnity is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come into the mountain of the Lord, to the Rock of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|30|30: And the Lord shall cause his glorious voice to be heard, and shall show the descending blow of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and with the flame of a devouring fire, with cloudburst, and tempest, and hailstones.
verses.Isaiah|30|31: For through the voice of the Lord shall Assyria be beaten down; with a rod will he smite him.
verses.Isaiah|30|32: And in every place where the appointed staff shall pass, which the Lord shall lay upon him, it shall be with tambourines and lyres: and in battle of shaking will he fight with them.
verses.Isaiah|30|33: For its hearth is ordained of old; yes, for the king it is prepared: he has made it deep and large: its bonfire is of much fire and wood; the breath of the Lord, like a stream of brimstone, kindles it.
verses.Isaiah|31|1: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and depend on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not to the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!
verses.Isaiah|31|2: Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.
verses.Isaiah|31|3: Now Egypt is man, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, the helper shall stumble, and the one who is helped shall fall down, and they shall all perish together.
verses.Isaiah|31|4: For thus has the Lord spoken to me, Like the lion and the young lion roaring on their prey, though a multitude of shepherds is called out against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.
verses.Isaiah|31|5: As birds hovering, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem; he will defend it and deliver it; he will pass over it and spare it.
verses.Isaiah|31|6: Turn to him from whom you have deeply revolted, O children of Israel.
verses.Isaiah|31|7: For on that day every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made to you for a sin.
verses.Isaiah|31|8: Then shall Assyria fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall become bondslaves.
verses.Isaiah|31|9: And his rock shall pass away in terror, and his princes desert the banner in fear, says the Lord, whose hearth is in Zion, and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
verses.Isaiah|32|1: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and as for princes, they shall rule in judgment.
verses.Isaiah|32|2: And a man shall be as hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
verses.Isaiah|32|3: And the eyes of them that see shall not be blind, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.
verses.Isaiah|32|4: The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.
verses.Isaiah|32|5: The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful.
verses.Isaiah|32|6: For the vile person speaks villainy, and his heart works iniquity, to practise hypocrisy, and to utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and he will cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
verses.Isaiah|32|7: The instruments also of the churl are evil: he devises wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, and the needy when he speaks right.
verses.Isaiah|32|8: But the liberal devises liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand.
verses.Isaiah|32|9: Rise up, you women that are at ease, hear my voice; you complacent daughters, give ear to my speech.
verses.Isaiah|32|10: In a year and some days, you shall be troubled, you complacent women; for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come.
verses.Isaiah|32|11: Tremble, you women that are at ease; be troubled, you complacent ones: strip, and make yourselves bare, and gird sackcloth upon your loins.
verses.Isaiah|32|12: Striking the breasts, for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
verses.Isaiah|32|13: Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers; yes, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city:
verses.Isaiah|32|14: because the palaces shall be forsaken; the city with its stir shall be deserted; the fort and tower shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;
verses.Isaiah|32|15: until a spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest.
verses.Isaiah|32|16: Then judgment shall dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness remain in the fruitful field.
verses.Isaiah|32|17: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and assurance for ever.
verses.Isaiah|32|18: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in secure dwellings, and in quiet resting places;
verses.Isaiah|32|19: and it shall hail in the downfall of the forest, and the city shall descend into the valley.
verses.Isaiah|32|20: Blessed are you that sow beside all waters, that let the feet of the ox and the ass range freely.
verses.Isaiah|33|1: Woe to the spoiler, and thou wast not spoiled; and the traitor, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end of betraying, they shall betray thee.
verses.Isaiah|33|2: O Lord, be gracious to us; we have waited for Thee: be Thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
verses.Isaiah|33|3: At the noise of the tumult the people fled; at the lifting up of Thyself the nations were scattered.
verses.Isaiah|33|4: And your spoil shall be gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar: as the running of locusts shall he rove about upon it.
verses.Isaiah|33|5: The Lord is exalted; for he dwells on high: he has filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.
verses.Isaiah|33|6: And he shall be the stability of thy times, a store of salvation, wisdom and knowledge: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
verses.Isaiah|33|7: Behold, the mighty ones shall cry outside: ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly.
verses.Isaiah|33|8: The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceases: he has broken the covenant, he has despised the cities, he regards no man.
verses.Isaiah|33|9: The earth mourns and languishes: Lebanon is ashamed and withers: the Sharon is like the Arabah; and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
verses.Isaiah|33|10: Now will I rise, says the Lord; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself.
verses.Isaiah|33|11: You shall conceive chaff, you shall bring forth stubble: your breath is a fire that shall devour you.
verses.Isaiah|33|12: And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut down that are burned in the fire.
verses.Isaiah|33|13: Hear, you that are far off, what I have done; and, you that are near, acknowledge my might.
verses.Isaiah|33|14: The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness has surprised the flatterers. Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
verses.Isaiah|33|15: He that walks righteously, and speaks uprightly; he that despises the gain of oppressions, that shakes his hands from holding of bribes, that stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from seeing evil;
verses.Isaiah|33|16: he shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the fortresses of rocks: bread shall be given him; his water shall be sure.
verses.Isaiah|33|17: Thy eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off.
verses.Isaiah|33|18: Thy heart shall muse on terror. Where is the scribe? where is the receiver? where is he that counted the towers?
verses.Isaiah|33|19: Thou shalt not see the fierce people, the people of a deeper speech than thou canst understand; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not apprehend.
verses.Isaiah|33|20: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thy eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tent that shall not be taken down; its pegs shall not be removed for ever, nor shall any of its cords be broken.
verses.Isaiah|33|21: But there the Lord in majesty will be for us a place of broad rivers and streams; wherein no galley with oars can go, neither shall gallant ship be able to pass by it.
verses.Isaiah|33|22: For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.
verses.Isaiah|33|23: Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not strengthen the socket of their mast, they could not spread the sail: then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.
verses.Isaiah|33|24: And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.
verses.Isaiah|34|1: Come near, O nations, to hear; and hearken, O people: let the earth hear, and all that is in it; the world, and all things that come out of it.
verses.Isaiah|34|2: For the Lord has indignation against all the nations, and fury against all their armies: he has utterly destroyed them, he has delivered them to the slaughter.
verses.Isaiah|34|3: Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stench shall come up out of their carcasses, and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.
verses.Isaiah|34|4: And all the host of heaven shall rot away, and the heavens shall be rolled together like a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falls off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.
verses.Isaiah|34|5: For my sword is sated in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Edom, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.
verses.Isaiah|34|6: The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness: with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
verses.Isaiah|34|7: And wild oxen shall come down with them, and bullocks with bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.
verses.Isaiah|34|8: For it is the day of the Lord's vengeance, and the year of recompenses for the cause of Zion.
verses.Isaiah|34|9: And its streams shall be turned into pitch, and its dust into brimstone, and its land shall become burning pitch.
verses.Isaiah|34|10: It shall not be quenched night or day; its smoke shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.
verses.Isaiah|34|11: But wild birds of night shall possess it; the owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the plummet of emptiness.
verses.Isaiah|34|12: They shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none shall be there, and all her princes shall be nothing.
verses.Isaiah|34|13: And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in her fortresses: and it shall be a habitation of wild dogs, and a court for owls.
verses.Isaiah|34|14: The wild creatures of the desert also meet with the jackals, the scops owl shall cry to his fellow; the tawny owl also shall rest there, and find for herself a place of rest.
verses.Isaiah|34|15: There shall the great owl make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and brood under her shadow: there shall the kites also be gathered, every one with her mate.
verses.Isaiah|34|16: Seek out of the book of the Lord, and read: none of these shall be missing, none shall want her mate; for my speech has commanded, and his spirit has gathered them.
verses.Isaiah|34|17: And he has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.
verses.Isaiah|35|1: The wilderness and the arid land shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom like the tulip.
verses.Isaiah|35|2: It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of the Lebanon shall be given to it, the excellency of the Carmel and the Sharon, they shall see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God.
verses.Isaiah|35|3: Strengthen the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.
verses.Isaiah|35|4: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even with a divine recompense; he will come and save you.
verses.Isaiah|35|5: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
verses.Isaiah|35|6: Then shall the lame man leap as a hart and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.
verses.Isaiah|35|7: And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water: the habitation of jackals shall become a pasture for cattle, an enclosure of reeds and rushes.
verses.Isaiah|35|8: And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness: the unclean shall not pass over it; and he shall be to them a guide, and fools shall not err in it.
verses.Isaiah|35|9: No lion shall be there, nor any ravenous beast shall go up on it, they shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there:
verses.Isaiah|35|10: and the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
verses.Isaiah|36|1: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.
verses.Isaiah|36|2: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool in the highway of the washer's field.
verses.Isaiah|36|3: Then Eliakim, Hilkiah's son, who was over the house, came out to him, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah Asaph's son, the recorder.
verses.Isaiah|36|4: And Rabshakeh said to them, Say now to Hezekiah, Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this in which thou trustest?
verses.Isaiah|36|5: I said, A mere word with the lips is thy counsel and strength for war: now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?
verses.Isaiah|36|6: Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, in Egypt; on which if a man lean, it will go into his arm, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him.
verses.Isaiah|36|7: But if thou say to me, We trust in the Lord our God: is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, You shall worship before this altar?
verses.Isaiah|36|8: Now therefore make a wager, I pray thee, with my master the king of Assyria, and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.
