verses.Jeremiah|31|2: Thus says the Lord, The people who were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness; when Israel sought for rest.
verses.Jeremiah|31|3: The Lord appeared of old to me, saying, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore I have remained true to thee.
verses.Jeremiah|31|4: Again I will build thee, and thou shalt be built, O virgin of Israel: thou shalt again be adorned with thy timbrels, and shalt go out dancing with them that make merry.
verses.Jeremiah|31|5: Thou shalt yet plant vines upon the mountains of Samaria: the planters shall plant, and shall enjoy the fruit.
verses.Jeremiah|31|6: For there shall be a day, that the watchmen upon the mount Ephraim shall cry, Arise, and let us go up to Zion to the Lord our God.
verses.Jeremiah|31|7: For thus says the Lord; Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout on the hilltops of the nations: announce, praise, and say, O Lord, save Thy people, the remnant of Israel.
verses.Jeremiah|31|8: Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the ends of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travails with child together: a great company shall return there.
verses.Jeremiah|31|9: They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, in which they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
verses.Jeremiah|31|10: Hear the word of the Lord, O you nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd keeps his flock.
verses.Jeremiah|31|11: For the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he.
verses.Jeremiah|31|12: Therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow to the bounty of the Lord, for wheat, and for wine, and for oil, and for the young of the flock and of the herd: and their soul shall be like a watered garden; and they shall not languish in sorrow any more.
verses.Jeremiah|31|13: Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, both young men and old together: for I will turn their mourning to joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
verses.Jeremiah|31|14: And I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|31|15: Thus says the Lord; A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be comforted for her children, because they are not.
verses.Jeremiah|31|16: Thus says the Lord; Keep thy voice from weeping, and thy eyes from tears: for thy work shall be rewarded, says the Lord; and they shall come back again from the land of the enemy.
verses.Jeremiah|31|17: And there is hope for thy future, says the Lord, and thy children shall come back again to their own border.
verses.Jeremiah|31|18: I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself thus; Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, like an untrained calf: turn me back, and I shall be turned; for Thou art the Lord my God.
verses.Jeremiah|31|19: For after I had returned away, I repented; and after I was instructed, I smote upon my thigh: I was ashamed, and even confounded, because I did bear the reproach of my youth.
verses.Jeremiah|31|20: Is Ephraim my dear son? is he a darling child? for whenever I speak of him, I earnestly remember him still: therefore my inward parts are moved for him; I will surely have mercy on him, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|31|21: Set up waymarks for thyself, make thee signposts: set thy heart towards the highway, the way on which thou didst go: turn back, O virgin of Israel, turn back to these thy cities.
verses.Jeremiah|31|22: How long wilt thou turn about, O thou faithless daughter? for the Lord has created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall court a man.
verses.Jeremiah|31|23: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Yet again they shall use this speech in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I shall bring back their captivity; The Lord bless thee, O habitation of justice, and mountain of holiness.
verses.Jeremiah|31|24: And in it shall dwell Judah, and all its cities together, the farmers, and they that go out with the flocks.
verses.Jeremiah|31|25: For I will satisfy the weary soul, and I replenish every languishing soul.
verses.Jeremiah|31|26: Upon this I awoke, and beheld; and my sleep was sweet to me.
verses.Jeremiah|31|27: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of beast.
verses.Jeremiah|31|28: And it shall come to pass, that as I have watched over them, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to break down, and to destroy, and to afflict; so will I watch over them, to build, and to plant, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|31|29: In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
verses.Jeremiah|31|30: But every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eats sour grapes, his teeth shall be set on edge.
verses.Jeremiah|31|31: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:
verses.Jeremiah|31|32: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which covenant of mine they broke, although I was their master, says the Lord;
verses.Jeremiah|31|33: but this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord; I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people,
verses.Jeremiah|31|34: and they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest of them, says the Lord: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.
verses.Jeremiah|31|35: Thus says the Lord, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea that its waves roar; the Lord of hosts is his name:
verses.Jeremiah|31|36: If those ordinances depart from before me, says the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.
verses.Jeremiah|31|37: Thus says the Lord; If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, then I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, says the Lord God.
verses.Jeremiah|31|38: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when the city shall be built to the Lord from the tower of Hananeel to the corner gate.
verses.Jeremiah|31|39: And the measuring line shall go out further straight to the hill Gareb, and shall turn round to go to Goath.
verses.Jeremiah|31|40: And the whole valley of the dead bodies, and of the ashes, and all the fields as far as the wadi of Kidron, to the corner of the horse gate towards the east, shall be holy to the Lord; it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more for ever.
verses.Jeremiah|32|1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.
verses.Jeremiah|32|2: At that time, the king of Babylon's army was besieging Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the house of the king of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|32|3: For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, why dost thou prophesy, and say, Thus says the Lord, Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it;
verses.Jeremiah|32|4: and Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes:
verses.Jeremiah|32|5: and he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there shall he be until I visit him, says the Lord: though you fight with the Chaldeans, you shall not prosper?
verses.Jeremiah|32|6: And Jeremiah said, The word of the Lord has come to me, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|32|7: Behold, Hanameel the son of Shallum thy uncle shall come to thee, saying, Buy my field that is in Anathoth: for the right of redemption is thine to buy it.
verses.Jeremiah|32|8: So Hanameel my uncle's son came to me in the court of the guard according to the word of the Lord, and said to me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth, which is in the country of Benjamin: for the right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine; buy it for thyself. Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|32|9: And I bought the field from Hanameel my uncle's son, that was in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, seventeen shekels of silver.
verses.Jeremiah|32|10: And I subscribed the deed, and sealed it, and took witnesses, and weighed the money in the balances.
verses.Jeremiah|32|11: So I took the deed of the purchase, both that which was sealed, containing the terms and conditions, and which was open:
verses.Jeremiah|32|12: and I gave the deed of the purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanameel my uncle's son, and in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the deed of the purchase, before all the men of Judah that sat in the court of the guard.
verses.Jeremiah|32|13: And I charged Baruch before them, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|32|14: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Take these documents, this deed of the purchase, both that which is sealed, and this open deed; and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may last for many days.
verses.Jeremiah|32|15: For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be bought again in this land.
verses.Jeremiah|32|16: Now when I had delivered the deed of the purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|32|17: Ah Lord God! behold, Thou hast made the heaven and the earth by Thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for Thee:
verses.Jeremiah|32|18: Thou showst loyal love to thousands, and dost recompense the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them: O great and mighty God! the Lord of hosts is his name,
verses.Jeremiah|32|19: Great in counsel, and mighty in performance: Thy eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men: to give every one according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings:
verses.Jeremiah|32|20: who has set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, to this day, and in Israel, and among mankind: and hast made Thee a name, as at this day;
verses.Jeremiah|32|21: and hast brought Thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with great terror;
verses.Jeremiah|32|22: and hast given them this land, which Thou didst swear to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey;
verses.Jeremiah|32|23: and they came in, and possessed it; but they obeyed not Thy voice, neither followed Thy law; they have done nothing of all that Thou didst command them to do: therefore Thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them:
verses.Jeremiah|32|24: behold the siege works are come to the city to take it; and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans that fight against it, because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence: and what Thou hast spoken is come to pass; and, behold, Thou seest it.
verses.Jeremiah|32|25: And Thou hast said to me, O Lord God, Buy the field for money and take witnesses; though the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.
verses.Jeremiah|32|26: Then came the word of the Lord to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|32|27: Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there anything too hard for me?
verses.Jeremiah|32|28: Therefore thus says the Lord; Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he shall take it:
verses.Jeremiah|32|29: and the Chaldeans, that fight against this city, shall come and set fire to this city, and burn it together with the houses, upon whose roofs they have offered incense to the Baal, and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke me to anger.
verses.Jeremiah|32|30: For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have done only evil before Me, from their youth: for the children of Israel have only provoked Me to anger with the work of their hands, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|32|31: For this has been to Me as a provocation of My anger and of My fury from the day that they built it and to this day; that I should remove it from before My face,
verses.Jeremiah|32|32: because of all the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.Jeremiah|32|33: And they have turned their back to me, and not their face: though I taught them, teaching them from morning till night, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction.
verses.Jeremiah|32|34: But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it.
verses.Jeremiah|32|35: And they built the high places of the Baal, which are in the valley of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire to Molech; which I did not command them, nor did it come into my mind that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.
verses.Jeremiah|32|36: And now therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning this city, of which you say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence;
verses.Jeremiah|32|37: behold, I will gather them out of all countries, into which I have driven them in My anger, and in My fury, and in great wrath; and I will bring them back to this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely:
verses.Jeremiah|32|38: and they shall be My people, and I will be their God:
verses.Jeremiah|32|39: and I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for their good, and that of their children after them:
verses.Jeremiah|32|40: and I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from doing good to them; but I will put My fear in their hearts, that they shall not turn aside from me.
verses.Jeremiah|32|41: And I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will truly plant them in this land, with My whole heart and with My whole soul.
verses.Jeremiah|32|42: For thus says the Lord; Just as I have brought all this great evil upon this people, so will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
verses.Jeremiah|32|43: And fields shall be brought in this land of which you say, It is desolate without man or beast; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.
verses.Jeremiah|32|44: Men shall buy fields for money, and subscribe deeds, and seal them, and take witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the coastal plain, and in the cities of the south: for I will cause their captivity to return, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|33|1: Moreover the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the second time, while he was still confined in the court of the guard, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|33|2: Thus says the Lord the maker of it, the Lord that formed it, to establish it; the Lord is his name;
verses.Jeremiah|33|3: Call to me, and I will answer thee, and show thee great and mighty things, which thou knowst not.
verses.Jeremiah|33|4: For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city, and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah, which are thrown down to withstand the siege works and the sword;
verses.Jeremiah|33|5: they come to fight with the Chaldeans, and thereby to fill them with the dead bodies of those men, whom I shall stay in my anger and in my fury, those on account of whose wickedness I have hid my face from this city.
verses.Jeremiah|33|6: Behold, I will bring it healing and cure, and I will cure them, and will reveal to them the abundance of peace and truth.
verses.Jeremiah|33|7: And I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first.
verses.Jeremiah|33|8: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, in which they have sinned against me; and I will pardon all their iniquities, in which they have sinned against me, and in which they have transgressed against me.
verses.Jeremiah|33|9: And it shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth, who shall hear all the good that I do to them: and they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and for all the prosperity that I procure to it:
verses.Jeremiah|33|10: Thus says the Lord; Again there shall be heard in this place, (which you say shall be desolate without man and without beast, namely, in the cities of Judah, and in the desolate streets of Jerusalem, that are without man, and without inhabitant, and without beast,)
verses.Jeremiah|33|11: the voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say, Praise the Lord of hosts: for the Lord is good; for his loyal love endures for ever: when they shall bring the sacrifice of thanksgiving into the house of the Lord. For I will cause the captivity of the land to return, as at the first, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|33|12: Thus says the Lord of hosts; Again in this place, which is desolate without man and without beast, and in all its cities, shall be a habitation of shepherds who make their flocks lie down.
verses.Jeremiah|33|13: In the cities of the mountains, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the south, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shall the flocks pass again under the hands of him that counts them, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|33|14: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will perform that good thing which I have promised to the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|33|15: In those days, and at that time, will I cause an offshoot of righteousness to grow up for David; and he shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
verses.Jeremiah|33|16: In those days shall Judah be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell safely: and this is the name whereby she shall be called, namely, The Lord is our righteousness.
verses.Jeremiah|33|17: For thus says the Lord; David shall never lack a man sitting upon the throne of the house of Israel;
verses.Jeremiah|33|18: Neither shall the priests the Levites lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to burn meal offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.
verses.Jeremiah|33|19: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|33|20: Thus says the Lord; If you can break My covenant with the day, and My covenant with the night, and that there should not be day and night in their season;
verses.Jeremiah|33|21: then also My covenant may be broken with David My servant, that he should not have a son to reign upon his throne; and with the Levites the priests, My ministers.
verses.Jeremiah|33|22: As the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David My servant, and the Levites that minister to me.
verses.Jeremiah|33|23: Moreover the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|33|24: Hast thou not observed what this people have spoken, saying, The two families which the Lord has chosen, he has cast them off? thus they have despised My people, so that they should no more be a nation in their sight.
verses.Jeremiah|33|25: Thus says the Lord; If I have not appointed my covenant with day and night, the ordinances of heaven and earth;
verses.Jeremiah|33|26: then will I cast away the seed of Jacob and David my servant, and not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. No, for I will cause their captivity to return, and have mercy on them.
verses.Jeremiah|34|1: The word which came to Jeremiah from the Lord, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth of his dominion, and all the people, fought against Jerusalem, and against all its cities, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|34|2: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel; Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and tell him, Thus says the Lord; Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire:
verses.Jeremiah|34|3: and thou shalt not escape out of his hand, but shalt surely be taken, and be delivered into his hand; and thy eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth, and thou shalt go to Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|34|4: Yet hear the word of the Lord, O Zedekiah king of Judah; Thus says the Lord of thee, Thou shalt not die by the sword:
verses.Jeremiah|34|5: but thou shalt die in peace: and with the burnings of thy fathers, the former kings which were before thee, so shall they make a burning for thee; and they will lament thee, saying, Ah master! for I have pronounced a word, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|34|6: Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,
verses.Jeremiah|34|7: when the army of the king of Babylon fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish, and against Azekah; for these fortified cities remained of the cities of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|34|8: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, after the king Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people which were at Jerusalem, proclaim liberty to them;
verses.Jeremiah|34|9: that every man should let his Hebrew manservant, and every man his Hebrew maidservant, go free; that none should enslave any of them, namely a man of Judah, being his brother.
verses.Jeremiah|34|10: Now when all the princes, and all the people, who had entered into the covenant, heard that every one should let his manservant, and every one his maidservant, go free, that none should enslave them any more, then they obeyed, and let them go.
verses.Jeremiah|34|11: But afterwards they relapsed, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection for servants and for handmaids.
verses.Jeremiah|34|12: Therefore the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah from the Lord saying,
verses.Jeremiah|34|13: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel; I made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|34|14: At the end of seven years, shall you release every man his brother being a Hebrew, who has been sold to thee; and when he has served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free from thee: but your fathers hearkened not to Me, neither inclined their ear.
verses.Jeremiah|34|15: And you now turned, and had done right in My sight, in proclaiming liberty every man to his neighbour; and you had made a covenant before Me in the house which is called by My name:
verses.Jeremiah|34|16: nevertheless you relapsed and have profaned My name, and everyone of you has caused his servant, and his handmaid, (whom he had set at liberty at their pleasure,) to return, and has brought them into subjection, to be to you for servants and for handmaids.
verses.Jeremiah|34|17: Therefore thus says the Lord; since you have not hearkened to Me, in proclaiming liberty, everyone to his brother, and everyone to his neighbour: behold, I proclaim a liberty for you, says the Lord, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine; and I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.
verses.Jeremiah|34|18: And I will give the men that have transgressed My covenant, who have not performed the words of the covenant which they made before Me, when they cut the calf in two, and passed between its sections,
verses.Jeremiah|34|19: the princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land, who passed between the sections of the calf;
verses.Jeremiah|34|20: I will give them into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life: and their dead bodies shall be for food to the birds of the heaven, and to the beasts of the earth.
verses.Jeremiah|34|21: And Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes will I give into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life, and into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, who are gone up from you.
verses.Jeremiah|34|22: Behold, I will command, says the Lord, and cause them to return to this city; and they shall fight against it, and burn it with fire: and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.
verses.Jeremiah|35|1: The word which came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|35|2: Go to the house of the Rechabites, and speak to them, and bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.
verses.Jeremiah|35|3: Then I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah, and his brothers, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;
verses.Jeremiah|35|4: and I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was by the chamber of the princes, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the door:
verses.Jeremiah|35|5: and I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites goblets full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, Drink wine.
verses.Jeremiah|35|6: But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, You shall drink no wine, neither you, nor your sons for ever:
verses.Jeremiah|35|7: Neither shall you build a house, nor sow seed, nor plant a vineyard, nor have one: but all your days you shall dwell in tents; that you may live many days in the land where you sojourn.
verses.Jeremiah|35|8: And we have obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab our father in all that he charged us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters;
verses.Jeremiah|35|9: nor to build houses for us to dwell in; neither have we vineyard, nor field, nor seed:
verses.Jeremiah|35|10: but we have dwelt in tents, and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
verses.Jeremiah|35|11: But it came to pass, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up into the land that we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of Syria: so we dwell at Jerusalem.
verses.Jeremiah|35|12: Then came the word of the Lord to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|35|13: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Go and tell the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will you not receive instruction to hearken to my words? says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|35|14: The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, has been kept; for to this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: yet I have spoken to you, from morning till night; but you did not hearken to me.
verses.Jeremiah|35|15: I have also sent to you all my servants the prophets, sending them from morning till night, saying, Return now every man from his evil way, and amend your doings, and go not after other gods to serve them, and then you shall dwell in the land which I have given to you and to your fathers: but you have not inclined your ear, nor hearkened to me.
verses.Jeremiah|35|16: For the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have kept the commandment of their father, which he commanded them; but this people has not hearkened to me:
verses.Jeremiah|35|17: therefore thus says the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I have pronounced against them: because I have spoken to them, but they have not heard; and I have called to them, but they have not answered.
verses.Jeremiah|35|18: And Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Because you have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according to all that he has commanded you:
verses.Jeremiah|35|19: therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not lack a man to stand before me for ever.
verses.Jeremiah|36|1: And it came to pass in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|36|2: Take a scroll, and write in it all the words which I have spoken to thee about Israel, and about Judah, and about all the nations, from the day I spoke to thee, from the days of Josiah, and to this day.
verses.Jeremiah|36|3: It may be that the house of Judah will hear all the evil which I purpose to do to them; that they may return every man from his evil way; that I may forgive their iniquity and their sin.
verses.Jeremiah|36|4: Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah: and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord, which he had spoken to him, upon a scroll.
verses.Jeremiah|36|5: And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am confined; I cannot go into the house of the Lord:
verses.Jeremiah|36|6: therefore go thou and read in the scroll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the Lord in the ears of the people in the Lord's house upon the fast day: and also thou shalt read them in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities.
verses.Jeremiah|36|7: It may be they will present their supplication before the Lord, and will return every one from his evil way: for great is the anger and the fury that the Lord has pronounced against this people.
verses.Jeremiah|36|8: And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the Lord in the Lord's house.
verses.Jeremiah|36|9: And it came to pass in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before the Lord to all the people in Jerusalem, and to all the people that came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem.
verses.Jeremiah|36|10: Then Baruch read in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the Lord's house, in the ears of all the people.
verses.Jeremiah|36|11: When Micaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, had heard out of the book all the words of the Lord,
verses.Jeremiah|36|12: then he went down into the king's house, into the scribe's chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there, Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
verses.Jeremiah|36|13: Then Micaiah declared to them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people.
verses.Jeremiah|36|14: Therefore all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, Take in thy hand the scroll in which thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch the son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand, and came to them.
verses.Jeremiah|36|15: And they said to him, Sit down now, and read it in our ears. So Baruch read it in their ears.
verses.Jeremiah|36|16: Now it came to pass, when they had heard all the words, they turned to one another in fear, and said to Baruch, We will surely tell the king of all these words,
verses.Jeremiah|36|17: and they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now, How didst thou write all these words at his mouth?
verses.Jeremiah|36|18: Then Baruch answered them, He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink in the book.
verses.Jeremiah|36|19: Then the princes said to Baruch, Go, hide thyself, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where you are.
verses.Jeremiah|36|20: And they went in to the king to the court, but they deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and recited all the words in the ears of the king.
verses.Jeremiah|36|21: So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll: and he took it out of the chamber of Elishama the scribe. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes who stood beside the king.
verses.Jeremiah|36|22: Now the king sat in the winter house in the ninth month: and there was a fire in the brazier burning before him.
verses.Jeremiah|36|23: And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he would cut it with a penknife, and cast it into the fire that was in the brazier, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.
verses.Jeremiah|36|24: Yet they were not afraid, nor rent their garments, neither the king, nor any of his servants that heard all these words.
verses.Jeremiah|36|25: Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah even pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll: but he would not listen to them.
verses.Jeremiah|36|26: But the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet: but the Lord hid them.
verses.Jeremiah|36|27: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll, with the words which Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|36|28: Take thee again another scroll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first scroll, which Jehoiakim the king of Judah has burned.
verses.Jeremiah|36|29: And thou shalt say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, Thus says the Lord; Thou hast burned this scroll, saying, Why hast thou written in it to say that The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall cut off from it both man and beast?
verses.Jeremiah|36|30: Therefore thus says the Lord of Jehoiakim king of Judah; He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day, and to the frost by night.
verses.Jeremiah|36|31: And I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them; but they hearkened not.
verses.Jeremiah|36|32: Then Jeremiah took another scroll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah; who wrote in it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire: and there were added to them besides many similar words.
verses.Jeremiah|37|1: And king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|37|2: But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, hearkened to the words of the Lord, which he spoke by the prophet Jeremiah.
verses.Jeremiah|37|3: And Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to the prophet Jeremiah, saying, Pray for us to the Lord our God.
verses.Jeremiah|37|4: Now Jeremiah came in and went out among the people: for they had not put him into prison.
verses.Jeremiah|37|5: Then Pharaoh's army was come out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem.
verses.Jeremiah|37|6: Then came the word of the Lord to the prophet Jeremiah saying,
verses.Jeremiah|37|7: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel; Thus shall you say to the king of Judah, that sent you to me to inquire of me; Behold, Pharaoh's army, which is come out to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land.
verses.Jeremiah|37|8: And the Chaldeans shall come back, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire.
verses.Jeremiah|37|9: Thus says the Lord; Do not deceive yourselves, saying, The Chaldeans shall surely depart from us: for they shall not depart.
verses.Jeremiah|37|10: For even if you had smitten the whole army of the Chaldeans that fight against you, and there remained but wounded men among them, yet should they rise up every man in his tent, and burn this city with fire.
verses.Jeremiah|37|11: And it came to pass that when the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army,
verses.Jeremiah|37|12: then Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to slip out from these amongst the people.
verses.Jeremiah|37|13: And when he was in the gate of Benjamin, a sentry was there, whose name was Jeriah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, Thou art deserting to the Chaldeans.
verses.Jeremiah|37|14: Then Jeremiah said, It is false; I am not deserting to the Chaldeans. But he did not hearken to him: so Jeriah seized Jeremiah, and brought him to the princes.
verses.Jeremiah|37|15: So the princes were angry with Jeremiah, and struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe: for they had made that the prison.
verses.Jeremiah|37|16: When Jeremiah was entered into the pit, and into the cells, and Jeremiah had remained there many days;
verses.Jeremiah|37|17: then Zedekiah the king sent, and took him out: and the king asked him secretly in his house, and said, Is there any word from the Lord? And Jeremiah said, There is: for, said he, thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|37|18: Moreover Jeremiah said to king Zedekiah, How have I offended against thee, or against thy servants, or against this people, that you have put me in prison?
verses.Jeremiah|37|19: Where are now your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, The king of Babylon shall not come against you, nor against this land?
verses.Jeremiah|37|20: Therefore hear now, I pray thee, O my lord the king: let my supplication, I pray thee be accepted before thee; that thou cause me not to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.
verses.Jeremiah|37|21: Then Zedekiah the king commanded that they should commit Jeremiah to the court of the guard, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread out of the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was spent. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
verses.Jeremiah|38|1: Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchijah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken to all the people, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|38|2: Thus says the Lord, He that remains in this city shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: but he that goes over to the Chaldeans shall live; for he shall have his life for a prey, and shall live.
verses.Jeremiah|38|3: Thus says the Lord, This city shall surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, who shall take it.
verses.Jeremiah|38|4: Therefore the princes said to the king, We pray thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakens the hands of the men of war that remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words to them: for this man seeks not the welfare of this people, but their hurt.
verses.Jeremiah|38|5: Then Zedekiah, the king said, Behold, he is in your hand: for the king can do nothing against you.
verses.Jeremiah|38|6: Then they took Jeremiah and cast him into the pit of Hammelech the king's son, which was in the court of the guard: and they let Jeremiah down with ropes. And in the pit there was no water, but only mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.
verses.Jeremiah|38|7: Now when Ebed-melech the Cushi, a eunuch who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the pit; (the king was sitting in the gate of Benjamin)
verses.Jeremiah|38|8: then Ebed-melech went out of the king's house, and spoke to the king, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|38|9: My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the pit; and he may well die there of hunger: seeing that there is no more bread in the city.
verses.Jeremiah|38|10: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushi, saying, Take from here thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the pit, before he dies.
verses.Jeremiah|38|11: So Ebed-melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took from there old rags and worn out clothes, and let them down by ropes into the pit to Jeremiah.
verses.Jeremiah|38|12: And Ebed-melech the Cushi said to Jeremiah, Put now these old rags and clothes into thy armpits under the ropes. And Jeremiah did so.
verses.Jeremiah|38|13: So they drew up Jeremiah with the ropes, and took him up out of the pit: and Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
verses.Jeremiah|38|14: Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet to him into the third entry that is in the house of the Lord: and the king said to Jeremiah, I will ask thee something; hide nothing from me.
verses.Jeremiah|38|15: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, If I declare it to thee, wilt thou not surely put me to death? and if I give thee counsel, thou wilt not hearken to me.
verses.Jeremiah|38|16: So Zedekiah the king swore secretly to Jeremiah, saying, As the Lord lives, that made us this soul, I will not put thee to death, neither will I give thee into the hand of these men that seek thy life.
verses.Jeremiah|38|17: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt indeed go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou and thy house shall live:
verses.Jeremiah|38|18: but if thou wilt not go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.
verses.Jeremiah|38|19: And Zedekiah the king said to Jeremiah, I am afraid of the men of Judah who have deserted to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they torture me.
verses.Jeremiah|38|20: But Jeremiah said, They shall not deliver thee. Obey now the voice of the Lord, which I speak to thee: so it shall be well with thee, and thy soul shall live.
verses.Jeremiah|38|21: But if thou refuse to go out, this is the word that the Lord has shown me.
verses.Jeremiah|38|22: And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah's house shall be brought out to the princes of the king of Babylon, and those women shall say, Thy familiar friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, they are turned away back.
verses.Jeremiah|38|23: So they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.
verses.Jeremiah|38|24: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, Let no man know of these words, and thou shalt not die.
verses.Jeremiah|38|25: But if the princes hear that I have talked with thee, and they come to thee, and say to thee, Tell us now what thou hast said to the king, hide it not from us, and we will not put thee to death; and also what the king said to thee:
verses.Jeremiah|38|26: then thou shalt say to them, I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathan's house, to die there.
verses.Jeremiah|38|27: Then all the princes came to Jeremiah and asked him: and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they left off speaking with him; for the matter was not overheard.
verses.Jeremiah|38|28: So Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard until the day that Jerusalem was taken: And he was there when Jerusalem was taken.
verses.Jeremiah|39|1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and they besieged it.
verses.Jeremiah|39|2: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, a breach was made in the city.
verses.Jeremiah|39|3: And all the princes of the king of Babylon, came in, and sat in the middle gate, namely Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer Rab-mag, with all the remainder of the princes of the king of Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|39|4: And it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah, and all the men of war saw them, then they fled, and went out of the city by night, by the way of the king's garden, by the gate between the two walls: and he went out the way of the Arabah.
verses.Jeremiah|39|5: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him.
verses.Jeremiah|39|6: Then the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes: also the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|39|7: Moreover he put out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with fetters, to carry him to Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|39|8: And the Chaldeans burned the king's house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.Jeremiah|39|9: Then Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city and the deserters who had deserted to him, with the rest of the people that remained.
verses.Jeremiah|39|10: But Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, who had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
verses.Jeremiah|39|11: Now Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|39|12: Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do to him as he shall say to thee.
verses.Jeremiah|39|13: Then sent Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard, and Nebushasban, the Rab-saris, and Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag and all the princes of the king of Babylon:
verses.Jeremiah|39|14: and they sent, and took Jeremiah out of the court of the guard, and committed him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him home: so he dwelt among the people.
verses.Jeremiah|39|15: Now the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the guard, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|39|16: Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Cushi, saying, Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.
verses.Jeremiah|39|17: But I will deliver thee on that day, says the Lord: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid;
verses.Jeremiah|39|18: for I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey to thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|40|1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, after Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him bound as he was in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were carried away as exiles to Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|40|2: And the captain of the guard took Jeremiah, and said to him, The Lord thy God has pronounced this evil upon this place.
verses.Jeremiah|40|3: Now the Lord has brought it, and done according as he has said: because you have sinned against the Lord, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you.
verses.Jeremiah|40|4: And now, behold, I release thee this day from the chains which were upon thy hand. If it seem good to thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look after thee: but if it seem ill to thee to come with me into Babylon, do not come: behold, all the land is before thee: wherever it seems good and convenient for thee to go, go there.
verses.Jeremiah|40|5: (Then since he did not yet turn about;) Go back then, said he, Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has made governor over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people: or go wherever it seems convenient to thee to go. So the captain of the guard gave him an allowance of food and a present, and let him go.
verses.Jeremiah|40|6: Then Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and dwelt with him among the people that were left in the land.
verses.Jeremiah|40|7: Now when all the captains of the forces which were in the fields, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed to him men, and women, and children, and of the poor of the land, of them that were not carried away captive to Babylon;
verses.Jeremiah|40|8: then they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, namely, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maachathite, they and their men.
verses.Jeremiah|40|9: And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men, saying, Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.
verses.Jeremiah|40|10: As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us: but as for you, gather wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.
verses.Jeremiah|40|11: Likewise when all the men of Judah that were in Moab, and among the children of Ammon, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan;
verses.Jeremiah|40|12: then all the men of Judah returned out of all places unto which they were driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, to Mizpah, and gathered a great abundance of wine and summer fruits.
verses.Jeremiah|40|13: Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were in the countryside, came to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
verses.Jeremiah|40|14: and said to him, Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the children of Ammon has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee? But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam did not believe them.
verses.Jeremiah|40|15: Then Johanan the son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: why should he slay thee, that all Judah that are gathered to thee should be scattered, and the remnant of Judah should perish?
verses.Jeremiah|40|16: But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said to Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.
verses.Jeremiah|41|1: Now it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and some of the chief officers of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah.
verses.Jeremiah|41|2: Then Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and the ten men that were with him arose, and struck Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
verses.Jeremiah|41|3: And Ishmael slew all the men of Judah that were with him, with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war.
verses.Jeremiah|41|4: And it came to pass on the second day after the killing of Gedaliah, (and no man knew it,)
verses.Jeremiah|41|5: that there came certain men from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty men, (their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves,) with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|41|6: And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out of Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, that he said to them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.
verses.Jeremiah|41|7: And when they came into the midst of the city, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him.
verses.Jeremiah|41|8: But ten men were found among them that said to Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have in the countryside hidden stores, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he desisted, and did not slay them among their brethren.
verses.Jeremiah|41|9: Now the pit wherein into which Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was that which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.
verses.Jeremiah|41|10: Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, the king's daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the children of Ammon.
verses.Jeremiah|41|11: But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
verses.Jeremiah|41|12: then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great pool of waters that are in Gibeon.
verses.Jeremiah|41|13: Now it came to pass, that when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad.
verses.Jeremiah|41|14: So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah turned about and came back, and went to Johanan the son of Kareah.
verses.Jeremiah|41|15: But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the children of Ammon.
verses.Jeremiah|41|16: Then Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, took all the remnant of the people from Mizpah, whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, (after the latter had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam,) mighty men of war, and the women, and the children, and the eunuchs whom he then brought from Gibeon:
verses.Jeremiah|41|17: and they departed, and dwelt in Chimham, which is by Beth-lehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
verses.Jeremiah|41|18: because of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because of Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
verses.Jeremiah|42|1: Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even to the greatest, came near,
verses.Jeremiah|42|2: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, Let now our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us to the Lord thy God, for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thy eyes see us: )
verses.Jeremiah|42|3: that the Lord thy God may show us the way in which we may walk, and the thing we may do.
verses.Jeremiah|42|4: Then Jeremiah the prophet said to them, I have heard you; behold, I will pray to the Lord your God according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatever thing the Lord shall answer you, I will declare it to you; I will keep nothing back from you.
verses.Jeremiah|42|5: Then they said to Jeremiah, The Lord be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not act according to all the things for which the Lord thy God shall send thee to us.
verses.Jeremiah|42|6: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the Lord our God.
verses.Jeremiah|42|7: And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
verses.Jeremiah|42|8: Then he called Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
verses.Jeremiah|42|9: and he said to them, Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your supplication before him;
verses.Jeremiah|42|10: If you will still abide in this land, then I will build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up: for I repent of the evil that I have done to you.
verses.Jeremiah|42|11: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; be not afraid of him, says the Lord: for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
verses.Jeremiah|42|12: And I will show mercies to you, that he may have mercy upon you, and let you return to your own land.
verses.Jeremiah|42|13: But if you say, We will not dwell in this land, neither obey the voice of the Lord your God,
verses.Jeremiah|42|14: saying, No; but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the shofar, nor have hunger for bread; and there will we dwell:
verses.Jeremiah|42|15: and now therefore hear the word of the Lord, you remnant of Judah; thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; If indeed you set your faces to enter into Egypt and go to sojourn there;
verses.Jeremiah|42|16: then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which you feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, of which you were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there you shall die.
verses.Jeremiah|42|17: And all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: and none of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.
verses.Jeremiah|42|18: For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; As my anger and my fury has been poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured out upon you, when you shall enter into Egypt: and you shall be an oath, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and you shall see this place no more.
verses.Jeremiah|42|19: The Lord has said concerning you, O remnant of Judah; Do not go into Egypt: know certainly that I have forewarned you this day.
verses.Jeremiah|42|20: For you have gone astray at peril of your lives, when you sent me to the Lord your God, saying, Pray for us to the Lord our God; and according to all that the Lord our God shall say, so declare to us, and we will do it.
verses.Jeremiah|42|21: And now I have this day declared it to you; but you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, nor anything for which he has sent me to you.
verses.Jeremiah|42|22: Now therefore know certainly that you shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place where you desire to go and to sojourn.
verses.Jeremiah|43|1: And it came to pass, that when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking to all the people all the words of the Lord their God, for which the Lord their God had sent him to them, all these words,
verses.Jeremiah|43|2: then Azariah the son of Hoshaiah and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men, spoke, saying to Jeremiah, Thou speakest falsely: the Lord our God has not sent thee to say, Do not go into Egypt to sojourn there:
verses.Jeremiah|43|3: but Baruch the son of Neriah sets thee on against us, to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us into Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|43|4: So Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, and all the people, did not obey the voice of the Lord, to dwell in the land of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|43|5: But Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, took all the remnant of Judah, that were returned from all nations, into which they had been driven, to dwell in the land of Judah;
verses.Jeremiah|43|6: men, and women, and children, and the king's daughters, and every person that Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, together with Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.
verses.Jeremiah|43|7: And they came into the land of Egypt: for they did not obey the voice of the Lord: thus they came to Tahpanhes.
verses.Jeremiah|43|8: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|43|9: Take great stones in thy hand, and hide them in the mortar in the brick work, which is at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;
verses.Jeremiah|43|10: and say to them, Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid; and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them.
verses.Jeremiah|43|11: And when he comes, he shall smite the land of Egypt, and deliver such as are for death to death; and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword.
verses.Jeremiah|43|12: And I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he shall burn them, and carry them away captives: and he shall fold up the land of Egypt, as a shepherd folds up his garment; and he shall go out from there in peace.
verses.Jeremiah|43|13: And he shall break up the pillars of Beth-shemesh, that are in the land of Egypt; and he shall burn with fire the houses of the gods of Egypt.
verses.Jeremiah|44|1: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the men of Judah who dwelt in the land of Egypt, who dwelt at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|44|2: Thus says the Lord of hosts the God of Israel; You have seen all the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, and upon all the cities of Judah; and, behold, this day they are a ruin, and no one dwells in them,
verses.Jeremiah|44|3: because of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to anger, in that they went to burn incense, and to serve other gods, whom they knew not, neither they, you, nor your fathers.
verses.Jeremiah|44|4: Yet I sent to you all my servants the prophets, sending them from morning till night, saying, Oh, do not do this abominable thing that I hate.
verses.Jeremiah|44|5: But they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness, to burn no incense to other gods.
verses.Jeremiah|44|6: So that my fury and my anger was poured forth, and was kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they have become a waste and a desolation, as at this day.
verses.Jeremiah|44|7: Therefore now thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; Why do you commit this great evil against your souls, to cut off from you man and woman, child and suckling, from the midst of Judah, leaving you no remnant;
verses.Jeremiah|44|8: in that you provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt into which you are gone to dwell, that you might cut yourselves off, and that you might be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.Jeremiah|44|9: Have you forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives which they have committed in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?
verses.Jeremiah|44|10: They are not humbled to this day, neither have they feared, nor followed my law, nor my statutes, that I set before you and before your fathers.
verses.Jeremiah|44|11: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, and to cut off all Judah,
verses.Jeremiah|44|12: and I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; they shall be consumed, and by the sword and by the famine: they shall die, from the least even to the greatest, by the sword and by the famine: and they shall become an oath, an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach.
verses.Jeremiah|44|13: For I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence:
verses.Jeremiah|44|14: so that none of the remnant of Judah, who are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or survive, to return to the land of Judah, to which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none but fugitives shall return.
verses.Jeremiah|44|15: Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great multitude even all the people that dwelt in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|44|16: As for the word that thou hast spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not hearken to thee,
verses.Jeremiah|44|17: but we will certainly do everything that we uttered with our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem: for then we had plenty of bread, and were well off, and saw no evil.
verses.Jeremiah|44|18: But since we left off burning incense to the queen of heaven, and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.
verses.Jeremiah|44|19: And when we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured out drink offerings to her, did we alone make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her, without our menfolk?
verses.Jeremiah|44|20: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men, and to the women, and to all the people who had given him that answer, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|44|21: The incense that you burned in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, you, and your fathers, your kings, and your princes, and the people of the land, did not the Lord remember them, and came it not into his mind?
verses.Jeremiah|44|22: so that the Lord could no longer bear the evil of your doings, and the abominations which you committed; therefore is your land a ruin, and an astonishment, and a curse, without inhabitant, as at this day.
verses.Jeremiah|44|23: Because you burned incense, and because you sinned against the Lord, and did not obey the voice of the Lord, nor followed his law, nor his statutes, nor his testimonies; therefore this evil has happened to you, as at this day.
verses.Jeremiah|44|24: Moreover Jeremiah said to all the people, and to all the women, Hear the word of the Lord, all those of Judah who are in the land of Egypt:
verses.Jeremiah|44|25: thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel saying; You and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hands, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to her: if you will accomplish your vows, accomplish them; and if you will perform your vows, then perform them.
verses.Jeremiah|44|26: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all those of Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, says the Lord, that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, the Lord God lives.
verses.Jeremiah|44|27: Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.
verses.Jeremiah|44|28: Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, who are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs.
verses.Jeremiah|44|29: And this shall be a sign to you, says the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, that you may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil:
verses.Jeremiah|44|30: thus says the Lord; Behold, I will give Pharaoh Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, who was his enemy, and sought his life.
verses.Jeremiah|45|1: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|45|2: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel to thee, O Baruch;
verses.Jeremiah|45|3: Thou didst say, Woe is me now! for the Lord has added grief to my pain; I am weary in my sighing, and I find no rest.
verses.Jeremiah|45|4: Thus shalt thou say to him, The Lord says thus; Behold, that which I have built I break down, and that which I have planted I pluck up, namely this whole land.
verses.Jeremiah|45|5: And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says the Lord: but thy life I will give to thee for a prey in all the places to which thou goest.
verses.Jeremiah|46|1: The word of the Lord which came to Jeremiah the prophet against the nations;
verses.Jeremiah|46|2: against Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah.
verses.Jeremiah|46|3: Order the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.
verses.Jeremiah|46|4: Harness the horses; and mount, O horsemen, and stand to with your helmets; polish the spears, and put on the coats of mail.
verses.Jeremiah|46|5: Why have I seen them dismayed and turning back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled away, and they do not look back: terror all around, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|46|6: Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall towards the north by the river Euphrates.
verses.Jeremiah|46|7: Who is this that rises like the River, and like streams of turbulent waters?
verses.Jeremiah|46|8: Egypt rises like the River, and like streams of turbulent waters: and he says I will go up, and I will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.
verses.Jeremiah|46|9: Come up, O horses; and rage, O chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; Ethiopia and Put, that handle the shield; and Ludim, that handle and bend the bow.
verses.Jeremiah|46|10: For this is the day of the Lord God of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be sated, and drink its fill of their blood: for the Lord God of hosts has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
verses.Jeremiah|46|11: Go up to Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, daughter of Egypt: in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured.
verses.Jeremiah|46|12: The nations have heard of thy shame, and thy cry has filled the land: for the mighty man has stumbled against the mighty, and they are both fallen together.
verses.Jeremiah|46|13: The word that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt.
verses.Jeremiah|46|14: Declare in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and report in Noph and in Tahpanhes: say, Stand to, and prepare thyself; for the sword shall devour round about thee.
verses.Jeremiah|46|15: Why are thy valiant men swept away? None of them stood, because the Lord did thrust him down.
verses.Jeremiah|46|16: He made many to fall, indeed, one fell upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.
verses.Jeremiah|46|17: They did cry there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has passed the time appointed.
verses.Jeremiah|46|18: As I live, says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts, Surely as Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.
verses.Jeremiah|46|19: O thou daughter dwelling in Egypt, furnish thyself with the baggage of Exile: for Noph shall be waste and desolate without inhabitant.
verses.Jeremiah|46|20: Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction comes; it comes out of the north.
verses.Jeremiah|46|21: Also her hired men in the midst of her are like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together: they did not stand, because the day of their calamity was come upon them, and the time of their punishment.
verses.Jeremiah|46|22: Her sound is like that of a snake on the move; for they shall march with force and come against her with axes, like hewers of wood.
verses.Jeremiah|46|23: They shall cut down her forest, says the Lord, though it cannot be searched; because they are more numerous than locusts, and are innumerable.
verses.Jeremiah|46|24: The daughter of Egypt shall be confounded; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.
verses.Jeremiah|46|25: The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says; Behold, I will punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all those who trust in him:
verses.Jeremiah|46|26: and I will deliver them into the hand of those who seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants: and afterwards it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|46|27: But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be quiet and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
verses.Jeremiah|46|28: Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, says the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in due measure; yet will I not utterly destroy thee.
verses.Jeremiah|47|1: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before Pharaoh smote Gaza.
verses.Jeremiah|47|2: Thus says the Lord; Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all its fullness; the city, and those who dwell in it; then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl.
verses.Jeremiah|47|3: At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his stallions, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers do not look back to their children for feebleness of hands;
verses.Jeremiah|47|4: because of the day that comes to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyre and Zidon every helper that remains: for the Lord will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.
verses.Jeremiah|47|5: Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off; O remnant of their valley, how long wilt thou gash thyself?
verses.Jeremiah|47|6: O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still.
verses.Jeremiah|47|7: How can it be quiet, seeing the Lord has given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there he has appointed it.
verses.Jeremiah|48|1: Against Moab thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe to Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kirjathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed.
verses.Jeremiah|48|2: There shall be no more praise of Moab: in Heshbon they have devised evil against it; come, and let us cut it off from being a nation. Also thou shalt be cut down, O Madmen; the sword shall pursue thee.
verses.Jeremiah|48|3: A voice of crying shall come from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.
verses.Jeremiah|48|4: Moab is destroyed; her little ones have raised a cry.
verses.Jeremiah|48|5: For in the ascent of Luhith with continual weeping shall they go up; for in the going down of Horonaim they have heard the distressing cry of destruction.
verses.Jeremiah|48|6: Flee, save your lives, and be like the juniper tree in the wilderness.
verses.Jeremiah|48|7: For because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: and Chemosh shall go out into exile, his priests and his princes together.
verses.Jeremiah|48|8: And the spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape: the valley also shall be ruined, and the plain shall be destroyed, as the Lord has spoken.
verses.Jeremiah|48|9: Give wings to Moab, that it may flee and get away: for her cities shall be desolate, without any to dwell in them.
verses.Jeremiah|48|10: Cursed be he that does the work of the Lord negligently, and cursed be he that keeps back his sword from blood.
verses.Jeremiah|48|11: Moab has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his lees, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither has he gone into exile: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed.
verses.Jeremiah|48|12: Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send to him tilters who will tilt him, and will empty his vessels, and break their bottles.
verses.Jeremiah|48|13: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth-el their confidence.
verses.Jeremiah|48|14: How say you, We are mighty and strong men for the war?
verses.Jeremiah|48|15: Moab is spoiled, and they have gone up into her cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
verses.Jeremiah|48|16: The calamity of Moab is near at hand, and his affliction hastens space.
verses.Jeremiah|48|17: All you that are about him, bemoan him, and all you that know his name; say, How is the strong staff broken, and the glorious rod!
verses.Jeremiah|48|18: Thou daughter that dost inhabit Dibon, come down from thy glory, and sit in thirst; for the spoiler of Moab shall come upon thee, and he shall destroy thy strongholds.
verses.Jeremiah|48|19: O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that flees, and her that escapes, and say, What is done?
verses.Jeremiah|48|20: Moab is confounded; for it is broken down: howl and cry; tell it in Arnon, that Moab is spoiled,
