verses.Jeremiah|48|21: and judgment is come upon the plain country; upon Holon, and upon Jahzah, and upon Mephaath,
verses.Jeremiah|48|22: and upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Beth-diblathaim,
verses.Jeremiah|48|23: and upon Kirjathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon,
verses.Jeremiah|48|24: and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
verses.Jeremiah|48|25: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|48|26: Make him drunk: for he magnified himself against the Lord: Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he too shall be in derision.
verses.Jeremiah|48|27: For was not Israel a derision to thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou didst speak of him, thou didst wag the head.
verses.Jeremiah|48|28: O you that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that makes her nest in the sides of the mouth of the abyss.
verses.Jeremiah|48|29: We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogance and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
verses.Jeremiah|48|30: I know, says the Lord, his insolence, and his injustice; his pratings have wrought injustice.
verses.Jeremiah|48|31: Therefore will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; there will be mourning for the men of Kir-heres.
verses.Jeremiah|48|32: O vine of Sibmah I will weep for thee with the weeping of Jazer: thy branches are gone over the sea, they reach to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage.
verses.Jeremiah|48|33: And joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting of joy; their shouting shall be no shouting.
verses.Jeremiah|48|34: From the cry of Heshbon to Elealeh, to Jahaz, they have uttered their voice; from Zoar to Horonaim, Eglat, Shelishiiah; for also the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate.
verses.Jeremiah|48|35: Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, says the Lord, him that offers in the high place, and him that burns incense to his gods.
verses.Jeremiah|48|36: Therefore my heart shall moan for Moab like flutes, and my heart shall moan like pipes for the men of Kir-heres: because the abundance that he has gained has perished.
verses.Jeremiah|48|37: For every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: upon all the hands shall be gashes, and upon the loins sackcloth.
verses.Jeremiah|48|38: There shall be lamentation generally upon all the housetops of Moab, and in its streets; for I have broken Moab like an unwanted vessel, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|48|39: They shall howl, saying, How is it broken down! how has Moab turned her back with shame! so shall Moab be a derision and a cause of despair to all them about him.
verses.Jeremiah|48|40: For thus says the Lord; Behold, he shall fly like an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab.
verses.Jeremiah|48|41: Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are surprised, and the mighty men's hearts in Moab at that day shall be like the heart of a woman in her pangs;
verses.Jeremiah|48|42: and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he has magnified himself against the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|48|43: Terror, and pit, and snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|48|44: He that flees from the Terror shall fall into the pit; and he that gets up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, upon Moab, the year of their punishment, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|48|45: In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stood without strength: for a fire has gone out of Heshbon and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and has devoured the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the roaring people.
verses.Jeremiah|48|46: Woe to these, O Moab! The people of Chemosh is perishing: for thy sons are taken into captivity, and thy daughters into thraldom.
verses.Jeremiah|48|47: Yet I will bring back the captivity of Moab in the latter days, says the Lord. Thus for the judgment of Moab.
verses.Jeremiah|49|1: Concerning the children of Ammon, thus says the Lord; Has Israel no sons? has he no heir? why then does Malcham inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?
verses.Jeremiah|49|2: Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the children of Ammon; and it shall become a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel dispossess those who dispossessed him, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|49|3: Howl, O Heshbon, for Ai is plundered: cry, O daughters of Rabbah, gird yourselves with sackcloth; lament, and run to and fro by the hedges; for Malcham shall go into exile, and his priests and his princes together.
verses.Jeremiah|49|4: Why dost thou glory in the valleys? thy valley flows with blood, O backsliding daughter, that trusts in her treasures, saying, Who shall come against me?
verses.Jeremiah|49|5: Behold, I will bring terror upon thee, says the Lord God of hosts, from all those who are round about thee; and you shall be driven out every man straight before him; and there shall be none to take in the wanderer.
verses.Jeremiah|49|6: And afterwards I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|49|7: Concerning Edom, thus says the Lord of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? has counsel perished from the prudent? has their wisdom vanished?
verses.Jeremiah|49|8: Flee, turn back, dwell in the deeps, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time when I punish him.
verses.Jeremiah|49|9: If grape gatherers come to thee, would they not leave some gleanings? if thieves by night, they will destroy only till they have enough.
verses.Jeremiah|49|10: But I have stripped Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is plundered, and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he himself is no more.
verses.Jeremiah|49|11: Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.
verses.Jeremiah|49|12: For thus says the Lord; Behold, they to whom it did not appertain to drink of the cup shall surely drink; and art thou one who shall go scot free? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink.
verses.Jeremiah|49|13: For I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all its cities shall be perpetual ruins.
verses.Jeremiah|49|14: I have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent to the heathen, saying, Gather yourselves together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.
verses.Jeremiah|49|15: For, lo, I have made thee small among the nations, despised among men.
verses.Jeremiah|49|16: Thy terribleness has deceived thee, and the pride of thy heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldst make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from there, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|49|17: Also Edom shall be a desolation: everyone that goes by it shall be horrified, and shall hiss at all her disasters.
verses.Jeremiah|49|18: As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbour cities, says the Lord, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.
verses.Jeremiah|49|19: Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the wild country of the Jordan against a strong sheepfold: for in a moment I will make him run over her: and whoever is chosen, I will appoint him over her; for who is like me? and who will set me a time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me?
verses.Jeremiah|49|20: Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he has taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the least of the flock shall drag them away: surely their fold shall be appalled at them.
verses.Jeremiah|49|21: The earth is moved at the noise of their fall; the sound of her cry is heard at the Red Sea.
verses.Jeremiah|49|22: Behold, he shall come up and fly like the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah: and at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
verses.Jeremiah|49|23: Concerning Damascus. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad: for they have heard evil tidings: they are fainthearted; there is anxiety on the sea; it cannot be quiet.
verses.Jeremiah|49|24: Damascus is grown feeble, and turns herself to flee, and fear has gripped her: anguish and sorrows have seized on her, like a woman in travail.
verses.Jeremiah|49|25: How was the city of praise left without succour, the city of my joy!
verses.Jeremiah|49|26: Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be cut off in that day, says the Lord of hosts.
verses.Jeremiah|49|27: And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben-hadad.
verses.Jeremiah|49|28: Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon shall smite, thus says the Lord; Arise, go up to Kedar, and plunder the men of the east.
verses.Jeremiah|49|29: Their tents and their flocks shall be taken away: they shall take to themselves their curtains, and all their vessels, and their camels; and they shall cry to them, Terror on every side!
verses.Jeremiah|49|30: Flee, get you far off, dwell in the deeps, O inhabitants of Hazor, says the Lord; for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has taken counsel against you, and has conceived a purpose against you.
verses.Jeremiah|49|31: Arise, get you up to a nation at ease, that dwells in security, says the Lord, who have neither gates nor bars, dwelling alone.
verses.Jeremiah|49|32: And their camels shall be a booty, and the multitude of their cattle a spoil: and I will scatter to every wind those who have the corners of their hair cut off; and I will bring their calamity from every side says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|49|33: And Hazor shall be a den of jackals, and a desolation for ever: there shall no man abide there, nor any son of man dwell in it.
verses.Jeremiah|49|34: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,
verses.Jeremiah|49|35: Thus says the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.
verses.Jeremiah|49|36: And upon Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and will scatter them to all those winds; and there shall be no nation to which the outcasts of Elam shall not come.
verses.Jeremiah|49|37: For I will cause Elam to lose heart before their enemies, and before them that seek their life: and I will bring evil upon them, my fierce anger, says the Lord; and I will send the sword after them, till I have consumed them:
verses.Jeremiah|49|38: and I will set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from there the king and the princes, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|49|39: But it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring back the captivity of Elam, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|50|1: The word that the Lord spoke against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans by Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.Jeremiah|50|2: Declare among the nations, and publish, and set up a banner; proclaim, and conceal not: say, Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces; her idols are put to shame, her images are shattered.
verses.Jeremiah|50|3: For out of the north comes up a nation against her, who shall make her land desolate, and none shall dwell in it: they shall remove, they shall depart, both man and beast.
verses.Jeremiah|50|4: In those days, and in that time, says the Lord, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together, going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the Lord their God.
verses.Jeremiah|50|5: They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces towards it, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the Lord in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten.
verses.Jeremiah|50|6: My people has been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their resting place.
verses.Jeremiah|50|7: All that found them have devoured them: and their adversaries have said, We are not guilty, because they have sinned against the Lord, the habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers.
verses.Jeremiah|50|8: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and depart from the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the he goats before the flocks.
verses.Jeremiah|50|9: For, lo, I will raise and cause to come up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the north country: and they shall array themselves against her; from there she shall be taken: their arrows shall be like those of a death dealing warrior; none shall return in vain.
verses.Jeremiah|50|10: And the land of the Chaldeans shall be a spoil: all that plunder her shall be satisfied, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|50|11: Because you were glad, because you rejoiced, O robbers of my heritage, because you are grown fat like the heifer at grass, and you neigh like stallions;
verses.Jeremiah|50|12: your mother shall be greatly ashamed; she that bore you shall be disgraced: behold, shall be the last of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
verses.Jeremiah|50|13: Because of the wrath of the Lord it shall not be inhabited, but it shall be wholly desolate: everyone that goes by Babylon shall be horrified, and shall hiss because of all her plagues.
verses.Jeremiah|50|14: Array yourselves against Babylon round about: all you that bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she has sinned against the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|50|15: Shout against her round about: she has submitted herself: her butresses are fallen, her walls are thrown down: for it is the vengeance of the Lord. Take vengeance upon her; as she has done, do to her!
verses.Jeremiah|50|16: Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him that handles the sickle in the time of harvest! For fear of the oppressing sword they shall turn everyone to his people, and they shall flee everyone to his own land.
verses.Jeremiah|50|17: Israel is a scattered sheep; the lions have driven him away: first the king of Assyria devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar has broken his bones.
verses.Jeremiah|50|18: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria.
verses.Jeremiah|50|19: And I will bring Israel back again to his habitation, and he shall feed on the Carmel and the Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and the Gilead.
verses.Jeremiah|50|20: In those days, and in that time, says the Lord, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, but they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I will leave as a remnant.
verses.Jeremiah|50|21: Go up against the land of Merathaim, against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: lay waste and utterly destroy after them, says the Lord, and do according to all that I have commanded thee.
verses.Jeremiah|50|22: A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.
verses.Jeremiah|50|23: How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!
verses.Jeremiah|50|24: I have laid a snare for thee, and thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|50|25: The Lord has opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation: for the Lord God of hosts has a work to do in the land of Chaldeans.
verses.Jeremiah|50|26: Come against her from the utmost border, open her stables: cast her up like heaps of grain, and destroy her utterly! let nothing of her be left!
verses.Jeremiah|50|27: Slay all her bullocks; let them go down to the slaughter: woe to them! for their day is come, the time of their punishment.
verses.Jeremiah|50|28: The voice of them that flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, the vengeance for his temple.
verses.Jeremiah|50|29: Call together the archers against Babylon: all you that bend the bow, camp against it round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her deeds; according to all that she has done, do to her: for she has been proud against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Jeremiah|50|30: Therefore shall her young men fall in the streets, and all her men of war shall be cut off in that day, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|50|31: Behold, I am against thee, O thou arrogant one, says the Lord God of hosts: for thy day is come, the time that I will punish thee.
verses.Jeremiah|50|32: And the arrogant one shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities and it shall devour all round about him.
verses.Jeremiah|50|33: Thus says the Lord of hosts; The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captive held them fast; they refused to let them go.
verses.Jeremiah|50|34: Their redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is his name: he will surely plead their cause, that he may give rest to the land, but unrest to the inhabitants of Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|50|35: A sword upon the Chaldeans, says the Lord, and upon the inhabitants of Babylon, and upon her princes, and upon her wise men!
verses.Jeremiah|50|36: A sword upon the liars; and they shall become fools: a sword upon her mighty men; and they shall be dismayed!
verses.Jeremiah|50|37: A sword upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her; and they shall become the women: a sword upon her treasures; and they shall be robbed!
verses.Jeremiah|50|38: A drought upon her waters; and they shall be dried up for it is a land of carved idols, and they are mad over things of horror.
verses.Jeremiah|50|39: Therefore the wild beasts of the desert shall dwell there, with jackals and desert owls: and it shall be no more inhabited forever; neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation.
verses.Jeremiah|50|40: As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbour cities, says the Lord; so shall no man abide there, neither shall any son of man dwell in it.
verses.Jeremiah|50|41: Behold, a people shall come from the north, and a great nation, and many kings shall be raised up from the farthest parts of the earth.
verses.Jeremiah|50|42: They shall hold the bow and javelin: they are cruel, and will not show mercy: their voice shall roar like the sea, and they shall ride upon horses, everyone lined up, like a man to the battle, against thee, O daughter of Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|50|43: The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands have grown feeble: anguish has taken hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail.
verses.Jeremiah|50|44: Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the wild country of the Jordan against a strong sheepfold: for in a moment I will make them run over her: and whoever is chosen I will appoint him over her; for who is like me? and who will set me a time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me?
verses.Jeremiah|50|45: Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he has taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the land of Chaldeans: Surely the least of the flock shall drag them away: surely the fold shall be appalled at them!
verses.Jeremiah|50|46: At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations.
verses.Jeremiah|51|1: Thus says the Lord; Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against them that dwell in Leb-kamai, a destroying wind;
verses.Jeremiah|51|2: and will send to Babylon winnowers, and they shall winnow her, and shall empty her land: for in the day of trouble they shall be against her round about.
verses.Jeremiah|51|3: Against him that bends let the archer bend his bow, and against him that lifts himself up in his coat of mail: and spare not her young men; destroy utterly all her host.
verses.Jeremiah|51|4: Thus the slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and they that are thrust through in her streets.
verses.Jeremiah|51|5: For Israel has not been widowed, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts; though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.Jeremiah|51|6: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and let every man save his life: be not cut off in her iniquity; for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance; he will render to her a recompense.
verses.Jeremiah|51|7: Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord's hand, that made all the earth drunk: the nations have drunk of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.
verses.Jeremiah|51|8: Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed: wail for her; take balm for her pain, perhaps she may be healed.
verses.Jeremiah|51|9: We would have healed Babylon, but she was not healed: forsake her, and let us go every one to his own country: for her judgment reaches to heaven, and is lifted up to the skies.
verses.Jeremiah|51|10: The Lord has brought forth our vindication: come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.
verses.Jeremiah|51|11: Select the arrows; fill up the quivers: the Lord has raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes: for his purpose against Babylon is to destroy it; because it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance for his temple.
verses.Jeremiah|51|12: Set up a banner upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set up the watchmen, prepare the ambushes: for the Lord has both devised and done that which he spoke against the inhabitants of Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|51|13: O thou that dwellest upon many waters, abundant in treasures, thy end is come, and the measure of thy greed.
verses.Jeremiah|51|14: The Lord of hosts has sworn by himself, saying, Surely I will fill thee with men as with locusts; and they shall raise shout against thee.
verses.Jeremiah|51|15: He has made the earth by his power, he has established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heaven by his understanding.
verses.Jeremiah|51|16: When his voice resounds with great mass of water in the heavens, and he raises vapours from the ends of the Earth; when he makes lightning flashes among the rain, and brings forth the wind out of his storehouses:
verses.Jeremiah|51|17: every man becomes stupid, without knowledge: every founder is put to shame by his carved idol: for his molten image is false, and there is no breath in them.
verses.Jeremiah|51|18: They are vanity, the work of delusion: in the time of their punishment they shall perish.
verses.Jeremiah|51|19: The portion of Jacob is not like them; for he is the fashioner of all things, and (Israel) is the tribe of his inheritance: the Lord of hosts is his name.
verses.Jeremiah|51|20: Thou art my chief and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will destroy kingdoms;
verses.Jeremiah|51|21: and with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and its rider;
verses.Jeremiah|51|22: with thee also will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I shatter old and young; and with thee will I shatter the young man and the maid;
verses.Jeremiah|51|23: I will also break in pieces with thee the shepherd and his flock; and with thee will I break in pieces the farmer and his yoke of oxen; and with thee will I break in pieces governors and deputies.
verses.Jeremiah|51|24: And I will pay back to Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldeans all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|51|25: Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, says the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out my hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.
verses.Jeremiah|51|26: And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|51|27: Set up a banner in the land, blow a shofar among the nations, prepare the nations against her, call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz; appoint a captain against her; cause the horses to come up like bristling locusts.
verses.Jeremiah|51|28: Prepare nations for war against her, the kings of the Medes, its governors, and all its deputies, and all the land of his dominion.
verses.Jeremiah|51|29: And the land trembles and withers in pain: for every purpose of the Lord shall be performed against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.
verses.Jeremiah|51|30: The mighty men of Babylon have ceased to fight, they have remained in their fortresses: their might has failed; they have become like women: her dwellingplaces have been set on fire, her bars are broken.
verses.Jeremiah|51|31: One runner shall run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken on every side,
verses.Jeremiah|51|32: and that the fords are seized, and the thickets have been burned with fire, and the men of war are panic stricken.
verses.Jeremiah|51|33: For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; The daughter of Babylon is like a threshingfloor, it is time to thresh her: yet a little while, and the time of her harvest shall come.
verses.Jeremiah|51|34: Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me, he has crushed me, he has made me an empty vessel; like a crocodile, he has swallowed me up, he has filled his belly with my delicacies, he has scoured me clean.
verses.Jeremiah|51|35: The violence done to me and to my flesh shall be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldeans, shall Jerusalem say.
verses.Jeremiah|51|36: Therefore thus says the Lord; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her spring dry.
verses.Jeremiah|51|37: And Babylon shall become heaps, a dwellingplace for jackals, an astonishment, and a hissing, without inhabitant.
verses.Jeremiah|51|38: They shall roar together like lions: they shall growl like lions' whelps.
verses.Jeremiah|51|39: When they are heated, I will make feasts for them, and I will make them drunk, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not awake, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|51|40: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats.
verses.Jeremiah|51|41: How is Sheshach taken! and how is the praise of the whole earth surprised! how is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations!
verses.Jeremiah|51|42: The sea is come up upon Babylon: she is covered with the multitude of its waves.
verses.Jeremiah|51|43: Her cities are a desolation, a dry land, and a wilderness, a land in which no man dwells, neither does any son of man pass by them.
verses.Jeremiah|51|44: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will take out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up; and the nations shall not flow together any more to him: the very wall of Babylon has fallen.
verses.Jeremiah|51|45: My people, go out of the midst of her, and deliver every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|51|46: And lest your heart faint, and you fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land: for a rumour shall both come one year, and after that in another year shall come a rumour, and there will be violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
verses.Jeremiah|51|47: Therefore, behold, days are coming, when I will do judgment upon the carved idols of Babylon: and her whole land shall be put to shame, and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her.
verses.Jeremiah|51|48: Then the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|51|49: As Babylon has caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the land.
verses.Jeremiah|51|50: You that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still; remember the Lord afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.
verses.Jeremiah|51|51: We are ashamed, because we have heard reproach: shame has covered our faces: for strangers are come into the sanctuaries of the Lord's house.
verses.Jeremiah|51|52: Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will do judgment upon her carved idols: and through all her land the wounded shall groan.
verses.Jeremiah|51|53: Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from Me shall spoilers come to her, says the Lord.
verses.Jeremiah|51|54: A sound of a cry comes from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans:
verses.Jeremiah|51|55: because the Lord has spoiled Babylon, and has quelled from her midst the great clamour; when her waves roar like great waters, noise of their voice is sounded:
verses.Jeremiah|51|56: because the spoiler is come upon her, upon Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, every one of their bows is broken: for the Lord God of recompenses shall surely pay back.
verses.Jeremiah|51|57: And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise men, her governors, and her deputies, and her mighty men: and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not awake, says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
verses.Jeremiah|51|58: Thus says the Lord of hosts; The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the people shall labour in vain, and the nations for the fire; and they shall be weary.
verses.Jeremiah|51|59: The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, when he went with Zedekiah, the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And this Seraiah was marshal of the camp.
verses.Jeremiah|51|60: So Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come upon Babylon, namely all these words that are written against Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|51|61: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When thou comest to Babylon, and shalt see, and shalt read all these words;
verses.Jeremiah|51|62: then shalt thou say, O Lord, Thou hast spoken against this place, to cut it off, that none shall remain in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate forever.
verses.Jeremiah|51|63: And it shall be, when thou hast made an end of reading this book, that thou shalt bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates:
verses.Jeremiah|51|64: and thou shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise, because of the evil that I will bring upon her: and they shall be weary. Thus far the words of Jeremiah.
verses.Jeremiah|52|1: Zedekiah was twenty one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.Jeremiah|52|2: And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.Jeremiah|52|3: For through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he cast them out from his presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|52|4: And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it, and built a siege work against it round about.
verses.Jeremiah|52|5: So the city was besieged until the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
verses.Jeremiah|52|6: And in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine was severe in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.Jeremiah|52|7: Then the city was breached, and all the men of war fled, and went out of the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden; (now the Chaldeans were by the city round about:) and they went by the way of the plain.
verses.Jeremiah|52|8: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
verses.Jeremiah|52|9: Then they took the king, and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him.
verses.Jeremiah|52|10: And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
verses.Jeremiah|52|11: Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.
verses.Jeremiah|52|12: Now in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.Jeremiah|52|13: And he burned the house of the Lord, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great house he burned with fire:
verses.Jeremiah|52|14: and all the army of the Chaldeans, that were with the captain of the guard, broke down all the walls of Jerusalem round about.
verses.Jeremiah|52|15: Then Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away into exile certain of the poor of the people, and the residue of the people that remained in the city, and the deserts who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
verses.Jeremiah|52|16: But Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left certain of the poor of the land for vinedressers and for fieldworkers.
verses.Jeremiah|52|17: Also the pillars of brass that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the Lord, the Chaldeans broke, and carried all the brass of them to Babylon.
verses.Jeremiah|52|18: The pans also, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which they ministered, they took away.
verses.Jeremiah|52|19: And the bowls, and the firepans, and the basins, and the pans, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the bowls both that which was of gold in gold, and that which was of silver in silver, the captain of the guard took away.
verses.Jeremiah|52|20: The two pillars, one sea, and twelve brass bulls that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the Lord: the brass of all these vessels was unweighed.
verses.Jeremiah|52|21: And as for the pillars, the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits; and a thread of twelve cubits did compass it; and its thickness was four fingers: it was hollow.
verses.Jeremiah|52|22: And a capital of brass was upon it; and the height of one capital was five cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the capitals round about, all of brass. The second pillar also and the pomegranates were like these.
verses.Jeremiah|52|23: And there were ninety six pomegranates on a side; and all the pomegranates upon the network were a hundred round about.
verses.Jeremiah|52|24: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
verses.Jeremiah|52|25: he also took out of the city an officer, who had the charge of the men of war; and seven of those men who were near the king's person, who were found in the city; and the scribe of the chief of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city.
verses.Jeremiah|52|26: So Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
verses.Jeremiah|52|27: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was exiled out of his own land.
verses.Jeremiah|52|28: This is the number of the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand and twenty three men of Judah:
verses.Jeremiah|52|29: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away from Jerusalem eight hundred and thirty two persons:
verses.Jeremiah|52|30: in the twenty third year of Nebuchadrezzar, Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away into exile of the men of Judah seven hundred and forty five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred.
verses.Jeremiah|52|31: And it came to pass in the thirty seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty fifth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him out of prison,
verses.Jeremiah|52|32: and spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon,
verses.Jeremiah|52|33: and changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life.
verses.Jeremiah|52|34: And for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him by the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
verses.Lamentations|1|1: How does the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become like a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become a vassal!
verses.Lamentations|1|2: She weeps sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: among all her lovers she has none to comfort her: all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they have become her enemies.
verses.Lamentations|1|3: Judah is gone into exile because of affliction, and because of great servitude: she dwells among the nations, she finds no rest: all her persecutors overtook her within the straits.
verses.Lamentations|1|4: The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn assembly: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins are afflicted, and she is in bitterness.
verses.Lamentations|1|5: Her adversaries have become the chief, her enemies prosper; for the Lord has afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: her infants are gone into captivity before the enemy.
verses.Lamentations|1|6: And from the daughter of Zion all her splendour is departed: her princes are become like harts that find no pasture, and they are gone without strength before the pursuer.
verses.Lamentations|1|7: Jerusalem remembers in the days of her affliction and of her miseries all her pleasant things that she had in the days of old, when her people fell into the hand of the enemy, and none did help her: the adversaries saw her, and gloated at her destruction.
verses.Lamentations|1|8: Jerusalem has grievously sinned; therefore she is become loathsome: all that honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness: she herself also sighs, and turns backward.
verses.Lamentations|1|9: Her filthiness was in her skirts; she took no thought of her last end; therefore she came down astonishingly: she has no comforter. O Lord, behold my affliction: for the enemy has magnified himself.
verses.Lamentations|1|10: The adversary has spread out his hand upon all her pleasant things: for she has seen that heathen nations invade her sanctuary, those whom Thou didst forbid to enter into Thy congregation.
verses.Lamentations|1|11: All her people sigh, they seek bread; they have given their pleasant things for food to relieve the soul: see, O Lord, and consider; how abject I am become.
verses.Lamentations|1|12: Is it nothing to you, all you that pass by? behold, and see if there is any pain like my pain, which is done to me, with which the Lord has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.
verses.Lamentations|1|13: From above he has sent fire into my bones, and it prevails against them: he has spread a net for my feet, he has turned me back: he has made me desolate and faint all the day.
verses.Lamentations|1|14: The yoke of my transgressions is fastened on by his hand: they are knit together, and come up upon my neck: he has made my strength to fall, the Lord has delivered me into the hands of those against whom I am not able to rise up.
verses.Lamentations|1|15: The Lord has spurned all my mighty men in the midst of me: he has called an assembly against me to crush my young men: the Lord has trodden the virgin, the daughter of Judah, as in a winepress.
verses.Lamentations|1|16: For these things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me: my children are desolate, because the enemy has prevailed.
verses.Lamentations|1|17: Zion spreads out her hands, and there is none to comfort her: the Lord has commanded against Jacob, adversaries round about him: Jerusalem is like a menstruous woman among them.
verses.Lamentations|1|18: The Lord is righteous; for I have rebelled against his word: hear, I pray you, all the peoples, and behold my pain: my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.
verses.Lamentations|1|19: I called for my lovers, but they deceived me: my priests and my elders perished in the city, while they sought food for themselves to relieve their souls.
verses.Lamentations|1|20: Behold, O Lord; for I am in distress: my bowels are troubled; my heart is turned within me; for I have grievously rebelled: abroad the sword bereaves, at home it is like death.
verses.Lamentations|1|21: They have heard that I sigh: there is none to comfort me: all my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that Thou hast done it: Thou wilt bring the day that Thou hast called, and they shall be like me.
verses.Lamentations|1|22: Let all their wickedness come before Thee; and do to them, as Thou hast done to me for all my transgressions: for my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.
verses.Lamentations|2|1: How has the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven to earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!
verses.Lamentations|2|2: The Lord has swallowed up without pity all the habitations of Jacob: he has thrown down in his wrath the strongholds of the daughter of Judah; he has brought them down to the ground: he has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
verses.Lamentations|2|3: He has cut off in his fierce anger all the horn of Israel: he has drawn back his right hand from before the enemy, and he has burned against Jacob like a flaming fire, which devours round about.
verses.Lamentations|2|4: He has bent his bow like an enemy: with his right hand set like an adversary, he has slain all that were pleasant to the eye: in the tent of the daughter of Zion, he has poured out his fury like fire.
verses.Lamentations|2|5: The Lord was like an enemy: he has swallowed up Israel, he has swallowed up all her palaces: he has destroyed his strongholds, and has increased in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.
verses.Lamentations|2|6: And he has stripped his tabernacle, as if it were a garden: he has destroyed his place of assembly: the Lord has caused the appointed seasons and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and has spurned in the indignation of his anger both king and priest.
verses.Lamentations|2|7: The Lord has cast off his altar, he has abhorred his sanctuary, he has given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces; they have made a noise in the house of the Lord, as in the day of a solemn assembly.
verses.Lamentations|2|8: The Lord has purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion: he has stretched out a line, he has not withdrawn his hand from destroying: therefore he made the rampart and the wall to lament; they languish together.
verses.Lamentations|2|9: Her gates are sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars: her king and her princes are among the nations: there is no law; her prophets also find no vision from the Lord.
verses.Lamentations|2|10: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.
verses.Lamentations|2|11: My eyes fail with tears, my bowels are troubled, my liver is poured upon the earth, for the breach of the daughter of my people; because the children and the sucklings swoon in the broad places of the city.
verses.Lamentations|2|12: They say to their mothers, Where is corn and wine? when they swoon like wounded men in the broad places of the city, when their soul is poured out into their mothers' bosom.
verses.Lamentations|2|13: What shall I take to witness for thee? what shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?
verses.Lamentations|2|14: Thy prophets have seen for thee vain and foolish visions: and they have not exposed thy iniquity, to restore thy captivity; but have prophesied for thee burdens of falsehood and deceit.
verses.Lamentations|2|15: All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?
verses.Lamentations|2|16: All thy enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth: they say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we have looked for; we have found it, we have seen it.
verses.Lamentations|2|17: The Lord has done that which he devised; he has fulfilled his word that he commanded in the days of old: he has thrown down without pity: and he has caused the enemy to rejoice over thee, he has raised up the horn of thy adversaries.
verses.Lamentations|2|18: Their heart cried to the Lord. O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night: give thyself no rest; let not the apple of thy eye cease.
verses.Lamentations|2|19: Arise, cry out in the night: in the beginning of the watches pour out thy heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands towards him for the life of thy young children, that faint for hunger at the head of every street.
verses.Lamentations|2|20: Behold, O Lord, and consider to whom Thou hast done this. Shall the women eat their fruit, their cherished babes? shall priest and prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.Lamentations|2|21: Young and old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; Thou hast slain them in the day of Thy anger; Thou hast killed, and not pitied.
verses.Lamentations|2|22: Thou hast called as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors round about, so that in the day of the Lord's anger none escaped or remained: those that I have cherished and brought up my enemy has consumed.
verses.Lamentations|3|1: I am the man who has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.
verses.Lamentations|3|2: He has led me, and brought me into darkness, but not into light.
verses.Lamentations|3|3: Surely he is turned against me; he turns his hand against me all the day.
verses.Lamentations|3|4: He has made my flesh and my skin to waste away; he has broken my bones.
verses.Lamentations|3|5: He has built a mound against me, and has beset me round about at head and hell.
verses.Lamentations|3|6: He has set me in dark places, as those who are long ago dead.
verses.Lamentations|3|7: He has hedged me about, so that I cannot get out: he has made my chain heavy.
verses.Lamentations|3|8: Even when I cry and call for help, he stops up my prayer.
verses.Lamentations|3|9: He has enclosed my ways with hewn stone, he has made my paths crooked.
verses.Lamentations|3|10: He is to me like a bear lying in wait, and like a lion in secret places.
verses.Lamentations|3|11: He has turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces: he has made me desolate.
verses.Lamentations|3|12: He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.
verses.Lamentations|3|13: He has caused the arrows of his quiver to enter into my reins.
verses.Lamentations|3|14: I am become a derision to all my people; and their song all the day.
verses.Lamentations|3|15: He has filled me with bitterness, he has sated me with wormwood.
verses.Lamentations|3|16: He has also broken my teeth with gravel stones, he has pressed me down into the ashes.
verses.Lamentations|3|17: My soul is far removed from peace: I have forgotten prosperity.
verses.Lamentations|3|18: And I said, My strength and my hope are perished from the Lord.
verses.Lamentations|3|19: Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.
verses.Lamentations|3|20: My soul has them still in remembrance, and is bowed down within me.
verses.Lamentations|3|21: This I recall to my mind, therefore I have hope:
verses.Lamentations|3|22: that the Lord's steadfast love has not ceased, and that his compassions do not fail.
verses.Lamentations|3|23: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
verses.Lamentations|3|24: The Lord is my portion, says my soul; therefore I will hope in him.
verses.Lamentations|3|25: The Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul that seeks him.
verses.Lamentations|3|26: It is good that a man should quietly hope for the salvation of the Lord.
verses.Lamentations|3|27: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
verses.Lamentations|3|28: Let him sit alone and keep silence, because he has taken it upon him.
verses.Lamentations|3|29: Let him put his mouth in the dust; perhaps there may be hope.
verses.Lamentations|3|30: Let him offer his cheek to him who strikes him; let him take his fill of insult.
verses.Lamentations|3|31: For the Lord will not cast off for ever:
verses.Lamentations|3|32: but though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the abundance of his steadfast love.
verses.Lamentations|3|33: For he does not willingly afflict or grieve the children of men.
verses.Lamentations|3|34: To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth,
verses.Lamentations|3|35: to turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most High,
verses.Lamentations|3|36: to subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approves not.
verses.Lamentations|3|37: Who is he that says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord commands it not?
verses.Lamentations|3|38: Out of the mouth of the most High do not both good and evil come?
verses.Lamentations|3|39: Why then does a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?
verses.Lamentations|3|40: Let us search and try our ways, and turn back to the Lord.
verses.Lamentations|3|41: Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.
verses.Lamentations|3|42: We have transgressed and have rebelled: Thou hast not pardoned.
verses.Lamentations|3|43: Thou hast covered with anger, and pursued us: Thou hast slain, Thou hast not pitied.
verses.Lamentations|3|44: Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, so that prayer should not pass through.
verses.Lamentations|3|45: Thou hast made us offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.
verses.Lamentations|3|46: All our enemies have opened their mouths wide against us.
verses.Lamentations|3|47: Fear and the pit are come upon us, desolation and destruction.
verses.Lamentations|3|48: My eye runs down with rivers of water for the breach of the daughter of my people.
verses.Lamentations|3|49: My eye trickles down, and ceases not, without any intermission,
verses.Lamentations|3|50: till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.
verses.Lamentations|3|51: My eye affects my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
verses.Lamentations|3|52: They chased me sore, like a bird, those who hate me without cause.
verses.Lamentations|3|53: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast stones upon me.
verses.Lamentations|3|54: Waters flowed over my head; then I said, I am cut off.
verses.Lamentations|3|55: I called upon Thy name, O Lord, out of the nethermost pit.
verses.Lamentations|3|56: Thou hast heard my voice: hide not Thy ear at my sighing, at my cry.
verses.Lamentations|3|57: Thou didst draw near in the day that I called upon Thee: Thou didst say,
verses.Lamentations|3|58: Fear not. O Lord, Thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul; Thou hast redeemed my life.
verses.Lamentations|3|59: O Lord, Thou hast seen my wrong: judge my cause.
verses.Lamentations|3|60: Thou hast seen all their vengeance and all their devices against me.
verses.Lamentations|3|61: Thou hast heard their insult, O Lord, and all their devices against me;
verses.Lamentations|3|62: the lips of those who rose up against me, and their muttering against me all the day.
verses.Lamentations|3|63: Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their song.
verses.Lamentations|3|64: Render to them a recompense, O Lord, according to the work of their hands.
verses.Lamentations|3|65: Give them sorrow of heart; Thy curse be on them!
verses.Lamentations|3|66: Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the Lord.
verses.Lamentations|4|1: How is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed! the hallowed stones are poured out at the top of every street.
verses.Lamentations|4|2: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!
verses.Lamentations|4|3: Even the jackals draw out the breast, they give suck to their young ones: the daughter of my people is become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.
verses.Lamentations|4|4: The tongue of the sucking child cleaves to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the young children ask bread, and no man gives it to them.
verses.Lamentations|4|5: They that did feed on dainties are desolate in the streets: they that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.
verses.Lamentations|4|6: For the doom of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, that was overthrown as in a moment, no hands being laid upon her.
verses.Lamentations|4|7: Her Nazarites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk, they were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing was as of sapphire:
verses.Lamentations|4|8: now their visage is blacker than coal; they are not known in the streets: their skin is shrivelled upon their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.
verses.Lamentations|4|9: Those slain with the sword are better than those slain with hunger: for when pierced through, the former do ooze with the produce of the fields.
verses.Lamentations|4|10: Hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children: they were their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
verses.Lamentations|4|11: The Lord has accomplished his fury; he has poured out his fierce anger, and has kindled a fire in Zion and it has devoured its foundations.
verses.Lamentations|4|12: The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world, would not have believed that the adversary and the enemy would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.Lamentations|4|13: It was for the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, who shed the blood of the just in the midst of her.
verses.Lamentations|4|14: They wandered blind through the streets, polluted with blood, so that none could touch their garments.
verses.Lamentations|4|15: Away! unclean! they cried at them; away! away! do not touch. So they fled, and wandered away: among the nations it was said, They shall no longer sojourn here.
verses.Lamentations|4|16: The anger of the Lord has divided them; he will no more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests, they were not gracious to the elders.
verses.Lamentations|4|17: As for us, our eyes do yet fail for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.
verses.Lamentations|4|18: They hunt our steps, that we cannot walk in our broad places: our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come.
verses.Lamentations|4|19: Our pursuers were swifter than the vultures in the sky: they chased us upon the mountains, they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
verses.Lamentations|4|20: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord, was taken in their pits, of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.
verses.Lamentations|4|21: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz; the cup shall also pass over to thee: thou shalt be drunken, and strip thyself bare.
verses.Lamentations|4|22: The punishment of thy iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into exile: he will visit thy iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will uncover thy sins.
verses.Lamentations|5|1: Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our insult.
verses.Lamentations|5|2: Our inheritance is turned over to strangers, our houses to aliens.
verses.Lamentations|5|3: We are become orphans and fatherless, our mothers are like widows.
verses.Lamentations|5|4: We have drunk our water for money; our own wood is sold to us.
verses.Lamentations|5|5: We are pursued to our necks: we labour, and have no rest.
verses.Lamentations|5|6: We have given the hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to be satisfied with bread.
verses.Lamentations|5|7: Our fathers have sinned, and are no more; but we bear their iniquities.
verses.Lamentations|5|8: Servants rule over us: there is none to deliver us out of their hand.
verses.Lamentations|5|9: We get our bread with the peril of our lives because of the sword of the wilderness.
verses.Lamentations|5|10: Our skin is hot like an oven because of the burning famine.
verses.Lamentations|5|11: Women are ravished in Zion, and maidens in the cities of Judah.
verses.Lamentations|5|12: Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders are not honoured.
verses.Lamentations|5|13: Young men drag the millstone, and youths stumble under the wood.
verses.Lamentations|5|14: The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their music.
verses.Lamentations|5|15: The joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned into mourning.
verses.Lamentations|5|16: The crown is fallen from our head: woe to us, that we have sinned!
verses.Lamentations|5|17: For this our heart is faint; for these things our eyes are dim.
verses.Lamentations|5|18: Because of the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, foxes prowl over it.
verses.Lamentations|5|19: Thou, O Lord, art enthroned forever; Thy throne is from generation to generation.
verses.Lamentations|5|20: Why dost Thou forget us forever, why dost Thou so long forsake us?
verses.Lamentations|5|21: Turn us to Thee, O Lord, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old:
verses.Lamentations|5|22: unless Thou hast utterly rejected us; and art exceedingly angry against us.
verses.Ezekiel|1|1: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
verses.Ezekiel|1|2: In the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of the exile of king Jehoiachin's,
verses.Ezekiel|1|3: the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there upon him.
verses.Ezekiel|1|4: And I looked, and, behold, a storm wind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire flaring up, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst of it, as it were the colour of electrum, out of the midst of the fire.
verses.Ezekiel|1|5: Also out of the midst of it came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man.
verses.Ezekiel|1|6: And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.
verses.Ezekiel|1|7: And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass.
verses.Ezekiel|1|8: And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and as for their faces and their wings (of those four)
verses.Ezekiel|1|9: their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went everyone straight forward.
verses.Ezekiel|1|10: As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man, and they four had the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle.
verses.Ezekiel|1|11: Thus were their faces: and their wings were divided upwards; two wings of everyone were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies.
verses.Ezekiel|1|12: And they went everyone straight forward: wherever the spirit was minded to go, they went; they turned not when they went.
verses.Ezekiel|1|13: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like coals of fire, burning like the appearance of torches: it flashed up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning.
verses.Ezekiel|1|14: And the living creatures ran and returned like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
verses.Ezekiel|1|15: Now as I beheld the living creatures, behold one wheel upon the earth by the living creatures, with his four faces.
verses.Ezekiel|1|16: The appearance of the wheels and their work was like the colour of an emerald: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.
verses.Ezekiel|1|17: When they went, they went toward their four sides: and they turned not when they went.
verses.Ezekiel|1|18: As for their rims, they were so high that they were dreadful, and their rims were full of eyes round about them four.
verses.Ezekiel|1|19: And when the living creatures moved, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
verses.Ezekiel|1|20: Wherever the spirit was minded to go, they moved, for the spirit was minded to go there; and the wheels were lifted up along with them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
verses.Ezekiel|1|21: When those moved, these moved; and when those stood still, these stood still; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up along with them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
verses.Ezekiel|1|22: And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the colour of the terrible ice, stretched out over their heads above.
verses.Ezekiel|1|23: And under the firmament their wings were held straight, the one toward the other: everyone had two, which covered them, namely, everyone two, which covered their bodies.
verses.Ezekiel|1|24: And when they moved, I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, the noise of a tumult, like the noise of a host: when they stood still, they let down their wings.
verses.Ezekiel|1|25: And there was a voice from above the firmament that was over their heads; when they stood still, they let down their wings.
verses.Ezekiel|1|26: And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it.
verses.Ezekiel|1|27: And I saw something like the colour of electrum, like the appearance of fire round about enclosing it; from what appeared to be his loins upward, and from what appeared to be his loins downward, I saw what appeared to be fire, and there was a brightness round about him.
verses.Ezekiel|1|28: As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard the voice of one that spoke.
verses.Ezekiel|2|1: And he said to me, Son of man, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak to thee.
verses.Ezekiel|2|2: And a spirit entered into me when he spoke to me, and set me upon my feet, and I heard him that spoke to me.
verses.Ezekiel|2|3: And he said to me, Son of man, I sent thee to the children of Israel, to rebellious tribes that have rebelled against me: they and their fathers have transgressed against me, to this very day.
verses.Ezekiel|2|4: For the children are defiant and stiffhearted. I do send thee to them; and thou shalt say to them, Thus says the Lord God.
verses.Ezekiel|2|5: And they, whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse to hear, (for they are a rebellious house,) yet they shall know that there has been a prophet among them.
verses.Ezekiel|2|6: And thou, son of man, be not afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns be with thee, and thou dost sit upon scorpions: be not afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a rebellious house.
verses.Ezekiel|2|7: And thou shalt speak my words to them, whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse to hear: for they are most rebellious.
verses.Ezekiel|2|8: But thou, son of man, hear what I say to thee; Be not thou rebellious like that rebellious house: open thy mouth, and eat that which I give thee.
verses.Ezekiel|2|9: And when I looked, behold, a hand was sent to me; and, lo, a scroll of a book was in it;
verses.Ezekiel|2|10: and he spread it before me; and it was written inside and outside: and in it was written lamentations, and mourning, and woe.
verses.Ezekiel|3|1: And he said to me, Son of man, eat what thou findest; eat this scroll, and go and speak to the house of Israel.
verses.Ezekiel|3|2: So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat that scroll.
verses.Ezekiel|3|3: And he said to me, Son of man, feed thy belly, and fill thy bowels with this scroll that I give thee. Then I did eat it; and it became as sweet as honey in my mouth.
verses.Ezekiel|3|4: And he said to me, Son of man, go, get thee to the house of Israel, and speak with my words to them.
verses.Ezekiel|3|5: For thou art not sent to a people of a strange speech and of a hard language, but to the house of Israel;
verses.Ezekiel|3|6: not to many peoples of a strange speech and of a hard language, whose words thou canst not understand. Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened to thee.
verses.Ezekiel|3|7: But the house of Israel will not hearken to thee; for they will not hearken to me: for all the house of Israel are defiant and hardhearted.
verses.Ezekiel|3|8: Behold, I have made thy face hard against their faces, and forehead strong against their foreheads.
verses.Ezekiel|3|9: Like adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be downcast at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.
verses.Ezekiel|3|10: Moreover he said to me, Son of man, all my words that I shall speak to thee take to thy heart, and hear with thy ears.
verses.Ezekiel|3|11: And go, get thee to the exiles, to the children of thy people, and speak to them, and tell them. Thus says the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse to hear.
verses.Ezekiel|3|12: Then a spirit took me up, and I heard behind me a voice of a great rushing, saying, Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place;
verses.Ezekiel|3|13: also the noise of the wings of the living creatures as they touched one another, and the noise of the wheels along with them, and a noise of a great rushing,
verses.Ezekiel|3|14: so a spirit lifted me up, and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit; and the hand of the Lord was strong upon me.
verses.Ezekiel|3|15: Then I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, that dwelt by the river Chebar, and I sat where they sat, and remained there overwhelmed among them for seven days.
verses.Ezekiel|3|16: And it came to pass at the end of seven days that the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.Ezekiel|3|17: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel: and when thou shalt hear a word at my mouth, thou shalt give them warning from me.
verses.Ezekiel|3|18: When I say to the wicked man, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thy hand.
verses.Ezekiel|3|19: Yet if thou warn the wicked man, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast saved thy soul.
verses.Ezekiel|3|20: Again, when a righteous man turns from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and I lay a stumblingblock before him he shall die: because thou hast not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he has done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at thy hand.
verses.Ezekiel|3|21: Nevertheless if thou warn the righteous man, that the righteous sin not, and he does not sin, then he shall surely live, because he is warned; and thou hast saved thy soul.
verses.Ezekiel|3|22: And the hand of the Lord was there upon me; and he said to me, Arise, go out into the plain, and I will talk with thee there.
verses.Ezekiel|3|23: Then I arose, and went out into the plain: and, behold, the glory of the Lord stood there, as the glory which I saw by the river Chebar: and I fell on my face.
verses.Ezekiel|3|24: Then a spirit entered into me, and set me upon my feet; and he spoke with me, and said to me, Go, shut thyself within thy house.
verses.Ezekiel|3|25: But thou, O son of man, behold, they shall put cords upon thee, and shall bind thee with them, and thou shalt not go out among them:
verses.Ezekiel|3|26: and I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be to them a reprover: for they are a rebellious house.
verses.Ezekiel|3|27: But when I speak with thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say to them, Thus says the Lord God; He that hears, let him hear; and he that refuses to hear, let him refuse: for they are a rebellious house.
verses.Ezekiel|4|1: Thou also, son of man, take thee a brick, and lay it before thee, and trace upon it a city, namely, Jerusalem:
verses.Ezekiel|4|2: and lay siege against it, and build a siege wall against it, and cast a mound against it; set camps also against it, and set battering rams against it round about.
verses.Ezekiel|4|3: And take thou an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city: and set thy face towards it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
verses.Ezekiel|4|4: Moreover lie thou upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it: according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquity.
verses.Ezekiel|4|5: For I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, by an equivalent number of days, three hundred and ninety days: so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
verses.Ezekiel|4|6: And when thou hast accomplished them, lie again on thy right side, and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah: I have appointed thee forty days, each day for a year.
verses.Ezekiel|4|7: Therefore thou shalt set thy face towards the siege of Jerusalem, and thy arm shall be uncovered, and thou shalt prophesy against it.
verses.Ezekiel|4|8: And, behold, I will lay cords upon thee, so that thou shalt not be able to turn thyself from one side to another, till thou hast completed the days of thy siege.
verses.Ezekiel|4|9: Take thou also wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and spelt, and put them in one vessel, and make thee bread from them; for the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon thy side, three hundred and ninety days shalt thou eat it.
verses.Ezekiel|4|10: And thy food which thou shalt eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day: once a day shalt thou eat it.
verses.Ezekiel|4|11: Thou shalt drink also water by measure, the sixth part of a hin: once a day shalt thou drink.
verses.Ezekiel|4|12: And thou shalt eat it like barley cakes, and thou shalt bake it with human excrement, in their sight.
verses.Ezekiel|4|13: And the Lord said, Thus shall the children of Israel eat their bread, unclean, among the nations, whither I will drive them.
verses.Ezekiel|4|14: Then I said, Ah Lord God, behold my soul has never been polluted: for from my youth up even till now I have not eaten that which dies of itself, or is torn by beasts, nor did loathsome meat ever come into my mouth.
verses.Ezekiel|4|15: Then he said to me, Lo, I have given thee cow's dung instead of human dung, and thou shalt prepare thy bread upon that.
verses.Ezekiel|4|16: Moreover he said to me, Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight, and with anxiety; and they shall drink water by measure, and in appalment:
verses.Ezekiel|4|17: that they may lack bread and water, and be appalled with one another, and waste away for their iniquity.
verses.Ezekiel|5|1: And thou, Son of man, take a sharp knife; a barber's razor take for thyself; and pass it over thy head, and over thy beard: then take balances to weigh, and divide the hair.
verses.Ezekiel|5|2: Thou shalt burn with fire a third part in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled: and thou shalt take a third part, and smite about it with the sword: and a third part thou shalt scatter to the wind; and I will draw out a sword after them.
verses.Ezekiel|5|3: Thou shalt also take from these a small number, and bind them in thy skirts.
verses.Ezekiel|5|4: Then take more of them, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; from there a fire shall come forth into all the house of Israel.
verses.Ezekiel|5|5: Thus says the Lord God; This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations; and countries are round about her.
verses.Ezekiel|5|6: And she has rebelled against my judgments more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries that are round her: for they have refused my judgments, and as for my statutes, they have not followed them.
verses.Ezekiel|5|7: Therefore thus says the Lord God; Because you have been more turbulent than the nations that are round about you, and have not walked in my statutes, nor have you kept my judgments, nor have you done according to the practices of the nations that are round about you;
verses.Ezekiel|5|8: therefore thus says the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, am against thee, and will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations.
verses.Ezekiel|5|9: And I will do in thee that which I have not done, and like which I will not do again, because of all thy abominations.
verses.Ezekiel|5|10: Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments in thee, and the whole remnant of thee will I scatter to all the winds.
verses.Ezekiel|5|11: Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God; Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thy abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall my eye spare, neither will I have any pity.
verses.Ezekiel|5|12: A third part of thee shall die with the pestilence, and with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of thee: and a third part shall fall by the sword round about thee; and I will scatter a third part to all the winds, and I will draw out a sword after them.
verses.Ezekiel|5|13: Thus shall my anger spend itself, and I will relieve my fury upon them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know that I the Lord have spoken it in my zeal, when I have spent my fury in them.
verses.Ezekiel|5|14: Moreover I will make thee a desolation, and a reproach among the nations that are round about thee, in the sight of all that pass by.
verses.Ezekiel|5|15: So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment to the nations that are round about thee, when I shall execute judgments in thee in anger and in fury and in furious rebukes. I the Lord have spoken it.
verses.Ezekiel|5|16: When I shall send upon them the evil arrows of famine, which shall be for destruction, which I will send to destroy you: and I will increase the famine upon you, and will break your staff of bread:
verses.Ezekiel|5|17: so will I send upon you famine and evil beasts, and they shall bereave thee; and pestilence and blood shall pass through thee; and I will bring the sword upon thee. I the Lord have spoken.
verses.Ezekiel|6|1: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.Ezekiel|6|2: Son of man, set thy face towards the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,
verses.Ezekiel|6|3: and say, You mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God; Thus says the Lord God to the mountains, and to the hills, to the ravines, and to the valleys; Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.
verses.Ezekiel|6|4: And your altars shall be desolate, and your sun images shall be broken: and I will cast down your slain men before your idols.
verses.Ezekiel|6|5: And I will lay the dead carcasses of the children of Israel before their idols; and I will scatter your bones round about your altars.
verses.Ezekiel|6|6: In all your dwelling places the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolate; that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your sun images may be cut down, and your works may be wiped out.
verses.Ezekiel|6|7: And the slain shall fall in the midst of you, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.Ezekiel|6|8: Yet will I leave a remnant, that you may have some that shall escape the sword among the nations, when you shall be scattered through the countries.
verses.Ezekiel|6|9: And your fugitives shall remember me among the nations whither they shall be carried captives, when I have broken their wanton heart, which has departed from me, and their eyes, which go astray after their idols: and they shall loathe themselves for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.
verses.Ezekiel|6|10: And they shall know that I am the Lord, and that not in vain did I say that I would do this evil to them.
verses.Ezekiel|6|11: Thus says the Lord God; Smite with thy hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say, Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel! for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.
verses.Ezekiel|6|12: He that is far off shall die of the pestilence; and he that is near shall fall by the sword; and he that remains and is besieged shall die by the famine: thus will I spend my fury upon them.
verses.Ezekiel|6|13: Then shall you know that I am the Lord, when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill, in all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols.
verses.Ezekiel|6|14: So will I stretch out my hand upon them, and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness to Diblath, in all their habitations: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.Ezekiel|7|1: Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
