verses.Joel|4|16: And the Lord roars out of Zion, and utters his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shake: but the Lord will be a shelter for his people, and a stronghold for the children of Israel.
verses.Joel|4|17: So shall you know that I am the Lord your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and no strangers shall pass through her any more.
verses.Joel|4|18: And it shall come to pass on that day, that the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the water courses of Judah shall flow with water, and a fountain shall issue from the house of the Lord, and shall water the valley of Shittim.
verses.Joel|4|19: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence done to the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.
verses.Joel|4|20: But Judah shall remain for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
verses.Joel|4|21: And though I have acquitted them, those who shed their blood I have not acquitted; and the Lord will dwell in Zion.
verses.Amos|1|1: The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa which he saw concerning Israel in the day of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.Amos|1|2: And he said, The Lord will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the pastures of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither.
verses.Amos|1|3: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Damascus, I will turn away its punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away its punishment; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron:
verses.Amos|1|4: but I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which will devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.
verses.Amos|1|5: And I will break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the valley of Aven, and him who holds the sceptre from the house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into exile to Kir, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|1|6: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Gaza, I will turn away its punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away its punishment; because they carried away into exile a whole captivity, to deliver them up to Edom:
verses.Amos|1|7: but I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, which shall devour its palaces:
verses.Amos|1|8: and I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him who holds the sceptre from Ashkelon, and I will turn my hand against Ekron: and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish, says the Lord God.
verses.Amos|1|9: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Tyre, I will turn away its punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away its punishment; because they delivered up a complete captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant:
verses.Amos|1|10: but I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre, which shall devour its palaces.
verses.Amos|1|11: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, I will turn away its punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away its punishment; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger tore perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever:
verses.Amos|1|12: but I will send a fire upon Teman, which shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.
verses.Amos|1|13: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, I will turn away their punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away their punishment; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border:
verses.Amos|1|14: but I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the storm:
verses.Amos|1|15: and their king shall go into exile, he and his princes together, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|2|1: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Moab, I will turn away its punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away its punishment; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime:
verses.Amos|2|2: but I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth: and Moab shall die amidst tumult, shouting, and the sound of the shofar:
verses.Amos|2|3: and I will cut off the judge from their midst, and will slay all his princes with him, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|2|4: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Judah, I will turn away his punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away his punishment; because they have despised the law of the Lord, and have not kept his commandments, and their lies, after which their fathers have walked, have led them astray:
verses.Amos|2|5: but I will send a fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.
verses.Amos|2|6: Thus says the Lord; For three transgressions of Israel, I will turn away his punishment, but for the fourth I will not turn away his punishment; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes;
verses.Amos|2|7: that pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and turn aside the way of the humble: and a man and his father will go in to the same girl, to profane my holy name:
verses.Amos|2|8: and they lay themselves down beside every altar upon clothes taken in pledge, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god.
verses.Amos|2|9: Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.
verses.Amos|2|10: Also I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and led you forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.
verses.Amos|2|11: And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O you children of Israel? says the Lord.
verses.Amos|2|12: But you gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not.
verses.Amos|2|13: Behold, I will press you down in your place, as a cart presses down that is full of sheaves.
verses.Amos|2|14: So the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not retain his force, nor shall the mighty man deliver himself:
verses.Amos|2|15: nor shall he who handles the bow stand; and he who is swift of foot shall not deliver himself: nor shall he who rides the horse deliver himself.
verses.Amos|2|16: And he who is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked on that day, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|3|1: Hear this word that the Lord has spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.Amos|3|2: You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.
verses.Amos|3|3: Can two walk together, unless they be agreed?
verses.Amos|3|4: will a lion roar in the forest, when he has no prey? will a young lion cry out of his den, if he has taken nothing?
verses.Amos|3|5: Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where there is no lure for it? does a snare spring up from the earth, and have taken nothing at all?
verses.Amos|3|6: Shall a shofar be sounded in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall evil befall a city, and the Lord has not done it?
verses.Amos|3|7: Surely the Lord God will do nothing, without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets.
verses.Amos|3|8: The lion has roared, who will not fear? the Lord God has spoken, who can but prophesy?
verses.Amos|3|9: Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults within her, and the oppressed in her midst.
verses.Amos|3|10: For they know not to do right, says the Lord, who store up violence and robbery in their palaces.
verses.Amos|3|11: Therefore thus says the Lord God; An adversary there shall be and shall surround the land; and he shall bring down thy strength from thee, and thy palaces shall be spoiled.
verses.Amos|3|12: Thus says the Lord; As the shepherd takes out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear; so shall the children of Israel that dwell in Samaria, escape with the corner of a bed, and the corner of a couch.
verses.Amos|3|13: Hear, and testify in the house of Jacob, says the Lord God, the God of hosts,
verses.Amos|3|14: that in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel upon him I will also punish the altars of Beth-el: and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground.
verses.Amos|3|15: And I will smite the winter house and the summer house together; and the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an end, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|1: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their lords, Bring, that we may drink.
verses.Amos|4|2: The Lord God has sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the days shall come upon you, when you will be taken with hooks, and your remnant with fishhooks.
verses.Amos|4|3: And you shall go out at the breaches, every one straight before her; and you shall be cast away into Harmon, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|4: Come to Beth-el, and transgress; to Gilgal and multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes after three days:
verses.Amos|4|5: and offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and proclaim and publish the free will offerings: for this you like, O you children of Israel says the Lord God.
verses.Amos|4|6: And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet you have not returned to me, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|7: And I too have withheld the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it did not rain, withered.
verses.Amos|4|8: So two or three cities wandered to one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied: yet have you not returned to me, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|9: I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the cutting locust devoured them: yet have you not returned to me, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|10: I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men I have slain with the sword, and I have taken away your horses; and I have made the stench of your camp to come up to your nostrils: yet have you not returned to me, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|11: I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were as a brand plucked out of the burning: yet have you not returned to me, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|4|12: Therefore thus will I do to thee, O Israel: and because I will do this to thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.
verses.Amos|4|13: For, lo, he that forms the mountains, and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his thought, that makes the morning darkness, and treads upon the high places of the earth, The Lord, the God of hosts, is his name.
verses.Amos|5|1: Hear this word which I take up against you, a lamentation, O house of Israel.
verses.Amos|5|2: The virgin of Israel is fallen; she shall no more rise: she is forsaken upon her land; there is none to raise her up.
verses.Amos|5|3: For thus says the Lord God; The city that went out a thousand shall have a hundred left, and that which went forth a hundred shall have ten left for the house of Israel.
verses.Amos|5|4: For, thus says the Lord to the house of Israel, Seek me and you shall live:
verses.Amos|5|5: but do not seek Beth-el, nor enter into Gilgal, and do not pass to Beer-sheba; for Gilgal shall surely go into exile, and Beth-el shall come to nought.
verses.Amos|5|6: Seek the Lord, and live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and devour it, and there be none to quench it in Beth-el,
verses.Amos|5|7: O you who turn judgment to wormwood, and cast down righteousness to the ground.
verses.Amos|5|8: He who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns deepest darkness into morning, and makes the day darken into night: that calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name:
verses.Amos|5|9: who sends forth destruction against the strong, the destruction that comes against the fortress.
verses.Amos|5|10: They hate him who reproves in the gate, and they abhor him that speaks uprightly.
verses.Amos|5|11: Therefore, since you trample upon the poor, and take from him exactions of wheat: you have built houses of hewn stone, but you shall not dwell in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink wine of them.
verses.Amos|5|12: For I know your many transgressions and your mighty sins: you that afflict the just, that take a bribe, and turn aside the poor at the gate.
verses.Amos|5|13: Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time; for it is an evil time.
verses.Amos|5|14: Seek good, and not evil, that you may live: and so the Lord, the God of hosts, shall be with you, as you have spoken.
verses.Amos|5|15: Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish justice in the gate: it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
verses.Amos|5|16: Therefore the Lord, the God of hosts, the Lord, says thus; Lamentation shall there be in all streets; and they shall say in all the highways, Alas! alas! and they shall call the farmer to mourning, and to wailing such as are skilful in lamentation.
verses.Amos|5|17: And in all vineyards there shall be wailing: for I will pass through thee, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|5|18: Woe to you that desire the day of the Lord! why would you have this day of the Lord; it is darkness, and not light.
verses.Amos|5|19: As if a man did flee from a lion, and a bear met him; or went into the house, and leaned his hand on the wall, and a snake bit him.
verses.Amos|5|20: Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness, and not light? even very dark, and no brightness in it?
verses.Amos|5|21: I hate, I despise your feasts, and I will not smell the sacrifices of your solemn assemblies.
verses.Amos|5|22: Though you offer me burnt offerings and your meal offerings, I will not accept them: neither will I regard the peace offerings of your fat beasts.
verses.Amos|5|23: Take away from me the noise of thy songs; for I will not hear the melody of thy lutes.
verses.Amos|5|24: But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
verses.Amos|5|25: Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
verses.Amos|5|26: But you shall carry Sikkut your king, and Chiun, your images, the star image of your God which you made for yourselves,
verses.Amos|5|27: and I will cause you to go into exile beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is the God of hosts.
verses.Amos|6|1: Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria, who are named chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel come!
verses.Amos|6|2: Pass to Calneh, and see; and from there go to Hamath the great: then go down to Gath of the Philistines: are they better than these kingdoms? or is their border greater than your border?
verses.Amos|6|3: You that put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence to come near;
verses.Amos|6|4: that lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;
verses.Amos|6|5: that pluck the strings of the lute, and devise for themselves instruments of music, like David;
verses.Amos|6|6: that drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the ruin of Joseph.
verses.Amos|6|7: Therefore now they shall go into exile at the head of the exiles; and the revelry of those who stretched themselves out shall pass away.
verses.Amos|6|8: The Lord God has sworn by himself, The Lord, the God of hosts says, I abhor the pride of Jacob, and I hate his palaces: therefore I will deliver up the city with all that is in it.
verses.Amos|6|9: And it shall come to pass, if there remain ten men in one house, that they shall die.
verses.Amos|6|10: And if a man's uncle, he that burns him, shall take him up, to bring the bones out of the house, and shall say to him that is in the recesses of the house, Is there yet any with thee? and he shall say, No; then shall he say, Hold thy tongue: for we must not make mention of the name of the Lord.
verses.Amos|6|11: For, behold, the Lord commands, and he will smite the great house into splinters, and the little house into chips.
verses.Amos|6|12: Do horses run upon the rock? does one plough there with oxen? for you have turned judgment into gall, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood:
verses.Amos|6|13: you who rejoice in a thing of nought, who say, Have we not taken to us horns by our own strength?
verses.Amos|6|14: For, behold, I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel, says the Lord the God of hosts; and they shall afflict you from the entrance of Hamath to the wadi of the Arabah.
verses.Amos|7|1: Thus the Lord God showed me; and, behold, he was forming locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and, lo, it was the latter growth after the king's mowings.
verses.Amos|7|2: And it came to pass, that when they had made an end of eating the grass of the land, then I said, O Lord God, forgive, I beseech thee: how shall Jacob stand? for he is small.
verses.Amos|7|3: The Lord relented concerning this: It shall not be, said the Lord.
verses.Amos|7|4: Thus did the Lord God show me: and, behold, the Lord God called to judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep, and was eating up the land.
verses.Amos|7|5: Then I said, O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee: how shall Jacob stand? for he is small.
verses.Amos|7|6: The Lord relented concerning this: This also shall not be, said the Lord God.
verses.Amos|7|7: Thus he showed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.
verses.Amos|7|8: And the Lord said to me, Amos, what dost thou see? And I said, A plumbline. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pardon him any more:
verses.Amos|7|9: and the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
verses.Amos|7|10: Then Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos has conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
verses.Amos|7|11: For thus Amos says, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away into exile out of their own land.
verses.Amos|7|12: And Amaziah said to Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
verses.Amos|7|13: but do not prophesy again any more at Beth-el: for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is a royal house.
verses.Amos|7|14: Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, I am no prophet, neither am I a prophet's son; but I was a herdman, and a dresser of sycamore trees:
verses.Amos|7|15: and the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said to me, Go, prophesy to my people Israel.
verses.Amos|7|16: Now therefore hear the word of the Lord: Thou sayst, Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.
verses.Amos|7|17: Therefore thus says the Lord; Thy wife shall be a harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in an unclean land: and Israel shall surely go into Exile out of his land.
verses.Amos|8|1: Thus the Lord God showed me: and behold a basket of summer fruit.
verses.Amos|8|2: And he said, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A basket of summer fruit. Then the Lord said to me, The end is come upon my people of Israel; I will not again pardon him any more.
verses.Amos|8|3: And the songs of the temple shall become wailings on that day, says the Lord God: many will be the dead bodies; in every place they shall be cast forth; O hush.
verses.Amos|8|4: Hear this, O you that swallow up the needy, so as to destroy the poor of the land,
verses.Amos|8|5: saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the efa small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances of deceit?
verses.Amos|8|6: that we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes; and sell the refuse of the wheat?
verses.Amos|8|7: The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob, saying, Surely I will never forget any of their deeds.
verses.Amos|8|8: Shall not the land tremble for this, and everyone mourn that dwells in it? and it shall all rise up like the River; and it shall overflow and sink down like the River of Egypt.
verses.Amos|8|9: And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord God, that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day:
verses.Amos|8|10: and I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring up sackcloth upon all loins, and baldness upon every head; and I will make it as the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
verses.Amos|8|11: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord God, when I will send a famine in the land, not a famine for bread, nor a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the Lord:
verses.Amos|8|12: and they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.
verses.Amos|8|13: In that day shall the fair virgins and young men faint for thirst.
verses.Amos|8|14: They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, As thy god, O Dan, lives; and As the road to Beer-sheba lives; they shall fall, and never rise up again.
verses.Amos|9|1: I saw the Lord standing besides the altar: and he said, Smite the capitals, that the thresholds may shake: and break them in pieces over the head of all of them; and I will slay the remnant of them with the sword: not a single one of them shall flee away, and not a single one of them shall escape.
verses.Amos|9|2: Though they dig into Sheol, from there shall my hand take them; though they climb up to heaven, from there will I bring them down:
verses.Amos|9|3: and though they hide themselves in the top of the Carmel, I will search and take them out from there; and though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea, from there will I command the serpent, and he shall bite them:
verses.Amos|9|4: and though they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it shall slay them: and I will set my eyes upon them for evil, and not for good.
verses.Amos|9|5: And the Lord God of hosts is he that touches the land, and it melts, and all that dwell therein mourn: and it rises up all of it like the River and sinks down like the River of Egypt.
verses.Amos|9|6: It is he that builds his upper chambers in the heavens, and has founded his stairway in the earth; he that calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out upon the face of the earth: the Lord is his name.
verses.Amos|9|7: Are you not as much mine as the children of the Ethiopians, O children of Israel? says the Lord. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Syria from Kir?
verses.Amos|9|8: Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, says the Lord.
verses.Amos|9|9: For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.
verses.Amos|9|10: All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, who say, The evil shall not overtake or meet us.
verses.Amos|9|11: On that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and repair its breaches; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old:
verses.Amos|9|12: that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the nations, who are called by my name, says the Lord who does this.
verses.Amos|9|13: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when the ploughman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him who sows seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt.
verses.Amos|9|14: And I will bring back the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink their wine; they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
verses.Amos|9|15: And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them, says the Lord thy God.
verses.Obadiah|1|1: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God concerning Edom; We have heard tidings from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the nations. Arise, and let us rise up against her in battle.
verses.Obadiah|1|2: Behold, I will make thee small among the nations: thou art greatly despised.
verses.Obadiah|1|3: The pride of thy heart has deceived thee, thou who dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; who says in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?
verses.Obadiah|1|4: Though thou dost soar aloft like the eagle, and though thou dost set thy nest among the stars, from there I will bring thee down, says the Lord.
verses.Obadiah|1|5: If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grape gatherers came to thee, would they not leave some gleanings of grapes?
verses.Obadiah|1|6: How has Esau been pillaged! how are his hidden things sought out!
verses.Obadiah|1|7: All the men of thy confederacy have driven thee to the border: the men who were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee; they who eat thy bread have laid a snare under thee. There is no discernment in him,
verses.Obadiah|1|8: for shall I not in that day, says the Lord, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?
verses.Obadiah|1|9: And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that everyone from the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.
verses.Obadiah|1|10: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob, shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.
verses.Obadiah|1|11: On the day that thou didst stand aloof, on the day that strangers took captive his substance, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, then thou too wast one of them.
verses.Obadiah|1|12: But thou shouldst not have looked on the day of thy brother on the day of his misfortune; nor shouldst thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction; nor shouldst thou have spoken proudly on the day of distress.
verses.Obadiah|1|13: Thou shouldst not have entered into the gate of my people on the day of their calamity; nor shouldst thou have been among those that looked on their affliction on the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance on the day of their calamity;
verses.Obadiah|1|14: nor shouldst thou have stood on the crossway, to cut off those of his who escaped; nor shouldst thou have delivered up those of his who remained on the day of distress.
verses.Obadiah|1|15: For the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations: as thou hast done, it shall be done to thee: thy deeds shall return upon thy own head.
verses.Obadiah|1|16: For as you have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the nations drink continually, indeed, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.
verses.Obadiah|1|17: But upon mount Zion, there shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their own possessions.
verses.Obadiah|1|18: And the house of Jacob shall be fire, and the house of Joseph flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord has spoken it.
verses.Obadiah|1|19: And they of the south shall occupy the mountain of Esau; and they of the Shephelah the land of the Philistines: and they shall occupy the field of Ephraim and the field of Samaria: and Benjamin shall occupy the Gilead.
verses.Obadiah|1|20: And this exiled host of the children of Israel who are among the Kenaanim as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad, shall occupy the cities of the south.
verses.Obadiah|1|21: And liberators shall ascend upon mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord's.
verses.Jonah|1|1: Now the word of the Lord came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
verses.Jonah|1|2: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
verses.Jonah|1|3: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, and went down to Japho; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare of it, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.
verses.Jonah|1|4: But the Lord hurled a great wind upon the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship seemed likely to be wrecked.
verses.Jonah|1|5: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man to his god, and threw out the articles that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it for them. But Jonah was gone down into the recesses of the ship; and he lay down, and was fast asleep.
verses.Jonah|1|6: So the shipmaster came to him, and said to him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, perhaps God will think upon us, that we perish not.
verses.Jonah|1|7: And they said everyone to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
verses.Jonah|1|8: Then they said to him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; what is thy occupation? and where dost thou come from? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
verses.Jonah|1|9: And he said to them, I am a Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.
verses.Jonah|1|10: Then the men were exceedingly afraid, and they said to him, Why hast thou done this? For the men knew that he had fled from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.
verses.Jonah|1|11: Then they said to him, What shall we do to thee, that the sea may be calm for us? for the sea grew more and more tempestuous.
verses.Jonah|1|12: And he said to them, Take me up, and cast me into the sea; so shall the sea be calm for you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
verses.Jonah|1|13: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to land; but they could not: for the sea grew more and more tempestuous against them.
verses.Jonah|1|14: So they cried to the Lord, and said, We beseech Thee, O Lord, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O Lord, hast done as it pleased Thee.
verses.Jonah|1|15: So they took up Jonah, and cast him into the sea: and the sea ceased from its raging.
verses.Jonah|1|16: Then the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice to the Lord, and made vows.
verses.Jonah|2|1: Now the Lord had appointed a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights.
verses.Jonah|2|2: Then Jonah prayed to the Lord his God out of the fish's belly,
verses.Jonah|2|3: and said, I cried to the Lord out of my distress, and he heard me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried and Thou didst hear my voice.
verses.Jonah|2|4: For Thou didst cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all Thy billows and Thy waves passed over me.
verses.Jonah|2|5: Then I said, I am cast out of Thy sight; yet I will look again towards Thy holy temple.
verses.Jonah|2|6: The waters compassed me about, to the point of death: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
verses.Jonah|2|7: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars closed on me forever: yet hast Thou brought up my life from the pit, O Lord my God.
verses.Jonah|2|8: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in to Thee, into Thy holy temple.
verses.Jonah|2|9: They that guard lying vanities forsake their loyalty.
verses.Jonah|2|10: But I will sacrifice to Thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to the Lord.
verses.Jonah|2|11: And the Lord spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
verses.Jonah|3|1: And the word of the Lord came to Jonah the second time, saying,
verses.Jonah|3|2: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim to it the message that I bid thee.
verses.Jonah|3|3: So Jonah arose, and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey in extent.
verses.Jonah|3|4: And Jonah began to enter the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Another forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
verses.Jonah|3|5: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
verses.Jonah|3|6: For word came to the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
verses.Jonah|3|7: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:
verses.Jonah|3|8: but let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily to God: and let them turn everyone from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
verses.Jonah|3|9: Who can tell? God may turn and relent, and turn away from his fierce anger, so that we perish not.
verses.Jonah|3|10: And God saw their deeds, in that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, which he had said that he would do to them; and he did not do it.
verses.Jonah|4|1: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was vexed.
verses.Jonah|4|2: And he prayed to the Lord, and said, I pray thee, O Lord, was not this my saying, when I was still in my own country? Therefore I fled beforehand to Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and great in love, and repentest of the evil.
verses.Jonah|4|3: Therefore now, O Lord, take my life from me, I pray thee; for it is better for me to die than to live.
verses.Jonah|4|4: Then the Lord said, Art thou so greatly vexed?
verses.Jonah|4|5: So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there he made himself a shelter and sat under it in the shade, till he might see what would come to pass in the city.
verses.Jonah|4|6: And the Lord God appointed a castor oil plant, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his distress. And Jonah was exceeding glad of the plant.
verses.Jonah|4|7: But God appointed a worm when the dawn came up the next day, and it attacked the plant, so that it withered.
verses.Jonah|4|8: And it came to pass, when the sun arose, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat down upon the head of Jonah, so that he fainted; so he asked that he might die, and he said, It is better for me to die than to live.
verses.Jonah|4|9: And God said to Jonah, Art thou so greatly vexed on account of the plant? And he said, I am greatly vexed to death.
verses.Jonah|4|10: Then the Lord said, Thou art concerned about the castor oil plant, for which thou hast not laboured, and which thou didst not rear, which came up in a night, and perished in a night:
verses.Jonah|4|11: and should I not be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred and twenty thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
verses.Micah|1|1: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, Jehizkiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.Micah|1|2: Hear, all you peoples; hearken, O earth, and all that is in it: and let the Lord God be witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
verses.Micah|1|3: For, behold, the Lord comes out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth.
verses.Micah|1|4: And the mountains shall melt under him, and the valleys shall be split, like wax before the fire, and like water that is poured down a steep place.
verses.Micah|1|5: All this is for the transgression of Jacob, and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and what are the high places of Judah? are they not Jerusalem?
verses.Micah|1|6: Therefore I will turn Samaria into a heap of rubble in the field, into a place for planting vines; and I will pour her stones into the valley, and I will lay bare her foundations.
verses.Micah|1|7: And all her carved idols shall be beaten to pieces, and all her hires shall be burned with the fire, and all her idols will I lay desolate: for she gathered them of the hire of a harlot, and they shall return to the hire of a harlot.
verses.Micah|1|8: For this I will wail and howl, I will go stripped and naked: I will make a wailing like jackals, and a mourning like owls.
verses.Micah|1|9: For her wound is incurable; for it has come as far as Judah; it has reached the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.
verses.Micah|1|10: Declare it not at Gath, weep not at all: in Bet-leafra roll thyself in the dust.
verses.Micah|1|11: Pass away, thou inhabitant of Saphir in nakedness and shame: the inhabitant of Zaanan did not come forth to the mourning of Beth-ezel: he will take away from you that standing still!
verses.Micah|1|12: For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good tidings: but evil came down from the Lord to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.Micah|1|13: Harness the chariot to the steed, O inhabitant of Lachish: she was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion: for the transgressions of Israel were found in thee.
verses.Micah|1|14: Therefore shalt thou give presents to Moresheth-gath: the houses of Achzib are a dried up stream to the kings of Israel.
verses.Micah|1|15: Yet will I bring an impropriator upon thee, O inhabitant of Mareshah: the glory of Israel shall come to Adullam.
verses.Micah|1|16: Make thyself bald, and crop thy hair for the children of thy delight; make a wide baldness on thy head like a vulture; for they are exiled from thee.
verses.Micah|2|1: Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they execute it, because it is in the power of their hand.
verses.Micah|2|2: And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.
verses.Micah|2|3: Therefore thus says the Lord; Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which you shall not remove your necks; nor shall you go haughtily: for it will be a time of evil.
verses.Micah|2|4: In that day shall they take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, saying, We are utterly spoiled: he changes the position of my people; how he removes it from me, and divides our field amongst renegades!
verses.Micah|2|5: Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast the line by lot in the congregation of the Lord.
verses.Micah|2|6: They preach, saying, Do not preach: they shall not preach concerning these things, that they shall not take shame.
verses.Micah|2|7: O thou that art named the house of Jacob, is the spirit of the Lord straitened? are these his doings? do not my words do good to him that walks uprightly?
verses.Micah|2|8: And against my people he raises him up as an enemy: you pull off the mantle from the front of the garment of them that pass by securely returning from war.
verses.Micah|2|9: The women of my people you cast out from their pleasant houses; from their children you take away my glory for ever.
verses.Micah|2|10: Arise, and depart; for this is not your place of rest; because of its uncleanness, it shall destroy with a grievous destruction.
verses.Micah|2|11: If a man walking in wind and falsehood would lie, saying, I will preach to thee of wine and of strong drink; he would even be the preacher of this people.
verses.Micah|2|12: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together like the sheep into a fold and like the flock in the midst of their pasture; they shall make a great noise by reason of the multitude of men.
verses.Micah|2|13: The breaker is come up before them: they have broken in, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king passes on before them, and the Lord at the head of them.
verses.Micah|3|1: And I said, Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and you rulers of the house of Israel; Is it not for you to know justice?
verses.Micah|3|2: You who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones;
verses.Micah|3|3: who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and like meat within the cauldron.
verses.Micah|3|4: Then shall they cry to the Lord, but he will not answer them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, because they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.
verses.Micah|3|5: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and whoever puts nothing into their mouths, they prepare war against him.
verses.Micah|3|6: Therefore it shall be night for you, that you shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark for you, that you shall not divine; and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them.
verses.Micah|3|7: Then shall the seers be put to shame, and the magicians confounded: yea, they shall all cover their lips; for there is no answer from God.
verses.Micah|3|8: But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of might, to declare to Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.
verses.Micah|3|9: Hear this, I pray you, you heads of the house of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel, that abhor justice, and pervert all equity;
verses.Micah|3|10: that build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.
verses.Micah|3|11: The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priest thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? no evil can come upon us.
verses.Micah|3|12: Therefore shall Zion for your sake be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps of rubble, and the mountain of the house like the high places of the forest.
verses.Micah|4|1: But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established on the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and peoples shall stream towards it.
verses.Micah|4|2: And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for law shall go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
verses.Micah|4|3: And he shall judge between many peoples, and decide concerning strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, nor shall they learn war any more.
verses.Micah|4|4: But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the Lord of hosts has spoken it.
verses.Micah|4|5: For let all people walk everyone in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.
verses.Micah|4|6: In that day, says the Lord, I will assemble her that limps, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted;
verses.Micah|4|7: and I will make her that limped a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion, from henceforth, and forever.
verses.Micah|4|8: And thou, O tower of the flock, the stronghold of the daughter of Zion, to thee shall it come; the former dominion shall come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.Micah|4|9: Now why dost thou cry out aloud? is there no king in thee? is thy counsellor perished? that pangs have seized thee as a woman in travail.
verses.Micah|4|10: Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt come to Babylon; there shalt thou be rescued; there the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thy enemies.
verses.Micah|4|11: And now many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled, and let our eyes look upon Zion.
verses.Micah|4|12: But they know not the thoughts of the Lord, neither do they understand his counsel: for he has gathered them as the sheaves to the threshing floor.
verses.Micah|4|13: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thy horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many peoples: and thou shalt devote their gain to the Lord, and their substance to the Lord of the whole earth.
verses.Micah|4|14: Now gash thyself, O daughter of troops: he has laid siege against us: they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.
verses.Micah|5|1: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou art little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth to me that is to be ruler in Israel; and his goings out are from ancient time, from days of old.
verses.Micah|5|2: Therefore will he give them up, until the time when she who travails has brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return to the children of Israel.
verses.Micah|5|3: And he shall stand and feed his flock in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God; and they shall abide: for now shall he be great to the ends of the earth.
verses.Micah|5|4: And this shall be peace; when Assyria shall come into our land, and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight princes of men.
verses.Micah|5|5: And they shall graze the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod with the keen blade: thus shall he deliver us from Assyria, when he comes to our land, and when he treads within our border.
verses.Micah|5|6: And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the Lord, like the showers upon the grass, that tarries not for man, nor waits for the sons of men.
verses.Micah|5|7: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations in the midst of many peoples like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, treads down, and tears in pieces, and none can deliver.
verses.Micah|5|8: Thy hand shall be lifted up upon thy adversaries, and all thy enemies shall be cut off.
verses.Micah|5|9: And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord, that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots:
verses.Micah|5|10: and I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strongholds:
verses.Micah|5|11: And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thy hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers:
verses.Micah|5|12: thy carved idols and thy pillars also will I cut off, out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thy hands.
verses.Micah|5|13: And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: and I will destroy thy cities.
verses.Micah|5|14: And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the nations, such as they have not heard.
verses.Micah|6|1: Hear now what the Lord says; Arise, contend before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice.
verses.Micah|6|2: Hear, O mountains, the Lord's controversy, and you strong foundations of the earth: for the Lord has a controversy with his people, and he will contend with Israel.
verses.Micah|6|3: O my people, what have I done to thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me.
verses.Micah|6|4: For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of bondage; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.Micah|6|5: O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam, the son of Beor answered him: from Shittim to Gilgal; that you may know the righteous acts of the Lord.
verses.Micah|6|6: With what shall I come before the Lord, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?
verses.Micah|6|7: will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.Micah|6|8: He has told thee, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love true loyalty, and to walk humbly with thy God?
verses.Micah|6|9: The Lord's voice cries to the city, and the man of wisdom shall see thy name: hear the rod, and who has appointed it.
verses.Micah|6|10: Are there yet the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the scant measure that is abominable?
verses.Micah|6|11: shall I count myself pure with wicked balances, and with a bag of deceitful weights?
verses.Micah|6|12: For its rich men are full of violence, and its inhabitants have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
verses.Micah|6|13: Therefore will I smite thee with sore wounds, and blight thee because of thy sins.
verses.Micah|6|14: Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy sickness shall be in thy inward parts; and thou shalt conceive, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou bringest forth I will give up to the sword.
verses.Micah|6|15: Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thyself with oil; and sweet wine, but shalt not drink wine.
verses.Micah|6|16: For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the deeds of the house of Ahab, and you walked in their counsels; that I should make thee a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof a hissing: therefore you shall bear the reproach of my people.
verses.Micah|7|1: Woe is me! for I am like the last of the summer fruits, like the grape gleanings of the vintage: there is no cluster to eat, no first ripe fruit that my soul desires.
verses.Micah|7|2: The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is no upright one among men: they all lie in wait for blood; each man hunts his brother with a net.
verses.Micah|7|3: Their hands are upon that which is evil, to do it diligently; the prince asks, and the judge is ready for a reward; and the great man utters the evil desire of his soul: and so they weave the web.
verses.Micah|7|4: The best of them is as a brier: the most upright is sharper than a thorn hedge: the day of thy watchmen and thy punishment comes; now shall their perplexity come.
verses.Micah|7|5: Trust not in a friend, put not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lies in thy bosom.
verses.Micah|7|6: For the son dishonours the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter in law against her mother in law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.
verses.Micah|7|7: Therefore I will look to the Lord; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me.
verses.Micah|7|8: Rejoice not against me, O my enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light to me.
verses.Micah|7|9: I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.
verses.Micah|7|10: Then my enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her; who said to me, Where is the Lord thy God? my eyes shall behold her: now she shall be trodden down as the mire of the streets.
verses.Micah|7|11: The day that thy walls are to be rebuilt, that day shall be far removed.
verses.Micah|7|12: But there shall be a day when they shall come to thee from Assyria, and from the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt even to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
verses.Micah|7|13: And the land shall be desolate because of them that dwell in it, for the fruit of their doings.
verses.Micah|7|14: Tend thy people with thy staff, the flock of thy heritage, who dwell solitarily in the wood, in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
verses.Micah|7|15: As in the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt I will show him marvellous things.
verses.Micah|7|16: The nations shall see and be ashamed of all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf.
verses.Micah|7|17: They shall lick the dust like a snake, they shall come trembling out of their holes like crawling things of the earth: they shall be afraid of the Lord our God, and shall fear because of thee.
verses.Micah|7|18: Who is a God like Thee, who pardons iniquity, and forgives the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he does not maintain his anger for ever, because he delights in mercy.
verses.Micah|7|19: He will again have compassion upon us; he will suppress our iniquities. And thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea;
verses.Micah|7|20: thou wilt show truth to Jacob, loyal love to Abraham, as thou hast sworn to our fathers from days of old.
verses.Nahum|1|1: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.Nahum|1|2: The Lord is a jealous and revenging God; the Lord revenges, and is full of wrath; the Lord takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he keeps wrath for his enemies.
verses.Nahum|1|3: The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means acquit the wicked: the Lord, his way is in the tempest and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
verses.Nahum|1|4: He rebukes the sea, and makes it dry, and dries up all the rivers: Bashan languishes, and Carmel, and the flower of Lebanon fades.
verses.Nahum|1|5: The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth is aroused at his presence, both the world, and all that dwell in it.
verses.Nahum|1|6: Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken up by him.
verses.Nahum|1|7: The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows them that trust in him.
verses.Nahum|1|8: But with an overrunning flood he will make an utter end of her place, and darkness shall pursue his enemies.
verses.Nahum|1|9: What do you contrive against the Lord? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.
verses.Nahum|1|10: For they are entangled with thorns, drunken as with their drink; they are devoured as stubble fully dry.
verses.Nahum|1|11: There is one come out of thee, that contrives evil against the Lord, a wicked counsellor.
verses.Nahum|1|12: Thus says the Lord; Though they are at peace, and likewise many, even so they shall be cut down, and it shall pass away. Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more.
verses.Nahum|1|13: For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds asunder.
verses.Nahum|1|14: And the Lord has given a commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the carved idol and the molten image: I will make thy grave; for thou art vile.
verses.Nahum|2|1: Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that brings good tidings, that announces peace! O Judah, keep thy feasts, perform thy vows: for the wicked one shall no more pass through thee; he is utterly cut off.
verses.Nahum|2|2: The batterer is come up against thee: guard the ramparts, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily.
verses.Nahum|2|3: For the Lord restores the pride of Jacob, like the pride of Israel: for plunderers have stripped them, and marred their vine branches.
verses.Nahum|2|4: The shield of his mighty men is made red, the valiant men are in scarlet: the chariots glitter with steel in the day of his preparation, and the spears of cypress wood are brandished.
verses.Nahum|2|5: The chariots shall rage in the streets, they shall jostle one against another in the squares: they seem like torches, they run to and fro like lightnings.
verses.Nahum|2|6: He remembers his valiant men: they stumble in their walk; they make haste to its wall, and the screen is prepared.
verses.Nahum|2|7: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
verses.Nahum|2|8: It is set up; she is uncovered; she is carried away; and her maidens moan as with the voice of doves, drumming on their breasts.
verses.Nahum|2|9: But Nineveh is like a pool of water long established: yet they flee away. Halt, halt, they cry; but none turns back.
verses.Nahum|2|10: Take the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold: for there is no end of the store: there is an abundance of all precious vessels.
verses.Nahum|2|11: She is empty, and void, and waste: and the heart melts, and the knees knock together, and there is trembling in all loins, and the faces of them all are covered with blackness.
verses.Nahum|2|12: Where is the den of the lions, and the feedingplace of the young lions, where the lion, and the lioness walked, and the lion's whelp, and none made them afraid?
verses.Nahum|2|13: The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his holes with prey, and his dens with ravin.
verses.Nahum|2|14: Behold, I am against thee, says the Lord of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.
verses.Nahum|3|1: Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departs not;
verses.Nahum|3|2: The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of prancing horses, and bounding chariots.
verses.Nahum|3|3: The horseman leaps up with his bright sword and glittering spear: and there is a multitude of slain, and a heap of carcasses; and there is no end of corpses; they stumble upon their corpses:
verses.Nahum|3|4: because of the multitude of the harlotries of the charming and bewitching harlot, that sells nations through her lewd practices, and families through her witchcrafts.
verses.Nahum|3|5: Behold, I am against thee, says the Lord of hosts; and I will uncover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will show the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.
verses.Nahum|3|6: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will make thee like dung.
verses.Nahum|3|7: And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?
verses.Nahum|3|8: Art thou better than No, that was situated among the rivers, that had the waters round about it, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea?
verses.Nahum|3|9: Ethiopia the mighty, and Egypt without end; Put and Lubim were thy help;
verses.Nahum|3|10: yet she went into Exile, into captivity: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets: and they cast lots for her honourable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
verses.Nahum|3|11: Thou also shalt be drunken: thou shalt be dazed, thou also shalt seek a refuge from the enemy.
verses.Nahum|3|12: All thy strongholds shall be like fig trees with the first ripe figs: if they are shaken, then they fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.Nahum|3|13: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women: the gates of thy land are set wide open to thy enemies: the fire has devoured thy bars.
verses.Nahum|3|14: Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strongholds: go into the clay, and tread the mortar, take hold of the brick mould.
verses.Nahum|3|15: There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off, it shall eat thee up like the locust: be swept away as with the locust, be swept away as with the swarming locust.
verses.Nahum|3|16: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the locust spreads itself, and flies away.
verses.Nahum|3|17: Thy crowned ones are like the locusts, and thy captains like swarms of grasshoppers, which camp in the hedges in the cold day, but when the sun arises they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
verses.Nahum|3|18: Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles are at rest: thy people are scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathers them in.
verses.Nahum|3|19: There is no healing for thy breach; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the report of thee clap the hands over thee: for upon whom has not thy wickedness passed continually?
verses.Habakkuk|1|1: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.
verses.Habakkuk|1|2: O Lord, how long shall I cry, and Thou wilt not hear! I cry out to Thee of violence, and Thou wilt not save!
verses.Habakkuk|1|3: Why dost Thou show me iniquity, and cause me to behold mischief? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there is strife; and contention raises its head.
verses.Habakkuk|1|4: Therefore law is slackened, and justice does not go out triumphantly: for the wicked man besets the righteous, so that justice goes out perverted.
verses.Habakkuk|1|5: Look among the nations, and behold, and be struck with amazement: for a deed will be performed in your days, which you will not believe, though it be told you.
verses.Habakkuk|1|6: For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, a bitter and impetuous nation, who shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwelling places that are not theirs.
verses.Habakkuk|1|7: They are terrible and dreadful: their justice and their dignity shall proceed of themselves.
verses.Habakkuk|1|8: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the wolves of the desert: and their horsemen shall spread themselves, and their horsemen shall come from far; they shall fly like a vulture hastening to devour.
verses.Habakkuk|1|9: They shall come all of them to do violence; their faces set towards the east: and they shall gather captives like sand.
verses.Habakkuk|1|10: And they shall scoff at kings, and princes shall be a scorn to them: they shall denote every stronghold; for they shall heap dust, and take it.
verses.Habakkuk|1|11: Then he shall vanish, and be gone like the wind, bearing his guilt: such is the strength imputed to his god.
verses.Habakkuk|1|12: Art thou not from everlasting, O Lord my God, my Holy One? we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast ordained them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for correction.
verses.Habakkuk|1|13: Thou art of eyes too pure to behold evil, canst not look on iniquity: why dost Thou look upon them that deal treacherously, and dost hold Thy peace when the wicked devours the man that is more righteous than he?
verses.Habakkuk|1|14: And dost make men like the fishes of the sea, like the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?
verses.Habakkuk|1|15: They take up all of them with the angle, they catch them in their net, and gather them in their drag: therefore they rejoice and are glad.
verses.Habakkuk|1|16: Therefore they sacrifice to their net, and burn incense to their drag; because by them their portion is fat, and their food plenteous.
verses.Habakkuk|1|17: Shall they therefore empty their net, and not spare to slay the nations continually?
verses.Habakkuk|2|1: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say to me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.
verses.Habakkuk|2|2: And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tablets, that he who reads it may run.
verses.Habakkuk|2|3: For there is still a vision for the appointed time; and it speaks concerning the end, and does not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not delay.
verses.Habakkuk|2|4: Behold, his soul is puffed up; it is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.
verses.Habakkuk|2|5: Moreover, wine is treacherous; the arrogant man shall not abide, whose desires gape wide like Sheol; and like death, he cannot be satisfied: for he has gathered to himself all the nations, and has collected to him all the peoples:
verses.Habakkuk|2|6: shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increases that which is not his! how long? and that loads himself with property taken in pledge!
verses.Habakkuk|2|7: Shall not thy exactors rise up suddenly against thee, and thy shakers awaken, and thou shalt be for plunder to them?
verses.Habakkuk|2|8: Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the peoples shall spoil thee; because of men's blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city, and all that dwell in it.
verses.Habakkuk|2|9: Woe to him that gets evil gain for his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil!
verses.Habakkuk|2|10: Thou hast devised shame to thy house by cutting off many peoples, and hast sinned against thy life.
verses.Habakkuk|2|11: For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it.
verses.Habakkuk|2|12: Woe to him that builds a town with blood, and establishes a city by iniquity!
verses.Habakkuk|2|13: Behold, is it not of the Lord of hosts that the peoples labour only for fire, and the nations weary themselves only for vanity?
verses.Habakkuk|2|14: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.
verses.Habakkuk|2|15: Woe to him that gives his neighbour drink, adding thy venom to it, and making him drunken also, that thou mayst look on their nakedness!
verses.Habakkuk|2|16: Thou art filled with shame instead of glory: drink thou also, and stagger: the cup of the Lord's right hand shall be turned to thee, and shameful disgrace shall be on thy glory.
verses.Habakkuk|2|17: For the violence done to Lebanon covers thee, and the spoil of beasts, which made them afraid, because of men's blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city, and to all that dwell therein.
verses.Habakkuk|2|18: What use is there in a carved idol, that its carver has fashioned, a molten image, and a teacher of lies? that the maker should trust in his own manufacture, when he makes dumb idols?
verses.Habakkuk|2|19: Woe to him that says to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, Can it teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in it.
verses.Habakkuk|2|20: But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.
verses.Habakkuk|3|1: A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk (upon Shigionoth).
verses.Habakkuk|3|2: O Lord, I have heard the report of Thee, and I was afraid: O Lord, revive Thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.
verses.Habakkuk|3|3: God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran (Selah). His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.
verses.Habakkuk|3|4: And there is a brightness as the light; rays issue from his hand: and there the hiding of his power is lodged.
verses.Habakkuk|3|5: Before him goes the pestilence, and burning coals go forth at his feet.
verses.Habakkuk|3|6: He stands and shakes the earth: he beholds, and causes the nations to tremble; and the everlasting mountains are dashed in pieces; the eternal hills bow. His ways are as of old.
verses.Habakkuk|3|7: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction: and the curtains of the land of Midian do tremble.
verses.Habakkuk|3|8: Is the Lord displeased against the rivers? is Thy anger against the rivers? is Thy wrath against the sea? that Thou ridest upon Thy horses, Thy chariots of salvation?
verses.Habakkuk|3|9: Thy bow is stripped bare, according to the oaths Thou didst address to the tribes. (Selah.) Thou wilt cleave the earth with rivers.
verses.Habakkuk|3|10: The mountains saw Thee, and they tremble: the stream of water passed by: the deep uttered its voice, and lifted up its hands on high.
verses.Habakkuk|3|11: The sun and moon stood still in their habitation: at the light of Thy arrows as they speed, and at the shining of Thy glittering spear.
verses.Habakkuk|3|12: Thou dost march through the land in indignation, Thou dost thresh the nations in anger.
verses.Habakkuk|3|13: Thou hast come forth for the salvation of Thy people, for the salvation of Thy anointed, Thou hast crushed the head of the house of the wicked, uncovering it from the foundation to the neck. (Selah.)
verses.Habakkuk|3|14: Thou hast pierced with his own shafts the head of his warriors, who come out as a storm wind to scatter me: their rejoicing is as to devour the poor secretly.
verses.Habakkuk|3|15: Thou hast trodden through the sea with Thy horses, through the heap of great waters.
verses.Habakkuk|3|16: When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the sound: rottenness enters my bones, and I tremble where I stand, that I should wait for the day of trouble: when he comes up against the people whom he invades.
verses.Habakkuk|3|17: Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no food; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls:
verses.Habakkuk|3|18: yet I will rejoice in the Lord, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
verses.Habakkuk|3|19: God, the Lord is my strength, and he makes my feet like those of deers, and he guides me on my high places (to the chief Musician; on my stringed instruments).
verses.Zephaniah|1|1: The word of the Lord which came to Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.Zephaniah|1|2: I will utterly consume all things from off the face of the earth, says the Lord.
verses.Zephaniah|1|3: I will consume man and beast; I will consume the birds of the sky, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumbling-blocks with the wicked; and I will cut off man from off the face of the earth, says the Lord.
verses.Zephaniah|1|4: I will also stretch out my hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off the remnant of the Baal from this place, and the name of the idolatrous priests with the priests;
verses.Zephaniah|1|5: and those who worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and those who worship, who swear to the Lord, and who yet swear by Malcham;
verses.Zephaniah|1|6: and those who are turned back from the Lord: and who have not sought the Lord, nor inquired for him.
verses.Zephaniah|1|7: Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord God: for the day of the Lord is at hand: for the Lord has prepared a festal meal, he has bid his guests.
verses.Zephaniah|1|8: And it shall come to pass on the day of the Lord's feast, that I will punish the princes, and the king's children, and all such as are clothed in foreign apparel.
verses.Zephaniah|1|9: And on the same day I will punish all those who leap over the threshold, who fill their masters' house with violence and deceit.
verses.Zephaniah|1|10: And it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord, that there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and a wailing from the second quarter, and a great crashing from the hills.
verses.Zephaniah|1|11: Wail, you inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the merchant peoples are undone; all that weigh silver are cut off.
verses.Zephaniah|1|12: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The Lord does neither good, nor evil.
verses.Zephaniah|1|13: Therefore their wealth shall become a prey, and their houses a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine of them.
verses.Zephaniah|1|14: The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hastens greatly, the sound of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly.
verses.Zephaniah|1|15: That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of ruin and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness.
verses.Zephaniah|1|16: A day of shofar and alarm against the fortified cities, and against the high towers.
verses.Zephaniah|1|17: And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord: and their blood shall be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.
verses.Zephaniah|1|18: Nor shall their silver or their gold be able to deliver them on the day of the Lord's wrath; but the whole land will be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make an end, indeed, a frightful end of all that dwell in the land.
verses.Zephaniah|2|1: Gather yourselves together, and assemble together, O unfeeling nation;
verses.Zephaniah|2|2: before the decree is brought forth, before the day when you pass away like chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord's anger come upon you.
verses.Zephaniah|2|3: Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth, who have performed his judgment; seek righteousness, seek humility: it may be you shall be hidden in the day of the Lord's anger.
verses.Zephaniah|2|4: For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon shall be a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up.
verses.Zephaniah|2|5: Woe to the inhabitants of the sea coast, the nation of the Cherethims! the word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will destroy thee, so that there shall be no inhabitant.
verses.Zephaniah|2|6: And the sea coast shall be pastures, and meadows for shepherds, and folds for flocks.
verses.Zephaniah|2|7: And it shall be an allotment for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed there; in the houses of Ashkelon they shall lie down in the evening: for the Lord their God shall remember them, and restore their captivity.
verses.Zephaniah|2|8: I have heard the taunt of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have taunted my people, and magnified themselves against their border.
verses.Zephaniah|2|9: Therefore as I live, says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be like Sodom, and the children of Ammon like Gomorrah, the breeding place of nettles, and saltpits, and a desolation for ever: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.
verses.Zephaniah|2|10: This they shall have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts.
verses.Zephaniah|2|11: The Lord will be terrible to them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, everyone from his place, all the islands of the nations.
verses.Zephaniah|2|12: You Ethiopians also, you shall be slain by my sword.
verses.Zephaniah|2|13: And he will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, dry like the wilderness.
verses.Zephaniah|2|14: And flocks shall lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts of the nations: both the little owl and the great owl shall lodge in its capitals; their voice shall sing in the window; desolation shall be in the threshold: for he has uncovered the cedar work.
verses.Zephaniah|2|15: This is the joyful city that dwelt securely, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in: every one that passes by her shall hiss, and gesture with his hand.
verses.Zephaniah|3|1: Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city!
verses.Zephaniah|3|2: She did not obey the voice; she did not accept correction; she did not trust in the Lord; she did not draw near to her God.
verses.Zephaniah|3|3: Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves at evening; they gnaw no bones in the morning.
verses.Zephaniah|3|4: Her prophets are worthless, treacherous persons: her priests have polluted the sanctuary, they have violently perverted law.
verses.Zephaniah|3|5: The Lord is just; he is in her midst; he will not do iniquity: every morning he brings his judgment to light; it does not fail; but the unjust knows no shame.
verses.Zephaniah|3|6: I have cut off nations: their pinnacles are desolate; I have made their streets waste, so that none passes by: their cities are destroyed, so that there is no man, there is no inhabitant.
verses.Zephaniah|3|7: I said, Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt accept correction; then her dwelling would not have been cut off, according to all that I had threatened to bring upon her. However, they were up early and corrupted all their doings.
verses.Zephaniah|3|8: Therefore wait for me, says the Lord, until the day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them my indignation, all my fierce anger: for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy.
verses.Zephaniah|3|9: For then I will convert the peoples to a purer language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve him with one consent.
verses.Zephaniah|3|10: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia come my suppliants, the daughters of Puzai, who bring my offering.
verses.Zephaniah|3|11: On that day thou shalt not be ashamed for all thy doings, in which thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee those who rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty in My holy mountain.
verses.Zephaniah|3|12: And I will leave in the midst of thee a poor and lowly people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.
verses.Zephaniah|3|13: The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
